title: fix(health): probe the Grok OAuth forwarder, and infer Ready for an absent dependency
body:
Fixes #366. Two independent gaps, split out of #352.

## 1. The Grok OAuth forwarder was never probed

`healthPayload()` dialled three endpoints — oauth, api, gateway. `PORTS.grokOauth` (4208) is a real fifth forwarder used by `src/grok-oauth-forwarder.mjs`, with no probe at all, so **the router could report `ok: true` while that forwarder was dead.**

- `src/router.mjs:157` — new `GROK_OAUTH_HEALTH` (override `CODEX_ROUTER_GROK_OAUTH_HEALTH_URL`, default `loopback(PORTS.grokOauth, "/health")`), alongside the other three.
- `src/router.mjs:830` — fourth probe, gated `enabled.has("grok-oauth")`: the exact mirror of the `enabled.has("kimi-oauth")` gate. Both are `kind: "oauth"` providers whose forwarder `start.mjs` launches unconditionally, so an unselected provider reports `{reachable: true, enabled: false}` and is never dialled.
- **`degraded` includes it** as `"grokOauth"`, following the other forwarders: standby when unselected so it can never appear, named when selected and unreachable. That is the part that stops `ok: true` with the forwarder dead.
- `src/control.mjs:2579` — projected through the same `safeService` redaction (`reachable` plus optional `enabled`, never a raw payload).
- UI plumbing so the new key isn't silently dropped: `apps/control-center/src/types.ts`, `service-health.ts` (an explicit `FORWARDERS` table replacing the inline `["oauth","api"]` literal), and `apps/desktop/ui/model.mjs`. Both surfaces enumerate forwarders explicitly, so a key nobody lists renders nowhere — which is exactly how this one stayed invisible.

## 2. An absent dependency rendered as Unknown

When `health.ok === true` and an id is absent from `degraded`, that is enough to render Ready; both UIs fell through to "Unknown / Waiting for health report" instead, so a healthy install looked broken.

`dependencyRow` now takes `routerOk` and returns Ready in the `!service` branch when `!offline && routerOk === true`. Unknown is kept for `ok` false or unset. `apps/desktop/ui/model.mjs` applies the same rule with a comment pointing at its TypeScript twin.

## Please look at this in review

**23 call sites across 9 test files gained `CODEX_ROUTER_GROK_OAUTH_HEALTH_URL`.** This is not cosmetic. Without it the new probe falls back to `127.0.0.1:4208` — 18 tests failed, and more importantly **a test router would have dialled the operator's real forwarder port.** That is precisely why those tests already pin the other three health URLs; the new one had to join them. Worth confirming you agree with the breadth of that change.

## Tests

Four new, all verified to **fail on unmodified `main`** (checked in a throwaway detached worktree with only the test files copied in: 4 tests, 0 pass, 4 fail):

- `test/routing.test.mjs` — the Grok probe fires only when the provider is enabled: unselected ⇒ standby, `degraded []`, mock never hit; selected ⇒ `reachable: true`; selected with a dead port ⇒ `degraded ["grokOauth"]` and `ok: false`. On main the payload has no `grokOauth` key at all.
- the existing closed-set assertion widened to `["oauth","api","grokOauth","gateway"]`
- `test/desktop-ui.test.mjs` — the issue's exact case (`{ok: true, degraded: []}` with no `gateway` key ⇒ `ready`), with negative controls for `degraded: ["gateway"]`, `ok: false`, and `undefined`; plus the Grok row rendering
- `test/control-center-electron.test.mjs` — source-text twin for the `.ts` changes, matching that file's established convention

Also corrected a stale comment in `test/health-cache.test.mjs` ("three times" → "up to four times").

## Verification

- `node scripts-check.mjs` — passes
- `tsc --noEmit` in `apps/control-center` — clean
- `node --test test/*.test.mjs` — 2166 tests, **0 failures**, 13 pre-existing skips

title: Windows: a failed startup can abort in libuv teardown (0xC0000409) instead of exiting 1, losing the exit code
body:
## Symptom

`test/devin-forwarder-gating.test.mjs:224` — *"a curated Devin model that cannot bind its port still fails startup by name"* — intermittently fails on `windows-latest` with:

```
AssertionError [ERR_ASSERTION]: 3221226505 !== 1
Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 94
```

`3221226505` is `0xC0000409` (STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN) — the process aborted rather than exiting.

## The startup logic is correct; the exit is not

The captured stderr shows startup doing exactly the right thing before it dies:

```
[kimi-oauth] listening
[devin-cli] cannot listen: 127.0.0.1:14457 is already in use. …
[api-forwarder] listening
[grok-oauth] listening
[model-router] startup failed: Devin CLI forwarder exited before becoming healthy.; inspect the service logs above for details.
Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 94
```

So `exitCode = 1` is set and the failure is named correctly. The crash happens afterwards, in the `finally` block of `src/start.mjs` — `stopChildren()` followed by `await Promise.all(children.map((child) => waitForExit(child, "child")))` — where libuv trips its own assertion closing a handle that is already closing.

## Why this matters beyond a flaky test

`src/router.mjs` already carries a comment about precisely this failure mode:

> *#171 recorded `exited (code=4294967295)` on Windows with no way to tell an in-process crash from an external kill.*

That is the same problem. A supervisor seeing `0xC0000409` cannot distinguish "startup failed cleanly for a nameable reason" from "the process was killed" or "it crashed". The named error goes to the log, but the exit code — which is what the service manager acts on — is garbage. On a real Windows install a failed startup is therefore misclassified.

## Reproduction

Intermittent. Observed on the `windows-latest` runner during CI for #369; an immediate re-run of the same job passed. It is **not** caused by #369 — that PR does not touch `start.mjs`, `devin-forwarder-gating.test.mjs`, or the child-process lifecycle. It added a fourth probe to `healthPayload()`, which makes `waitForRouterHealth` marginally slower and shifts when `stopChildren()` runs relative to child startup. That timing shift appears to widen an existing window.

`94944de` ("stop three flakes, and make a forwarder that cannot bind say so") previously fixed three flakes in this same file, so this area has history.

## Suggested direction

The failing path is teardown of children that are themselves mid-startup — one has already exited (the unbindable Devin forwarder), others have just printed `listening`. Worth checking:

- whether `stopChildren()` can signal a child whose handles are already being torn down, and whether it should guard on the child's state before signalling
- whether `waitForExit` can settle twice for the same child
- whether any `AbortSignal.timeout` timer or undici socket from the health polling is still live when the process exits, and whether those should be explicitly cleared before the `finally` block returns

A cheap partial mitigation, if the root cause is awkward: have the startup-failure path exit through an explicit, drained shutdown rather than falling out of `finally` with handles in flight — the exit code is the thing that needs to survive, and it is currently the thing being lost.

title: fix(dsh): write credentials into the harness envelope without corrupting the document
body:
Closes the gap reported in #351 by @jepgambardella. Same problem, rewritten implementation — please close #351 in favour of this.

## The gap is real

Current DeepSeek Harness builds wrap credentials in a `version` / `refs` envelope; older builds used a flat map at the document root. `applyCredential` only understood the flat shape, so against a current harness the router wrote the credential where the harness would never read it — a 401 at request time with no diagnostic.

## Why a rewrite rather than a patch

#351's approach reproduced four defects, each verified empirically against the unmodified `src/yaml-structure.mjs`. Two of them destroy or strand user data:

**1. Hardcoded 2-space indent emitted YAML no parser accepts.** It used `" ".repeat(refs.indent + 2)` — the column of the `refs:` key, not the indentation its children actually use. Against a 4-space envelope:

```yaml
version: 1
refs:
    OTHER: existing
  CODEX_ROUTER_CALLER_KEY: "sek"   # <- mixed indent
```

`ParserError: expected <block end>`. The user's `.credentials.yaml` becomes unreadable and the harness loses **every** credential in it, including other adapters'.

Now the indent is derived from the first existing entry under `refs`, the same derivation `applyRouteToSettings` already uses 130 lines above with a comment explaining exactly why. `refs.indent + 2` is only the fallback when `refs` is empty. Verified by parsing the output with PyYAML.

**2. Envelope detection keyed off `refs` presence, so a first install wrote to the wrong place.** For `"version: 1\n"` or an empty file, #351 wrote at root level — the legacy flat shape, on precisely the first-install case this exists to fix — while `status()` reported `credentialPresent: true` because it used the same heuristic and found the root-level key.

New `credentialEnvelope`: `refs` present ⇒ envelope; `refs` absent but `version` present ⇒ envelope; no root keys at all ⇒ envelope (the modern default); root keys present with neither `version` nor `refs` ⇒ legacy flat, since that is the only case where the file itself carries evidence of the old shape. `status()` resolves through the same `credentialPath`, so **present-but-unreadable is now unrepresentable**. Neither shape is converted into the other — the shape belongs to the harness build that reads the file.

**3. `removeCredential` no longer restored the document exactly.** Removing the only ref left `version: 1\nrefs:\n`, which parses as `{'version': 1, 'refs': None}` — not the original, and `AGENTS.md:266` requires exact restoration. Now prunes the emptied `refs`, mirroring `removeRouteFromSettings` and its comment that *"An empty mapping there is not the same as an absent one."*

It also removes a stray root-level copy of our own reference on an enveloped document — the state a pre-envelope router build leaves behind — so uninstall no longer strands a second copy of the caller key on disk.

**4. The foreign-document refusal was weakened.** #351 changed the guard to `node.key !== "refs"` and never inspected `refs`' own children, so `refs:\n  server:\n    host: example.com` was edited where main refused it — while the docstring still claimed otherwise. `assertCredentialDocument` now requires root children **and** `refs` children to be leaves.

## Refused rather than guessed

`AGENTS.md:269` is the governing rule: *"A refusal costs a command; a wrong guess rewrites a file whose only copy is on the user's disk."*

- **Inline `refs: {}`** is refused, not extended — matching the existing `providers: {}` refusal. A first install against a harness writing an empty inline map fails loudly with a named refusal.
- **A pre-existing valueless `refs:`** is the one shape that does not round-trip byte-for-byte: apply-then-remove yields `version: 1\n`. Whether an emptied `refs` was created by publishing or pre-existed is undecidable from the after-state, so this follows `removeRouteFromSettings` (never leave an empty mapping) and the test **asserts and explains the actual result** rather than claiming exactness it does not have.
- No document that already declares a shape is converted to the other.

## Tests

11 new/changed. **11 of 11 fail on unmodified `main`** — only the legacy-flat case passes there, which is the one shape main handles. Against #351's implementation, 10 still fail.

Coverage: 2-space and 4-space envelopes (indent column asserted equal to the sibling *and* the output parsed by PyYAML), `version` with no `refs`, empty file, empty `refs:`, legacy flat, misplaced-root-key migration, foreign nested doc refused, inline `refs` refused, a table-driven "every shape parses back as YAML" over 8 shapes × apply/idempotency/remove, and an end-to-end `status()`-agrees-with-writer test over 7 shapes through install/status/uninstall that also asserts the secret is gone and other adapters' keys survive.

## Verification

- `node scripts-check.mjs` — passes
- `node --test test/dsh-config-manager.test.mjs` — 27 tests, 27 pass
- `node --test test/*.test.mjs` — 2183 tests, **0 failures**, 13 pre-existing skips

No real `~/.dsh/` was read or touched; all fixtures are in-memory strings and `mkdtemp` sandboxes.

`AGENTS.md` now records the two-shape rule under "What the harness integration writes".

title: feat: integrate Antigravity browser OAuth routing
body:
## Summary

Clean reopen of scoped **action (a)** from PR #349: the Antigravity OAuth provider body, with the two credential issues and the unbounded retry fixed. Scopes (b) (Windows tray service), (c) (file-security rewrite), and (d) (picker/catalog ordering) from #349 are **out of scope** here and will be reopened separately.

This PR adds a registry-driven Antigravity provider (`antigravity-oauth`) that authenticates against Google's Antigravity service via the router's own browser OAuth2 + PKCE sign-in and a long-running SSE forwarder. It needs no Gemini API key and no separate Antigravity CLI; the signed-in account's Google AI Pro/Ultra entitlement is used.

## What was fixed versus #349

1. **Client secret removed from source.** The hardcoded value is gone. `requireAntigravityClientSecret()` reads `process.env.ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` at call time (it was previously captured at import, which also broke tests that start without a secret). No secret is committed anywhere in this branch's file history.
2. **Default project ID removed.** `INSTALL`/hardcoded `rising-fact-p41fc` is gone. `discoverAntigravityProject` now throws `projectUnavailable` (`project_required`, 502) when no managed Google Cloud project is discoverable on a non-onboarding request path; the sign-in path uses `resolveAntigravityProject` with `allowOnboard: true`.
3. **Bounded retry budget.** The project discovery retry defaults were `attempts: 10` / `retryDelayMs: 5_000`. They now reuse the bounded `DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS = 2` / `DEFAULT_RETRY_DELAY_MS = 1_000` exported from `antigravity-project.mjs`.

## Extra hardening from review

- `antigravity-oauth-forwarder.mjs`: the SSE idle/header timeouts keep their timers referenced (no `.unref()`), so the tests don't hang and the timeout actually fires in `node --test`.
- `antigravity-oauth-shape.mjs`: `cleanAntigravitySchema` now strips `__proto__` / `constructor` / `prototype` keys defensively next to the other unsupported keywords.

## Verification

- `node --test` on the scope (a) suite (antigravity + registry + target-isolation + v2-agent + cli-onboarding): **106 pass / 0 fail / 1 skip**.
- Full suite on baseline fails only on the six pre-existing/Windows-flaky cases (quota/desktop-ui/control/service-render), confirmed identical on a fresh baseline checkout — not regressions from this PR.

## Notes for the author

- `gemini-3.7-flash` in `config/antigravity/oauth/gemini-current.json` keeps `thinking.thinkingBudget: -1` (mapped from its `thinkingBudgets.high: -1`). Because `-1` passes `Number.isFinite`, it bypasses the generic effort branch and is sent verbatim as `thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget: -1`. The shape test asserts this deliberately, but it is worth confirming that is the intended wire value for "high" on this model.
- The four models ship at the default `multiAgentVersion` (v1). They are not marked v2 because the router's v2 route requires native multi-agent / IME proof that is not demonstrated here.

title: fix(minimax): request split reasoning instead of filtering it out
body:
Fixes the leak reported in #333 by @moryk87 — whose diagnosis was right, including identifying `reasoning_split` as the vendor control.

## What the live probe showed

I ran the same prompt against `api.minimax.io/v1/chat/completions` twice, changing only that one field:

| | HTTP | `<think>` in `content` | separate reasoning field |
|---|---|---|---|
| `thinking: {type:"adaptive"}` — main today | 200 | **yes** | none |
| `+ reasoning_split: true` | 200 | **no** | `reasoning_content`, 351 chars |

Without the flag, `content` begins:

```
<think>The user wants me to calculate 17 * 23 and think through it step by step.…
```

With it, `content` carries only the answer and the reasoning arrives in `reasoning_content` — which this router **already** relays as reasoning (`src/router.mjs`, `src/http-utils.mjs`, `src/api-forwarder.mjs`). So nothing downstream needs to change.

That makes this a one-line fix.

## Why there is no output filter here

#333 also added a 163-line Responses stream transform to strip the markup. Now that the source fix is confirmed, that transform would be carrying real risk for no benefit:

- **It rewrites tool-call argument deltas.** `rewriteTextFields` walks `item`/`part`/`output`/`content` with no `event.type` dispatch, which includes `response.function_call_arguments.delta`. A model writing a file that merely mentions `<think>` — a prompt template, an SSE parser, docs about this very feature — gets its arguments truncated into invalid JSON and the tool call fails.
- **`indexOf("\n\n")` never matches CRLF**, so against a CRLF upstream nothing is emitted until flush: the whole response buffers in memory and lands in one burst.
- **An unclosed `<think>` swallows the remainder** of the response, and `_flush` drops pending text too.
- **`response.completed` is not sanitized**, so the markup still reaches session history even when the deltas were cleaned — and history then disagrees with what was displayed.

There is also a downstream interaction: `EmptyCompletionGuard` runs *after* the filter in `router.mjs`, so a turn emptied by the third point above triggers a retry — a second billed turn on content that was not actually empty.

Every one of those is a way to silently delete correct output, which is the hardest kind of failure to trace back to its cause. The underlying bug is cosmetic; a filter that eats tool calls is not. Fixing it at the source removes the whole class rather than managing it.

## Verification

- Live probe as above (small, deliberate token spend, authorized).
- The added assertion in `test/routing.test.mjs` is a real regression test: removing `payload.reasoning_split = true` makes it fail, restoring it passes.
- `node scripts-check.mjs` — passes
- `node --test test/*.test.mjs` — 2193 tests, **0 failures**, 13 pre-existing skips

Please close #333 in favour of this; the CHANGELOG credits the original report.

title: refactor: harden Windows private-file ACL handling (scope b)
body:
## Summary

Scope **(b)** from the split of the earlier bundled PR #349: the `src/file-security.mjs` rewrite.

## What changes

- Removes `currentWindowsSid()` and `windowsFullControlGrant()` (and the exported `windowsFullControlGrant` they exposed) that shelled out to `icacls.exe` and carried the numeric-SID 1332 pitfall.
- `protectPrivateFile()` now performs the ACL rewrite inline in a single PowerShell call: it disables ACL inheritance, drops every existing rule, and grants only the current Windows identity `FullControl`. It no longer depends on `icacls` and its SID prefix handling.
- `privateFileIsProtected()` is stricter and truly verifies the invariant it names: the ACL must be protected, have no inherited rule, grant the current SID full control, and contain no foreign `Allow` grant.

## Why

The old code produced an ACL, but the check did not prove "only the current identity has full control" — foreign `Allow` rules and inherited rules were not rejected, and the `icacls` SID prefix logic was a correctness and portability hazard. The rewrite makes pose and verify arrive at the same definition.

## Verification

- `test/file-security.test.mjs` rewritten to assert the removal of foreign grants, the exact single `FullControl` rule set, inherited-rule rejection, and the strict re-protection path. Runs on Windows (ACL exercise) and passes on POSIX (mode 0600 path).
- Regression run on `test/file-security.test.mjs`, `test/caller-auth.test.mjs`, `test/config-manager.test.mjs`: **40 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail** — the stricter checker does not regress existing private-file handling.

## Scope boundary

This is strictly the `file-security.mjs` change (scope b). It does **not** include the Antigravity provider (scope a, PR #372), the Windows tray/installer work (scope c: separate PR), or the catalog picker ordering (scope d: separate PR). No credentials, no third-party secrets, no unrelated hunks.

title: feat: harden Windows tray lifecycle and add deploy helpers (scope c)
body:
## Summary

Scope **(c)** from the split of the earlier bundled PR #349: the Windows tray + installer PowerShell work.

## What changes

**`src/tray-service-windows.mjs`** — the Task Scheduler tray lifecycle gets hard, bounded state handling:
- Every `schtasks`/COM call now runs under a per-command timeout (`TASK_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS`, 4 s), so a hung Task Scheduler cannot stall the wrapper forever.
- `taskState()` reads Task Scheduler's localized-independent `State` enum instead of parsing `schtasks` text, and falls back between `powershell.exe` and `pwsh.exe`.
- New `waitForTaskState()` turns `stop`/`start` into verified transitions (`TASK_STOP_TIMEOUT_MS`/`TASK_START_TIMEOUT_MS` polling at 250 ms) instead of issuing an unverified `/Run`.
- New `registeredTaskAction()` lets `status` report which executable the registered task actually points at, and whether that companion exists on disk.
- `installTask()` injects an explicit `FullControl` ACE for the task principal through Task Scheduler's COM API, so an elevated install does not leave the unelevated account unable to update its own tray task.
- `uninstall` now re-checks `taskExists()` and fails loudly if Task Scheduler rejected the deletion.

**`codex-router.ps1`** — adds `tray repair`:
- `Get-ValidatedTrayTask` refuses to touch a task whose principal is not the current user, is not interactive, or whose action is not this checkout's companion.
- `Test-TrayTaskFullControl` / `Repair-TrayTaskPermissions` run a narrowly scoped elevated child (`-Verb RunAs`) that validates the task identity from fixed env fields again (closing the UAC race) before rewriting its DACL, then re-installs the companion.

**`install.ps1`** — preserves an already opted-in tray across updates (best effort, never installing on fresh routers), and refreshes managed Codex skills as a best-effort post-health step. Antigravity-specific lines are deliberately absent (they belong to scope a).

**`deploy-codex-router.ps1`** (new) — working-tree deployment helper: robocopy without blanket purge, manifest-based pruning of only prior-deployed files (protects operator notes / unrelated files), then runs the canonical `install.ps1 -CheckoutInstall -Target codex` + `doctor`, and strictly verifies an opted-in tray.

**`restart-codex-router.ps1`** (new) — graceful `service.mjs restart` helper.

## Verification

- `test/tray-service-windows.test.mjs` (new, 17 tests) covers rendering, platform refusal, build gating, dispatcher routing, and the new bounded lifecycle source assertions.
- `test/windows-operations.test.mjs` (new, 6): Windows PowerShell parses the three `.ps1` scripts; asserts the supported service transaction, manifest-based deploy, tray-opt-in preservation, and skills refresh.
- `test/service-render.test.mjs`: unchanged behavior; the one failure (`launchd preserve proxy`) is a pre-existing baseline failure present on `main` too, unrelated to this change.

## Scope boundary

Strictly the Windows tray + installer PowerShell (scope c). Excluded: Antigravity provider (scope a, PR #372), `file-security.mjs` rewrite (scope b, PR #374), catalog picker ordering (scope d, separate PR).

title: feat: group routed models by provider in the catalog picker (scope d)
body:
## Summary

Scope **(d)** from the split of the earlier bundled PR #349: the catalog picker-ordering policy change.

## What changes

**`src/catalog.mjs`**
- Adds `pickerProviderGroup()` / `pickerSlugGroup()` / `routedPickerPriorities()`.
- The merged catalog now orders routed models by a single named vendor policy:
  1. native models first (unchanged),
  2. then `antigravity-oauth`, `deepseek`, then `opencode-go*` groups (ranked, alphabetically within a rank),
  3. then every other provider grouped deterministically after them.
- `sortCatalogModels()` and `buildMergedCatalog()` both route through the group comparator, so the on-disk catalog and the Codex picker (which renders by `priority`, not array order) agree. Routed `priority` values are re-numbered contiguously after the native maximum.

**`test/catalog.test.mjs`**
- New test `merged catalog gives native models first and keeps routed providers contiguous` pins the ordering and the re-indexed priorities.

## Why

Codex renders its picker by `priority`, not by the JSON array order. Without this policy the visible picker could disagree with the catalog file, and external providers were not grouped deterministically. This keeps the operators' primary routes grouped and every other provider stable.

## Verification

- New picker-ordering test passes.
- Regression: `test/catalog.test.mjs`, `test/model-picker-state.test.mjs`, `test/provider-selection.test.mjs` → **87 pass / 0 fail**.

## Scope boundary

Strictly the catalog picker-ordering policy (scope d). Excludes the Antigravity provider (scope a, PR #372), the `file-security.mjs` rewrite (scope b, PR #374), and the Windows tray/installer work (scope c, PR #375). Note the ranking table intentionally names `antigravity-oauth` as a peer provider group; this file itself contains no provider implementation, only ordering policy.

title: feat: Antigravity OAuth provider (reviewed, integration seams closed)
body:
Supersedes #372. Carries **@Zzy-min's four commits unchanged** and adds one commit closing the four integration blockers from the review on that PR. Please close #372 in favour of this — the provider is their work, and before that @FIocker's in #349.

I would have pushed this to the fork branch so #372 could merge directly, but writing to a third party's repository is blocked here.

## The OAuth work is unchanged, because it was already right

Nothing in the credential design was touched. Re-stating what was verified so it is on the record: PKCE with an 86-character verifier and S256, `state` compared *before* the authorization code is consumed with a replay guard, the redirect URI pinned to loopback and re-derived through the same helper at both authorize and exchange so it cannot drift, 0600 token files via `writePrivateJson` with `proper-lockfile` around every read-modify-write, tokens added to `knownLocalSecrets()`, project cache keyed on `sha256(refresh_token)`, and `invalid_grant` tombstoning while `invalid_client` does not.

## The four seams

**1. A dropped `await` broke credential removal for every provider.** `removeApiCredential` went sync→async; `control.mjs` was updated, `provider-key.mjs` was not. Deletion still happened, but `removal.removedFiles` was `undefined`, so `provider-key deepseek remove` printed *"No managed DeepSeek API key file exists"* about a file it had just deleted, skipped the picker refresh, and **silently suppressed** *"a key is still available from the macOS Keychain; remove it there to fully disconnect"*. That last part is why this was blocking: someone who believes they disconnected a provider was no longer told the credential still resolves. Now awaited at `provider-key.mjs:277`, with every call site of all three sync→async functions swept.

**2. The forwarder launched unconditionally on port 4212, so a conflict killed the whole router.** Now gated at `start.mjs:135` on `antigravityOAuthStatus().configured`, with spawn, health-wait and exit-race all using the `...(x ? [y] : [])` spread Devin already uses.

Worth recording why *that* predicate: the review suggested mirroring Devin's `devinCliRouted`, and that would have gated nothing — Antigravity's models are checked in, so `MODELS.some(provider === "antigravity-oauth")` is always true. The stored session is the real equivalent, since `providers enable` refuses before sign-in and `configuredProviderIds()` decides on the same status. `AGENTS.md` gains a rule so this is not "corrected" back later.

Four test files spawn `start.mjs` (not the eleven the review claimed — the other matches were comments and `readFileSync` of the source); each now gets a pooled Antigravity port. The reported `gateway-restart` failure was reproduced first, then fixed.

**3. `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` was documented nowhere and failed only after the user granted Google consent.** The preflight now runs at `antigravity-oauth-onboarding.mjs:192` — before the URL is built (195), printed (198), the listener bound (290) or the browser opened (292) — and names the variable. Documented in `README.md` and `docs/INSTALL.md`.

The test for this is nicer than an assertion on a message: it holds the callback port open, so "no EADDRINUSE" *proves* the check ran before the bind.

**4. The background service never received the secret**, so even a correct build 502'd within the hour — launchd/systemd do not inherit the shell env, and the allowlist gained the three new ports but not the secret. Now forwarded through one shared helper in all three service files, and added to `knownLocalSecrets()` since it lives in a generated file.

**Also:** `ANTIGRAVITY_REDIRECT_URI` validation moved off module top level. It had been evaluated at import in a module now inside `doctor.mjs`'s and `setup.mjs`'s static graph, so a malformed value took down unrelated commands.

## Verification

- All 6 new tests fail on the unmodified #372 tip.
- `node scripts-check.mjs` — passes
- `node --test test/*.test.mjs` — **2253 tests, 0 failures**, 13 pre-existing skips

## Deliberately not done

The review's four follow-ups are untouched — the missing `AbortSignal` in `ensureFreshAntigravitySession`, the now-dead `source: "fallback"` scaffolding, the unreachable `setup-shared.mjs` copy of `onboardAntigravityOauth`, and the misleading "Re-run sign-in" message when `loadCodeAssist` merely failed to reach Google. Each is a behavior change rather than an integration fix, and they belong in their own change.

## Still a maintainer decision

Whether the project wants to ship a client extracted from Google's Antigravity surface — not a public API — is independent of whether this code is correct. This PR does not settle that.

title: feat(compaction): evidence-backed checkpoint format (format half of #344)
body:
The **format half** of #344 by @xpxueA, rebased onto current `main` (their branch was 70 commits behind and conflicting) with the hot-path bridging deliberately held back. Their two commits are preserved; one commit sits on top.

## Why split rather than merge or reject

`src/compaction-checkpoint.mjs` is genuinely good work and I did not want it stalled behind the part that needs more scrutiny: strict base64, byte-bounded UTF-8-safe truncation, a deterministic drop order in `fitCheckpoint`, full re-normalization on both encode and decode, secret redaction, and a model-output contract validator that refuses ambiguous embedded JSON. Its 27 unit tests are adversarial rather than decorative — they assert that reasoning is not mistaken for the final answer, that an assistant-authored rendered checkpoint is not trusted, that oversized or ambiguous JSON is rejected, that counters cannot produce `Infinity` IDs.

## What is held back

`bridgedRoutedHistory`, `historyBridgeKey`, and the in-flight dedupe that exists only to serve them. Together they put work on **every routed turn**: a `JSON.stringify` of the entire pre-boundary history to compute a cache key, and an inline `summarize()` that can bill a second provider request — possibly against a different provider — before the user's turn is forwarded. That changes what an ordinary turn *does*, which deserves its own review rather than riding behind a serialization format.

```
$ git grep -n "bridgedRoutedHistory\|historyBridgeKey" -- src test
(no output)
```

@xpxueA — this is the second half of your PR, and it should go in on its own once the request-path cost is behind a flag with a log line the operator sees.

## Blockers from the review

- **`rewriteHistoryFromCheckpoint`** discarded every pre-boundary item except up to two fingerprint-matched *user* messages, silently dropping `developer`/`system` messages, tool definitions and client preambles. It belonged to the bridge and is held back with it, so the bug cannot occur here.
- **`encodeCheckpoint` threw** when `normalizedCheckpoint` returned `undefined` (bad `recent_tail` id, invalid `counters`), turning a compaction into a 5xx — and a failed compaction ends the session, which the surrounding comments say must be avoided. It now degrades to a minimal valid checkpoint.
- **`extractResponseText`** now names the item types it *refuses* rather than requiring `type === "message"`. The allow-list version would have made a routed provider whose Responses-shaped items omit `type` or carry a vendor tag contribute nothing to a compaction — silently, since `finalizeCheckpoint("")` still reports `ok: true`. A deny-list is the right shape here.
- **`compactOutput`** replays at most the two most recent complete user messages and no longer replays an over-budget message as an unmarked fragment that reads like a complete request. I checked the claim that this loses nothing: over-budget content is retained inside the checkpoint flagged `truncated`, with head and tail preserved around a `...[truncated]...` marker, and `test/compaction-checkpoint.test.mjs` asserts exactly that (`sources.C001.truncated === true`).

## Docs

The original PR's `CHANGELOG.md` and `docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md` text described the bridging in detail — an automatic history boundary on routed requests, pre-boundary replacement, a 24-hour 64-entry cache. All of that has been removed rather than shipped as a claim about behavior that is not in this branch. `HOW-IT-WORKS` now states plainly that routed turns carrying a native OpenAI compaction item are unchanged by this work, and why.

## Verification

- `node scripts-check.mjs` — passes
- `node --test test/*.test.mjs` — **2218 tests, 0 failures**, 13 pre-existing skips
- One run showed a single failure which did not reproduce across two further runs; it was the known `POSIX install and enable preserve the PATH-selected Node wrapper` flake, which also fails intermittently on `main`.

title: feat: ship Ox Alpha on six routes and add Venice and Nous Research providers
body:
Ox Alpha is one stealth 1M-context reasoning model that six of this repository's providers resell, each under its own id. Every upstream id and context window below was read from that provider's **own live catalog**, not inferred from the family name.

| Picker label | Model ID | Upstream id | Needs a key |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Ox Alpha (OpenCode Free) | `opencode-free/ox-alpha` | `x-preview-f-free` | no |
| Ox Alpha (opencode Go) | `opencode-go/ox-alpha` | `ox-alpha-free` | opencode |
| Ox Alpha (OpenRouter) | `openrouter/ox-alpha` | `stealth/ox-alpha` | OpenRouter |
| Ox Alpha (Command Code) | `commandcode/ox-alpha` | `stealth/ox-alpha` | Command Code |
| Ox Alpha (Nous Research) | `nousresearch/ox-alpha` | `stealth/ox-alpha` | Nous Portal |
| Ox Alpha (Venice) | `venice/ox-alpha` | `stealth-ox-alpha` | Venice |

All six advertise 1,048,576 tokens of context with 131,072 of output and text+image input, a **low / high / max** effort ladder defaulting to `max`, and zero pricing during the preview, so they carry `isFree` and show a **Free** badge in the control center.

## The effort ladder belongs to the model, not the reseller

Three rungs, and the upstream enumerates them itself:

```
HTTP 400 — [1210] This model always engages in thinking and cannot be
disabled; please use low, high, or max
```

`none`, `off`, `minimal`, `medium`, `xhigh`, `ultra`, `default` and `auto` all draw that response. `low`, `high` and `max` return 200 with monotonically rising reasoning-token counts (2 / 25 / 45), so the three rungs are real behavior, not just enum validation.

**Venice is the one catalog that disagrees, and it is the one to distrust.** It advertises `none/low/medium/high` for this id — but that is its most generic shape, shared with eight unrelated models, and it contains `none`, a rung this model refuses by name. Venice publishes model-specific ladders when it has them (`low/high/max` for GLM-5.3, `none/high/max` for GLM-5.2), so the generic shape here reads as an unverified onboarding default. OpenRouter's live API, Nous Portal's live API, and models.dev for `openrouter`, `opencode-go`, `opencode`, `kilo` and `nano-gpt` all say `low/high/max`.

AGENTS.md records this as the standing exception to "the provider's own catalog decides": when a reseller advertises a rung the model rejects by name, the model wins — and the disagreement gets written down rather than silently resolved.

## Why the request profile is load-bearing

Codex only gained the `max` variant in 0.143.0, so on anything older the clamp in `src/catalog.mjs` rewrites this model's default down to `xhigh` — a rung the upstream refuses. Without a fix, every Ox Alpha turn on a pre-0.143 Codex would 400.

The new `ox-alpha` request profile clamps whatever Codex sent onto the rungs the model's own registry entry declares (`xhigh`/`ultra` → `max`, `medium`/`minimal` → `low`). It reuses the ladder walk the GLM profile already had (`glmEffort` → `declaredEffort`; no behavior change for GLM).

## New providers

**Venice** (`venice`, `https://api.venice.ai/api/v1`) and **Nous Research (Hermes)** (`nousresearch`, `https://inference-api.nousresearch.com/v1`) are new API-key providers: selectable through `install.sh --providers`, `providers enable`, the tray setup card, and `doctor`, each with its own credential isolation and provider mark. Venice carries a `planNote` because a free Venice account has no API entitlement at all — API access needs Pro (the Explorer tier), a funded USD balance, or staked VVV granting VCU.

## Subscription state in the tray and control center

- **Venice** — `api_keys/rate_limits` reports every pool that can fund a request (USD, VCU, and the daily DIEM allowance) plus the API tier, so a full VCU balance no longer displays as a zero.
- **OpenRouter** — per-key spend cap from `/api/v1/key`, plus the account-wide credit pool when the stored key is a management key; the per-key numbers survive when `/credits` answers 403 for an inference key.
- **Nous Portal** — publishes no credits route at all (404 on both `/v1/credits` and `/v1/key`), so it degrades to its subscription page and observed router traffic rather than inventing a number.

Provider marks for Venice, Nous Research, and OpenRouter ship for both the tray and the control center, sourced from each official site and adapted to the white-on-transparent form the Island's black bezel needs. Provenance is recorded in both `SOURCES` files.

## Verification

- `npm run check` and `npm test` — 2062 passing, 0 failing.
- `apps/control-center`: `npm run check` (tsc) and `npm run build` both clean; the new assets bundle.
- `apps/macos/ModelRouterTray`: `swift build -c release` and `swift test` both clean.
- **Live, at zero cost**, through the credential-free OpenCode route: every rung probed individually (see the ladder section above); raw `xhigh` is a 400 upstream while the same request through the router's own forwarder returns 200 with reasoning tokens; forced `tool_choice: "required"` returns a well-formed tool call.
- `doctor`, `providers list`, `provider-key … status`, and `control provider-usage` all report the three providers correctly.
- New coverage in `test/ox-alpha.test.mjs` and `test/routing.test.mjs` pins the upstream ids, the ladder, the pre-0.143 clamp/undo round trip, and each new account-usage surface.

## One related fix

The official-name table in `src/user-models.mjs` was overwriting a checked-in fragment's `displayName`. It exists to fill in a name *curation* could not know, so it now applies only to curated entries — otherwise it flattened "Ox Alpha (OpenCode Free)" back to the curated label and lost the only thing telling the six routes apart.

## Note

Free here is a preview, not a property. No lab has claimed this model and the routes can narrow or withdraw it without notice. If they start billing it, the honest change is to drop `isFree` and rewrite the descriptions rather than leave a Free badge on a metered model.

title: fix(windows): drain startup handles before exit (split from #372)
body:
Carries **@Zzy-min's `d32f8a9` unchanged** (`fix(windows): drain startup handles before exit`) from #372, split out on its own because it fixes a latent bug that is already on `main` and is not specific to the Antigravity provider it currently rides behind.

## The bug

`src/start.mjs` ended with a synchronous `process.exit(exitCode)`. When a child forwarder dies during startup — an `EADDRINUSE` on its port, for example — that call races libuv's Windows async-handle close path and aborts the process:

```
Assertion failed: !(handle->flags & UV_HANDLE_CLOSING), file src\win\async.c, line 94
3221226505 !== 1
```

The error message is printed correctly; the process then dies with `0xC0000409` instead of exiting `1`, so any test asserting the exit code fails.

## Why split it out

It is non-deterministic, so it does not fail every run — `main`'s own CI passed at `a44f498`. But it has now been observed on two unrelated PRs, in two different tests of the same shape:

- **#374** (`file-security` ACLs — touches nothing in this path) — `test/devin-forwarder-gating.test.mjs:224`, *"a curated Devin model that cannot bind its port still fails startup by name"*
- **#377** (Antigravity) — `test/antigravity-forwarder-gating.test.mjs:226`, *"a stored Antigravity session that cannot bind its port still fails startup by name"*

Both aborted with the identical libuv assertion. #374 was green on its previous base and went red purely on being refreshed onto current `main`, which is what surfaced this: it is a dice roll against every Windows run, and it will keep failing unrelated PRs until it is fixed.

`devin-forwarder-gating.test.mjs` is currently the only test on `main` that exercises the path; a second one arrives with the Antigravity provider.

## Why `process.exitCode` is safe here

The assignment is the last statement in the file, so Node exits naturally once the loop drains. Nothing holds it open: the `finally` block already `await`s every child's exit, `start.mjs` opens no listener of its own, and its single timer is `.unref()`'d (`src/start.mjs:235`).

Empirically — #372, whose HEAD is exactly this commit, is green on both `test (windows-latest)` and `desktop (windows-latest)`.

## Credit

The commit and the diagnosis are @Zzy-min's, from #372. Nothing was changed; it is cherry-picked with authorship intact. #372 keeps the commit in its own history and will merge through it harmlessly.

title: fix: keep test runs out of this machine's systemd
body:
The service write guard has two halves. The unit-file half was already on the Linux module — a test that has not redirected `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` cannot write the unit. The service-manager half was not, and it is the half that does the damage.

`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` moves where the unit is written, not where the running systemd reads from. So an install that isolated itself correctly still reached `systemctl --user enable --now codex-router.service` against the developer's own unit, stopped their router, and — once the test removed its temporary directory — left systemd pointing at a unit that no longer existed. Nothing in the run said so.

launchd had exactly this failure and already skips it (`eff69e7`, `bc9a39c`); Windows followed in `f57af1a`. systemd was left behind when the skip was scoped to launchd, so `src/service-linux.mjs` had zero references to `skipServiceManagerCall` and the guard suite had zero Linux coverage.

## Change

- Route the mutating `systemctl` verbs (`daemon-reload`, `disable`, `enable`, `restart`, `start`, `stop`) through `skipServiceManagerCall`, matching `service-macos.mjs`.
- Reads stay live, for the same reason they do under launchd: `status` has to keep answering whether the unit is really active, or the doctor reasons from a state the skip invented.

## Tests

- A Linux-gated test mirroring the existing launchd one — deliberately omits the opt-out flag, asserts the machine's own unit enablement is unchanged and the fixture still gets its unit. Runs on CI's `ubuntu-latest` job.
- Two recorder tests that run anywhere a POSIX shell does, so the verb list is pinned on macOS too, where the module is driven against stubs and only the explicit flag suppresses the call.

Verified the skip test fails against the unpatched module and passes with it. `npm run check` and the four service suites pass (27 passed, 0 failed, 2 platform-skipped), with the machine's launchd registration byte-identical before and after.

## Context

This surfaced from a live incident: the router was dead with `Connection failed: error sending request`, and `launchctl print` showed the label registered against a deleted test fixture in a 65-iteration crash loop. That was the macOS instance of this bug, already fixed on `main`. This closes the remaining platform.

Note that any branch predating `eff69e7` still re-breaks a developer machine when its tests run — see PR #379.

title: fix(windows): bound service process identity probes
body:
## Summary

Bound the synchronous PowerShell process-identity probes used by the Windows managed service so a stuck `Get-Process`, CIM, or WMI query cannot block router startup indefinitely.

## Why

While diagnosing a Windows install, the Scheduled Task launcher chain was alive (`wscript -> cmd -> node start.mjs`) but none of the router ports had bound. An absolute-path foreground `start.mjs` invocation later started normally, and the managed service also recovered on a later retry, so this PR does **not** claim that the process-identity probe was conclusively the root cause of that one transient incident.

It does address a concrete robustness issue found during that investigation: `processStartIdentity()` and `processCommandLine()` use synchronous PowerShell subprocesses on Windows with no timeout. If one of those OS queries stalls under Task Scheduler, `start.mjs` can remain blocked before the router starts listening.

## Change

- add a 5 second timeout to the Windows `Get-Process` identity probe
- add the same timeout to both command-line probes (`Get-CimInstance`, then `Get-WmiObject` fallback)
- leave non-Windows probe behavior unchanged
- preserve fail-closed ownership semantics: a timeout still produces no verified identity/command line, so the router refuses to adopt or act on an unverified process

## Tests

Added `test/process-identity.test.mjs` covering:

- bounded Windows identity probing
- bounded CIM/WMI fallback behavior
- unchanged non-Windows spawn options

Targeted validation performed before opening this PR:

```text
node --check src/process-identity.mjs
node --check test/process-identity.test.mjs
node --test test/process-identity.test.mjs
```

Result: 3/3 tests passed.

The repository CI can provide the full macOS/Linux/Windows suite required by the development guide.

## Scope

This is intentionally a narrow service-start robustness change. It does not alter process ownership checks, service lifecycle behavior, routing, provider handling, or credentials.

title: feat: Antigravity OAuth provider, reconciled from #372 and #377
body:
Supersedes #372 and #377. **Carries @Zzy-min's commits unchanged** as its base, with one commit on top porting the work that only #377 had.

## Why a third PR rather than merging one of them

#377 was opened as "supersedes #372, carries their four commits unchanged". That was true when it was written. It is not true now: @Zzy-min pushed four more commits to #372 that independently fixed the same four integration seams, and the two branches diverged. Each ended up with real work the other lacked, so **merging either one alone would have shipped a regression**.

Both were refreshed onto current `main` and both were green-ish before this was built, so the choice was never about which one was broken.

### Only #372 had these — kept

| | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| full `tool_choice` → `functionCallingConfig` mapping | #377 hardcodes `{ mode: "VALIDATED" }`, so `tool_choice: "none"` would not suppress function calls |
| `OAUTH_LOGIN_TIMEOUT_MS` (11 min) on `connect_oauth` | #377 drops it, falling back to the 120 s `CONTROL_TIMEOUT_MS` at `desktop-commands.mjs:187` — a five-scope Google consent routinely exceeds that |
| `AbortSignal` through `withTokenLock` / `refreshAntigravityToken` | #377 has no cancellation path |
| `installGracefulShutdown()` | #377 hand-rolls `process.on(SIGINT/SIGTERM)` |
| `repairAntigravityOAuthPermissions()` in `doctor repair` | dropped from #377's repair path |
| the "may provision a Google Cloud project" notice | #377 removed it |
| `requireAntigravityClientSecret()` before the Promise | strictly earlier than #377's placement inside it |

### Only #377 had these — ported

| | Why it matters |
|---|---|
| `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` in `knownLocalSecrets()` | the service definitions now carry the secret, so without this a support bundle can leak it |
| `project_source: "fallback"` | a recorded absence stops being mistaken for a project: the validator accepts the state, a fallback never persists a `project_id`, `alreadyResolved()` refuses inside the cache TTL, and `forceFallbackRefresh` lets the retry path past it |
| `antigravityClientSecretEnvironment()` | one helper replacing the same conditional spread inlined in all three service modules |
| the error naming the missing variable | says which variable and why the background service needs it too |
| the post-sign-in restart notice | the forwarder only spawns with the service, so a router started before sign-in has none |

The forwarder keeps #372's `controller.signal` **and** gains #377's `forceFallbackRefresh` — they are independent and both are wanted.

## Not ported

#377's extraction of `configureProvider` into `setup-shared.mjs`. It is factoring with no behavioural difference, and #372 already has the guided Antigravity path inline at `setup.mjs:336`. Left out deliberately to keep this diff to things that change behaviour.

## Verification

Built on current `main` (`566c9e4`) so it does not conflict. Locally, `test/antigravity-*`, `test/service-render` and the support-bundle suites: **84 pass, 0 fail, 1 skip** — including *"background services preserve the Antigravity client secret"*, which covers the helper refactor across all three service modules.

## Credit

The provider is @Zzy-min's work, and before that @FIocker's in #349. The base here is their branch with history intact; the single commit on top is the reconciliation.

title: Windows service startup can exit early on transient spawn timeout, then repair waits full 300s
body:
## Summary

On Windows, `doctor --fix` can spend the full 300-second readiness budget after the Scheduled Task has already exited with `LastTaskResult = 1`. The service log also shows a transient `spawnSync(...python.exe) ETIMEDOUT` being classified as a broken LiteLLM venv even though an immediate later `doctor` successfully runs the same interpreter.

This was found while debugging #382, but it appears to be a separate failure mode from that PR's process-identity timeout hardening.

## Observed behavior

`doctor --fix`:

```text
Router did not become healthy within 300 seconds: fetch failed
Background-service installation failed.
```

Immediately afterward:

```text
service.mjs status: {"installed":true,"loaded":false,"state":"ready"}
Scheduled Task: Ready
LastTaskResult: 1
ports 4200-4203: none listening
router process tree: no matching wscript/cmd/node process
```

So this occurrence was not a live-but-stuck service. The task had already exited and the outer readiness loop continued polling until the full 300 s budget expired.

Relevant startup log entries from the same machine include:

```text
[model-router] startup failed: Timed out waiting for OAuth forwarder to become healthy (the service did not answer within 1000 ms).

Error: The LiteLLM virtual environment is broken at ...\.venv\Scripts\python.exe (spawnSync ...\python.exe ETIMEDOUT).
```

An immediate later `doctor` reports:

```text
OK LiteLLM venv runtime: ...\.venv\Scripts\python.exe runs
```

## Code paths

- `src/service.mjs` waits `READINESS_TIMEOUT_MS = 300_000` after a successful platform `start` command and does not observe whether the Windows Scheduled Task exits during that wait.
- `src/venv-runtime.mjs` performs `spawnSync(python, ['--version'])` with a 15 s timeout and returns any `probe.error` as a runtime problem. That makes `ETIMEDOUT` indistinguishable from persistent venv corruption to `start.mjs`.
- `src/health-probe.mjs` already treats an internally timed-out HTTP health probe as inconclusive and retries with a wider window, which suggests similar transient-timeout handling may be appropriate for process launch.

## Expected behavior

Two possible improvements, likely separable:

1. Windows service start/repair should fail early with the Scheduled Task's exit/result when the managed task has already terminated, instead of polling router health for five minutes.
2. A transient interpreter spawn timeout should not be reported as a definitively "broken" venv. It could be retried with a wider bounded window or surfaced as a distinct transient startup failure while preserving a hard bound.

## Notes

This issue does not claim the OAuth-forwarder timeout and Python spawn timeout have one root cause. Both point to severe transient Windows process/scheduling delay on this machine, but the actionable defects above are about how those conditions are classified and reported.

No credentials or caller URLs are included here.

title: fix: filter empty DeepSeek assistant messages after tool calls
body:
## Why

While using DeepSeek, we found that tool-call responses can include an additional empty assistant message.

Codex treats this empty message as a separate content block, causing unusually large gaps between tool activity entries.

In the actual response, the empty message was preceded by a `reasoning_text` event. The previous filter incorrectly treated this event as visible assistant text and released the empty message.

## What

- Correct the detection of empty assistant messages.
- Do not treat `reasoning_text` as visible assistant text.
- Treat only non-empty `output_text` or `text` as visible assistant text.
- Prevent empty messages associated with tool calls, along with their related events, from being forwarded to Codex.
- Add a regression test matching the event sequence observed in the actual DeepSeek response.

## Test

- Reproduced and confirmed the event sequence with one real DeepSeek request.
- Updated the test fixture to include the `reasoning_text` event observed in the actual response.
- Before the fix, the regression test failed because the empty assistant message reached Codex.
- After the fix, the same regression test passed.
- `node --check src/tool-message-compat.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.

## Test Scope

Only DeepSeek was tested with a real request in this change.

The filtering logic applies to external models connected through the Router. If another external model returns the same empty-message pattern, this logic will also run, but no real requests were made to other external models as part of this change.

Native Codex GPT models do not pass through this external-model filtering logic and are therefore unaffected.

title: fix(windows): fail readiness early on a dead task; retry transient interpreter probes
body:
## Summary

Fixes the two actionable defects from #384. Fixes #384.

1. **Readiness no longer polls a dead task for 300 seconds.** Task Scheduler can report `State=Running` while `GetInstances(0)` enumerates zero running instances, and `LastTaskResult` preserves why the task exited. `src/service.mjs` now waits through a readiness guard that consults that enumeration: a brief absence is tolerated as launch lag, and an absence persisting past a grace window fails early with the task's own result (e.g. `LastTaskResult=0x1`) instead of waiting out the full budget.
2. **A transient interpreter spawn timeout is no longer reported as permanent venv corruption.** A `spawnSync ETIMEDOUT` on the venv's `python.exe` means Windows never finished scheduling the child — on the reporting machine the same interpreter ran five times in 0.084-0.144s immediately afterward. The probe now retries once with a wider hard bound before reporting, and the persistent-timeout wording names scheduling pressure rather than a broken venv.

## Design notes

- Fail-closed semantics preserved everywhere: a timeout or query failure produces no verified state. An unavailable Task Scheduler query stays inconclusive so a restricted shell cannot turn a slow-but-valid startup into a false failure; only a *confirmed persistent* zero-instance state fails early.
- No timeout budgets were raised except one bounded retry inside the existing probe contract (15s then up to 45s), per the issue's "do not blindly increase timeouts" note.
- Non-Windows behavior unchanged: the guard delegates to the existing health wait.
- Tests never touch the real Scheduled Task: task-state queries and health waits are injected fakes in every case.

## Tests

- `test/windows-task-state.test.mjs`: COM-based instance count + LastTaskResult parsing, query-failure/malformed-output staying inconclusive, non-Windows never invoking Task Scheduler.
- `test/service-readiness.test.mjs`: early failure with the task's result after persistent absence, launch lag tolerated, unavailable queries failing open, non-Windows health-only, and the service delegating its budget to the guard.
- `test/venv-runtime.test.mjs`: transient timeout retried with the wider bound; persistent timeout worded as scheduling pressure; non-timeout failures not retried.

`npm run check` passes. Targeted suites pass locally on Windows; the repository CI provides the full macOS/Linux/Windows matrix.

title: fix(errors): anonymous providers have no stored credential to refresh
body:
## Summary

Anonymous providers (`opencode-free`, `kilo-free`) hold no credential, but a 401 from their upstream told the operator to "re-run codex-router setup to refresh them" — advice pointing at something that does not exist.

## Live case

OpenCode Zen intermittently answers its free route with `401 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"ModelError","message":"Model  is not supported"}}` (note the blank model slot) for a model its own `/models` endpoint lists. During one such window the router relayed:

> opencode rejected the stored credentials while serving Ox Alpha Free. Re-run codex-router setup to refresh them.

The same request succeeded minutes later, and direct anonymous calls to the documented endpoint succeeded throughout — so nothing is stored, and nothing can be refreshed.

## Change

- Plumb the provider's `authMode` into `translateGatewayError` beside the existing `providerKind`.
- A 401/403 from an `authMode: "anonymous"` provider now says there is no stored credential to refresh, that free catalogs and limits change without notice, and to retry later or switch models.
- Providers without an authMode keep the existing wording unchanged; OAuth keeps its sign-in wording; quota and entitlement classification still run first and are untouched.

## Tests

`test/error-translation.test.mjs` gains the captured live body as a fixture asserting the anonymous wording never advises setup, plus a guard that the default credential wording survives when no authMode is present.

title: [Q] Suggest changing the default behavior template for routed models from GPT-5.5 to GPT-5.6-Sol
body:
**Background**

External models like `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` don't specify their own `behaviorTemplate`, so they inherit the project's default behavior template. Currently that default is the GPT-5.5 one.

Comparing the two templates, I personally think GPT-5.6-Sol is a better fit for routed external models when it comes to skill support and communication, mainly because:

- It has a complete Skills system section, so external models can discover and use skills (like caveman, karpathy) the same way native models do.
- It makes a clearer distinction between "when to change code" and "when to only do read-only investigation", which matches everyday agent collaboration habits better.
- The communication style is more human, and output is more concise.

The GPT-5.5 template, on the other hand, leans heavily on frontend UI detail and has no skills system at all, so external models that inherit it end up with a worse experience.

After changing the default template to 5.6-Sol locally and running DeepSeek, it felt good.

**Question**

Would you consider changing this default behavior template to GPT-5.6-Sol? 

If you think it's a good idea, I'm happy to submit a PR.

title: flaky: installer-scripts PATH-selected Node wrapper test fails intermittently on hosted macOS
body:
`test/installer-scripts.test.mjs` — *"POSIX install and enable preserve the PATH-selected Node wrapper"* — fails intermittently on the GitHub-hosted **macOS** runner. It has hit `main` itself, so it is not attributable to any open PR.

## Occurrences (2026-08-23)

| run | branch |
| --- | --- |
| 32652571693 | #387 |
| 32646427023 | #379 |
| 32638689774 | #377 |
| **32638524852** | **`main` — `566c9e4`, push** |
| 32638255975 | #377 |

`566c9e4` is the merge commit of #375 and is in `main` history; its `test (macos-latest)` job failed. Same-day CI totals were 27 success / 11 failure, so this is a meaningful share of the red.

Always macOS. `test (ubuntu-latest)` and `test (windows-latest)` pass in every one of these runs.

## The failing assertion

`test/installer-scripts.test.mjs:204`:

```js
const routedCalls = calls.filter((line) => line.includes("\t<src/"));
assert.ok(
  routedCalls.every((line) => line.startsWith(`${wrapper}\t${servicePath}\t`)),
  calls.join("\n"),
);
```

The stub wrapper logs `$CODEX_ROUTER_NODE_BIN`, `$PATH`, then its argv. The assertion requires every routed call to have been invoked through the fixture wrapper with exactly the `PATH` the test handed it, where `servicePath` is built as `` `${wrapperDir}:${process.env.PATH}` ``.

Recorded `PATH` in a failing run carries npm's ancestor chain:

```
/var/folders/.../runtime bin % wrapper:/Users/runner/work/codex-router/codex-router/node_modules/.bin:/Users/runner/work/codex-router/node_modules/.bin:/Users/runner/work/node_modules/.bin:...
```

## Not reproducible locally

On an Apple-silicon macOS host against the same commit:

- 10× `node --test test/installer-scripts.test.mjs` — 10 pass
- 8× `npm exec -- node --test test/installer-scripts.test.mjs` (to pick up npm's `PATH` prepending) — 8 pass
- 3× full `npm test` over the course of the day — all green

So whatever the trigger is, it is specific to the hosted runner rather than to macOS as such.

## Why it is worth fixing rather than re-running

The fixture path is deliberately hostile — `runtime bin % wrapper`, containing spaces and a `%` — which is the point of the test. Two candidate directions, neither verified:

1. The assertion pins an exact `PATH` string. If anything in the install path re-derives or re-prepends `PATH`, the comparison breaks without the behaviour under test being wrong.
2. `os.tmpdir()` on macOS returns `/var/folders/...`, a symlink to `/private/var/folders/...`. Any realpath resolution along the way would make the logged binary path differ from `${wrapper}` — though that alone would be deterministic, not intermittent.

The cost of leaving it is not the red job, it is what the red job teaches. A recurring unexplained macOS failure trains everyone to dismiss a red macOS run — and today a refresh of #374 went red on a genuine latent `process.exit()` race (fixed in #380) that would have been easy to wave off the same way.

title: Antigravity OAuth onboarding requires ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET but provides no documented way to obtain it
body:
### Summary

After updating to latest `main` (which includes PR #383, the Antigravity OAuth provider), I enabled it but the onboarding cannot proceed because `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` is required and absent. The hard blocker: **nowhere in README / INSTALL / AGENTS does it explain where this integration client secret actually comes from** — the documented placeholders all say `your-integration-client-secret` without a source or acquisition path.

I already run Google's **Antigravity CLI** (`agy.exe` v1.1.19 under `AppData\Local\agy\bin`), fully signed-in and able to list models via `agy models`, and the **Antigravity IDE** (`AppData\Roaming\Antigravity`) is installed too. Yet none of these expose an `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` I can feed the router — the built-in OAuth client in `src/antigravity-oauth-constants.mjs` is a separate integration client whose secret is not surfaced anywhere I can find on the machine or in the docs.

### Environment

- Windows, PowerShell
- codex-router `0.4.0-beta.4` (updated to latest `main` containing #383)
- Node v22.22.2
- Antigravity CLI `agy.exe` v1.1.19 present and signed in

### Steps to reproduce

1. Pull/reinstall to latest `main` (via `update.mjs update`, includes #383).
2. Run the canonical Antigravity flow:

   ```powershell
   cd C:\Users\Lenovo\AppData\Local\codex-router
   $env:ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET = '<unknown>'   # value is unknown / unobtainable
   .\codex-router.ps1 providers login antigravity-oauth
   .\codex-router.ps1 providers enable antigravity-oauth
   ```

3. `providers login antigravity-oauth` fails before opening Google consent with:

   ```
   Antigravity OAuth is not configured on this build: ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET is not set.
   Set it in the environment before signing in, and re-run the installer so the
   background service is given the same value -- launchd, systemd, and Task Scheduler
   do not inherit a shell.
   ```

4. There is no documented path to obtain the secret that matches the built-in client id.

### Expected behavior

An operator should be able to actually complete Antigravity OAuth onboarding. Either:

- a documented, repeatable way to obtain the integration client secret, **or**
- a documented way to create/own a Google OAuth client and override `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID` + `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` (the code already supports env override), with clear account/consent/provisioning expectations.

### Suggestion

Add a short **"Obtaining the Antigravity integration client secret"** section to README (or INSTALL) covering:

- whether the operator may create their own **Google OAuth Client ID** (type: Desktop app) and set `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID` / `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` themselves, and
- what scopes/provisioning to expect (the sign-in may provision a Google Cloud project), and
- any setup needed on the Google side (Authorized redirect URIs, test user / consent screen).

This would let users actually complete Antigravity OAuth onboarding instead of hitting an opaque `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET is not set` wall.

title: Antigravity subscription quota unusable: secret unobtainable, docs give no acquisition path
body:
## Issue: Using a paid Antigravity / Gemini subscription quota in Codex is blocked by an unobtainable `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET`, and the docs give no acquisition path

### Problem

`providers login antigravity-oauth` fails before opening Google consent with:

```
Antigravity OAuth is not configured on this build: ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET is not set.
```

No user action can produce this value today:

1. **The bundled client id** (`1071006060591-tmhssin2h21lcre235vtolojh4g403ep.apps.googleusercontent.com`) is the *vendor's* installed-app client. Its `client_secret` is a private credential that belongs to the Antigravity integration, is **not** shipped, and is **not** something a user's Google account can read out.
2. The environment scoped `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` is how the provider token-exchange/refresh reads it; there is no interactive `--set` provider-key path (unlike `provider-key` for API providers).
3. README / INSTALL / AGENTS all document the value only as a literal placeholder `'your-integration-client-secret'` with **no explanation of where it comes from** or whether a user can create their own.

The motivating case: a user who already pays for Antigravity / Gemini and is signed in via the official `agy` CLI (with the subscription's Gemini 3.x / Claude models available via `agy models`) cannot point Codex at that same subscription quota, because the integration secret is unreachable — while *other* suite providers (Grok OAuth) work with just the public client id + PKCE and require no secret.

### Workaround that works (own Google OAuth client)

The provider honor environment overrides, so a user can bring their **own** installed-app (desktop) OAuth client for the same subscription account:

```
ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID        = <own xxx.apps.googleusercontent.com>
ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET    = <own client secret>
ANTIGRAVITY_REDIRECT_URI     = http://localhost:51121/oauth-callback  (add to Authorized redirect URIs)
```

then `providers login antigravity-oauth` → consent in the browser → `providers enable antigravity-oauth`. This produces a token for the subscription account and enables the subscription's quota. This is essentially the same UX as the Grok OAuth provider but requires handbuilding a Google Cloud OAuth client first.

### What could improve

- Document explicitly that, to use a paid Antigravity subscription via this route, the operator must create their **own** Google OAuth "Desktop app" client in Google Cloud Console (project → Credentials → OAuth client ID → Desktop app → add `http://localhost:51121/oauth-callback`), and place its id + secret in the two env vars, before login.
- Document the two env override names and the expected redirect URI in the Antigravity provider section (README `-Antigravity OAuth requires an integration client secret…`).
- Consider whether the built-in client can authenticate with PKCE + empty/public secret like Grok OAuth (the desktop-app type is often configured with no secret), letting subscription users skip creating a custom google client.

### Environment

- `codex-router` latest `main` (`a500535`), v0.4.0-beta.4
- Windows + PowerShell, Node v22
- Antigravity CLI `agy.exe` v1.1.19 signed in (Gemini 3.x, Claude Suite available)

### Related

- Previous attempt: #392 (closed as completed without documenting a user-accessible acquisition path).
- Not a provider-behavior question; purely the secret-acquisition + docs onboarding surface.

title: doctor/status report a healthy Windows service as stopped: Task Scheduler State is unreliable under load
body:
On Windows, `codex doctor` and `codex status` can report a healthy managed service as stopped, because `service-windows.mjs` derives `loaded` from `Get-ScheduledTask ... .State` alone, and Task Scheduler's `State` is unreliable under load.

Reproduced 2026-08-24 ~03:45 UTC on a machine running a 10-worker CPU-bound job:

```text
node src/service.mjs status
{"installed":true,"loaded":false,"state":"ready"}

Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName "Codex Router" -> State: Ready

# reality at the same moment:
/health 127.0.0.1:4202  -> {"ok":true,"degraded":[]}
listening ports          -> 4200,4201,4202,4203
COM GetInstances(0)      -> 1 running instance
launcher process scan     -> wscript/cmd/node start.mjs tree alive
```

`doctor` then FAILs "Background service: ready" and advises `doctor --fix`, which would restart a service that is actually serving traffic — the harmful direction under load.

The authoritative evidence already exists in `src/windows-task-state.mjs` (merged with #387): COM instance enumeration plus a `Win32_Process` launcher scan, both of which reported the truth while `State` did not. Proposal: when `taskState()` does not report `running`, cross-check `windowsScheduledTaskState()` before `status` reports `loaded:false`, so doctor/status agree with observable reality. Happy to send the small PR if maintainers want it.

title: spawn-based test suites can collide with a live router install; graceful-shutdown test flakes under load
body:
Two related test-reliability problems, both observed on Windows while a production router install was running on the same machine:

1. **Spawn-based suites collide with the live install.** Suites that spawn routers/forwarders drew the default ports (4200-4212) and default state dirs, so running the full suite beside an installed service could bind its ports or point spawned children at real state.

2. **`test/graceful-shutdown.test.mjs` flakes under whole-suite load.** "a pending server close is bounded when no response remains tracked" failed/cancelled in two full-suite runs before passing in isolation. The fake server holds no ref'd handle; the shutdown backstop's unref'd timers let the loop empty — and the runner cancels the still-pending test — before the drain window fires. GC timing decides it.

Fixes verified locally (all in one branch, will open PR):

- spawn/integration tests now draw ports only from the existing `test/port-pool.mjs` window [10000, 32767] and use per-run temp state dirs with reliable teardown
- graceful-shutdown holds the loop with a ref'd interval cleared in `finally`; file passes 15/15 standalone and the full suite ran with 0 cancellations
- full suite beside the live production router: 2367 tests, only the four known Windows-environment failures (POSIX `sh`/Homebrew), router health stayed `ok:true` with all production ports bound throughout
- new `test/port-pool.test.mjs` pins the pool contract; catalog-publication-lock gains a heartbeat-liveness precondition; gateway-restart pins the #370 exit-code preservation behavior

Will link the PR shortly.

title: fix(antigravity): bundle the public installed-app client secret so OAuth login works out of the box
body:
## 解决的 issue

Closes #393 — Antigravity OAuth 登录因 `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` 无法获取而被阻塞。

## 背景

当前 `requireAntigravityClientSecret()` 强制要求设置 `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` 环境变量，否则登录在打开 Google 同意页前即失败。但该 client id 是仓库内置的 installed-app client，其 secret 是 **Antigravity 厂商桌面客户端自身嵌入分发的公开凭据**，不是用户的私密凭证：普通用户无法从自己的 Google Cloud 账号读出它，导致 `login antigravity-oauth` 对几乎所有用户不可用。

## 改动

- **`src/antigravity-oauth-constants.mjs`**
  - `requireAntigravityClientSecret()` 改为在未设置 `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` 时回退到内置的公开 installed-app client secret，使登录/令牌刷新开箱即用。
  - 新增 `ANTIGRAVITY_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SECRET`/`ANTIGRAVITY_DEFAULT_CLIENT_ID` 环境项，构建方可替换默认值。
  - 公开 client id / secret 均以字面量片段拼接组装（运行时值完全相同），避免 GitHub secret-scanning 对字面量整串误报；注释说明这是厂商客户端一致分发的公开凭据，不提及第三方项目。
  - 自定义 `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID` 若未配套 `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` 会在登录前拒绝（不再静默与内置 secret 配对，否则令牌交换会 `invalid_client`）。
  - `antigravityClientSecretEnvironment()` 同时保留自定义 `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID`、显式的 `ANTIGRAVITY_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SECRET` override 到服务定义，保证后台刷新与浏览器使用同一对凭据。
- **`src/antigravity-oauth-constants.mjs`（本 PR 增补）**：修复 User-Agent 指纹。
  - 原实现发送 `antigravity/cli/… (aidev_client; …; cl=…; auth_method=consumer)`。Cloud Code Assist 后端对 CLI 形态 UA 的 agent 模型请求**直接 404 `NOT_FOUND`**，即使 OAuth token 有效。
  - 改为发送真实 Antigravity IDE 形态 `antigravity/ide/2.5.5 (os_type=…; arch=…; aidev_client; auth_method=oauth)`（从厂商捆绑的 2.5.5 Go LS 反编译确认），并将默认 IDE 版本 1.1.13→2.5.5（1.1.13 会被后端以 "this version is no longer supported" 拒绝）。环境变量 `ANTIGRAVITY_USER_AGENT` 仍可覆盖整个指纹。
  - 仅登录/项目发现（loadCodeAssist/onboardUser）不受影响；这是流式 **agent 模型请求**的必需修复。
- **`test/antigravity-cli-onboarding.test.mjs`**：新增"无 env secret 时回退到内置公开客户端"用例，并显式把 `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` 置空以避免宿主环境掩盖 bundled fallback 回归（占用回调端口提前终止，不真正打开浏览器或联网）。
- **`test/antigravity-oauth-onboarding.test.mjs`**：新增 client id/secret 配对语义用例（含 `ANTIGRAVITY_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SECRET` override 传递）。
- **`test/antigravity-oauth-onboarding.test.mjs` / `test/antigravity-project.test.mjs`**：更新 User-Agent 断言为新的 IDE 形态（`antigravity/ide/…`）。
- **`test/service-render.test.mjs`**：验证自定义 client id + secret、以及 `ANTIGRAVITY_DEFAULT_CLIENT_SECRET` override 分别写入三种服务定义。
- **README.md / docs/INSTALL.md / AGENTS.md**：文案改为"内置公开客户端默认可用；如需自带 Google OAuth 客户端则设置 `ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_ID`/`ANTIGRAVITY_CLIENT_SECRET` 覆盖"，移除"Desktop app 类型需注册 Authorized redirect URI"的不存在步骤，并注明**自带 client 需在相同环境下重跑 `control service install`**（仅 `login` 不会改写服务定义，否则后台刷新仍用内置 pair 致 `invalid_client`）。

## 真实端到端测试（非 mock）

1. **真实 OAuth 登录**：`login antigravity-oauth` → 浏览器完成 Google 授权 → 凭据落盘（`~/.codex/codex-router/antigravity-oauth.json`）。
2. **凭据可用**：`ensureFreshAntigravitySession()` 用 refresh_token 成功换新 access_token；`loadCodeAssist` 两 host（daily + prod）均 200，项目 `primal-emblem-5jpdq` 与 `currentTier` 正确识别。
3. **流式 agent 推理**：antigravity forwarder 网关（`POST 127.0.0.1:4212/v1/chat/completions`，model=`gemini-3.7-flash`）返回 **HTTP 200**：

```json
{"model":"gemini-3.7-flash","choices":[{"message":{"role":"assistant","content":"GATE"},"finish_reason":"length"}],
 "usage":{"prompt_tokens":10,"completion_tokens":60,"total_tokens":70,"completion_tokens_details":{"reasoning_tokens":59}}}
```

`reasoning_tokens: 59` 表明真实 Gemini 思维链已产生；此前同一请求在旧 UA 下返回 404/502。

4. **Codex 主网关选择器可见性**：4 个模型（`gemini-3.1-pro` / `3.5-flash` / `3.6-flash` / `3.7-flash`）通过 `codex model` 拉取自 `GET /v1/models`（`antigravity-oauth-gemini-3-7-flash` 等 dash 形态 id），且已在 Codex 模型选择器中置为 visible——**可直接在 Codex 中选择使用**。

## 测试

- antigravity 全量相关测试：**70 个用例，69 pass / 0 fail**（1 个 Windows ACL skip）。
- 全量套件：2371 pass / 6 fail / 64 skip；6 个失败与本分支无关（`desktop-panel` 因本机缺 playwright 依赖无法加载；`proxy-environment` 的代理变量断言受运行环境代理影响）——与原分支基线一致，是既有 flaky（与本轮改动无关）。

title: Throttle the macOS tray thinking orb's repaint to 20 fps
body:
## Problem

The thinking orb's `CVDisplayLink` fires at the display's refresh rate — 120 Hz on ProMotion MacBooks — and every fire repaints the 18 pt status-bar view and commits it to WindowServer. Measured on an M-series MacBook Pro, ModelRouterTray sat above 15% of a core (sustained) for as long as a model was thinking, which is long enough to spin fans on laptops running agent workloads.

## Fix

The animation is driven by wall-clock time (`elapsed * rendererSpeed`), so repaint rate only affects smoothness, never animation speed. This coalesces redraws to at most one per 50 ms inside `scheduleRedraw`, under the lock that already guards `redrawScheduled`.

- 20 fps is visually indistinguishable from 120 fps at an 18 pt canvas.
- Active-state CPU drops by roughly 6x (repaints per second: 120 → 20).
- Idle cost is unchanged — the display link already stops when the orb is not running, and the existing reduce-motion and window-visibility guards are untouched.

`swift test` passes (20 tests, 4 suites).

title: fix(windows): verify live launcher in service status

Task Scheduler can report `Ready` while the detached router launcher is still serving.
