title: fix: key harvested quota headers by cooldown scope
body:
## Why

Follow-up to the second finding in #575, which you asked for as its own change:

> The `cooldownScope` extraction suggests the direction is already "keep the identity, drop the second implementation". If that's right, the `api-forwarder.mjs:1228` one-liner is worth taking on its own so the two stores can't drift back apart — please do send it.

`recordUpstreamLimits` writes to two stores from one provider id, under two different keys:

```js
if (rateLimit) recordRateLimitSnapshot(canonicalProviderId(normalized.provider.id), rateLimit);
...
recordProviderCooldown(normalized.provider.id, { until, reason });   // keys by cooldownScope
```

`opencode-zen` is the one id where those two functions disagree — it is `variantOf: opencode-go`, so `canonicalProviderId` folds it into Go, while `cooldownScope` deliberately keeps it because Zen bills at its own `/zen` endpoint.

Reproduced offline on current `main`, no credentials and no provider request, by calling the two modules the way the forwarder does — the Go plan reports 900 requests left, then a Zen response reports 12:

```
--- today: canonicalProviderId keying ---
rate-limits.json keys: [ 'opencode-go' ]
opencode-go  remaining: 12
opencode-zen remaining: undefined
cooldownScope('opencode-zen') = opencode-zen -> snapshot: MISS
```

Two separately billed plans, one key. Zen's number is sitting under the Go plan's name, and the Go plan's own window is gone — the next Go response overwrites it back, so whichever plan answered last wins and the entry is mislabelled either way. Zen's window cannot be read back either: every cooldown-scope consumer looks it up as `opencode-zen`, an id the file never held — `activeProviderCooldown` and `nextQuotaCooldownExpiry` key by `cooldownScope` (`provider-cooldown.mjs:53,75`).

To be precise about what this does *not* claim: the usage card is not affected today. `headerQuota` uses the raw id (`provider-account-usage.mjs:655`), but `providerAccountUsageSnapshot` filters variants out (`:1025`, `.filter((provider) => !provider.variantOf)`), so `opencode-zen` never reaches that path — one account entry per credential, as intended. Confirmed by executing it: with `providerIds: ["opencode-go", "opencode-zen"]` the returned snapshot has no `opencode-zen` key. The overwrite above is the effect that is live today; the unreadable-Zen half is the cooldown readers.

## What changed

`recordUpstreamLimits` keys the snapshot by `cooldownScope` — the same identity `recordProviderCooldown` two lines below already uses, so the two stores cannot drift apart again. The comment now records why the scope and the canonical id are not interchangeable here.

`opencode-zen` is the only id affected. Every other provider and variant — `commandcode-messages`, `opencode-go-messages`, `opencode-go-responses`, `opencode-free-responses` — has `cooldownScope === canonicalProviderId` and keeps the exact key it has today:

```
id                       variantOf      canonical      cooldownScope
commandcode-messages     commandcode    commandcode    commandcode
opencode-go-messages     opencode-go    opencode-go    opencode-go
opencode-go-responses    opencode-go    opencode-go    opencode-go
opencode-zen             opencode-go    opencode-go    opencode-zen   <-- DIVERGES
opencode-free-responses  opencode-free  opencode-free  opencode-free
```

A `rate-limits.json` already carrying a Zen-written entry under `opencode-go` needs no migration: it is last-write-wins telemetry with an `observedAt`, replaced by the next Go response that carries headers.

## Verification

- New `test/rate-limit-scope.test.mjs` spawns the real `src/api-forwarder.mjs` against a mock Zen upstream (a curated `opencode-zen` user model via `MODEL_ROUTER_USER_MODELS`, `OPENCODE_ZEN_BASE_URL` pointed at the mock), with `rate-limits.json` pre-seeded with the Go plan's window. It asserts Zen's headers land under `opencode-zen` and that the Go entry is untouched. It fails on unpatched `main` (`expected: 7`, the Zen figure never filed) and passes with the change.
- `node --test test/rate-limit-quota.test.mjs test/provider-cooldown.test.mjs test/provider-account-usage.test.mjs test/rate-limit-headers.test.mjs test/model-failover.test.mjs` — 102/102 pass.
- `node --test test/commandcode-forwarder.test.mjs` — 5/5 pass; its existing `limits.commandcode.requests.remaining` assertion pins the unchanged canonical-parent behaviour for a variant that shares its plan.
- `npm run check` passes.

Not touched: the first finding in #575 (the unreachable `subagent-availability-sync` / `provider-cooldown` circuit-breaker half). Wiring it or deleting it is your call, and this change is independent of it either way.

title: fix: keep the whitespace an untagged answer starts with
body:
## Why

`src/reasoning-tag-stripper.mjs` has two forms of the same operation, and they disagree.

`stripThinkTags` trims the message's leading whitespace only when it actually removed a tag, and returns an untagged message by identity — the existing test says so explicitly (`stripThinkTags("Paris")`, *"no tags -> unchanged (identity)"*). It is the form used for `response.output_text.done` and for the stored message item in `output_item.done`.

`ThinkStreamStripper`, the delta-channel form, trimmed unconditionally:

```js
#leadTrim(out) {
  if (this.#emittedVisible) return out;
  const trimmed = out.replace(/^\s+/, "");   // even when nothing was stripped
  ...
```

So an ordinary answer opening with a newline — a fenced code block, a leading blank line — reached the client without it, while the terminal snapshot beside it kept it. The rendered answer and the stored one disagreed on a route that had leaked no reasoning at all. When the first delta was *only* whitespace, `#rewrite` saw `cleaned.length === 0` and dropped the event outright.

The class documents the invariant this breaks:

> The concatenation of every `feed`/`flush` return equals `stripThinkTags` of the concatenated input.

I checked it by property test rather than by reading — 300,000 random inputs over a tag-adjacent alphabet (`<`, `>`, `/`, `think`, `reason`, whitespace, letters), each split randomly across deltas, comparing the streamed concatenation against `stripThinkTags` of the same text:

```
=== BEFORE (unpatched main) ===
cases                            : 300000
divergences                      : 91975
UNTAGGED divergences             : 19575     <-- ordinary answers, no tag anywhere
unexplained by {unterminated open tag, tag after visible text}: 19575
    {"text":"\n","streamed":"","whole":"\n"}
    {"text":" a","streamed":"a","whole":" a"}
    {"text":"\tx","streamed":"x","whole":"\tx"}
```

One case in fifteen was an ordinary, reasoning-free answer being altered.

## What changed

Hold the leading whitespace instead of trimming it. By the first visible character the stripper knows whether a tag was removed, so it can emit or drop that whitespace exactly as `stripThinkTags` would. `#removedTag` records the removal; `#pendingLead` holds the whitespace.

The observed leak shapes are unaffected — the reasoning block is what comes first, so the removal is always known in time:

```
"<think>The capital of France is Paris.</think>\nParis"  ->  "Paris"
"\n</think>\n\nThe real answer starts here"              ->  "The real answer starts here"
```

After the change, no untagged message diverges, and nothing diverges that is not one of the two cases a streaming stripper cannot fix:

```
=== AFTER (patched) ===
cases                            : 300000
divergences                      : 81963
UNTAGGED divergences             : 0
unexplained by {unterminated open tag, tag after visible text}: 0
```

Both residual cases are pre-existing and deliberate, and I left them alone:

- **an unterminated `<think>`** — `flush` discards a span that never closed, which its comment states as intended;
- **a tag that appears only after visible text** — `stripThinkTags` trims the message's start retroactively, and a stream that already sent that text cannot retract it. The class comment now records this as the one exception to the stated invariant, rather than leaving the invariant overstated.

## Verification

- `test/reasoning-tag-stripper.test.mjs` — two new tests, both failing on unpatched `main` and passing with the change:
  - a streamed answer opening with `\n` keeps it across chunk sizes 0/1/7, and the delta concatenation equals the `output_text.done` snapshot;
  - a property test over every 3-piece combination of a tag-adjacent alphabet, in four splits each: an untagged message with visible text streams byte-for-byte.
- A third new test pins the whitespace-only-delta case as **unchanged**, so the hold cannot silently grow into it.
- A fourth pins where the two mechanisms meet — leading whitespace still held when a `<think>` starts arriving one character at a time across deltas (`"\n"`, `"<th"`, `"ink>hidden</think>"`, `"\nAnswer"` -> `"Answer"`). It passes before this change as well, so it characterises the new `#pendingLead` path rather than proving it.
- All 10 pre-existing tests in the file still pass (13/13 total).
- `npm run check` passes.

## One thing I did not fix

`ThinkStreamStripper.flush()` computes a remainder its comment says "is emitted" — *"normal-mode remainder -- including a lone `<` that never became a tag -- is emitted"* — but the only caller, the `output_text.done` branch of `#rewrite`, calls it for its side effect and discards the return value. So a message ending mid-tag loses that tail from the delta channel. Identical before and after this change:

```
in="a <"            deltas="a "            stripThinkTags="a <"
in="x<th"           deltas="x"             stripThinkTags="x<th"
in="5 < 6 and 7 <"  deltas="5 < 6 and 7 "  stripThinkTags="5 < 6 and 7 <"
```

The `output_text.done` snapshot carries the full text, so nothing is lost to a client that reads it. Emitting the remainder would mean synthesizing a final delta event, which is a wire change I did not want to make unasked — happy to send it separately if you want it. The property test excludes those inputs explicitly rather than silently.

title: fix: locate the checkout through symlinks in every bin/ command
body:
## What

Every command in `bin/` located the checkout with

    repo_dir=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)

`dirname $0` is only right when the script runs at its real path, and the logical `cd` is only right when no directory on the way is a symlink. `bin/codex-router` already walked the symlink chain, and its comment recorded that the siblings did not; this inlines the same walk into all 38 of them and resolves the root physically (`cd -P … && pwd -P`, the idiom `bin/model-router-tray:683` already uses).

Two distinct failures follow from the old form.

**A command linked onto PATH cannot find the checkout.** `ln -s ~/src/codex-router/bin/doctor ~/.local/bin/doctor` gives

    Error: Cannot find module '/Users/me/.local/src/doctor.mjs'

Relative links that climb out of a linked directory (GNU Stow's folded `~/bin`) are worse: the walk yields a path the kernel accepts, the logical `cd` strips `..` textually, and the command aborts under `set -e` on dash and macOS `/bin/sh`. Only bash invoked as `bash` retries physically and hides it.

**A root containing a linked directory makes commands silently do nothing.** 52 modules in `src/` guard main with `path.resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`. Node realpaths a main module but leaves `argv[1]` as written, so `node "$repo_dir/src/x.mjs"` with a logical `$repo_dir` fails that comparison: the module imports and the process exits 0, having done nothing.

## This also fixes Homebrew installs

The packaged install is the second case, and I did not expect this going in. The formula's wrapper execs `<prefix>/opt/<formula>/libexec/bin/codex-router`. That file is not a link — so the walk is a no-op there — but `opt/<formula>` is a link into the versioned keg, so `repo_dir` stayed on the `opt` path. Every command behind a guarded module (`agents`, `skills`, `caller-key`, `providers`, `update`, `refresh-catalog`, `support-bundle`, …) exited 0 without running. The commands that appeared to work — `--version`, `help`, `setup`, `doctor`, `control`, `panel`, `provider-key` — are the ones that never cross a guard, and the formula's `test do` block only runs those, so CI never saw it.

Reproduced in a keg-shaped fixture built from this repo's own files: on `99d526d`, `codex-router skills` exits 0 with no output; with this patch it prints usage and exits 2. `test/bin-symlink-resolution.test.mjs` now builds that layout by name so it stays covered.

I can only simulate the keg layout here rather than install the formula, so please sanity-check this against a real `brew install` before trusting the claim.

## Behaviour changes worth flagging

- `bin/install`'s five closing API-key hints printed `$repo_dir`, which is now the versioned keg path for a packaged reader — stale after the next `brew upgrade`. They now print `${CODEX_ROUTER_SOURCE_ROOT:-$repo_dir}`, so a packaged install names the stable `opt` path and a checkout is unchanged.
- `bin/model-router-tray` runs `$repo_dir/scripts/build-macos-tray-app.sh`, which seals its root into the tray bundle (`Contents/Resources/router-root` and Info.plist `ModelRouterSourceRoot`). For a checkout reached through a linked directory that sealed root is now physical rather than logical. Homebrew is not affected — the tray exits early when `CODEX_ROUTER_PACKAGE_MANAGER=homebrew`. Tell me if you would rather it kept the logical path.
- Otherwise `$repo_dir` is transient: it names the module to run, is `cd`'d into, and locates sibling commands. Node's own `SOURCE_ROOT` still comes from `CODEX_ROUTER_SOURCE_ROOT` when the wrapper exports it, so nothing persisted into launchd/systemd units changes.

## Why inline it 38 times

A sourced helper cannot be found before the path is resolved — `. helper` searches PATH, which is exactly what holds only the link. `readlink -f`/`realpath` need macOS ≥ 12.3; the dispatcher's existing walk depends on neither, and the one `readlink -f` in `bin/` (`model-router-tray:805`) sits in a Linux-only `/proc` branch behind a fallback. A node one-liner would put node on the critical path of `bin/install`, the script that decides where node comes from. So the siblings follow the dispatcher, and the static test pins the load-bearing lines in every copy so they cannot drift.

## Tests

`test/bin-symlink-resolution.test.mjs`:
- static: every `#!/bin/sh` command in `bin/` starts from `$0`, walks the chain, carries both `case` branches, derives a physical `repo_dir`, and never derives a path from bare `$0`
- `bin/skills`, `bin/agents --help`, `bin/doctor --help` through an absolute link, a relative link, a link to a link, a linked `bin/` directory, a linked checkout, and a keg-shaped wrapper — each must behave byte-for-byte as at the real path, under an isolated `HOME`/`CODEX_HOME`/`MODEL_ROUTER_STATE_DIR`. `skills` and `agents` reach guarded modules and so cover the silent-exit-0 shape; `doctor` prints usage unguarded and covers only the missing-module shape
- a control taking the resolver verbatim from `bin/skills`, showing the bare `dirname $0` form landing one level above the link's directory, and resolving the Stow layout

`sh -n` and `dash -n` pass on every script. Full suite locally on macOS: 3977 tests, 3947 pass, 28 skipped, 2 failures (`desktop-panel` needs playwright, a `search-sidecar` cancellation timing test) that reproduce unpatched on `99d526d`.

title: Windows: terminal window briefly appears periodically while Codex Router is running
body:
### Summary

After installing Codex Router on Windows, a terminal window briefly appears and disappears every few minutes.

The process responsible for the visible window has not yet been identified, so the connection to Codex Router is suspected rather than confirmed.

### Environment

- Windows 11
- Codex Router 0.5.1
- Installed revision: 99d526dcdc13dc4df3d817ad369b111626f602fc
- Electron Control Center with tray integration
- Per-user scheduled tasks for the router service and tray

### Observed behavior

With Codex Router running in the background, a terminal window periodically becomes visible and quickly disappears.

The interval is approximately a few minutes; it has not been measured precisely.

### Expected behavior

Background health checks and service-status queries should run without displaying a terminal window.

### Investigation so far

The registered `Codex Router` scheduled task has a one-minute repetition interval. Its action invokes `wscript.exe`, and the VBS launcher runs the command with window style `0` (hidden). Therefore, the scheduled task's launcher is already configured to hide its window.

However, in `src/service-windows.mjs`, the `schtasks()` helper calls:

```js
return execFileSync("schtasks.exe", args, {
  encoding: "utf8",
  stdio: options.quiet
    ? ["ignore", "ignore", "ignore"]
    : ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"],
});
```

This call does not specify `windowsHide: true`.

This is a possible source of the flashing window, but it has not been confirmed through process tracing or a before/after test.

### Questions

- Could background service-status queries through this helper cause a visible console window on Windows?
- Is this a known issue, or has it already been addressed?
- Would adding `windowsHide: true` to this helper be appropriate, and are there other background child-process calls that should be checked?

### Validation status

No local patch has been applied, and no fix is claimed. The exact process responsible for the visible window still needs to be identified.

title: chore: merge CHANGELOG.md bullets instead of conflicting on them
body:
## Why

Every change appends a bullet to the top of `CHANGELOG.md`'s `## Unreleased` section, so two branches that share no source file still collide there.

That is not a minor annoyance — it is currently the single largest source of conflicts in the open queue. Of the ten conflicting open pull requests, **seven conflict on `CHANGELOG.md` and nothing else**:

| PR | conflicting files before | after |
|---|---|---|
| #708 | CHANGELOG.md | none |
| #710 | CHANGELOG.md | none |
| #714 | CHANGELOG.md | none |
| #715 | CHANGELOG.md | none |
| #716 | CHANGELOG.md | none |
| #728 | CHANGELOG.md | none |
| #729 | CHANGELOG.md | none |

## What

Four lines plus a comment in `.gitattributes`:

```
CHANGELOG.md merge=union
```

`union` is git's built-in driver for exactly this shape — an append-only list whose entries are independent of each other. It keeps both sides' bullets rather than asking a human to re-type one.

## Verification

Each of the seven was re-merged against `main` with the attribute in place (`git merge-tree --write-tree`), and all seven go to zero conflicts. The three remaining conflicts are genuine source conflicts, untouched by this change:

- #720 — `test/tool-schema-root.test.mjs`
- #725 — `src/router.mjs`
- #605 — `src/chat-tool-surface.mjs`, `src/namespace-relay.mjs`, `src/router.mjs`, `test/provider-catalogs.test.mjs`

I also checked the merged output rather than just the conflict count: no conflict markers, and no bullet lost from either side.

## The tradeoff, stated plainly

When both sides edit the *same* bullet, `union` keeps both copies. In one of the test merges that produced a single duplicated bullet (210 where 209 were expected). That is a one-line delete with both wordings visible, rather than a conflict someone has to reconstruct from two halves — and it only ever applies to this one file.

If a cleaner shape is wanted later, the alternative is `changelog.d/` fragments assembled at release, which never conflict and never duplicate, at the cost of a release-time assembly step.

title: fix(commandcode): normalize nullable Gemini tool schemas
body:
Command Code's Gemini 3.8 Flash can reject a Codex turn before any tool runs when the supplied tools contain a nullable array. The reported rejection identifies the image-generation tool's `referenced_image_paths` parameter:

> schema specified other fields alongside any_of. When using any_of, it must be the only field set.

Normalize a single concrete type plus `null` into an explicit union on this provider/model route. The non-null branch keeps its constraints, so an array still declares its item type. For example:

```json
{"type":["array","null"],"items":{"type":"string"}}
```

becomes:

```json
{"anyOf":[{"type":"array","items":{"type":"string"}},{"type":"null"}]}
```

The compatibility pass runs after namespace flattening and tool-search history expansion, covering both initially supplied and later discovered definitions. It preserves tool identities, parameter requirements, and unrelated routes. The nullable rewrite skips nodes carrying composition, reference, or enum/const constraints, and nodes declaring several non-null types. Literal values in defaults and examples are not traversed as schemas.

The patch adds no dependency or model configuration change. It contains only this compatibility fix, its regression tests, and a changelog entry.

## Validation

- `npm run check` passed.
- `node --test --test-concurrency=2 --test-timeout=180000 test/gemini-tool-schema.test.mjs test/routing.test.mjs test/tool-schema-root.test.mjs test/namespace-relay.test.mjs test/namespace-relay-routing.test.mjs test/grok-reasoning-summary-compat.test.mjs test/reasoning-tag-stripper.test.mjs` passed: 400 tests, no failures or skips. Run with an isolated `CODEX_HOME` and no outer Router-state overrides, so the fixtures own their state directories.
- Removing only the new compatibility invocation makes the routing regression fail on the unrepaired schema. Restoring it makes the test pass.
- `git diff --check` passed.

The reported provider error and earlier local deployment motivated this fix. No new live provider request was made while preparing this PR. The converter test models the observed conversion; it is not a live Google or Command Code acceptance test. The full repository suite and other operating systems are left to CI.

title: fix: locate root config assignments with the TOML lexer
body:
## Why

Root config helpers treated assignment-shaped lines inside multiline strings as settings, silently rewriting user prose and journalling the wrong previous model.

## Changes

- Locate root settings with the TOML structural lexer. Root reads, writes and splitting stop at the first real table, so an invalid escape in a later table cannot change the selected assignment.
- Retain strict whole-document validation for login-free in-place changes.
- Decode ordinary string values with the lexer, including trailing comments; refuse multiline model settings before writing.
- Preserve assignment-shaped prose during native-catalog preparation, adoption, cleanup and restore.
- Use structural assignments and table boundaries for managed concurrency insertion, and recognize managed markers only as standalone comments when the document can be scanned.
- Include current main through 0964eef.

## Compatibility limit

Malformed root sections retain legacy best-effort matching for Windows prototype migration/disable. Prose preservation is guaranteed for structurally readable root sections; login-free in-place edits continue to refuse malformed documents. Optional agent settings are not inserted into unreadable documents.

## Verification

`node --test test/config-manager.test.mjs test/legacy-migration.test.mjs test/native-catalog-source.test.mjs test/native-catalog-drift.test.mjs test/target-integration.test.mjs test/login-free-app-server.test.mjs test/caller-key-client-refresh.test.mjs`

91 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed (Linux, Node 24.19.0). New coverage exercises quoted/commented model restoration, invalid trailing tables, prose containing managed markers and concurrency examples, catalog adoption/restore, strict login-free refusal, and multiline-model refusal without modifying the file.

`npm run check`, final `node --check src/config-manager.mjs`, and `git diff --check` passed. Windows CI is still required; local results do not establish Windows execution.

title: fix: keep the type a broken $ref cycle was declaring on Moonshot routes
body:
Related to #726; this does not claim to close that issue.

## Scope

Only locally curated Moonshot models with `toolSchemaRecursion: "flatten"` reach the type-preserving path. No shipped Kimi model enables flattening. The route that produced #726 has not been established. Stock Kimi and other providers retain their existing behavior.

## Changes

- Preserve explicitly declared target types when flattening a recursive reference on opted-in Moonshot routes; follow aliases with cycle detection.
- Prefer the referencing node's type-implying siblings. Ambiguous enum/union siblings prevent fallback to a contradictory target type. Explicit types remain untouched.
- Accept null options with the same behavior as omitted options.
- Share the unchanged Moonshot route predicate between router and forwarder.
- Merge current main to clear the conflict.

## Deliberate limitation

An untyped recursive union such as `N = anyOf(string, ref N)` still leaves an open branch after flattening. Neither a concrete target type nor the provider's intended recursive semantics is established, so this patch does not guess a type. A regression test records that limitation. Reference-only rings likewise remain open.

## Verification

405/405 tests passed across tool-schema-root, generic-routing, routing, namespace-relay, registry, commandcode-forwarder, deepseek-responses-routing, and grok-tool-facade. `npm run check` and `git diff --check` passed.

The forwarder regression starts the real process against a local mock endpoint using a user-curated kimi-api model with flattening enabled. It verifies the typed edge, a non-Moonshot flattening control retaining `{}`, and a model without flattening retaining its reference. Additional regressions cover conflicting enum/const/items/prefixItems/properties siblings, ambiguous siblings, input immutability, and null options.

No live provider requests were made.

title: [Bug]: commandcode/qwen3.8-flash intermittently persists a complete final answer twice inside one assistant message
body:
## Environment

- Codex Desktop 26.908.40834 on Windows
- codex-router at pristine commit `99d526dcdc13dc4df3d817ad369b111626f602fc`
- Model: `commandcode/qwen3.8-flash`
- Command Code GOAT account

## Confirmed symptom: persisted whole-answer duplication

`commandcode/qwen3.8-flash` intermittently produced a complete final answer twice.

This was not merely a UI double-render:

- The duplicated answer was visible in the Codex UI.
- The canonical rollout JSONL stored one assistant message item whose text contained two complete copies of the answer.
- The stored message was 1,850 characters long.
- The two copies began at character offsets 0 and 927.
- After normalizing the extra blank lines between them, the two blocks were identical 923-character copies.
- A unique marker inside the answer also occurred twice in that single assistant message.

The affected response followed a tool-heavy turn. Other tool-call turns did not consistently reproduce it, so the issue is intermittent rather than every-turn deterministic.

Expected behavior: one final assistant answer should be emitted, stored, and rendered once.

## Separate observation: possible history/context echo

During the same task, the model repeatedly and spontaneously reported that earlier pure-text assistant turns appeared twice in its current input context even though those turns were stored only once in the canonical rollout.

It initially reported:

- pure-text assistant turns appeared twice;
- tool-call turns appeared once;
- user turns appeared once.

Later it reported that user turns also appeared twice.

This is a repeated model-side observation, but it is **not transport-confirmed evidence**. No provider-bound request body was captured, and the model cannot authoritatively inspect the serialized request structure. I therefore cannot establish whether this was actual history duplication, another request-assembly representation, or model misinterpretation.

A sanitized comparison of the provider-bound turn-2 message structure with the canonical rollout would be needed to confirm or reject this part.

## Secondary output-quality observation

The same task also contained occasional mixed-language fragments inside Korean answers, for example:

- `两层`
- `조사じゃなかった`

I am including this only as a secondary observation. It may be model-generation garbling and is not sufficient to attribute to the router.

## Impact

The confirmed persisted duplication:

- doubles output and stored-history tokens for the affected answer;
- pollutes subsequent assistant history;
- may make later generations imitate the duplicated format.

The possible context echo, if confirmed separately, would add further input-token and context-coherence impact.

## Related observation

Issue #654 reports a more severe duplication-amplification pattern with Hy4, together with reasoning/tag leakage. I am not claiming the same root cause: this Qwen report is intentionally limited to the confirmed single-message whole-answer duplication and the separately labeled, unconfirmed context observation.

## Diagnostic request

Could you compare, for an affected turn:

1. the raw provider response before router transformation;
2. the router’s normalized Responses output;
3. the final assistant message committed to the Codex rollout?

That should distinguish provider-generated repetition, router transformation duplication, and Codex-side finalization.

title: Explicit cross-model create_thread delegation with user-approved routed models
body:
## Summary

Allow a routed parent session to create a new Codex task on another explicitly-chosen **routed** model (e.g. `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash`), removing the one manual model-picker click in an otherwise fully working cross-model workflow. This keeps the billing/provider safety boundary intact by requiring explicit user authorization instead of silent routing.

## Workflow proven today (manual version works end to end)

1. Parent task running on `opencode-go-responses/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` creates a worker task (`create_thread`, projectless) and monitors it (`wait_threads` / `read_thread`).
2. New tasks land on the default model, so the user flips the worker's picker to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash by hand.
3. Parent sends the assignment via `send_message_to_thread`, waits, reads the result.
4. Worker writes code, parent executes and verifies it (tests passed).

Everything except step 2 is already orchestratable. Step 2 is the only manual click.

## The gap

- In a routed session, `create_thread` exposes no `model` parameter at all (only `prompt` / `target` / `thinking` / `title`), so the model cannot be set at creation.
- `send_message_to_thread` accepts a `model` override, but only OpenAI models — no routed models.
- Related upstream Codex issues: openai/codex#37120 (`create_thread` validation not synchronized with app-server model/list) and openai/codex#14039 (per-subagent model/provider/profile selection).

The Router skill deliberately pins in-session subagents to the parent model and treats an explicit model as a user-visible task choice. Agreed — this request is the middle ground, not a removal of that boundary.

## Proposal

Support explicit cross-model delegation where the user has approved the model in advance, e.g. a standing permission like "Muse may delegate ordinary coding to DeepSeek/GLM", enforced as:

- `model` must already be enabled in the user's Router catalog (Router knows every enabled model, provider, and billing route).
- The model/provider must be explicitly authorized by the user (an allow-list), never silently chosen.
- The spawned task visibly shows which model was selected.
- No silent fallback to another model — if Codex refuses the model, fail clearly rather than using the default.
- The billing/provider boundary crossing is recorded.

Possible shape (illustrative):

```
create_thread(model = "opencode-go/deepseek-v4-1-flash", prompt = "...")
```

Since Router already relays `codex_app__create_thread` to Codex, brokering an explicit, authorized `model` through that relay looks like the natural implementation point.

title: fix: gate leaked tool-call recovery to Hy4, and make its capture linear
body:
Reopens #722, which GitHub auto-closed when #715 merged and deleted its base branch. Same branch, same commits, retargeted at `main`.

**This is the gate for code that is already on `main`.** #715 landed the recovery transform; this PR is what scopes it. Until this merges, `src/router.mjs:4420` reads:

```js
const leakedToolCalls = route ? leakedToolCallRecoveryTransform(contentType) : undefined;
```

— installed for **every routed provider**, with no `usesLeakedToolCallRecovery` on `main` at all.

## Why that matters

The transform scans a model's visible answer and reasoning text for Hy4's `<tool_calls:NONCE>...</tool_calls:NONCE>` markup and converts it into real `function_call` items. The nonce is **not a secret**: nothing in `src/` generates or stores one. `OPEN_RE` captures it from the model's own opening tag and the closing tag is built from that capture, so open/close agreement is free to anything that emits both.

So on `main` today, any routed model — Claude via `commandcode-messages`, GPT, DeepSeek, GLM — that *quotes* that markup has it converted into a call Codex executes. Quoting this repository's own `AGENTS.md`, a diff, or a web page is enough. Measured on the pre-gate code, a single visible-channel sentence describing the syntax produced three injected `function_call` items, one carrying a destructive recursive-delete argument.

This PR restores `usesLeakedToolCallRecovery(route)`, matching `/(?:^|\/)hy4-preview$/`. Enumerated across all 141 `upstreamModel` values in `config/**/*.json`: only `hy4-preview` and `tencent/hy4-preview` match, covering all six shipped Hy4 routes and nothing else.

## Also on this branch, also missing from `main`

**Linear capture.** #715's version held the open span as one growing string and re-scanned it per delta, synchronously on the router's event loop. Measured through the real transform:

| span | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| 1 MB | 1508 ms | 28 ms |
| 4 MB | 18312 ms | 94 ms |

**The trailing-gap trim.** `parseLeakedToolCalls` ended with a backtracking `\s+$` replace, which retries from every start offset of a whitespace run not at end of string. `MAX_CAPTURE_BYTES` does not bound it — that cap is on the streaming capture, while the `.done` snapshot and stored-item paths pass whole-provider text. 200 KB of padding blocked the event loop for 15 s; 400 KB for ~55 s. Replaced with `trimEnd`, verified identical across all 65536 BMP code points.

**One recovery per item.** Summary and content channels shared one span stream, so a single item's calls were recovered — and executed — twice.

## Known limitation, stated plainly

The gate narrows the injection channel; it does not close it. On an Hy4 route the only check on a recovered call is `NAME_RE`, a format check. The request's declared `tools` array is in scope in `handleResponses` and is never passed to the transform. Threading it through and dropping any recovered call whose name was not declared is the real mitigation, and should follow.

title: fix: keep an explicit subagent model instead of pinning it to the routed parent
body:
## Problem

`codex-router` writes `expose_spawn_agent_model_overrides = true` into the
managed `multi_agent_v2` block, so Codex offers a model override on
`spawn_agent`. The router then discarded that override:
`injectSessionModelForSpawnCalls` rewrote `spawn_agent.model` to the routed
parent on every call.

The effect is that a routed parent can only spawn copies of itself.
Cross-provider delegation, such as a DeepSeek parent delegating to a native
OpenAI model, is impossible even though the picker exists and
`subagent-report.mjs` lists those models as spawnable.

Reproduced on a live routed session:

- a child requested on `gpt-6-astra` reported `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`
- a child requested with a bogus model id also ran as the parent, with no
  client-side validation error

## Change

Keep an explicit subagent model; only a call that omits the model inherits the
parent. This mirrors what the router already does for `create_thread`.

There is no enum to police here. Codex ships `model` on the tool schema as a
plain string:

```json
{"type":"string","description":"Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed."}
```

so `sanitizeSpawnAgentModel` never fires against a current client. Codex
validates the value itself and rejects anything outside its list:

```
Unknown model `totally-bogus-model-xyz` for spawn_agent. Available models:
gpt-6-astra, gpt-5.6-sol, gpt-5.6-terra, gpt-5.6-luna, gpt-5.5
```

An invented name therefore still cannot cross a billing boundary. The sanitizer
keeps its guard for a client version that does ship an enum: the item it clears
arrives without a model and inherits the parent as before.

## Testing

- `test/subagent-model-inherit.test.mjs` covers a kept explicit model, the
  absent/empty/non-string cases that still inherit the parent, and the
  wire-level preserve-or-inherit split driven through the real
  `flattenNamespaceTools` -> `buildNamespaceLookups` ->
  `rewriteNamespaceResponsePayload` path.
- `test/namespace-relay.test.mjs`: the existing pin test now asserts that an
  advertised override survives and that only an unadvertised one is pinned.
- `node --test` over the namespace-relay, namespace-relay-routing,
  subagent-completion, subagent-model-inherit and catalog suites: 259 pass, 0
  fail.
- `node scripts-check.mjs` passes.
- Live from a routed parent after the change, the router served child turns on
  `gpt-6-astra` and on `gpt-5.6-luna` per its own request log. Before the change
  the same calls were served on the parent.

title: Set default-tier model aliases in Claude Code launcher
body:
## Problem

Claude Code sessions routed through the router keep dying inside spawned subagents with:

```
Agent terminated early due to an API error: There's an issue with the selected model
(claude-opus-5[1m]). ... (error type model_not_found, HTTP 404, model sent to the
API: claude-opus-5)
```

The existing `CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL` pin does **not** cover this case. Two distinct agent paths ignore it:

- **Built-in agents** (Explore, Plan, ...) — they resolve `opus`-tier requests through the default-tier alias (`ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL`), not the subagent override.
- **User-defined agents** whose frontmatter pins `model: opus` — same alias path.

With neither the alias nor the subagent var matching, Claude Code falls back to the literal Anthropic id `claude-opus-5`. The router serves neither, so the request goes upstream verbatim and 404s — killing every spawned agent of that type while the main loop keeps working (its model is pinned correctly). Verified by spawning an Explore agent and a general-purpose agent in the same session: general-purpose succeeded, Explore 404'd.

## Fix

Set the three default-tier aliases to `catalog.defaultModel` alongside the existing pins, so every opus/sonnet/haiku-tier resolution inside a routed session lands on a served model.

Verified locally by importing `claudeRouterEnvironment()` with the real caller secret — all six model vars now emit the routed default.

title: fix: background Windows job owners are kept windowless
body:
Background Windows commands requested with `stdio: "inherit"` could allocate a console for their PowerShell Job owner. Hiding was previously disabled for every inherited stream; even after the TTY correction, libuv's `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` was still omitted whenever a standard descriptor was inherited. The original child-only probe therefore missed the owner-console gap reported in review.

For hidden Windows calls without a TTY, three fresh pipes are now used and stdin, stdout, and stderr are forwarded. Output is forwarded as raw bytes through asynchronous descriptor writes: synchronous Windows `process.stdout.write()` was demonstrated to block deadlines when downstream was left unread. Partial writes are completed, output is drained before successful settlement, and early stdin closure is handled.

Direct inheritance is retained for actual TTYs, explicit `windowsHide: false`, and POSIX. The existing Job Object, barrier, and process-tree cleanup mechanisms are preserved. The static PowerShell guard's comment has been narrowed to its actual coverage.

Validation:

- On Windows 11 with Windows Terminal Preview configured as the default terminal, zero console-window handles were verified for both the contained command and its actual PowerShell owner. The exact new owner regression was failed against the previous PR commit `4cc5a08`, as expected. A visible Terminal flash was not independently established by that probe.
- Native stream regressions were passed on Node 22.23.1 and Node 24.19.0: 3 MiB binary output per stream with delayed readers and immediate caller exit; 2 MiB input checksum; early input closure; and deadline rejection with target retirement before unread output was drained. Restoring synchronous writes caused the deadline regression to fail.
- Partial writes, zero-progress writes, cancellation after child close, and late write errors were covered by additional deterministic tests. Success, failure, abort, deadline, and abrupt-owner-exit cleanup were rechecked.
- The 16-file Node 24 Windows/desktop/process/service/install/control suite was passed: **224 passed, 19 platform skips, 0 failures**. Repository syntax checks were passed. Two independent agents were used for implementation critique and native runtime verification; no actionable findings remained.

An already pending OS write cannot be cancelled without closing the caller's global descriptor. Timeout rejection and child retirement are bounded; natural parent exit can still await that write until downstream is drained or closed. TTY detection remains based on `isTTY`; Git Bash/MSYS2-specific console prompts were not validated.

The direct synchronous repair launches in `doctor.mjs` and `control.mjs::runDoctor`, plus scheduler/service-launch changes, remain outside this shared-runner patch. The proposed coordination is #744 first, followed by #674 rebased onto it. [Fresh CI for `2d589d7`](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/34811966553) has passed on Windows, macOS, and Linux, including both Electron jobs and the native macOS build. Deterministic provider-discovery checks have also passed; the live catalog audit and Homebrew install jobs were skipped.

Related: #565, #571, #674.

title: chore: remove the unreachable provider circuit-breaker subsystem
body:
Resolves the first finding of #575. The second finding was fixed separately in #728.

## What was dead

`src/subagent-availability-sync.mjs` had zero references anywhere in the repository — `startSubagentAvailabilitySync()` was never called — and six of `provider-cooldown.mjs`'s seven exports (`quotaResetAt`, `activeProviderCooldown`, `temporarilyUnavailableSubagentSlugs`, `nextQuotaCooldownExpiry`, `recordProviderCooldown`, `cooldownErrorPayload`) had no production callers. Every live `recordProviderCooldown` call resolves to the same-named function at `model-failover.mjs:255`.

As @c8dhjp4tyv-bit noted when filing, both files entered in `350971d` and were never wired, while `model-failover.mjs` (`9731681`, five days earlier) already owned the job.

## Why removing rather than wiring

`model-failover.mjs` is the same idea, done better, and already live:

| | `model-failover.mjs` (live) | `provider-cooldown.mjs` (removed) |
|---|---|---|
| Max window | 6h | 24h |
| Recovery | `clearProviderCooldown` on first success | none — the window just runs out |
| Corrupt store | tolerated as "nothing cooled" | — |
| Entry cap | 64 | unbounded |
| Routing effect | already filters cooled providers in `rankFailoverCandidates` | — |

Wiring the dead copy would have left two cooldown stores disagreeing about the same subscription, the second with a laxer bound and no way to recover early from a quota that refilled ahead of schedule.

The one capability it had that nothing else does — withdrawing subagent slugs from the catalog while a quota window is open — is not worth its price. It spawned `catalog.mjs` as a child process off the request path on every quota failure, contending for the catalog publication lock, to correct a picker listing for a model that failover already routes around transparently.

## What stays

`cooldownScope` — extracted after this subsystem was written, and now the shared identity for `provider-cooldowns.json` and `rate-limits.json` following #728. It keeps `provider-cooldown.mjs` as its home and keeps its own test.

Worth noting the docs mattered here as much as the code: `test/provider-cooldown.test.mjs` passed and read like a live contract ("opens a durable provider circuit", "temporarily remove subagent models"), and both `OPENCODEX_IMPLEMENTATION_ROADMAP.md` and `OPENCODEX_FEATURE_GAP_SPEC.md` cited the module as shipped provider-resilience support. That combination is what made an inert subsystem look like a working quota circuit. The roadmap claim itself stays true — cooldowns *are* implemented, by `model-failover.mjs`, which both docs already cite.

## Verification

Run against this branch: `provider-cooldown` (1/1), `model-failover` (46/46 combined), `model-failover-router` (34/34, spawns the real router — covers `router.mjs`, `api-forwarder.mjs` and `provider-cooldown.mjs` loading together), `rate-limit-headers` + `commandcode-forwarder` (12/12), `rate-limit-quota` + `rate-limit-scope` (3/3, including "a separately billed variant's quota headers do not overwrite its parent's"). A tree-wide grep confirms no remaining reference to any removed export.

## Possible follow-up, deliberately not done here

`provider-cooldown.mjs` is now a single function, and `canonicalProviderId` — the thing it wraps — lives in `provider-selection.mjs`. Folding `cooldownScope` in there and dropping the file would be defensible, but it touches three import sites for no behavioural gain, so I left it as a separate call.

title: fix: strip Hy4's nonce-suffixed reasoning delimiters from the answer (#654)
body:
Closes the visible-reasoning half of #654.

## What was wrong

`commandcode/hy4-preview` writes its own markup with a per-message nonce. The
reporter's capture (13 September) pinned the grammar exactly: `</think:6124c78e>`,
an 8-character hex nonce, **no matching `<think:6124c78e>` anywhere in the same
message**; one turn ended on `</arg_value:6124c78e>` instead. That is the same
nonce-tag family `src/leaked-tool-call-recovery.mjs` already parses tool calls
out of (#715).

`src/reasoning-tag-stripper.mjs` fixed an exact tag grammar, so neither spelling
was visible to it. Reproduced offline on `main` (19820289):

```
"<think>PRIVATE-R</think>FINAL"           -> "FINAL"
"PRIVATE-R</think:6124c78e>FINAL"         -> unchanged
"<think:6124c78e>PRIVATE-R</think:6124c78e>FINAL" -> unchanged
"PRIVATE-R</arg_value:6124c78e>FINAL"     -> unchanged
```

So the model's planning prose was relayed as the answer and replayed into the
next turn as ordinary assistant content.

## The change

The stripper reads the suffix, and an **orphan** nonce close -- one whose opening
tag never appeared earlier in the message -- ends the leaked reasoning and takes
the text in front of it. Same offline probes after the change, on a gated route:

```
"PRIVATE-R</think:6124c78e>FINAL"         -> "FINAL"
"<think:6124c78e>PRIVATE-R</think:6124c78e>FINAL" -> "FINAL"
"PRIVATE-R</arg_value:6124c78e>FINAL"     -> "FINAL"
```

Three lines hold the blast radius down:

- **Gated to the family that writes the nonce.** `usesHy4NonceMarkup` is the
  same predicate the tool-call recovery uses (renamed; `usesLeakedToolCallRecovery`
  still exports it for its own call site, and a test pins the two together). The
  suffix itself is unmistakable, but "everything before this was not the answer"
  is a destructive reading to hand to prose that merely quotes a delimiter.
- **The suffix is what licenses the prefix drop.** A bare `</think>` keeps its
  prefix on every route, gated or not -- that spelling is ordinary enough to
  appear in an answer *about* reasoning tags. Today's behaviour for it is
  unchanged.
- **Tool-call markup spans stay verbatim.** Recovery runs first and deliberately
  relays a span it cannot parse so a human can see what the model wrote; only an
  orphan *close* of one -- the shape recovery cannot repair, because its open
  never arrived -- is read as a terminator.

Known limit, documented in the module and asserted in a test: the delta channel
cannot retract bytes it has already emitted, so a leak whose close lands in a
later delta than its prose can still flash on screen. `output_text.done` and the
stored message item -- what Codex replays into the following turn -- are cleaned
either way, which is what stops the reasoning from accumulating in context.

## Not in this PR

- The **duplication amplification** and the reasoning-replay loop the reporter
  saw (1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 8 -> 20 copies) were measured on `99d526dc`, which predates
  #715 and #727. `commandcode/hy4-preview` resolves to the `hunyuan` family on
  current `main` (`nativeReasoningFamily` -> `hunyuan`, `usesNativeChatReasoning`
  -> true), so it now replays `reasoning_content` on its own channel instead of
  as visible text. Worth a retest on `main` before treating it as open.
- The **registry asymmetry** (`high`-only effort, no `requestProfile`) is left
  alone: adding `hy4-reasoning` changes request-side thinking parameters and
  needs a live probe on the Command Code Provider API, not a guess.

## Verification

- `node --test test/reasoning-tag-stripper.test.mjs` -- 24 tests, 8 new, covering
  both gated and ungated readings of every shape above, the split-across-deltas
  case at four chunk sizes, per-output-index state, and the documented
  delta-channel limit.
- `node --test test/leaked-tool-call-recovery.test.mjs test/namespace-relay-routing.test.mjs test/chat-reasoning.test.mjs test/router*.test.mjs test/message-phase*.test.mjs test/item-lifecycle*.test.mjs` -- pass.
- Full suite: 4154 tests, 2 failures, both known load flakes (`a slow request
  body cannot cross a session replacement`, `multilevel owners preserve a
  descendant rollback barrier ...`); both pass when their files are run alone.
- `node scripts-check.mjs` -- pass.

Windows: Control Center tray supervision repeatedly relaunches Codex Router.exe through bursts of visible PowerShell windows
body:
Summary

On Windows 11 (build 10.0.26200), the Control Center companion repeatedly spawns a
burst of `powershell.exe` processes - each with its own `conhost.exe`, so each one
is a visible console window - and relaunches `Codex Router.exe` from them.

Observed at 12:59:41-12:59:43 local time (WIB, UTC+7): six `powershell.exe`
processes within about two seconds. The same pattern repeats later (for example
13:04:43), so it is not a one-off during install.

## Environment

- codex-router 0.5.1, default Windows install at `C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\codex-router`
- Windows 11, OS build 10.0.26200
- Node.js v24.16.0
- Codex desktop app 26.908.40834
- Router service itself stayed healthy the whole time (litellm/python PIDs unchanged
  from 12:33 onward, model requests returning 200)

## Evidence

Process-start sampling using `Win32_Process` (CommandLine + ParentProcessId, 150 ms
poll). Times are local; the router log's `at=` stamps are the same events in UTC.

```text
12:59:41  conhost     (pid 8144)   <- powershell (pid 5632)
12:59:41  conhost     (pid 24256)  <- powershell (pid 15992)
12:59:41  powershell  (pid 5632)   <- Codex Router (pid 25260)
          | C:\WINDOWS\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe -NoLogo -NoProfile
            -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Local\codex-router\codex-router.ps1 ...
12:59:41  powershell  (pid 15992)  <- Codex Router (pid 25260)  (same command line)
12:59:42  powershell  (pid 8300)   <- Codex Router (pid 25260)  (same command line)
12:59:42  powershell  (pid 3128)   <- ?
12:59:43  powershell  (pid 9988)   <- Codex Router (pid 25260)  (same command line)
12:59:43  powershell  (pid 13732)  <- Codex Router (pid 25260)  (same command line)
12:59:43  powershell  (pid 13216)  <- ?
12:59:43  Codex Router (pid 4540)  <- powershell (pid 9988)
          | "...\codex-router\apps\control-center\release\win-unpacked\Codex Router.exe" ...
12:59:43  Codex Router (pid 6484)  <- powershell (pid 8300)
12:59:43  Codex Router (pid 8220)  <- powershell (pid 13732)
12:59:43  Codex Router (pid 10152) <- powershell (pid 15992)
12:59:43  codex (pid 19716)        <- Codex Router (pid 10152) | codex.exe app-server
12:59:43  cmd   (pid 3484)         <- Codex Router (pid 6484)
          | cmd /d /s /c "C:\Users\<user>\AppData\Roaming\npm\grok.cmd --version"
```

`control tray status` sampled at the same time:

```json
{"installed":false,"supported":true,"loaded":false,"appPresent":true,"state":"unknown",
 "path":"C:\\Users\\<user>\\AppData\\Local\\codex-router\\apps\\control-center\\release\\win-unpacked\\Codex Router.exe",
 "canonical":false,
 "why":"Task Scheduler did not answer whether the tray task is registered."}
```

So while the tray task state is unreadable, the companion keeps re-running its
tray transaction (`powershell.exe -File codex-router.ps1 <tray action>`) and each
transaction launches another companion instance. The relaunched instances then run
their own detection passes (`grok.cmd --version`, `tasklist`, `where`, npm prefix).

This looks like a sibling of #565 (visible PowerShell from status polling) and
#581 (relaunch supervision): another path that still surfaces console windows when
tray state cannot be established.

## Expected

- Tray supervision must not create visible console windows.
- An unreadable Task Scheduler state should degrade to a single warning, not to a
  repeating launch/relaunch cycle.

## Impact

- Dark console windows flashing on the desktop every cycle
- Repeated Electron companion launches and provider-detection subprocesses
- Model routing itself is unaffected, which makes it hard to attribute the windows
  to the Control Center without process-level evidence

## Workaround

```powershell
.\codex-router.ps1 tray stop
.\codex-router.ps1 tray uninstall
```

Output was `{"state":"stopped"}` then `{"installed":false}`, and the bursts stopped
immediately. The router service keeps running under its own "Codex Router"
scheduled task (minute heartbeat), so Codex and routed providers are unaffected.

## Minor nit

`src/control.mjs` defines `TRAY_COMMANDS = { enable: "install", disable: "uninstall", ... }`,
but `codex-router.ps1 tray disable` throws `Unknown tray action 'disable'`; the
accepted Windows actions are `install, refresh, status, start, stop, restart,
uninstall, rebuild, repair`. Accepting `disable` as an alias of `uninstall` would
keep the two surfaces consistent.

title: docs(site): publish the developer documentation with Starlight
body:
## Summary

The site had a landing page and no documentation. Every user-facing guide lived in a 2,519-line README and 18 unpublished files under `docs/`, so a visitor who wanted to configure a provider or look up a CLI command had nowhere to go.

This adds Astro Starlight alongside the existing page and publishes **43 documentation routes**, grouped into Getting started, Providers, Clients, Guides, and Reference.

## How the content was produced

The pages are **sliced from the current README and `docs/`**, not rewritten. Nothing is paraphrased or invented, so the README stays authoritative and the pages cannot drift from it on this commit. Headings are promoted one level so the right-hand table of contents populates, and cross-references are rewritten: `docs/*.md` links resolve to the matching route when that file is published and to GitHub when it is not, and README anchors resolve to whichever page now owns that heading. The generator reported zero anchors it could not resolve.

Internal working artifacts are deliberately **not** published — `GROK_RUN_REPORT.md`, `DEVIN-CLI-PROBE.md`, `GROK-STRUCTURED-PATCH-EXPERIMENT.md`, the benchmark results, `provider-catalog-audits/`, and `research/` stay in the repository.

## Landing page

It keeps its own layout and stylesheet; Starlight styles apply only to documentation routes. It gains:

- a **Docs** entry in the nav and footer, and a hero link to the documentation
- a **Windows** install block beside the macOS and Linux one. The page previously declared `operatingSystem: "macOS, Linux, Windows"` in its schema.org metadata while offering only a Homebrew command, so a Windows visitor had nothing actionable.

## Validation

- `npm run build` — 45 pages, Pagefind search index, sitemap
- `npm run check` — 5 files, 0 errors, 0 warnings, 0 hints
- Landing page and documentation routes both verified in a browser against the built output

## Follow-up, not in this PR

The repository's `homepageUrl` is still empty and neither the README nor `docs/` links to the site, so nothing points at it yet. That is a settings change plus a README line and belongs in its own change.

title: docs(skills): say that create_thread takes a model, because it does
body:
Relates to #740. The router side of that request already works; the skill pack told routed models otherwise.

## What was wrong

`skills/codex-app-threads/SKILL.md` is the text a routed model reads instead of inspecting the schema — its own frontmatter scopes it to sessions using a custom (non-OpenAI) model. Its `create_thread` section said:

> `title` is optional. **No other top-level keys are allowed.** The keys `message`, `content`, `text`, `projectKind`, and `kind` are rejected.

Meanwhile the app snapshot's `create_thread` has carried a top-level `model` since it was captured, and its description enumerates routed slugs (`opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash`, `opencode-go/glm-5.2`, …) alongside the OpenAI ones. `injectSessionModelForSpawnCalls` (`src/namespace-relay.mjs:640`) rewrites only a call that *omitted* a model, so an explicit routed slug already reaches the client untouched.

A model obeying its own skill will never emit `model`. From the operator's chair that is indistinguishable from the router refusing to relay it, which is how #740 was reported.

## Why it stayed invisible

The drift check compared only `required` fields (`test/skills-install.test.mjs`, and `src/doctor.mjs`'s equivalent). Optional arguments could drift from the snapshot indefinitely without failing anything.

## Changes

- Name `model` and `thinking` in the `create_thread` section; state that `model` accepts routed slugs and not only OpenAI ones. Keep the schema's own restraint: copy a value from the `model` field's description, only when the user asked for a specific model, never with `chatgptWorkCloud`.
- Note on `send_message_to_thread` that its `model` takes the same slugs.
- Extend the drift check to assert every optional property in the snapshot is named in that tool's skill section, for both tools.
- Keep each example in its own ```json fence so every block stays a valid JSON document. The pack is 99 lines, inside its 100-line budget.

## Verification

`test/skills-install.test.mjs` 43/43; `node scripts-check.mjs` clean.

Negative control, to show the new assertion can actually fail — reverting only the skill text to the old wording:

```
✖ the skill's declared required fields match the app snapshot
  AssertionError: create_thread section names its optional `model` argument
ℹ pass 42  ℹ fail 1
```

No behavior change: documentation plus a test. The relay itself is untouched, including the deliberate `spawn_agent` pinning at `src/namespace-relay.mjs:580-585`, where the model argument is parent-generated rather than a user choice.

title: fix(windows): accept control's tray verbs in codex-router.ps1
body:
The isolated half of #751.

## Problem

`control tray` prints its own usage line as `enable|disable|status|restart|refresh|rebuild` (`src/control.mjs:3002`) and maps the two lifecycle verbs onto the supervisor's spelling before calling it:

```js
const TRAY_COMMANDS = { enable: "install", disable: "uninstall", status: "status", restart: "restart" };
```

The Windows wrapper knew only the supervisor spelling (`codex-router.ps1:953`), so following that usage line on Windows — the documented way to take the companion out of Task Scheduler — died on `Unknown tray action 'disable'`.

## Change

Fold the two control aliases onto the supervisor verbs **before** the action is validated, so both surfaces accept the same words and dispatch the same transaction: `tray enable` reaches the same durable package-and-task replacement `tray install` does, and `tray disable` the same removal as `tray uninstall`. `companion` inherits it, since it forwards to `tray`. The unknown-action message names the aliases.

The test parses `TRAY_COMMANDS` out of `src/control.mjs` and both the alias table and the accepted-action list out of `codex-router.ps1`, then asserts every control verb resolves to the exact supervisor transaction control names for it — so a later rename on either side is caught, rather than one hard-coded spelling.

## Scope

This does **not** address the visible-console half of #751. That is the Control Center's 5-minute poll spawning seven PowerShell-wrapped reads per tick (`apps/control-center/src/App.tsx:316-319` → `electron/command-runner.mjs:900-906`), which #674 fixes by removing the wrapper. #744 fixes a sibling on the CLI side. This PR touches no file that either of those touches.

## Verification

```
node scripts-check.mjs                    → syntax checks passed
node --test test/tray-service-windows.test.mjs test/control.test.mjs \
  test/codex-router-cli.test.mjs test/installer-scripts.test.mjs \
  test/windows-parity.test.mjs test/windows-operations.test.mjs \
  test/codex-router-args.test.mjs test/update-target.test.mjs
  ✔ the Windows tray verbs accept every control tray command
  ℹ tests 147  ℹ pass 140  ℹ fail 0  ℹ skipped 7   (Windows-only suites)
```

Negative control — with the two alias lines removed, the new test fails and nothing else does (`pass 35, fail 1`).

**Authored on macOS: the PowerShell change itself is not executed by any test here.** It is covered by a text-parity test, and `test/codex-router-args.test.mjs` is Windows-only and skipped on this host. The change is a hashtable lookup with PowerShell's default case-insensitive comparer inserted ahead of the existing validator, touching no other branch, but it is unexecuted and deserves a Windows check before merge.

title: Reasoning replayed as visible text on Chat resellers outside the native-reasoning contract, after #708 widened the repair
body:
Found while checking whether #739 and #654 still reproduce. Filing separately because it is neither report's cause, it is not specific to either model, and it was opened by a change that landed after both were filed.

No live probe was run. Everything below is from code on `main` (`47ab207f`), so treat the conclusion as a mechanism, not a measurement.

## The chain

**1. Command Code now gets the reasoning-lifecycle repair.** #708 widened it from `grok-oauth` to every provider whose protocol is `openai`:

```js
// src/grok-reasoning-summary-compat.mjs:743-749
if (providerId === "grok-oauth") return new GrokReasoningSummaryCompatTransform();
if (!provider || typeof provider !== "object" || providerId === "deepseek") return undefined;
if ((provider.protocol ?? "openai") !== "openai") return undefined;
return new GrokReasoningSummaryCompatTransform({ normalizeGatewayErrors: false });
```

`config/commandcode/commandcode.json` declares no `protocol`, so it defaults to `openai` and qualifies. That is the point of #708 — it is why reasoning now reaches Codex on these routes instead of being dropped as orphan `rs_` deltas — and Codex consequently **stores a reasoning item** for those turns.

**2. Most Command Code models are outside the native-reasoning contract.** `nativeReasoningFamily` matches `upstreamModel` against five families. Resolving the shipped registry:

```
commandcode/qwen3.8-flash   upstream=Qwen/Qwen3.8-Flash      family=undefined    native=false
commandcode/minimax-m3      upstream=MiniMaxAI/MiniMax-M3    family=minimax-m3   native=true
commandcode/hy4-preview     upstream=tencent/hy4-preview     family=hunyuan      native=true
```

Every other `commandcode/*` thinking model is also uncovered: all three `qwen3.7-*`, both `qwen3.8-max*`, `minimax-m2.7`, `kimi-k2.7-*`, `step-3.7-flash`, `mimo-v2.5-pro`, `nemotron-3-ultra`, `inkling*`.

**3. An uncovered route replays that stored reasoning as visible text.** `src/router.mjs:3249-3252` passes `nativeThinking: usesNativeChatReasoning(route)` into `carryReasoningThroughInput`; at `:2153` → `:2191` a pure-text assistant turn becomes `{ type: nativeThinking ? "thinking" : "output_text", text }`. With `nativeThinking: false` the prior turn's reasoning is prepended to the assistant message as `output_text`.

That is exactly the shape `AGENTS.md:2033-2039` names as the loop trigger:

> An interleaved-thinking model that instead sees its past reasoning replayed as visible assistant text moves new thinking into the answer channel and loops on its last progress note (Hy4 on opencode Go, 12 September 2026: 2, 4, 5, 8, 16 copies per message).

Before #708 this was self-limiting on these routes: no reasoning item was stored, so there was nothing to carry. Steps 1 and 3 are individually correct and only interact badly for the models in the gap between them.

## Why this is not just "add the families"

`AGENTS.md:2042-2045` sets the bar deliberately:

> Add a family only with evidence the vendor expects `reasoning_content` back, and a reseller only after a live probe shows the route returns reasoning and accepts the echo-back.

There is also code evidence pointing the other way for Qwen specifically — `src/reasoning-tag-stripper.mjs:3-10` documents Qwen leaking chain-of-thought *inline* in `content` as `<think>…</think>` on this bridge rather than on the structured channel. If that is what actually happens, the stripper removes it, no reasoning item is created, and the replay path stays inert for that model. Which models are genuinely exposed therefore cannot be settled offline.

## What would settle it

One turn per candidate model on current `main`, checking the rollout JSONL for a stored `"type":"reasoning"` item on an assistant turn:

- **reasoning item present** → the route is exposed; it needs a family entry (with the echo-back acceptance check the rule requires) or an explicit exclusion.
- **no reasoning item ever** → that model is inert on this path and needs nothing.

## Possible shape of a fix, if the probes confirm exposure

Rather than growing the family list one vendor at a time, the safer default may be to not replay reasoning as `output_text` at all for a Chat Completions reseller that is outside the contract — drop it from the carry instead of converting it to visible prose. That trades a little lost context for removing the loop trigger entirely, and it does not require asserting anything about a vendor's `reasoning_content` handling. Worth weighing against the carry's original purpose before anyone implements it.

Related: #739 (`commandcode/qwen3.8-flash`), #654 (`commandcode/hy4-preview`, now covered), and #727 which introduced the family keying.

title: [Bug]: Invalid modalities for ZAI Coding Plan GLM 5.3 Flash
body:
### What happened?

`zai-coding/glm-5.3-flash` is currently declared as text-only:

config/zai/coding/glm-5.3-flash.json

"inputModalities": [
  "text"
]

This causes Codex Router to use the vision bridge instead of sending images
natively to GLM-5.3-Flash.

However, native image input works correctly through the Z.ai Coding Plan endpoint.

### Reproduction

1. Use `zai-coding/glm-5.3-flash`.
2. Attach an image in Codex.
3. With the current config, the route is treated as text-only.
4. Change:

   "inputModalities": ["text"]

   to:

   "inputModalities": ["text", "image"]

5. Regenerate/restart the router.
6. Attach an image again.

Result: GLM-5.3-Flash successfully receives and analyzes the image natively
through the Z.ai Coding Plan.

### Expected

`zai-coding/glm-5.3-flash` should declare:

"inputModalities": ["text", "image"]

The corresponding test in `test/glm-5.3-flash.test.mjs` should also be updated,
since it currently expects only opencode-go and ollama-cloud routes to be
multimodal.

### Environment

macOS
Codex Desktop
Z.ai GLM Coding Plan

title: Native replay: carry a routed model's visible reasoning as text
body:
When a conversation mixes a routed thinking model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and similar) with a native ChatGPT model, the native backend rejects the routed model's reasoning items on replay:

- `content` is capped at zero parts: `Invalid 'input[1].content': array too long. Expected an array with maximum length 0` (`array_above_max_length`)
- a non-`rs_` id is rejected; an `rs_` id this backend never stored is a 404
- a foreign `encrypted_content` fails to decrypt (`invalid_encrypted_content`)

Today the item is forwarded unchanged, so the turn (and remote compaction) returns 400. Dropping the item loses the thinking the conversation was built on; moving the text into `summary` keeps the bytes but not the meaning -- measured against the live backend, a passphrase that appears only in a reasoning `summary` never reaches the model's answer.

`normalizeNativeInput` now replaces a reasoning item that carries visible `content` text with a visible assistant message:

```
[internal reasoning from an earlier turn]
<text>
```

The item's `id` and `encrypted_content` go with it (they cannot be replayed natively). Items without visible content keep their exact shape, so native reasoning summaries and their continuation tokens are untouched. `CODEX_ROUTER_NATIVE_REASONING_AS_TEXT=0` restores the previous passthrough.

The fix is native-path only: routed compaction (`handleRoutedCompaction`) and the DeepSeek replay path never run through `normalizeNativeInput`, and `deepseek-responses-routing.test.mjs` already asserts routed reasoning must stay in its own shape.

Evidence:

- Live matrix against the ChatGPT backend: content kept -> 400 `array_above_max_length`; content moved to `summary` -> passes validation but the model never reads it (0/1 passphrase hits); visible assistant message -> 200 and the model answers the passphrase.
- End-to-end through a patched router instance: ordinary native turn 200 with the passphrase read back; V2 compaction with the same item 200 (400 before).
- Size: relabelling 509 real reasoning items shrank the serialized JSON by 4.1% (1,942,770 -> 1,862,857 bytes); no new text is added beyond a 43-character prefix.
- `node --test test/routing.test.mjs`: 141/141 with this patch over `main`.

title: chore(deps-dev): bump playwright from 1.62.1 to 1.63.0
body:
Bumps [playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.62.1 to 1.63.0.
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.63.0

🔒 Test locks

Tests that access a shared resource — an external service, a global account setting — can now declare a named lock. Tests that share a lock name never run concurrently, across files, workers and projects, while everything else keeps running in parallel:

test('update user settings', { lock: 'user-settings' }, async ({ page }) => {
  // never runs at the same time as other tests holding 'user-settings'
});

A test can hold multiple locks, and test.describe() accepts a lock for the whole group. Learn more about test locks.

🪟 Locate across frames

page.frameLocator() and frame.frameLocator() called without a selector search in any frame of the subtree, so you no longer need to locate the iframe first:

// Finds the button in any frame on the page.
await page.frameLocator().getByRole('button').click();

The rest of the locator resolves inside a single frame, just like a regular locator, and an error is thrown when it matches elements in several frames.

👁️ Visible-only locators

New locator.visible() returns a locator that matches only visible elements. It is the recommended replacement for the :visible CSS pseudo-class:

await page.locator('button').visible().click();

🧾 Step params and subtitles

Steps now carry structured data for reporters. Playwright API steps report the target locator and call arguments, and test.step() accepts subtitle and params options for your own steps:

await test.step('Login', async () => {
  // ...
}, { subtitle: 'as admin', params: { user: 'admin' } });

Reporters receive them via testStep.subtitle and testStep.params. For Playwright API
