title: fix: read a quote as a quote only where a YAML node can begin
body:
## Why

`yaml-structure.mjs` opens the file by saying what it is for: splice one provider route into a settings document a harness owns, "without disturbing a single other byte of it", and refuse anything it cannot read plainly rather than guess.

`scanValue` treats every `'` and `"` as a quoting indicator. YAML only gives a quote that meaning where a node can begin. `note: don't edit` is a plain scalar carrying an apostrophe — PyYAML reads it as the string `don't edit` — but the lexer reads it as a quoted scalar that opens and never closes, so every line after it becomes a continuation of that scalar and registers no key.

That splits into two outcomes, and the quiet one is the dangerous one.

**When nothing later matches the quote,** the scan reaches end of file and refuses:

```
Refusing ambiguous YAML structure at line 6: a quoted scalar is unterminated.
```

The document is ordinary and the user has no way to act on that message. The router cannot publish, cannot remove, and cannot refresh a caller capability into that file.

**When a later line happens to carry a matching quote,** the scan finishes without complaint — having silently moved every key in between inside the node that opened it. `spliceYamlBlock` then writes the route at `anchor.endIndex + 1`, which is now past the end of somebody else's value:

```yaml
# before                                   # after publishing
llm-pi-ai:                                 llm-pi-ai:
  providers:                                 providers:
    my-proxy:                                  my-proxy:
      note: don't edit                           note: don't edit
theme: dark                                theme: dark
prompt: |                                  prompt: |
  it's fine to edit this                     it's fine to edit this
                                               codex-router:            <- inside `prompt`
                                                 baseURL: "http://…"
                                                 apiKeyEnv: "…"
```

`llm-pi-ai.providers.codex-router` does not exist, so the harness never sees a route — while `yamlValuePresent` and every status surface agree the publish went in. The user's `prompt` value silently grew four lines of YAML.

This reaches DeepSeek Harness `settings.yaml` and `.credentials.yaml`, omp `models.yml`, Hermes Agent `config.yaml`, and `caller-key-client-refresh.mjs` writing into all three. An apostrophe in a `description`, a `systemPrompt`, or an author's name is not an exotic input for those files.

## What changed

One function. `scanValue` now tracks whether the position it is at can begin a node, and opens a quoted scalar only there:

- the start of a value,
- after a flow collection's `[`, `{`, `,` or `:`,
- after a block sequence's `- `.

Whitespace separates tokens without ending a plain scalar, so it leaves the position as it found it; every other character ends one. `scanValue` also takes and returns the running flow depth instead of a per-line delta, because those positions cannot be known on a continuation line otherwise.

The rule is positional, not a blanket "ignore quotes". `a: "x: not a key"` and `b: ['c: no', "d: no"]` still have opaque quoted contents, `a: 'one\n  two'` still folds across lines, and `a: "never closed"` is still refused.

## Verification

Differential run against PyYAML: 27,045 generated documents that PyYAML accepts (nested mappings, block sequences, block scalars, flow collections, comments, quoted and plain scalars, apostrophes and unpaired double quotes, with and without a trailing newline). Each one is published, published again, and removed:

| on 27,045 valid YAML documents | `main` | this branch |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| refused outright | 6,956 | 0 |
| published output no longer parses as YAML | 184 | 0 |
| route written somewhere other than `llm-pi-ai.providers.codex-router` | 178 | 0 |
| clean round trip (publish → publish again → remove) | 19,727 | **27,045** |

The residual differences on both branches are the same one category and it is pre-existing: `joinLines` gives a document that lacked one a final newline, so a block scalar sitting at end of file gains one. Counted separately and excluded from the table above; no other value changes on either branch.

- Five new cases. Four fail on `main` and pass here: `an apostrophe inside a plain scalar is not an opening quote`, `an unpaired double quote inside a plain scalar is not an opening quote`, `a stray quote does not extend one node over the keys that follow it`, and `an apostrophe elsewhere in the document does not move the route`. The fifth (`a quote still opens a scalar wherever a node can begin`) passes on `main` too — it guards against the fix over-correcting rather than evidencing the bug, and I have labelled it as such.
- `node --test test/yaml-structure.test.mjs test/dsh-config-manager.test.mjs test/dsh-catalog.test.mjs test/routed-harness*.test.mjs test/caller-key*.test.mjs test/target-integration.test.mjs` — all pass.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Before/after measured by running `main`'s copy of the module side by side in a worktree, not from memory of what it used to do.

## Scope

I did not widen `PLAIN_KEY`. A mapping *key* carrying a `/` or a `:` is still declined, which is a separate question with its own blast radius — and #817 covers what that currently costs.

title: fix: refuse to edit a harness mapping this reader could not read whole
body:
## Why

`dsh-config-manager.mjs` opens with the rule it exists to enforce: the router owns exactly one key in each of the harness's two documents and "treats every other byte as somebody else's work."

It answers "does this mapping hold anything but ours?" with `node.children`. That map holds only the mapping keys the YAML lexer managed to *register*. A block sequence, a merge key, or a provider id the key grammar declines — `openrouter/free:` — lives inside the node while being invisible there, and its own entries are hoisted up as the parent's children instead.

`routed-harness-document.mjs` already knows this. Its `unaccountedLines` helper says so in a comment that names both blind spots, and adds: *"This is how removal came to splice away a whole `providers:` sequence and leave a zero-byte file."* That lesson never reached the DeepSeek Harness manager, which still has all of it.

**Publishing nests the route inside the user's provider.** The indent is copied off "the first sibling", which is now a hoisted grandchild two columns deeper:

```yaml
# before                                  # after `applyRouteToSettings`
llm-pi-ai:                                llm-pi-ai:
  providers:                                providers:
    openrouter/free:                          openrouter/free:
      api: openai-completions                   api: openai-completions
      baseURL: https://openrouter.ai/…          baseURL: https://openrouter.ai/…
                                                codex-router:          <- inside their provider
                                                  baseURL: "http://…"
                                                  …
```

The output is valid YAML, so nothing complains. `llm-pi-ai.providers.codex-router` does not exist, so the harness has no route — while every status read agrees the publish worked.

**Removal empties the file.** `children.size === 1` reads as "only ours", so the collapse walks up and splices `llm-pi-ai` away whole:

```
143 bytes  ->  0 bytes
```

```yaml
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    - id: my-proxy                          # somebody else's route
      baseURL: https://proxy.example/v1
    codex-router:
      baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:4202/v1"
```

A sequence registers no keys at all, so `providers.children` is just `codex-router`. This shape is already on disk anywhere an earlier build published.

**One comment line does the same.** `endIndex` deliberately stops before a trailing comment block, so a note the user wrote above our key sits inside `providers`' range without being inside ours:

```yaml
llm-pi-ai:
  providers:
    # my own routes live in providers.d
    codex-router:
      baseURL: "http://127.0.0.1:4202/v1"
```

`removeRouteFromSettings` on that returns `""`. 124 bytes to nothing, on a perfectly ordinary file, on uninstall.

**The credentials document has the matching failure — and it holds secrets.** `applyCredential`'s own comment spells out the consequence: *"`refs.indent + 2` is the column of the `refs:` key itself, so a document whose entries are indented four spaces would be handed a two-space sibling, and that mixed-indent block is not YAML any parser will read back. The whole file is the harness's credential store, so the loss would be every adapter's key, not ours."* A `refs:` whose entries the grammar declines registers no sibling, which is exactly how that fallback is reached:

```yaml
version: 1              version: 1
refs:              ->   refs:
    other/ref: sk-x         other/ref: sk-x
                          CODEX_ROUTER_CALLER_KEY: "sk-ours"    <- unreadable from here down
```

## What changed

`unaccountedLines` moves from `routed-harness-document.mjs` into `yaml-structure.mjs`, unchanged, and both managers import it. One answer to one question, in the module that owns the lexer whose blind spots it compensates for.

Four call sites in `dsh-config-manager.mjs`:

- `applyRouteToSettings` and `applyCredential` refuse before computing an indent, through a shared `assertReadableMapping` that mirrors `applyYamlValue`'s guard — comment lines filtered, since a comment is not a mapping entry we can collide with.
- `removeRouteFromSettings` and `removeCredential` stop the parent collapse when the region holds anything unaccounted, comments included, exactly as `removeYamlValue` already does.

A refusal names the line:

```
Refusing to edit llm-pi-ai.providers: line 3 (openrouter/free:) is not a mapping
entry this reader can account for.
```

## Refusing is not a regression here

For every document this now refuses, the current behaviour is already broken — the route goes somewhere the harness does not read, or the file stops parsing. Replacing a silent wrong write with a message naming the line is strictly better, and it is what the module says it does with anything it cannot read plainly.

Removal is the other way round: it now *succeeds* where it used to destroy the file, leaving an empty `providers:` behind when it cannot prove the section is ours alone. `removeYamlValue` already accepts that trade in the same words — "leaving an empty `providers:` behind is a cosmetic cost; splicing the user's content away is not recoverable."

## Verification

- Five new cases in `test/dsh-config-manager.test.mjs`, all five failing on `main` and passing here: publishing beside a declined key, publishing into a sequence, removal beside a sequence sibling, removal beside the user's comment, and the credentials envelope.
- `node --test test/dsh-config-manager.test.mjs test/routed-harness.test.mjs test/yaml-structure.test.mjs test/caller-key-client-refresh.test.mjs` — 84/84.
- `npm run check` passes.
- Each before/after measured by running `main`'s copy of the modules in a worktree beside this branch, not from recollection.

## Rebased onto #816

#816 has landed, so `main` is merged in here. Both touched `src/yaml-structure.mjs`, but different functions — `scanValue` there, the new `unaccountedLines` export here — so the merge was clean; `CHANGELOG.md` resolved by its own `merge=union` rule with all 36 of `main`'s bullets kept. The diff against `main` is still exactly the five files below and nothing else.

Re-verified on the merged tree:

- `node --test test/yaml-structure.test.mjs test/dsh-config-manager.test.mjs test/dsh-catalog.test.mjs test/routed-harness.test.mjs test/caller-key-client-refresh.test.mjs test/target-integration.test.mjs` — 111/111.
- `npm run check` passes.
- The #816 property run again, on the merged tree: 30,000 generated documents PyYAML accepts, **30,000 clean round trips**, no refusals. The new guard costs nothing on documents whose `providers:` this reader can read whole — it only fires on the shapes above, which are the ones that are silently broken today.

## What I did not do

Widening `PLAIN_KEY` to accept `/` and `:` would let `openrouter/free:` be *registered* rather than refused, which is a better outcome than either behaviour here. It changes what the lexer registers for every consumer, so it belongs in its own change with its own evidence. Happy to open it as an issue, or as a PR if you want it.

title: Kimi login hardcodes kimi.com (breaks outside China); multi_agent_v2 managed block collides with existing user key and breaks Codex config
body:
## Kimi login flow hardcodes the China-region `kimi.com` domain; global-region accounts can't complete auth

**Version:** `3ff694d` (2026-09-17)

### What happened

Running `kimi login` (via the setup smoke-test failure prompt, and standalone) opens a device-authorization URL on `www.kimi.com`:

```
https://www.kimi.com/code/authorize_device?user_code=XXXX-XXXX
```

For an account outside China, that page displays a reminder to use the global site instead and does not proceed to the actual sign-in screen — it just sits there. The flow only completes after manually editing the URL's domain from `kimi.com` to `kimi.ai`:

```
https://www.kimi.ai/code/authorize_device?user_code=XXXX-XXXX
```

Same domain (`kimi.com`) is used elsewhere for the OAuth token endpoint and a help link, so a global-region user likely hits this every time they authenticate, not just once.

### Where

- `src/kimi-oauth-session.mjs:28` — `"https://auth.kimi.com"`
- `src/kimi-oauth-onboarding.mjs:6` — `"https://www.kimi.com/help/kimi-code/cli-getting-started"`

Neither location offers a `.ai` alternative or detects/asks the account's region.

### Suggested fix

Either prompt for region (China / global) once during `kimi login` and persist the choice the way other providers persist config, or auto-detect from the account/response and retry on the other domain before failing. At minimum, the CLI could surface a "having trouble? try kimi.ai instead" hint rather than requiring the user to read the browser page and hand-edit the URL.

### Repro

1. Fresh setup, select Kimi Code OAuth.
2. Run `kimi login` (or hit the smoke-test's "run again" path).
3. Browser opens `www.kimi.com/code/authorize_device?...` for a non-China account.
4. Page shows a region reminder, does not proceed.
5. Manually swap to `www.kimi.ai/...` in the address bar — flow completes normally from there.

---

### Small aside, same setup session

Not filing separately since it's minor and probably just registry lag: the Antigravity model list (`src/antigravity-oauth-shape.mjs`) only goes up to `gemini-3.7-flash` — `gemini-3.8-flash` (released 2026-09-02, now Antigravity's own default model) isn't in the list yet, though it does show up correctly under the OpenRouter section. Mentioning in case it's useful alongside a routine model-registry refresh.

---

## Second, more serious issue found in the same setup pass: the `multi_agent_v2` managed block collides with a pre-existing user key and breaks Codex entirely

The `codex-router-multi-agent-v2-managed` block writer appends a top-level

```toml
multi_agent_v2 = { enabled = true, max_concurrent_threads_per_session = 6, ... }
```

directly under the existing `[features]` table, with no check for whether `features.multi_agent_v2` is already defined elsewhere in the file. If the user already has their own `[features.multi_agent_v2]` table (a completely reasonable thing to have — Codex documents and supports it directly), this produces a **duplicate key** and Codex refuses to start at all:

```
Error: /Users/wax/.codex/config.toml:265:1: duplicate key
```

`codex-router doctor` itself surfaces this clearly (`FAIL Codex config loads: ... duplicate key`), which is good — but the setup/install flow that WRITES the block in the first place doesn't check for it, so a user can walk away from a "successful" setup with a config that can't load at all until they notice and run `doctor` themselves (or, as here, until it's diagnosed by hand).

**Fix I applied locally:** merged the five `codex-router`-owned fields into the pre-existing `[features.multi_agent_v2]` table instead of a competing inline-table assignment, and removed the duplicate. Suggests the writer should detect an existing `features.multi_agent_v2` table (or any other key it's about to introduce) and merge into it rather than blindly appending a second, colliding definition.

title: [Union Alpha auto-compact thrash] auto_compact_token_limit can desync from context_window after curation/refresh, causing compact-thrashing (related to but distinct from #266)
body:
## `auto_compact_token_limit` can desync from `context_window`, causing compact-thrashing (a #266-adjacent regression, not the same bug)

**Version:** `3ff694d` (2026-09-17)

### What happened

Curated `openrouter/union-alpha` (a brand-new anonymous "stealth" listing) via `codex-router curate-models openrouter`. Codex began compacting far more often than expected on this model ("compact thrashing").

Inspecting `~/.codex/codex-router/merged-models.json`:

```json
{
  "slug": "openrouter/union-alpha",
  "context_window": 262144,
  "auto_compact_token_limit": 131072
}
```

`context_window` is correct (matches OpenRouter's advertised 262,144). `auto_compact_token_limit` is exactly **50%** of that — every other model in the same catalog sits at 85-95%:

| Model | context_window | auto_compact_token_limit | ratio |
|---|---|---|---|
| grok-4.6 | 500,000 | 440,000 | 88% |
| deepseek-v4-flash | 1,048,576 | 900,000 | 86% |
| glm-5.3 | 1,048,576 | 943,000 | 90% |
| union-alpha | 262,144 | **131,072** | **50%** |

131,072 also happens to be exactly Union Alpha's own advertised **max-completion-tokens** limit, not a fraction of its context window.

### Root cause (traced in source, not just symptom)

`curate-models.mjs` correctly computes `autoCompact` as `Math.floor(contextLength * 0.85)` in `curatedSizing()` (this is the fix that landed for #266 — `contextWindow` is now seeded from the provider's real advertised length). But that function's own neighboring comment says:

> "a window stored without it keeps whatever the conservative default said"

i.e., the authors were aware that some path can update `context_window` on an entry without recomputing `auto_compact_token_limit` alongside it — and that appears to be exactly what happened here. Union Alpha is a fresh/anonymous stealth listing; at curation time its metadata was likely incomplete or ambiguous, so it landed on a conservative fallback value close to its own max-output figure. Some later step (a `refresh-catalog` run, or the initial curation itself resolving `context_window` from a different, later-available field than the one that set `autoCompact`) corrected `context_window` to the true 262,144 without re-deriving `auto_compact_token_limit` from it.

This is not the same mechanism as #266 (which was about the *estimate* used on zero-`prompt_tokens` turns overshooting a correctly-small window). Here the *stored* threshold itself is stale relative to a *correctly* stored window — the two fields drifted apart. `model-registry.mjs`'s validator only checks `1 <= autoCompact <= contextWindow` (line ~864-868), which a desynced-but-still-valid pair like this passes silently.

### Suggested fix

- Whenever `context_window`/`contextWindow` is written or updated for an entry (curation, refresh, discovery re-resolution), always recompute `auto_compact_token_limit` from it via the same `AUTO_COMPACT_RATIO` rather than leaving a previously-stored value in place.
- Alternatively, add a `doctor` check comparing the ratio of `auto_compact_token_limit` / `context_window` per model against an expected band (e.g. 0.80-0.95) and flag outliers — this would have caught the desync immediately, the way `context-window-drift.mjs` already catches provider-exceeds-window cases.

### Workaround applied locally

Recomputed by hand: `int(262144 * 0.85) = 222822`, written directly into `merged-models.json`, `doctor` passes clean afterward. Not durable — a future `curate-models`/`refresh-catalog` run may regenerate the stale value again since the underlying desync path is still there.

title: SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN greedy backtracking truncates the requested-token count to its last digit ("4 tokens" instead of ~283,000)
body:
## `SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN` truncates the requested-token count to its last digit ("4 tokens" instead of the real ~283,000)

**Version:** `3ff694d` (2026-09-17)

### What happened

Hit a genuine context-window overflow on `openrouter/union-alpha` (one turn's tool input alone was 150,084 tokens; total request 282,974 vs. the model's real 262,144 window — a real overflow, not a router bug). The user-facing error codex-router surfaced was:

> "openrouter could not run Union Alpha (OpenRouter). The rendered prompt is **4 tokens**, exceeding the model's 262,144-token context window. This is a context-window or tokenizer/template mismatch, not high demand."

"4 tokens" vs. an actual ~283,000-token request — nonsensical, and actively misleading (reads as a tokenizer bug, not the real cause).

### Root cause

`src/error-translation.mjs`, `SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN`:

```js
const SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN =
  /maximum context length (?:is|of) (\d+)(?: tokens?)?.{0,80}(?:input|request).{0,40}(\d+)/i;
```

Both `.{0,80}` and `.{0,40}` are greedy. Against the raw upstream error:

```
This endpoint's maximum context length is 262144 tokens. However, you requested about 282974 tokens (132890 of text input, 150084 of tool input).
```

`.{0,80}` backtracks from its maximum length downward, so it finds the *last* possible position where `(?:input|request)` can start within budget — landing on "input" in "text input" (~72 chars in) rather than "request" in "you requested" (~21 chars in). From there, `.{0,40}` does the same thing to `(\d+)`: it backtracks to the *last* digit-starting offset within its 40-char budget, which lands on the trailing `4` of `150084` rather than its leading `1`. `(\d+)` then only extends forward, so it captures the single digit `"4"` and stops.

Reproduced directly:

```js
const SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN =
  /maximum context length (?:is|of) (\d+)(?: tokens?)?.{0,80}(?:input|request).{0,40}(\d+)/i;
const text = "This endpoint's maximum context length is 262144 tokens. However, you requested about 282974 tokens (132890 of text input, 150084 of tool input). Please reduce the length of either one...";
text.match(SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN);
// -> ['... 150084', '262144', '4']   <- group 2 is "4"
```

### Fix

Make both quantifiers lazy so the engine finds the *first* valid match instead of the last:

```js
const SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN =
  /maximum context length (?:is|of) (\d+)(?: tokens?)?.{0,80}?(?:input|request).{0,40}?(\d+)/i;
```

Same input now correctly yields `['262144', '282974']` — the real total requested-token count from litellm's own message, matching what's actually reported upstream.

### Why this matters beyond cosmetics

The composed message explicitly tells the user "this is a context-window or tokenizer/template mismatch, not high demand" — confident, specific, and wrong. A user hitting a real, simple overflow (their thread genuinely grew past the window) gets steered toward debugging a nonexistent tokenizer bug instead of just starting a shorter thread or compacting.

title: Fix greedy backtracking in SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN
body:
Fixes #821.

Both `.{0,80}` and `.{0,40}` gaps in `SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN` were greedy, so backtracking searches long-to-short and lands on the *last* valid position within budget instead of the first. Against a real overflow message with two `input`/`request` occurrences and a multi-digit number followed by more digits later in the string, this truncates the captured token count to a single trailing digit.

Repro (see the linked issue for the full trace):

```js
const text = "This endpoint's maximum context length is 262144 tokens. However, you requested about 282974 tokens (132890 of text input, 150084 of tool input).";
text.match(SWAPPED_CONTEXT_LENGTH_PATTERN);
// before: ['...', '262144', '4']
// after:  ['...', '262144', '282974']
```

## Changes

- `src/error-translation.mjs`: made both quantifiers lazy (`.{0,80}?`, `.{0,40}?`).
- `test/error-translation.test.mjs`: added a regression test using the exact failing message shape.

## Verification

- `node --test test/error-translation.test.mjs` — 42/42 passing, including the new case.
- Full `node --test test/*.mjs` was still running at the time of this PR (large suite); happy to report back once it completes, but the change is scoped to one regex in one function with direct, passing test coverage.

title: fix: drop reasoning flags on compaction requests to keyless providers
body:
## Problem

Compaction on a local (keyless) model fails immediately. The ordinary routed turn works, but compaction dies before any prompt is read.

## Root cause

The ordinary routed turn path already drops `reasoning` and `reasoning_effort` for keyless providers (see the existing keyless provider guards in the turn handler). LiteLLM forwards these fields as a `think` parameter that Ollama rejects.

The compaction path (`summarizeWith`) spreads the same client payload but was missing the same guard. Codex sends `reasoning` as an object with the compaction request, so LiteLLM forwards it and Ollama rejects it.

## Fix

Add the same keyless drop to `summarizeWith` that the turn path already has.

```js
if (providerForModel(route)?.keyless) {
  delete body.reasoning;
  delete body.reasoning_effort;
}
```

## Testing

- Added a test in `test/local-ollama-routing.test.mjs` asserting that a POST to `/responses/compact` with `reasoning` and `reasoning_effort` in the payload forwards neither field to the mock gateway.
- Verified locally with Ollama running a local model.

Mutation-testing note, for transparency rather than a blocker: five hand-written mutants were checked against the new guard. Removing the whole block, dropping only `reasoning`, dropping only `reasoning_effort`, and inverting the condition are all killed by the new test. One survivor remains: dropping unconditionally (ignoring the `keyless` check) also passes, because no upstream test asserts that reasoning is forwarded on compaction for a keyed provider. The keyed-provider compaction tests in `routing.test.mjs` and `deepseek-tool-message-compat.test.mjs` never assert reasoning survival either, so this is an existing suite-wide gap rather than one introduced here. Fixing it means adding a keyed-provider compaction fixture that sends `reasoning` and asserts it survives to the gateway, deliberately left out of scope for this PR.

title: feat(control-center): selecting a usage source should filter the page, not reorder it
body:
**What I expected**

Clicking a source in *Usage sources* would narrow the page to that provider — one set of allowance cards, one timeline, one summary.

**What happens instead**

Selection only reorders. The selected source's allowance rows move to the front of the list and every other source stays on the page:

- `apps/control-center/src/pages/UsagePage.tsx:160` builds `allowances` as `[selected source rows, ...everything else]`.
- `apps/control-center/src/pages/UsagePage.tsx:400` renders every non-subscription source unconditionally, so the source grid never shrinks.

So with Command Code selected I still see ChatGPT, opencode GoZen and OpenCode Free, just shuffled. On a page whose whole job is "what am I spending, on what", that reads as noise rather than focus — and it is easy to misread a neighbouring card's totals as the selected provider's.

**What I'd like**

- Selection filters: only the selected source's allowance cards and rows remain, with an obvious way back to the aggregate (`This router · all providers` already exists as a row).
- Or, if reordering is deliberate, make the state visible — keep the full grid but mark the selected card as *Selected* rather than leaving it to be inferred from position.

Happy to be told reordering is intentional; in that case the affordance is the part that needs work.

title: feat(control-center): usage source names are too small to scan
body:
On the Usage page the provider/source name is the thing you scan first, and it is the smallest text in the card.

Measured from `apps/control-center/src/pages/usage-status.css`:

- source name (`.us-source-name strong`): **9.5px**, weight 600 — line 930
- secondary description (`.us-source-name small`): **7.8px** — line 938
- group label above the grid (`.us-source-group-label`): 9px — line 883

At a normal window width the source grid is 3-up (`grid-template-columns: repeat(auto-fit, minmax(300px, 1fr))`, line 875), so "Command Code", "opencode GoZen" and "OpenCode Free" all render under 10px while the token values beside them get the same treatment. Identifying the row you want takes longer than it should, and it is worse at a glance.

Suggest a hierarchy fix rather than a redesign: raise the source name to roughly 12-13px (and/or increase weight or contrast), let the secondary description carry the small size, and leave the group label alone.

title: feat(control-center): show a cache-hit rate per provider on the Usage page
body:
Command Code advertises a ~98% prompt-cache hit rate, and the router already meters cached input — but there is nowhere to see the resulting *rate*, so there is no way to judge whether routing through the router costs more cache than running a provider's own harness.

**What already exists**

- `normalizeTokenUsage` reads `input_tokens_details.cached_tokens` / `prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens` / `prompt_cache_hit_tokens` (`src/response-usage.mjs:152`).
- `usage-events.jsonl` stores `cachedInputTokens` per event.
- `aggregateProviderUsage` keeps `cachedInputTokens`, `regularInputTokens` and a `cacheTelemetrySeen` flag across the retained ledger, explicitly so the dashboard does not have to reconstruct it from a capped 24-hour probe (`src/provider-usage.mjs:97`).
- The Usage page shows *Cached input* as an absolute token count (`UsagePage.tsx:733`, legend at `:901`) and the chart splits cached from regular input.

**What's missing**

The rate itself: `cachedInputTokens / inputTokens` over the selected range, per provider, next to the existing figures — e.g. "Cached input 41.2m (23%)". The absolute count answers "how much", not "how well", which is the number needed to compare a routed provider against its native harness.

**One caveat worth deciding up front**

For Command Code specifically the ratio is currently unmeasurable, because that route reports no prompt totals at all. On this install:

- 12 of 10,258 `commandcode` events carry `cachedInputTokens`
- recent `commandcode/deepseek-v4.1-flash` turns report `inputTokens: 0` with only `estimatedInputTokens` populated (e.g. 234,360 estimated against 0 reported)

So a cache-hit-rate column would read blank or 0% for Command Code until prompt totals are plumbed through on that path, which is arguably the more useful half of the request. Prefer rendering "not reported" rather than "0%" so a genuine zero cache hit stays distinguishable from an absent field.

title: feat(providers): show the Command Code monthly window on the Usage page
body:
**What's missing**

The Usage page shows Command Code's 5-hour and weekly windows but not its monthly one, even though the provider's own dashboard shows all three. Their Studio page renders a "Monthly Limit" bar that resets on the subscription's period end; the router's *Accounts and allowances* card stops at 5-hour and weekly.

**Where it comes from**

`commandCodeCreditsMetrics` (`src/provider-account-usage.mjs:291`) reads `payload.windowLimits` and emits only:

- `windowMetric("5-hour limit", windows.fiveHour)`
- `windowMetric("Weekly limit", windows.weekly)`

There is no monthly entry because the endpoint it calls — `GET https://api.commandcode.ai/alpha/billing/credits` — has no monthly window. Its shape is:

```
credits:      { belowThreshold, creditThreshold, monthlyCredits, purchasedCredits, freeCredits }
windowLimits: { limited, exceeded, fiveHour: { used, cap, resetAt, exceeded }, weekly: { ... } }
```

**How the provider calculates the monthly percentage**

From their web client, not reverse-engineered guesswork:

```js
total = max(monthlyCreditsGranted, tier.limits.totalCredits)   // x seatQuantity for org plans
used  = clamp(total - monthlyCreditsRemaining, 0, total)
pct   = round(used / total * 100)                              // hidden when status === "past_due"
```

`monthlyCreditsRemaining` is `credits.monthlyCredits`; `tier` is the subscription's `planId` resolved against a static plan table; the caption is the subscription's `currentPeriodEnd`. Worth noting their 5-hour and weekly bars are simpler — a straight `used / cap` from `windowLimits`, which is exactly what the router already renders.

**What the provider API already exposes**

All three of these work with a provider API key today:

- `GET /alpha/billing/credits` → `credits.monthlyCredits` (remaining), plus the two windows above
- `GET /alpha/billing/subscriptions` → `planId`, `quantity`, `status`, `currentPeriodEnd` (e.g. `planId: "individual-goat"`)
- `GET /alpha/usage/summary` → `totalMonthlyCredits`, `periodBasis: "billing-period"`

So the denominator is derivable without a new upstream field, two ways:

1. `planId` → monthly grant. The table is 8 public entries: Provider 15, Go 10, GOAT 70, Pro 30, Pro-v1 80, Max 150, Ultra 300, teams-pro x seats.
2. `credits.monthlyCredits + usage/summary.totalMonthlyCredits`.

Checked against the provider's own page: it moved from 89% to 90% as the balance fell over the same period, and both candidate denominators fit those readings. They differ by at most 1-2 points mid-range, so either is safe to ship.

**Suggested scope**

Render a `Monthly limit` metric on the Command Code account card beside the existing two, taking the cap from the plan lookup and the reset from `currentPeriodEnd`, mirroring the provider's own wording. Two details worth encoding:

- Suppress the metric (or label it) when the subscription status is `past_due`, matching the provider — don't render 0%.
- Prefer "not reported" over a derived number if the subscription read fails, so an unknown plan never renders as a confident percentage.

**Upstream**

The exact figure needs a field the provider API does not return yet: their web client reads `credits.monthlyCreditsGranted`, and `/alpha/billing/credits` omits it, which is why the derivation above exists at all. Asked for on their tracker — CommandCodeAI/command-code#675 (a `monthlyCreditsGranted` field, or a `windowLimits.monthly` entry alongside `fiveHour` / `weekly`). If that lands, option 1 collapses to a straight `used / cap` read and the local plan table can be deleted.

Happy to leave the derivation out and mark this blocked upstream if you would rather not carry a plan table at all — the two names above are the only inputs it needs.

title: fix: stop refusing routed children on the OpenCode Go routes
body:
## What

Two measured refusals on the OpenCode Go routes, each fixed on the exact provider that proved it.

- **`opencode-go-responses`: a delegated child died on its first turn.** Console Go implements the public Responses input schema only. It answers ` ``input[N]` did not match any supported type ` for Codex's `agent_message` collaboration item and ` ` input[N].content` ... ` for the `encrypted_content` part inside it, so a Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor child was refused on its first turn while the very same route served its parent normally. `consoleGoResponsesInput` converts the handoff into the ordinary user message the endpoint accepts and carries a still-opaque value as visible text; it runs on the turn and on a delegated transcript's compaction.

- **`opencode-go` Chat: `access_programs` refused the whole request.** Codex sends that top-level field because the merged catalog publishes the model's `available_access_programs`; Console Go answers `invalid request body: json: unknown field "access_programs"` before inference. Measured on `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash` and `opencode-go/glm-5.3` as delegated children. The field is now dropped for that provider only -- the Responses variant accepted the identical field unchanged in the same session.

## Evidence

Reproduced and isolated on the local caller endpoint before the change:

| Shape | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `agent_message` whose visible text ends at `Payload:` | 400 `input[1]` | 200 |
| `agent_message` with no visible text | 400 `input[1]` | 200 |
| `agent_message` whose visible text does not end at `Payload:` | 400 `input[1]` | 200 |
| `access_programs` on `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash` | 400 `unknown field` | 200 |
| `access_programs` on `opencode-go-responses/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` | 200 (unchanged) | 200 |

End to end after the change, with the routes confirmed in the router meter (`isSubagent: true`) rather than in the child's own claim: a routed parent delegated to `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (max), `opencode-go-responses/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (xhigh) and `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash` (max), and each child returned its exact marker with status 200.

## Tests

- New route tests in `test/namespace-relay-routing.test.mjs`: `OpenCode Go Responses carries a delegated task as an ordinary user message` and `Console Go Chat drops the access_programs field its endpoint refuses`. The second also asserts that the Responses route keeps the field, so the gate stays exact.
- `node --test test/namespace-relay-routing.test.mjs` -> 35/35
- `node --test test/namespace-relay.test.mjs` -> 132/132
- `node --test test/routing.test.mjs test/router-resilience.test.mjs test/deepseek-tool-message-compat.test.mjs test/subagent-certify.test.mjs` -> 264/264
- `npm run check` -> v2-agent applications valid (7), syntax checks passed

## Limits

- Both new gates are exact to the provider that was measured. Paid Zen and other Responses providers keep their native contract until their own endpoint proves the same restriction.
- The five-check v2 certification still cannot complete under a ChatGPT account (the native parent is refused), so these routes stay promoted by operator selection. This PR does not change that.

title: fix(control-center): the macOS tray uses the 512px app icon instead of a menu-bar template image
body:
**What it looks like**

On macOS the Control Center's menu-bar icon renders as a full-colour rounded square with the logo glyph inside, rather than a menu-bar glyph. It reads as a shrunken app tile dropped into the status area: noticeably heavier and squarer than the neighbouring status items, and it does not invert with the menu bar the way native status items do.

Re-reading a screenshot at 4x: a white outlined glyph on a blue-grey rounded square.

**Cause**

`apps/control-center/electron/main.mjs:267` builds the tray from `appIconPath()`:

```js
const image = nativeImage.createFromPath(appIconPath());
if (image.isEmpty()) throw new Error(`The tray icon could not be loaded from ${appIconPath()}.`);
const createdTray = new Tray(image);
```

`appIconPath()` (`:99`) resolves to `path.join(process.resourcesPath, "icon.png")` when packaged — the same asset used for the Dock (`app.dock.setIcon`, `:105`) and the window (`:122`). On the affected install that packaged file is 512x512, full colour, alpha present; the in-repo source `apps/control-center/assets/icon.png` is the same 512x512 image.

No template image is set and there is no dedicated menu-bar asset. macOS status items expect a template image — monochrome, alpha-only, authored around 16-18pt — so a 512px colour app icon is scaled down into that slot instead of being drawn as one. Electron only auto-treats an image as a template when the filename ends in `Template`, which `icon.png` does not.

**Suggested fix**

Add a small monochrome menu-bar asset (roughly 18pt, so 36px at 2x — black glyph on transparency, no background) and mark it as a template:

```js
const trayIcon = nativeImage.createFromPath(menuBarIconPath());
trayIcon.setTemplateImage(true);
const createdTray = new Tray(trayIcon);
```

Leave `appIconPath()` as-is; it is correct for the Dock and window icons, and the custom-icon support on the Swift side (#307 / #308) is a separate surface.

**Environment**

- macOS, Codex Router 0.6.0, installed `Codex Router.app` matching the v0.6.0 checkout
- The Swift menu-bar companion is not built on this machine (full Xcode is required, per `src/macos-developer-tools.mjs`), so the Electron tray is the only status item — which is how this is normally seen

title: Strip Codex access_programs on routed requests
body:
Codex now sends `access_programs` (`{cyber: standard}`) on every `/v1/responses` request (`ResponsesApiRequest` in `codex-rs`, set via `cyber_access_program::for_auth`). OpenAI accepts it, but strict upstreams with exact JSON decoding reject the whole turn:

`HTTP 400: Error from provider (Console Go): Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] invalid request body: json: unknown field "access_programs"`

Reproduced live on `opencode-go/glm-5.3-flash` (chat-completions hop via LiteLLM); retry after this patch succeeds.

The router already drops `client_metadata` at every routed boundary for the same reason. This drops `access_programs` alongside it:

- `src/router.mjs` turn builder (`buildRoutedRequest`)
- `src/router.mjs` compaction body (`summarizeWith`)
- `src/api-forwarder.mjs` `normalizeBody` (last hop before upstream)
- `src/oauth-forwarder.mjs` `normalizeKimiBody`

Native OpenAI traffic keeps both fields.

Tests: extended `router preserves native auth and isolates every external route` (native keeps, routed drops) and `API forwarder strips web_search_options for OpenCode Go chat models` (upstream never sees it). `npm run check` passes; both named tests pass. Note: the full `API forwarder` file pattern needs a clean env in some sandboxes -- a leaked `MODEL_ROUTER_API_PORT` overrides the harness ports.

title: fix: make Console Go Muse routes usable in collaboration
body:
Two defects made the paid Console Go Muse Contributor routes unusable inside a
multi-agent session, one on each side of the relationship. Both were measured
against the live routes, and both are fixed here.

## Delegating to a Muse child

A delegated child on these routes died before its first token:

```
opencode rejected the request for Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (opencode Go).
(HTTP 400: {"model":"muse-spark-1.3-contributor","error":{"param":"input[5]",
"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"Error from provider (Console Go):
Upstream request failed: [invalid_request_error] `input[5]` did not match any
supported type"}})
```

Codex hands work to a child as an `agent_message` item. When the parent is
routed, the task text is stored as plaintext under `encrypted_content`;
`normalizeRoutedAgentInput` recovers it and replaces that part with `input_text`,
but the item keeps `type: "agent_message"`, which is a Codex collaboration item
and not part of the public Responses schema. Console Go rejects that item type by
name on these two upstreams -- a request whose only input item is an
`agent_message` answers 400 with exactly the message above, while message,
reasoning and function items are accepted.

The Zen free pair and the native DeepSeek route already convert the handoff to an
equivalent user message (`zenFreeCompatibleInput`, `deepSeekResponsesInput`).
`consoleGoCompatibleInput` does the same on the exact upstreams measured
rejecting it (`muse-spark-1.2-contributor`, `muse-spark-1.3-contributor` behind
`opencode-go-responses`), at both places that build that route's body: the routed
turn (`buildRoutedRequest`) and compaction (`summarizeWith`), so a child session
cannot pass its first turn and then die on its first summary.

Sibling Console Go routes are not silently affected: `opencode-go-responses/gpt-5.6-luna`
answers the same item with its own contract (`Missing required parameter:
'input[0].author'`), and `grok-oauth/grok-4.6` reaches its provider through
LiteLLM's Chat bridge, which normalizes the item. They keep the item unchanged.

## Collaboration calls made from a Muse parent

With Muse Spark 1.3 as the parent, every collaboration tool answered
`unsupported call: collaboration__spawn_agent`. The stream described the same
call two different ways:

```
response.output_item.added  -> { name: "spawn_agent",   namespace: "collaboration" }
response.output_item.done   -> { name: "collaboration__spawn_agent" }
```

Codex executes the terminal item, so the restored `added` event never helped.
`normalizeResponsesEvent` restored the namespace only for
`response.output_item.added`; the `done` item and the `response.completed`
snapshot were forwarded exactly as the provider wrote them.

Both places now restore the same call, which also keeps the three descriptions of
one call in agreement on any Responses route that relays flattened names.

## Validation

- New test in `test/namespace-relay-routing.test.mjs`: the handoff reaches both
  Muse Contributor routes as a user message carrying the recovered task text,
  while a sibling Console Go route keeps the item it was written for. With
  `src/router.mjs` reverted the test fails; with the fix it passes.
- New test in `test/qwen-plan-namespace-restoration.test.mjs`: the terminal item
  and the completion snapshot come back namespaced. With `src/openai-adapters.mjs`
  reverted the test fails; with the fix it passes.
- `npm run check`.
- Affected suites green: `openai-adapters`, `qwen-plan-namespace-restoration`,
  `namespace-relay`, `namespace-relay-custom`, `namespace-relay-routing`,
  `commandcode-forwarder` and `grok-oauth-forwarder` (270 tests together).
- A full local `npm test` has three failures -- `test/desktop-panel.test.mjs`,
  "real Codex app-server completes signed-out turns through fallback and
  preserved providers" and "retry policy is bounded by one operation deadline and
  cancellation". They reproduce unchanged on `main` without these commits
  (checked in a clean worktree at c6f58a3), so they are environmental rather than
  caused by this change.
- Delegation on a running router: a routed parent delegated to Muse Spark 1.3
  children through the `general-worker` and `code-mapper` presets. One returned
  its marker, the other ran a shell command and reported its output; the route
  metered 200 for both.
- Wire check on the same router: a forced `collaboration__spawn_agent` call on
  `opencode-go-responses/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` now returns
  `{ name: "spawn_agent", namespace: "collaboration" }` in `added`, `done` and
  `completed.output`. Before the change `done` carried the flattened name, which
  is what Codex reported as `unsupported call`.
- Not verified here: a real Codex app session with a Muse parent running a
  collaboration tool end to end. The wire shapes above are what the app reads, so
  that step is a retest in the app rather than more code.

title: feat(providers) Multi-account not just ChatGPT
body: Would love a feature where we can add in multiple API keys and manage multiple accounts for the other providers, like I have multiple accounts with Opencode Go

title: feat: advertise code mode on every routed model
body:
Codex decides whether a model runs in code mode from that model's catalog entry.
`tool_mode: "code_mode_only"` is what gives the model the freeform `exec` custom
tool -- raw JavaScript, executed by `codex-code-mode-host`, whose calls arrive as
`custom_tool_call` items carrying the source in `input`. Every native entry that
has it (`gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-6-astra`,
`gpt-reserve`, the daybreak pair and `codex-auto-review`) also carries
`use_responses_lite`.

The router built every routed entry with `delete next.tool_mode`, so none of the
48 merged entries for routed providers advertised a tool mode, and no routed
model could use code mode at all.

## The relay can already carry it

Measured against a running router, sending
`{"type":"custom","name":"exec","description":"...","format":{"type":"text"}}`:

- `opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash` (Chat through LiteLLM) returns
  `custom_tool_call exec` with the JavaScript source.
- `opencode-go-messages/minimax-m3` and `opencode-go-messages/qwen3.8-max`
  (Messages API) do the same.
- `opencode-go-responses/muse-spark-1.3-contributor` (Console Go Responses,
  where `bridgeCustomTools` runs with `bridgeAll`) does the same: the custom
  tool is bridged for the upstream and the model's call is restored.
- `grok-oauth/grok-4.6` (xAI forwarder) accepts the custom tool directly and
  returns the same shape.
- A `custom_tool_call` + `custom_tool_call_output` history round-trips with HTTP
  200 on both the Chat and the Console Go Responses routes, and the model answers
  from the tool result.

## Fix

Routed entries now set `tool_mode: "code_mode_only"` explicitly instead of
dropping the field or inheriting a template's value. Keeping it out of the native
template path means a template change cannot move a routed route's tool mode.

`use_responses_lite` intentionally stays `false` for routed entries: it is the
internal `x-openai-internal-codex-responses-lite` transport, which the router
strips. If the app turns out to require that transport in addition to the switch,
it is the next lever, and this PR is the place to say so.

## Validation

- `test/catalog.test.mjs`: the three assertions that encoded "a routed entry
  never carries the native tool mode" now assert that code mode is advertised,
  and a new test pins that a template omitting the switch cannot suppress it.
  74/74 pass.
- `npm run check` passes.
- A full local `npm test` still shows only the three environmental failures that
  also fail on `main` without this commit (`test/desktop-panel.test.mjs`,
  "real Codex app-server completes signed-out turns through fallback and
  preserved providers", "retry policy is bounded by one operation deadline and
  cancellation"); everything else passes.
- Not verified here: that the Codex UI offers code mode for a routed model. That
  needs the app to reload this catalog and a routed session to try it, which is
  the retest this PR is waiting on.

title: fix: allow failover between separate OpenCode quota scopes
body:
`canonicalProviderId()` folds OpenCode Zen into Go through `variantOf`, which is correct for shared credential/selection ownership but too broad for quota failover: Go and Zen use separately billed endpoints with independent exhaustion.

Cooldown accounting already represents that distinction through `cooldownScope()`:

* Go Chat/Messages/Responses → `opencode-go`
* Zen Chat/Messages/Responses → `opencode-zen`

Use that same scope identity when excluding ordinary failover candidates.

This keeps protocol siblings within each quota scope excluded while allowing Go ↔ Zen failover when the other separately billed scope is still usable. Already-cooled scopes remain excluded, and compact-overflow same-family behavior is unchanged.

### Regression coverage

The new `rankFailoverCandidates offers separately billed Zen after Go exhaustion` test verifies both directions and confirms same-scope siblings remain excluded.

The regression fails on clean `origin/main` and passes with this change.

### Verification

* failover unit + router: 92/92
* cooldown + selection + routing: 163/163
* `npm run check`: pass
* `git diff --check`: clean

title: feat(doctor): warn when a listed route disappears from its provider catalog
body:
Provider discovery already records models that disappear from a provider's authoritative catalog, but that signal is currently only used for reporting. A statically listed route can therefore remain selectable after the provider withdraws the model and fail deterministically at runtime.

This adds a warn-only doctor check for listed routes that are positively absent from a fresh successful provider catalog.

The check intentionally fails open:

* stale/missing discovery does not warn
* failed/unreachable discovery does not warn
* empty discovery does not warn
* local-only routes are ignored
* no models are hidden or removed
* no user configuration is modified
* the warning disappears if the provider advertises the model again

Availability resolves per provider with a same-endpoint `variantOf` fallback, so a local override serving a known endpoint under its own id is still judged by the endpoint owner's list — without ever crossing to an unrelated provider's catalog.

Observed locally with a withdrawn OpenRouter route; tests use synthetic catalog data and contain no model-specific hardcoding.

### Verification

* new `withdrawn-listed-routes` tests: 7/7
* doctor + catalog-cache suites: 21/21
* registry: 42/42
* `npm run check`: pass
* `git diff --check`: clean

title: Fix open issues: Copilot stream ids (#814), Kimi region + multi_agent_v2 (#819), DeepSeek replay (#809), macOS tray (#829), Usage page (#824-#827)
body:
## Summary

Fixes for the reproducible open issues in one batch (each commit is scoped to one issue and independently revertable).

**#814 – Copilot Responses stream fails when response IDs change.** Copilot mints a fresh `response.id` on `response.created` / `response.in_progress` / `response.completed`, so the generic validator emitted `invalid_responses_stream` after text had already streamed. The stream transform now takes an opt-in `pinResponseId`:

```js
createResponsesStreamTransform(flatToNative, { pinResponseId: provider.authProfile === "github-copilot" })
// pinned route: later lifecycle events get response.id = <id from response.created>
// every other route: a completion under a different id is still a corrupt stream
```

A second `response.created` with a different id is still rejected on every route.

**#819 – Kimi region + `multi_agent_v2` collision.** `kimi login` now honours the official CLI's `~/.kimi` region (`kimi.com` mainland vs `kimi.ai` global, snake_case keys `base_url`/`oauth_host`) across OAuth, forwarder, usage, and setup (`src/kimi-region.mjs`), with separate credential slots per region. The managed `multi_agent_v2` block is skipped when the user's `config.toml` already owns that table or a dotted `multi_agent_v2.*` key, instead of writing a duplicate TOML key.

**#809 – DeepSeek stateless tool-result replay.** `requiresReasoningContentOnToolCalls(model)` is true only for DeepSeek-thinking / DeepSeek-family / `commandcode` → `deepseek-v4-flash` routes; on those, assistant `tool_calls` messages replayed without reasoning get `reasoning_content: ""` so upstream stops rejecting the replay. Existing reasoning is preserved.

**#829 – macOS Electron tray icon.** Tray uses a new monochrome `trayTemplate.png` / `@2x` (18/36px, generated from `RouterMark.svg` by `scripts/build-app-icon.sh`) with `setTemplateImage(true)`; Dock/BrowserWindow keep `appIconPath()`. Assets are packaged via `extraResources` and fingerprinted in `install-plan.mjs`.

**#824 / #825 / #826 – Usage page.** Selected source gets a `Selected · <name>` group and badge, other accounts move under "Other connected accounts" (still visible for comparison). Source names are 12.5px/650. Cached input shows `count (hit%)` when telemetry exists; `provider-usage.mjs` now tracks `cacheTelemetrySeen` per provider so a provider that never reported cache tokens shows "hit rate not reported" instead of `0%`.

**#827 – Command Code monthly window.** `commandCodeCreditsMetrics(payload, { summary, subscription })` derives `Monthly limit = credits.monthlyCredits (remaining) + summary.totalMonthlyCredits (used)`, reset at `subscription.currentPeriodEnd`. The two extra reads are optional (failure keeps the balance/5h/weekly cards); missing/invalid data, zero total, or `past_due` omit the card rather than show a guessed percentage.

Closes #814, closes #819, closes #809, closes #829, closes #824, closes #825, closes #826, closes #827.

Verification: `npm run check`, `npm test` (4361 tests, 0 fail), `apps/control-center npm test` (100 pass), `git diff --check`.

title: [Bug]: Generic-provider Responses stream ends with LiteLLM "in-stream error" frame instead of response.completed (codex 0.155-alpha reports stream disconnected)
body:
### What happened?

Streaming a **generic provider** (`providers generic add … --adapter openai-responses`, upstream = local Responses-API server) through the router: content is fully delivered, then the SSE stream codex receives ends with a LiteLLM error frame instead of a terminal `response.completed`:

```text
data: {"type": "response.output_item.done", ...}
data: {"type": "error", "message": "litellm.APIError: Response API in-stream error", "type": null, "param": null, "code": "500"}
```

codex **0.155.0-alpha.9** (ChatGPT.app bundled) treats this as a failed turn:

```text
ERROR: stream disconnected before completion: stream closed before response.completed
```

and retries, even though the full answer was already received. codex **0.153.4** (CLI) tolerates the trailing frame and is unaffected. Content always arrives; only the stream termination is wrong.

### Environment

- macOS (Apple Silicon), desktop app (ChatGPT.app bundled codex `0.155.0-alpha.9`), CLI `codex-cli 0.153.4`
- codex-router: main @ `5e1b49e6`
- LiteLLM: `1.96.0`
- Provider: generic, `--adapter openai-responses`, base-url `http://127.0.0.1:4319/v1` (local [jev-codex-router](https://github.com/0xNatoshi/jev-codex-router) server)
- Model: `jev/auto` (gateway model `jev-auto`)

### Reproduction (fully local, no external credentials)

```bash
curl -N http://127.0.0.1:4202/v1/responses \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $CALLER_SECRET" \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"jev/auto","input":"Reply with exactly OK","max_output_tokens":400,"stream":true}'
```

**Upstream side (captured at the generic provider's base-url, same request):** clean, properly framed SSE — `event: response.created` … `event: response.completed` + `data: [DONE]`, no error events.

**Router side (what codex receives):** data-only frames (no `event:` lines), ending `…output_item.done` → `data: {"type": "error","message": "litellm.APIError: Response API in-stream error", "code": "500"}`, no `response.completed`.

So the error frame is born inside the router's LiteLLM relay, not by the upstream.

### Where it raises

Router log:

```text
litellm/responses/streaming_iterator.py: _maybe_raise_for_error_event
→ litellm.MidStreamFallbackError: litellm.APIError: Response API in-stream error
  (Model Group=jev-auto, Available Model Group Fallbacks=None)
→ proxy async_data_generator emits {"type":"error", "code":"500"} to the client
```

### Possibly related

- #814 (Copilot Responses stream fails when response IDs change) — same symptom family, same LiteLLM `1.96.0`. In my capture the router-relayed stream also carries **different response ids** between `created` and the final events (the caller edge re-wraps responses), which matches that hypothesis.
- Setting `general_settings.disable_responses_id_security: true` does **not** change this.

### Workarounds attempted (no fix)

1. Making the upstream emit perfectly framed SSE (event lines + real `response.completed` + `[DONE]`) — direct-to-upstream capture is clean; router path still appends the error frame.
2. `disable_responses_id_security: true` in litellm.yaml — no effect.
3. Replacing the trailing error event at the upstream with a synthesized `response.completed` — error frame still generated by the relay.

### Suggested directions

- Ensure the LiteLLM Responses relay terminates client streams with a proper `response.completed` (synthesized from the last response snapshot if the upstream ended without one), and never appends an error frame after output has been delivered.
- Or route generic providers through the same dedicated-forwarder rail the built-in providers use, bypassing the LiteLLM Responses relay.

Happy to attach full SSE captures from both sides if useful.

title: Shorten and sharpen the router skill descriptions
body:
# Shorten and sharpen the router skill descriptions

Skill descriptions are loaded into context before a skill is used, so an
over-long `description:` is not free: it gets truncated in the listing, and it
makes the skill match far more often than it should. The old `codex-router`
text was the worst case, because one of its triggers was "a tool result just
arrived and more work remains" -- which is true at nearly every step of nearly
every task, so the skill fired constantly. This change trims all five
descriptions down to the identifying sentence plus a plain "use when" clause.

## codex-router

Before:

> Orientation for custom (non-OpenAI) models running in the Codex app through the codex-router proxy. Explains that the app's native tools arrive as flattened codex_app__ and mcp__ names, that the router restores them so the app executes them, which companion skills to read before threads, browser, or computer-use work, and that a turn with no tool call ends the task. Use when the session uses a custom (non-OpenAI) model, for example deepseek-v4-flash or mimo-v2.5, when codex_app__ or mcp__ tool names appear in the tool list, when a tool result just arrived and more work remains, or when thread, browser, or computer-use work is requested.

After:

> "Orientation for custom (non-OpenAI) models in the Codex app: how codex-router exposes the app's native tools, and which companion skill to read for thread, browser, or computer-use work."

## codex-app-threads

Before:

> Create, list, read, message, wait on, fork, rename, archive, and pin Codex threads (sidebar tasks), plus automations and app navigation, using the app-native codex_app tools. Use when the session uses a custom (non-OpenAI) model, for example deepseek-v4-flash or mimo-v2.5, and the user asks to create a thread or a new task or agent, list or read threads, send a message to a thread, wait for a thread, fork or rename a thread, archive or pin a thread, set up an automation or reminder, or open something in the Codex app.

After:

> Use the app-native codex_app tools to create, read, message, wait on, fork, rename, archive, and pin Codex threads and automations. Use when the user asks to manage Codex tasks.

## codex-in-app-browser

Before:

> Drive the Codex in-app browser (open, navigate, click, type, screenshot, read page state) through the app's own node_repl runtime. Use when the session uses a custom (non-OpenAI) model, for example deepseek-v4-flash or mimo-v2.5, and the user asks to use the in-app browser, open or navigate a page in it, test a local app in a browser, or click, type, or take a screenshot in the Codex browser panel.

After:

> "Drive the Codex in-app browser: open, navigate, click, type, screenshot, and read page state. Use when the task needs the app's browser, such as testing a local page."

## codex-computer-use

Before:

> Control local apps through Computer Use (the @oai/sky runtime) inside the Codex app. Use when the session uses a custom (non-OpenAI) model, for example deepseek-v4-flash or mimo-v2.5, and the user asks to control the computer, operate a desktop app's UI, use Safari or Chrome through computer use, click or type in an app, or take a screenshot of an app. Prefer purpose-built connectors, APIs, or CLIs when they exist.

After:

> Control local apps through the Codex app's Computer Use runtime. Use when the user asks to operate a desktop app or take a screenshot; prefer a purpose-built API or CLI when one exists.

## codex-router-media

Before:

> Generate video, music, speech, or images with the operator's MiniMax Token Plan subscription through the codex-router media CLI. Use when the session runs a MiniMax custom (non-OpenAI) model (for example minimax-m3) with the MiniMax Token Plan provider connected, and the user explicitly asks to create a video, a song or music track, spoken audio, or an image. Do not use for reading or analyzing existing media.

After:

> Generate images, video, music, or speech with the codex-router media CLI (MiniMax Token Plan). Use only when the user explicitly asks to create media; not for reading or editing existing media.

title: [Bug]: Native Responses reasoning is rewritten as visible assistant text on generic provider routes
body:
## What happened?

Generic provider routes configured with the `openai-responses` adapter rewrite replayed reasoning history as visible assistant text.

The production symptom was observed with GLM-5.3 through an OmniRoute route: previous progress or placeholder text was repeated after subsequent turns. OmniRoute is only the observed route; this report is intentionally provider-independent and does not claim OmniRoute itself is unsupported.

The router is `codex-router` main at `5e1b49e6e3fea1ada57f0e7fa6ca7612e9d17300`.

## Expected behavior

A native Responses route should preserve replayed input semantics. Reasoning items should remain reasoning items and should not be copied into visible assistant `output_text`.

## Actual behavior

In `src/router.mjs`, the request builder still calls `carryReasoningThroughInput()` for `openai-responses` providers. The Chat-Completions adaptation flags are all false on that path, but the helper is not a no-op:

- reasoning followed by a tool call can become a synthetic assistant `output_text` item;
- reasoning followed by an assistant answer can remain in the reasoning item and also be prepended to visible assistant text.

That can cause a thinking model to replay the same progress/placeholder text and loop.

## Reproduction

This is credential-free and does not require OmniRoute or a private endpoint. I executed the current helper in memory with sanitized input:

1. Create input containing a reasoning item with text `prior reasoning summary unavailable` followed by an assistant message and a user turn.
2. Route it through the generic `openai-responses` path.
3. Inspect the outbound input.

Observed result: the original reasoning item remains, and the same text is also inserted as assistant `output_text`. This is a helper-level reproduction; no credentials or live provider request are required.

The existing generic routing test covers Codex `phase` removal but does not cover reasoning replay.

## Scope and suggested direction

This appears to be a protocol-boundary bug: Chat-Completions reasoning carry is being applied to a native Responses route. A minimal fix candidate is to restrict that carry step to Chat-Completions routes while preserving the dedicated DeepSeek Responses path.

Please add regression coverage for:

- generic Responses reasoning followed by prose;
- generic Responses reasoning followed by a tool call;
- consecutive and trailing reasoning items;
- existing Chat behavior, native DeepSeek normalization, Console Go tool adaptation, and fallback/rebuild history.

The GLM/OmniRoute loop is the motivating observation, not proof that this mutation is the only provider-side cause.

## Related work

- [Issue #755](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/issues/755) and [PR #768](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/pull/768) address reasoning replay on Chat-Completions routes.
- [PR #315](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/pull/315) addresses direct Z.AI GLM reasoning/tool turns.
- [Issue #837](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/issues/837) concerns generic Responses stream termination, which is a different symptom.
- [Issue #539](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/issues/539) documents generic provider support.

## Harness and platform

- App: Codex
- Platform: macOS

No API keys, OAuth files, private base URLs, full prompts, or unredacted logs are included.
