title: fix: name the client a failed publication left behind
body:
## Summary

When a client publication fails, `runTargetPublicationProcess` threw the publisher's raw stderr as its own message. That made the error unreadable in four ways:

- A publisher dies on an uncaught error, so its stderr is a Node crash banner.
- When publication runs from `bin/control` (every Control Center picker toggle), the control process crashes too and wraps that banner in a second one.
- Nothing named the client that failed.
- The Control Center's `safeFailure` drops every line matching `SECRET_WORD` (`credential`, `secret`, …). Whenever the cause mentioned a credential, it removed the one line that explained the failure, leaving file paths and stack frames.

This is what a user saw when the DeepSeek Harness publisher refused its credentials document (see #968):

```
Error invoking remote method 'router-control:setPickerModel': Error: file:///…/src/target-integration.mjs:93 throw new Error(result.stderr.trim() || `Client publication exited with status ${result.status}.`); ^ at runTargetPublicationProcess …
```

Changes in `src/target-integration.mjs`:

- `runTargetPublicationProcess` takes a `client` option. Each of its seven call sites passes its picker name (`PICKER_NAMES.*`, or the routed harness's `displayName`).
- The new exported `publicationFailure(client, result)` builds the message:
  1. `<Client> was not updated.` on its own line.
  2. Then the innermost thrown message in the publisher's stderr: the last `…Error: …` line that isn't a nested banner's `file://` header.
  3. If there is none, the trimmed stderr; if that's empty, the exit status.
- The client line deliberately carries no detail, so it survives `safeFailure`'s line filter. I left that filter alone.

## Verification

New tests in `test/target-integration.test.mjs`. All three fail on `main` and pass with this change; the file is 17/17.

- A nested two-banner stderr reduces to `DeepSeek Harness was not updated.\n<refusal>`.
- Stderr with no thrown error falls back to its own text, and empty stderr falls back to the exit status.
- Passed through the Control Center's real `safeFailure`, the message keeps `DeepSeek Harness was not updated.` when the cause mentions a credential, and appends the cause when it doesn't.

Commands:

- `npm run check`: passed
- `npm test`: 4,714 passed, 33 skipped, 2 failed. The two failures are the same `test/login-free-app-server.test.mjs` failures that an untouched `origin/main` shows on this machine (real Codex CLI 0.160.0).

End to end on macOS, on an install at `bb0cc4a2` with this patch: `MODEL_ROUTER_DSH_CREDENTIALS=<file with a nested mapping> ./bin/control picker set <visible model> show` exits 1 with

```
Error: DeepSeek Harness was not updated.
Refusing to edit the harness credentials document: "server" holds a nested mapping, so this file is not a credential reference document.
```

and the Control Center's `safeFailure` turns that stderr into `DeepSeek Harness was not updated.` With the old relay, the same failure produced a fragment of the crash banner's source line.

## Changelog

`changelog.d/publication-error-client.md`

### Update after an independent QA review (commit `f4e2108`)

QA found two problems:

- Every publisher already catches its own error and prints only the message, so pulling an `Error:` line out of stderr rarely applied. Where it did apply, it dropped a wrapper's context (for example OpenClaw's `config command failed:`) and every line after the first.
- The message implied later clients were fine, even though publication stops at the first failure.

Changes:

- The publisher's stderr is relayed unchanged under the first line.
- The first line is now `<Client> was not updated, and any client after it was skipped.` It still contains none of the words the Control Center's filter drops.
- A publisher killed by a signal now reports `The publisher was stopped by SIGTERM.` instead of `exited with status null`.

Results:

- The tests are rewritten around what publishers actually print. All three fail against untouched `main`, and the file is 17/17 with the change.
- `npm test`: 4,714 passed, 33 skipped. The only failures are the same 2 pre-existing ones.

title: feat(tray): open the Control Center on its Settings page from Settings…
body:
## Summary

**This builds on #965.** The first commit is #965's; please review only the second, `f3dab6b`. Once #965 merges, only that commit remains.

With #965, **Settings…** (⌘,) opens the Control Center, but on its default or last page. This PR adds `settings` as a fixed navigation destination, and the Settings item requests it.

**Swift (tray):**
- Adds `ControlCenterDestination.settings` and `ControlCenterNavigationRequest(destination:)`. Only the Settings item uses them.
- `init?(url:)` is unchanged. It's the parser for widget and other external `codex-router://` URLs, and it still refuses `/settings`; its existing negative case stays.

**Control Center:**
- `settings` joins `NAVIGATION_DESTINATIONS`. A cold start gets it via `--router-destination`, a warm start via the URL the tray hands it.
- `controlCenterNavigationURL` now checks the path against that same list.
- The renderer routes the destination to the Settings view, and both `onNavigation` type unions gain it.
- The Control Center registers no URL scheme, so only the tray ever hands it such a URL.

**Tests:**
- The closed-set tests keep negative examples (`models`, `settings/`), and `settings` becomes a positive case.
- A new Swift test checks the Settings item's request, and that the external parser still refuses the URL that request produces.
- The production-renderer test now navigates to `settings` and waits for the Settings heading.

**Policy note:** this widens the Control Center's own allow-list by one parameterless page. The externally reachable surface (the tray's URL parser) is unchanged. If you'd rather keep the Control Center widget-only, #965 stands on its own.

## Verification

Fail without / pass with: with `navigation.mjs` and `App.tsx` reverted, both navigation tests in `test/control-center-electron.test.mjs` fail, and the production-renderer test times out waiting for the Settings heading. With the change, all pass.

Commands:

- `swift test --package-path apps/macos/ModelRouterTray`: 141 tests passed, including the new one; the release build is clean.
- In `apps/control-center`: `npm run check` passed; `npm test` gave 117 passed and 1 skipped (the Windows-only Job containment test).
- Root `npm run check`: passed.

Packaged run on macOS 26.6.2: tray and Control Center rebuilt with `bin/model-router-tray --preserve-window` on an install at `bb0cc4a2` with this change.

- After the fresh launch, no Settings window exists. That's #965.

QA found two gaps:

title: fix: process Ollama pull records that end at EOF
body:
## Summary

`streamOllamaPull` leaves a final record in its buffer when the daemon or a proxy omits the trailing newline. A final `{"status":"success"}` then reports an interrupted download, while an error after an earlier success can be missed.

Flush the UTF-8 decoder and process the remaining record at EOF. Truncated records still cannot confirm success. Both Local LLM and vision downloads use this helper.

## Verification

title: fix: fold sparse native output indices without array scans
body:
## Summary

A buffered native response with `output_index: 4294967296` loses the item because it becomes an array property. An index of `4294967294` instead creates an enormous sparse array whose final `filter()` can block the router.

Collect received items in a `Map`, then order them by index. Preserve replacement, unindexed append, and terminal snapshot behavior. Reject malformed indices with a 502 upstream error.

Chat-wire replay reads only a singular search query. A stored `action.queries` batch, `open_page`, or `find_in_page` therefore becomes an empty search marker, discarding what the previous turn actually did.

title: fix: preserve media output when a download is interrupted
body:
## Summary

MiniMax downloads currently write directly to `--out`. A connection failure truncates an existing image, audio track, or video and leaves a partial file at the requested path.

title: fix: avoid lossy JSON rewrites during cache usage normalization
body:
## Summary

The cache-usage compatibility pass serializes the entire upstream payload. Adding a cache alias can therefore round unrelated large numbers, collapse duplicate keys, or replace malformed UTF-8 in content.

Reuse the existing exact JSON guard and validate UTF-8 before rewriting. Unsafe lines retain their original bytes; ordinary cache aliases and choice-bearing usage normalization still work for Z.ai, OpenCode Go, and OpenRouter.

## Verification

title: Integration: Codex Router & AIML API
body:
Hi! I'm Hugo from aimlapi.com — an AI aggregator that gives access to 1000+ models in one API, trusted by 400k+ users.

We'd love to be available as a verified provider option inside Codex Router — so we went ahead and did all the technical work on our side.

To build our partnership, we offer a 50/50 revenue share on all traffic from this integration. (P.S.: tracking starts as soon as this release goes live, so no earnings will be lost during setup)

My contacts: hugo@aimlapi.com (email / Slack), Telegram: @hug0the

## Summary

Adds AI/ML API (`aimlapi`) as an OpenAI-compatible API-key provider. Before this, the registry had no AI/ML API provider.

- `config/aimlapi/aimlapi.json`: provider descriptor. Base URL `https://api.aimlapi.com/v1` (override: `AIMLAPI_API_BASE_URL`), key from `AIMLAPI_API_KEY`, `aimlapi-api-key.secret` or keychain service `codex-router-aimlapi`. Credentials, discovery, the catalog, tray onboarding (`add-key`) and `install.sh --providers aimlapi` read it from the registry, so they need no provider-specific code.
- 12 model routes in `config/aimlapi/`: GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6 Sol, GPT-6 Luna, Claude Opus 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5.5, Claude Sonnet 5, Gemini 3.8 Flash, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, GLM 5.2, Kimi K3, Grok 4.7, Qwen3.7 Max. Reasoning levels and input modalities were measured against the gateway (GLM 5.2, Grok 4.7 and Qwen3.7 Max are declared text-only). Priorities are 72–83, the same range where most OpenRouter and Nous Research routes already sit. No route claims `multiAgentVersion: "v2"`.
- `src/aimlapi-attribution.mjs`: attribution headers (`X-AIMLAPI-Source: agent/codex-router`, `X-AIMLAPI-Partner-ID`, `HTTP-Referer`, `X-Title`), added in `upstreamHeaders()` in `api-forwarder.mjs` and in model discovery. They are keyed on the resolved destination host (exact match on `api.aimlapi.com`), not on the provider id. If `AIMLAPI_API_BASE_URL` points somewhere else, nothing is attached, and no other host (including `api.aimlapi.com.example.net`) receives them.
- `src/provider-account-usage.mjs`: `provider-usage` for `aimlapi` reads `GET /v1/key`. A key with a spend limit gets a "Monthly spend" quota card. A key without one shows the month-to-date spend as a message. A disabled key is reported as disabled. The key is only sent there when the base URL's origin is exactly `https://api.aimlapi.com`.
- Tray: `aimlapi.svg` icon (source in `PROVIDER-ICON-SOURCES.md`) and the "AI/ML API" label in `IslandOverlay.swift` and `ModelRouterTrayApp.swift`.
- README and docs-site provider tables, plus `AIMLAPI_API_KEY` in the model-discovery workflow.
- Tests: new `test/aimlapi-attribution.test.mjs` with 6 tests. They cover the exact host match, the shipped provider being attributed, attribution following the destination rather than the provider id, no other registry provider resolving onto the gateway, the fixed header set, and a real forwarder process. That process routes `aimlapi-gpt-6-sol` to a local upstream as `openai/gpt-6-sol` with the AI/ML API key, and no attribution header leaks to it. Provider counts in `provider-catalogs.test.mjs` and listed slugs in `registry.test.mjs` are updated.

## Verification

- `npm run check`: v2-agent applications valid (7), changelog fragments valid (46), syntax checks passed.
- `npm test` on top of current `main`: 4804 tests, 4762 pass, 36 skipped. The other 6 (in `antigravity-cli-onboarding`, `desktop-panel`, `empty-completion-router`, `model-router-cli`, `setup-node-deps` and `skills-install`) fail the same way on unmodified `main` in the same Linux container, so they come from the environment, not from this change.
- Live, with an AI/ML API key (run on our fork with the same AI/ML API code): a real forwarder process routed `aimlapi-gpt-6-luna`, `aimlapi-claude-sonnet-5`, `aimlapi-gpt-6-1-sol` and `aimlapi-claude-sonnet-5-5` to the gateway and got answers. The outgoing request carries `X-AIMLAPI-Partner-ID`.

## Changelog

`changelog.d/aimlapi-provider.md`

Updates `smol-toml` from 1.8.0 to 1.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from smol-toml's releases.

v1.9.0

Huge update!!! This is most likely the largest update the library received since its release, with lots of new features and improvements.

Performance improvements

Significant parts of the internal parse logic have been rewritten, improving performance by 1.5x-2x. The library was already comfortably ahead of the others, but it is now faster than ever, sitting at 4x faster parse performance than the closest maintained implementation.

Problematic code paths have also been replaced by safer implementations, solving potential DoS vectors. See GHSA-r4xh-jqrq-34v2.

Note: the objects returned by the library now have a null prototype. This is a transparent change for 99.9% of users, and is one of the most significant contributors to the major performance gains in this version.

Full Temporal support

Version 1.8.0 brought support for Temporal in stringify; now the library is also able to emit Temporal objects instead of its own ad-hoc TomlDate object. It is not enabled by default, but it will become the default in v2. Enable by setting useLegacyDate: false in the parser's options.

Better Temporal support in stringify

Temporal support has been improved since it released: Temporal objects that cannot be represented (such as Temporal.PlainMonthDay) now throw an error (instead of silently emitting a bogus object).

A new option has been added to stringify to disallow Temporal objects that cannot be fully represented in TOML. This includes ZonedDateTime objects with a IANA timezone attached instead of a plain offset, and dates with a specific calendar value set. Enable by setting strictTemporal: true in the options.

Handling of unsafe keys

Since its release the library has been protected against prototype pollution attacks, setting properties like __proto__ using safe mechanisms that do not trigger prototype pollution. However, while the returned objects are safe on their own, they may become problematic if used carelessly.

Inspired by secure-json-parse, the library now offers a way to either drop unsafe properties from the returned object, or to throw an error and reject documents altogether. By default, these potentially unsafe keys are preserved and returned.

Miscellaneous updates

  • Unicode BOM is now gracefully accepted and ignored.
  • Table array headers are now properly checked again. Reported in #65.
  • Closed certain gaps where invalid whitespace would be accepted. Reported in #61.
  • Bogus local date and local time values with a UTC offset are no longer accepted.
  • Certain error messages are more accurate and handle errors at line boundaries better.
  • The default export of the lib is now formally deprecated; use a import * instead. Proposed in #50.
  • On Node 20+, strings that contain lone surrogates are now normalised to well-formed strings.
  • On Node 20+, keys that contain lone surrogates are now rejected.

Full Changelog: https://github.com/squirrelchat/smol-toml/compare/v1.8.0...v1.9.0

title: feat(transport): upstream Responses WebSocket client and pooled provider transport
body:
Split out of #967 per review: this is the transport layer (shared codec + upstream client + pooled provider transport + native opt-in). The edge relay that forwards incremental turns end to end stays in #967, stacked on this PR.

## What

- **`src/ws-frames.mjs`** — the RFC 6455 codec both directions of the Responses WebSocket protocol share, extracted from the edge's server side, plus the masked client mirror and a direction-parameterized frame parser.
- **`src/responses-ws-client.mjs`** — the client half of `responses_websockets=2026-02-06`, hand-rolled over `node:net`/`node:tls`. Undici's WebSocket cannot send client pings (a silent reasoning turn would be idle-killed between us and the provider) and reports a refused upgrade as a bare 1006 with no status or `OpenAI-Beta` header — the exact signals the fallback needs. `collectResponsesRequest` drives one `response.create` and resolves with a fetch-`Response`-shaped result whose body is SSE synthesized from frames, so the downstream pipeline consumes a WebSocket turn unchanged.
- **Provider transport flag** — generic providers can declare `transport: "websocket"` (requires `openai-responses`; validated in the schema, editable via `providers generic add|edit --transport`). Turns bypass LiteLLM (same shape as the DeepSeek Responses bypass) and terminate at the api-forwarder, which leases a pooled connection per provider — one in-flight turn per connection, since the protocol has no multiplexing. Confinement is unchanged: the ws(s) target is pinned to the configured origin and path, DNS is re-validated per connection, only the bound credential rides the handshake.
- **Native opt-in** — `MODEL_ROUTER_NATIVE_TRANSPORT`/`CODEX_ROUTER_NATIVE_TRANSPORT=websocket` (default `http`): the ChatGPT backend answers the upgrade route with a 401 today, and the native-retry contract tests model that HTTP-only upstream request-for-request.

## Failure semantics

Anything before the frame is sent — refused upgrade, unreachable host, full pool, in-effect proxy (the socket has no EnvHttpProxyAgent beneath it) — falls back to the HTTP path with a per-provider circuit breaker, so a provider without the protocol costs one handshake per window, not a turn. After the send, failures surface as errors and are never silently retried.

## Tests

`test/responses-ws-client.test.mjs` (handshake/beta contract, masked frames, idle pings + pong echo, SSE synthesis, error frames → non-ok responses, 426 fallback, mid-stream death errors the body, prelude timeout, abort, rate-limit header reconstruction, transport gates) and `test/generic-ws-routing.test.mjs` (real forwarder vs fake provider: pooled reuse across turns, credential/static-header confinement, HTTP fallback on refused upgrade). Verified manually against a live deployment speaking the protocol.

title: fix: ignore released lock heartbeat callbacks
body:
Releasing a router lock can crash the process when an already-dispatched heartbeat stat returns after unlock. proper-lockfile 4.1.2 also lets a cached old stat start a write against a reacquired lock directory.

Route all nine lock consumers through a shared public-fs adapter that stops delivering that lease's stat callbacks as soon as its official release begins. Release remains immediate; active compromise handlers, acquisition/retry/stale behavior, and official release errors remain intact. Cleanup preserves the original mutation error and surfaces genuine unlock failures.

Verification: 267 focused tests passed, one existing Windows-only test skipped locally; repository checks and whitespace checks passed. Actual unmodified dependency controls reproduce the crash and cached-stat writes. Regressions cover 2-second and 5-second lease reacquisition, reentrant callbacks, active compromise, concurrent release, real filesystem unlock failures, all nine consumers, and setup without dependencies. Native platform and complete-suite CI must pass before merge.

This fixes callbacks arriving after intentional release. Already-dispatched writes and theft of an unreleased stale lease retain the dependency's existing fencing limitations.

title: fix(devin): report permission denials without sign-in advice
body:
Devin Connect permission denials now report a fixed MCP, content-policy, or account-access diagnosis instead of asking the user to sign in again. The code is allowlisted, and client messages and logs never echo arbitrary upstream prompt, credential, or error text. Turn and compaction translation use the provider that actually served the request.

Authentication advice remains for 401 responses. Billing detection is limited to the two proved initial account-limit sentences; misleading quota or entitlement text later in a denied request keeps a permission error and cannot initiate a model switch. The initial implementation had a false-swap case, which is fixed and covered by regressions through the actual failover classifier.

Validation: `npm run check` and 389 Node22.19 tests pass, including Devin HTTP/Connect failures, error translation, failover, Claude/Gemini surfaces, WebSocket, and caller authentication. Independent actual-helper controls cover 76 cases plus four provider scopes. All provider traffic uses local fixtures; real Devin tool-schema acceptance remains tracked separately in #941. Fresh CI for the repaired head passed on Windows, Linux and macOS, including native app packaging and the locked-Python protocol. The merged tree matches the reviewed and tested candidate.

title: fix(gateway): close translated streams when callers cancel
body:
Canceling a translated Responses turn after the provider stream is acquired can leave the upstream connection open until the next read or fixture cleanup. The locked LiteLLM 1.96.0 conversion iterator lacks `aclose`, so its normal outer cleanup wrappers cannot release that stream.

Add the missing method through one passive gateway callback, delegating to LiteLLM’s existing HTTP-stream closer. Preserve existing native cleanup methods and the wrapper’s cancellation, idempotence and error behavior. Publish both repository callbacks privately before the generated YAML references them. No dependency upgrade is required.

Add a deterministic full-chain cancellation control that pauses before the next provider read and requires a positive pause marker before abort. Keep the original 60-second upstream-close limit and require no replay before and after the wait. Run that control and eight actual locked-SDK cases in protocol CI on Linux, macOS and Windows.

- Installation-disabled control fails at the original 60-second limit on Node 24.20; the repaired control closes the mock upstream in 3 ms without replay.

- Independent review passes actual socket ownership controls, native-versus-bridge cleanup parity and twelve publication/ownership fault cases. All 27 hunks are reviewed.

title: fix(catalog): bind native watcher to supervisor lifetime

- Run the optional immediate refresh through the periodic guard, block queued callbacks after disposal, and unref the background timer.

title: fix(websocket): release upgraded sockets when the peer drops
body:
## Summary

- `ResponsesWebSocketPeer.abort()` never closed the upgraded socket. `http.Server` hands over half-open-capable sockets, so a Codex client that disappeared without a close frame (TCP FIN, reset, killed process) ended only the readable side. The router kept the descriptor for the life of the process, one per dropped connection. A router up for two days held 405 `CLOSED` sockets (`lsof`), all with `readableEnded=true, writableEnded=false` and no parser attached.
- `abort()` now calls `socket.destroySoon()`, which flushes a pending close frame first and then releases the handle.
- Regression test: three upgraded connections dropped by FIN, by reset, and by close frame must all reach `destroyed` on the server side. Fails with `condition timed out` on `main`, passes with the fix.
- Changelog fragment added.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test test/responses-websocket.test.mjs`: 50 pass
- [x] New test fails against the unpatched module
- [x] `npm run check`

title: fix(websocket): hard-destroy the socket on transport end and error
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #986, which merged before the review fix landed on its branch.

- Codex review on #986 flagged that `destroySoon()` waits for the writable side to finish. A peer that stops reading and then sends a FIN leaves a relayed frame stuck in the kernel buffer, so that finish never comes and the descriptor stays open: the leak was still reachable.
- Transport-level ends (`end`, `error`, `close`) now call `socket.destroy()`. A received close frame keeps `destroySoon()` so the close reply still flushes.
- The regression test gains a fourth peer that pauses reading until the socket buffers are full and then half-closes. It times out on current `main` and passes with this change.

## Test plan

- [x] `node --test test/responses-websocket.test.mjs`: 50 pass

title: fix(clinepass): report an unsuccessful envelope instead of relaying it
body:
## Summary

The second symptom in #938, which e6b499aa did not cover.

- Cline's non-streaming Chat Completions endpoint can answer HTTP 200 with `{"success": false, "error": "empty response content"}` and no completion. The API forwarder relayed that body intact, so the gateway failed one hop later with `provider returned a response with no 'choices'` and the real cause never reached the caller.
- On the ClinePass Chat Completions route, an HTTP 200 JSON object with `success === false` and no root `choices` now gets a 500 `provider_api_proxy_error` with a fixed diagnosis: `clinepass_empty_response` for the known reason, `clinepass_unsuccessful_response` for anything else.
- ClinePass deployments are rendered with `num_retries: 0`. LiteLLM retries every status of 500 and above twice and has no per-status setting for 5xx, so without this the same prompt would reach Cline three times for a result the origin already produced. Trade-off: a transient 502/503 on a ClinePass turn is no longer retried inside the gateway, only by Codex.
- No upstream text is relayed or logged. The reason is matched against an allowlist and the message is router-authored, in line with the Devin permission diagnostics.
- Unchanged: the successful-envelope unwrap, bodies that still carry root `choices`, non-boolean `success`, malformed JSON, HTTP errors, SSE, and other providers.

This changes one behavior that `test/clinepass-forwarder.test.mjs` pinned: the `unsuccessful envelope` case was relayed intact with status 200. That path always ended in the gateway's 500, so the test now expects the 500. Say so if relaying it intact was deliberate for another reason.

Not addressed: making such requests succeed (streaming and aggregating server-side, option 2 in the issue).

Refs #938

title: feat(router): add opt-in goal continuation repetition guard
body:
Some custom models answer automatic goal continuations with the same short acknowledgement for several turns, without calling tools. Add an optional boolean `goalContinuationGuard` model flag that refuses the next generation locally after three completed, substantially repeated goal replies. No shipped model enables it.

The gate recognizes a bounded, canonical goal context with the same objective, combines commentary/final messages per turn, and resets on new instructions, tools, objective changes or ambiguous evidence. It preserves the transcript, provider options and Codex goal state. Compaction and native traffic are excluded. A refusal returns HTTP 400 with `router_goal_no_progress` before any provider request, and records one local usage row without fabricated upstream latency.

Validation:

- 119 focused and adjacent tests passed, covering registry validation, router refusal/reset behavior, failover, diagnostics and resilience.
- The mock router proves zero upstream requests for refusal, unchanged inputs/options for permitted traffic, and a permitted compaction request.
- Against unchanged upstream `d0855644`, the regression receives HTTP 200 instead of the expected 400; it passes with this change.
- `npm run check` and whitespace checks passed.
- Linux full CI passed on this head: 5,151 passed, zero failures and 40 platform-specific skips. macOS full CI also passed; Windows CI is still running.

This is an opt-in repetition heuristic, not a semantic measure of progress. Long replies, unfamiliar goal wrappers or evidence exceeding bounds pass through. See `docs/goal-continuation-guard.md` for activation and limitations.

title: feat(router): add opt-in GLM-5.3 repetition guard
body:
GLM-5.3 can occasionally emit the same prose continuously. Add an opt-in boolean `repetitionGuard` model flag that stops sustained repetition while preserving normal output. No shipped model enables it, and other families and non-SSE responses are unaffected.

The observer checks independent assistant text parts for a complete prose unit repeating across 4,096 characters, with bounded tails and frame storage. JSON openings, fenced code, tool payloads, reasoning and refusal parts are excluded. Healthy bytes remain unchanged; malformed or oversized frames pass through. A fragmented-frame regression also covers the incremental parser's linear accumulation.

A stop cancels upstream without retry/failover. Before relaying content it returns HTTP 400; after content it ends cleanly with `response.failed`. Deliberate local rejection uses nested `invalid_prompt`, which the [Codex 0.159.2 classifier](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ff6aec96948b70d94983af2641a6b67c94faeff5/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses_error.rs#L41) maps to a terminal error. The event retains `router_repetitive_generation` and the actual explanation. Ordinary transport failures retain their existing retryable classification. Missing upstream metadata uses a minimal local failure envelope without invented identity, matching [Codex's accepted error shape](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ff6aec96948b70d94983af2641a6b67c94faeff5/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses.rs#L1338).

Validation:

- 66 detector, registry and stream-failure tests passed, including healthy JSON/code, exact UTF-8 forwarding and 320,000 single-byte frame fragments.
- Seven mock-router scenarios passed: tracked/untrusted metadata, pre-content rejection, empty retry, completed-only repetition, disabled protection and normal JSON.
- Integration checks prove clean EOF, upstream cancellation, no replay, one usage row and exact counts/timing across both attempts.
- Against unchanged upstream `d0855644`, the regression incorrectly completes the repetitive stream; it passes with this change.
- `npm run check` and whitespace checks passed; independent protocol/diff review found no remaining actionable issue.
- Linux full CI passed on this head: 5,164 passed, zero failures and 40 platform-specific skips. macOS full CI also passed; Windows CI is still running. The local Windows full run encountered 19 failures (including symlink permissions, POSIX script execution and existing assertions); all 19 reproduce on unchanged upstream `d0855644` with the same failing locations and error codes. Final guard tests passed separately.

The same terminal classification was additionally confirmed in Codex `0.162.0-alpha.2`'s [SSE classifier](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.2/codex-rs/codex-api/src/sse/responses_error.rs) and [retry policy](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/rust-v0.162.0-alpha.2/codex-rs/protocol/src/error.rs).

This is a conservative heuristic: intentionally repeated prose can trigger it, and some loops pass through. Activation, bounds and client compatibility limits are documented in `docs/glm-repetition-guard.md`.

title: fix(edge): accept response.interrupt control frames from Codex
body:
## The bug

Codex 0.162 sends a `response.interrupt` control frame over the Responses WebSocket when the user cancels a turn:

```json
{"type":"response.interrupt","response_id":"resp_...","discard_partial_items":false}
```

The edge validated every message as `response.create` and answered:

```
Responses WebSocket messages must have type response.create.
```

`sendError` writes the frame to the client without logging, so the rejection is invisible server-side — the router log shows healthy turns while every cancel surfaces as a client error. (Confirmed against a live install: zero occurrences in the router log while the client hit it repeatedly. The message vocabulary is visible in the 0.162 binary: `response.interrupt`, `response_id`, `discard_partial_items` client-side, `response.cancelled` server-side.)

## The fix

- Interrupts are **control frames and bypass the serial request queue** — queued behind the in-flight turn, the interrupt would arrive after the generation it meant to stop.
- Handling aborts the active turn's controller, so the internal HTTP request (the thing stopping the provider from generating and billing) tears down immediately, and answers with `response.cancelled`, echoing `response_id` when present.
- A turn ended by its own interrupt no longer surfaces the synthetic `local_router_error` 500, and the socket stays usable for the next turn.
- An interrupt with no turn in flight is answered, not rejected.

## Tests

Two new tests in `test/responses-websocket-interrupt.test.mjs` using the existing edge harness: interrupt cancels the in-flight turn (internal request close observed, `response.cancelled` received, no error frame, next turn completes on the same socket), and the no-turn-in-flight case. Verified against a live router with a real mid-stream turn: interrupt → `response.cancelled` in ~20 ms, upstream aborted.

The same fix is part of the WebSocket-relay PR stack (#979 → #967), where relayed turns additionally forward the interrupt frame to the provider before tearing the hop down.

title: fix: handle Codex response.interrupt on persistent WebSockets
body:
Codex sends `response.interrupt` when a user interrupts or redirects an active turn. The router previously accepted only `response.create`, so that control message could leave a 400 error on the persistent connection and prevent the next turn from continuing.

Handle interruption outside the generation queue, abort the active local request, discard unfinished items, and finish with `response.incomplete` and reason `interrupted`. Completed output and observed usage remain available for continuation on the same socket. Completion races and late duplicate interrupts do not affect the following turn; oversized continuation state requires resending full context.

Validation:
- `node scripts-check.mjs`
- `node --test --test-timeout=600000 test/responses-websocket.test.mjs` — 56 passed.
- Regression coverage includes an active SSE interruption, same-socket continuation, a late interrupt after completion, completed JSON under write backpressure, and bounded pending-item/continuation state.

This cancels the local HTTP request; it does not guarantee that a remote provider stops billing an already dispatched generation. No live generation was used for validation.

The native macOS build, universal binaries/bundle seal and complete packaged lifecycle smoke passed on a fresh runner with the WebSocket implementation unchanged: [successful job](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/38045070326/job/114192842033). The separate CI readiness hardening is proposed in #1005 rather than bundled with this fix.

title: ci: wait for AppKit readiness before macOS lifecycle reopen
body:
The native macOS lifecycle smoke starts the tray executable directly, sleeps one second, checks only that its PID is alive, then sends its first reopen through `open`. A live process can still be registering or launching in AppKit; the smoke then fails in LaunchServices before reaching its lifecycle assertions. This was observed as `-600` in [PR #1004's job](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/38042342717/job/114184916590), despite successful native build/seal checks and all three platforms' runtime suites passing.

Wait up to 30 seconds for the exact PID and application bundle to report `NSRunningApplication.isFinishedLaunching` before sending that first reopen. A host exit or AppKit query error still fails immediately, and readiness arriving after the deadline is rejected. Keep all existing reopen, child replacement, ownership and clean-quit assertions.

Validation: syntax/changelog checks and eight deterministic tests passed, covering delayed registration, wrong PID/path, exit before/during the query, timeout, late replies, query failure and invalid inputs. The actual AppKit bridge and packaged lifecycle require this PR's macOS CI runner; they cannot be exercised on the local Windows host.

This is a CI readiness fix only; no production routing, application startup or WebSocket code changes.

title: fix: preserve native remote compaction stream failure causes
body:
A native Responses stream used for remote compaction can lose its connection after HTTP 200 without enough trustworthy metadata for a full response snapshot. The generic `error` fallback then hides the diagnosed cause behind Codex's “stream closed before response.completed” message.

Opt native streams into a minimal local `response.failed` envelope when response identity or sequence metadata is unavailable. Retain the complete failure envelope when metadata is trusted, and establish the expected SSE Content-Type for successful native streaming Responses that omit that header. Do not invent response IDs, timestamps, sequence numbers or usage. V1 compact JSON and explicit non-SSE responses retain their existing behavior.

Validation: syntax/changelog checks and 72 tests covering native retry, stream-failure observation and local remote-compaction fixtures passed on official main plus this patch. Fixtures exercise reset after headers, missing sequence metadata, unknown compaction events, missing Content-Type, successful ciphertext preservation, and V1/non-SSE exclusions. They assert one upstream attempt and no transport upgrade.

The patch preserves an actionable failure; it does not prevent origin/network resets or replay an already dispatched generation. No live generation was used for validation.

title: fix: flush held reasoning-tag text before stream completion
body:
The reasoning-tag stream adapter held possible delimiter prefixes such as `<th` or `x <`, then discarded that held text at completion. It also shared partial-tag state between text parts of the same output item.

Flush held text before the matching content/item/response completion, `[DONE]`, malformed-byte fallback or EOF. Keep each content part independent and retain its identity when emitting a tail. Inserted events adjust subsequent sequence numbers and retain framing without duplicating SSE IDs or logprobs. Unfinished reasoning spans continue to stay hidden under the existing opt-in grammar.

Validation: syntax/changelog checks and all 33 reasoning-tag adapter tests passed. The added incomplete-tail regression fails against unmodified official main. Coverage includes split bytes, whitespace, content-part interleaving, every terminal kind, EOF, invalid UTF-8, CRLF and sequence ordering.

This patch leaves route selection and reasoning-tag policy unchanged.

title: fix: preserve literal tags outside evidenced reasoning cleanup routes
body:
Applying reasoning-tag cleanup to every routed model deletes legitimate XML and quoted examples such as `<reason>disk full</reason>` and `<think>visible sample</think>`. A transport protocol or a similar model name does not establish that those tags are leaked reasoning.

Preserve unknown routes by default and validate an explicit model-scoped `reasoningTagPolicy`: `preserve`, `legacy-inline` or `hy4-nonce`. Keep automatic compatibility for the exact evidenced Qwen Plan Flash route and Hy4's established nonce markup; preserve bare tags on Hy4 unless explicitly opted in. An explicit `preserve` overrides either default. Registry and curation paths retain and validate the policy.

Validation: syntax/changelog checks and 49 tests passed on official main plus this patch, including a real isolated Router with a local mock upstream. That integration regression demonstrably fails against unmodified main because literal XML and fenced examples disappear. Registry tests cover invalid policies and attempts to apply Hy4 nonce semantics to an unrelated model.

The separate held-text flushing fix is excluded from this PR. No live generation was used for validation.

title: fix: preserve private temporary ownership during failed-write cleanup
body:
Failed private writes and OAuth profile copies can encounter a replaced temporary name or parent directory. Cleanup based only on the pathname can then delete an unrelated replacement.

Capture the exclusively created file's device/inode identity with BigInt precision and remove a temporary only while that identity still matches. Preserve the original operation error, attach cleanup failures, and retain existing profile symlink guards and custom protection callbacks. Async temporaries also use exclusive creation.

Validation against current main (`eb5acc9c`, including #1011, #1016 and #1017):
- All nine parent-replacement, leaf-replacement and 64-bit identity fault cases fail on unmodified main and pass with this fix.
- Local writer/ACL regression suite: 17 passed; one POSIX-only assertion skipped on Windows.
- Fresh cross-platform CI: [Linux, macOS, Windows and desktop checks](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/39107936235).

Earlier CI attempts exposed existing fixture/port and Windows helper-concurrency issues. Those support fixes are now in main; this branch incorporates them without expanding the ownership-cleanup feature. The previous Windows rerun also passed on October 16 (Asia/Singapore), superseding the older timeout result described here previously.

Bulk writer migrations, publication transactions and the separate AppData environment repair are outside this PR. Tests use synthetic profiles and credentials.

title: fix: distinguish generation completion from HTTP delivery
body:
An HTTP 200 stream may report a failed or incomplete generation, or end without any completion terminal. Treating that envelope as success inflates provider/model success totals and disagrees with the activity view and subagent outcome.

Record a bounded semantic `generationOutcome` separately from the committed `httpStatus`. Observe Responses terminals (including embedded statuses), JSON responses and Chat finish reasons without retaining or rewriting content. Preserve usage from failed generations, classify missing streamed terminals as indeterminate, and keep historical rows compatible without pretending their missing protocol evidence can be reconstructed. A retry has a fresh outcome observer; a later completion in the same attempt cannot erase a failure.

Validation:
- Syntax/changelog checks passed.
- 99 outcome, stream-usage, activity, provider aggregation, ledger and real Router tests passed.
- 78 adjacent native-retry, Router-resilience and stream-failure tests passed.
- The isolated real Router test exercises completed, failed, incomplete, embedded-failure and EOF-without-terminal streams plus completed/failed/status-missing JSON from a local synthetic upstream, verifies activity/ledger agreement and retained usage, and asserts no replay. It fails on unmodified main because the separate outcome/HTTP evidence is absent.

Retry policy, phase timing, direct routing and Control Center presentation are separate changes.

CI follow-up: the original three runtime jobs failed the same legacy child-diagnostic fixture, which omitted the completed status. The fixture now declares `status: completed`; the production classifier remains conservative. Both the real SSE/JSON Router regression and that legacy diagnostic passed after the fix.

Expanded local verification ran 256 tests: 225 passed and 31 failed (one existing key-pool CLI failure and 30 startup health/model wait timeouts). This run is not reported as green. A focused rerun of the two changed integration cases passed, and syntax/changelog checks passed. Fresh full Linux/macOS/Windows CI validates the complete branch.

title: test: isolate integration ports from POSIX credential leases
body:
The integration listener pool starts at 10000, overlapping both POSIX Antigravity kernel lease ranges (token mutation: 10000–19999; refresh: 20000–29999). A fixture can therefore deny a credential lease for its full 30-second wait horizon. A recent Linux run ended with a still-pending activation after about 32 seconds; its logs do not identify the occupying listener, so that particular collision cannot be certified from the log alone.

Allocate disjoint fixture blocks from 5000–9999 and 30000–32767 instead, excluding both lease ranges, managed router ports and the platforms' default ephemeral ranges. Keep the existing busy-port checks and fail explicitly if distinct blocks cannot be assigned.

Validation:
- Syntax/changelog checks passed.
- 170 port-pool contract, lease-isolation, real gateway-restart and routing tests passed after updating the existing range assertion.
- The new regression allocates 75 ports each for two large integration files, checks both range segments and uniqueness, then binds a fixture concurrently with the actual production lease listener helper. On unchanged main that valid lease bind fails with `EADDRINUSE`; it succeeds with the disjoint pool.

No credential-lock algorithm, lease identity, runtime service port, network configuration or private-file behavior changes.

CI follow-up: the initial range change missed the old `port-pool.test.mjs` floor assertion; this PR now updates it and explicitly excludes both lease windows. A separate macOS Electron fixture race produced a NaN PID; its independent fix is [#1014](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/pull/1014). Production PID/lock behavior is not changed here.

title: fix: distinguish generation outcomes in Control Center
body:
Dashboard and Status currently color HTTP 200 requests as successful even when the generation failed or never completed. Show the recorded generation outcome separately from HTTP delivery, keep billed token totals visible for every outcome, and mark older records as “Not recorded” instead of inventing completion evidence. Provider/model summaries distinguish recorded outcomes from historical requests and label the ledger window separately from rolling traffic.

The optional fields are compatible with existing backend snapshots. Backend outcome recording is independently proposed in #1010; this PR changes presentation only and includes English, Simplified Chinese and Traditional Chinese labels.

Validation:
- Root syntax/changelog checks and Control Center TypeScript checking/build passed.
- 25 outcome, usage and translation-contract tests passed.
- The new compiled-browser regression passed across Dashboard and Status, checks HTTP 200 failures, retained billed tokens, historical rows, summaries, success-only speed samples, and unclipped badges at 960/1280px. Screenshots were inspected.
- All 17 existing renderer tests passed.
- Against a freshly compiled unchanged main, the same new browser regression fails because a failed generation is displayed as `200` instead of `Failed`.

No backend routing, ledger writer, credential or service behavior is changed.

CI follow-up: Linux/macOS and the renderer/build checks passed on the original head. Windows failed the unchanged Antigravity rejected-client onboarding fixture (a null child exit status after its fixed 10-second spawn timeout). This PR changes no provider/login runtime or that fixture. One empty commit requests a fresh CI run without changing renderer code; no repeat-until-green loop is used.

title: fix: require non-delivery evidence before native generation replay
body:
A missing response or edge 5xx does not prove a generation POST was never executed. Require positive non-delivery evidence before the default native retry so a consumed request cannot be submitted twice.

Preserve bounded retries for safe methods and the explicit `CODEX_ROUTER_NATIVE_RETRY_POLICY=availability` opt-in. Refuse native generation redirects, recheck cancellation/output/budget gates before another submission, and record bounded attempt metadata without input, URLs or credentials.

Recognize Node's exact pre-handshake TLS `ECONNRESET`, which carries `host` but no `syscall`, as `not_sent`. The connection-phase diagnostic now identifies the target. Generic resets, consumed POSTs and interrupted response streams remain ineligible for default replay.

Validation:
- 111 relevant tests passed after merging current main, including retry policy, real delivery boundaries, transport diagnostics, usage events, router resilience, timing and generation outcomes.
- Real local TLS tests reproduce two handshake failures then successful recovery both directly and through HTTP CONNECT; the origin receives exactly one POST. The spawned native Router also recovers and records both safe retries.
- Exhaustion, cancellation, output permission, budget expiry and disabled retries prevent further submissions. Real resets after POST consumption or streamed output are never replayed.
- Syntax and changelog checks passed. The regression reproduced the pre-TLS misclassification before the fix.

This controls this router's automatic retries for one native request; an independent client retry remains outside that boundary. Image generation retains its zero-retry rule.

title: test: synchronize complete descendant PID publication
body:
The Electron owner-signal test waits for a PID file to exist and reads it immediately. File creation precedes the write, so CI can observe an empty file and pass NaN to process.kill. A macOS run exposed this in the SIGTERM descendant-drain test.

Wait for a complete positive decimal PID with the existing bounded readiness helper, and atomically rename the fixture's completed PID record into place before any reader can signal its owner. Keep the descendant-drain, exit-code and survival-marker assertions intact.

Validation:
- Syntax/changelog checks passed.
- Six local tests passed: empty/malformed publication and deadline regressions plus actual command timeout, overflow, success and failure descendant cleanup.
- The two actual owner-signal cases are POSIX-only and skipped on Windows; Linux/macOS CI must validate them.
- Both new PID-reader regressions fail against the exact unchanged-main helper.

Only test fixtures and their readiness checks change; production command execution is unchanged.

title: feat: compile immutable selected-route execution plans
body:
Selected routes need a shared, credential-independent execution decision before startup, dispatch and installers can consistently remove unused dependencies. Add a pure immutable plan compiler and a read-only query over the loaded registry and current selection.

The compiler respects the registry's effective per-model protocol, selected hidden callable routes, enabled generic descriptors and supported OAuth/Ollama adapters. Its deterministic fingerprint uses allowed routing and capability metadata, excludes credential/header values and URL secrets, and does not claim to fingerprint live environment or independently stored state. An exact pending Antigravity proof adds a readiness listener without changing the requestable-route identity.

This is an additive planning API: no current service startup, installer, Router dispatch, health or publication consumer changes in this PR. The Responses mapping describes the intended direct-forwarder execution boundary; the query is not an inventory of the presently running stack. Consumer adoption remains separately reviewable.

Validation:
- Syntax/changelog checks passed.
- 40 compiler, actual-registry/query and selection tests passed.
- 50 adjacent registry/runtime-descriptor tests passed.
- Tests cover mixed protocols, hidden routes, selection/variant precedence, immutability, endpoint/metadata rebinding, credential exclusion, and a real synthetic pending-proof positive control. The gateway-only query is verified not to inspect that OAuth credential.
- Tests use isolated synthetic state; installed configuration and credentials are unchanged.

title: test: release upstream listeners after failed Antigravity setup
body:
An Antigravity forwarder test starts its mock upstream before writing the private token and entering try/finally. If setup throws, such as a Windows ACL helper timeout, the listener survives the failed test and prevents the test process from exiting. A Windows CI job reached its 60-minute limit this way.

Register listener cleanup with the owning test context immediately after creating the server, pass that context through the stream fixture, and make repeated server/child cleanup safe. Preserve all original request, proof and failure assertions; the setup error still fails the test.

Validation:
- Changed-file syntax and changelog validation passed.
- All 20 forwarder/fixture tests passed on Windows using isolated synthetic state.
- A real subprocess regression injects a failure immediately after the listener starts. With this fix the process exits with the original failure; the exact unchanged-main helper reaches the same failure but remains alive until the bounded probe timeout.
- Direct node:test probe execution keeps the regression in one owned process, so a negative-control timeout does not leave an orphan test worker.

Only test fixture lifetime changes. Production OAuth behavior, private-file permissions and timeouts are unchanged.

title: ci: budget Windows fixture startup and ACL helper concurrency
body:
Windows runtime CI executes many fixtures that spawn real PowerShell ACL helpers. One run hit seven existing 15-second ACL helper deadlines, while another unchanged Antigravity CLI fixture exceeded its fixed 10-second child budget and returned a null exit status. The fixture deadline also reproduces under bounded local test-file execution.

Run every Windows test with two test-file workers, preserving all within-file request/race concurrency assertions, the ten-minute per-test limit and the one-hour job limit. Give Antigravity CLI fixtures a finite 30-second Windows child budget and report spawn errors directly; keep the POSIX fixture budget at ten seconds. No production ACL, request, login or permission policy changes.

Validation:
- Changed-file syntax, changelog validation and workflow condition/argument review passed.
- With the actual two-worker command and a real dependency directory, 35 local CLI, private-file ACL and forwarder tests passed; one POSIX-only file-mode case was skipped on Windows. Consent, rejected-client, probe and atomic-target protection assertions remain intact.
- The earlier ten-second fixture run failed the rejected-client case with a null exit status. A first junction-based local checkout also lacked symlink privileges when copying dependencies; final verification used the same real directory layout as CI instead of weakening that fixture.
- Full Windows CI must establish that the resource budget is sufficient; helper contention is an explanation to validate, not a claim that the original runner's CPU state was measured.

The separate listener-leak correction in [#1016](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/pull/1016) ensures an unrelated setup failure cannot keep a whole test process alive until the job limit. These CI support changes remain separate from the private temporary ownership feature in #1009.

title: feat(copilot): support enterprise account hosts
body:
## Summary

Copilot routing previously used the public GitHub account API. Add `control github-copilot host status|set HOST|clear` for GitHub Enterprise Cloud data-residency tenants, while keeping `github.com` as the default. One host applies to all Copilot credentials.

Persist the selection using the existing protected-state writer. Each account, inference, quota and catalog operation snapshots the selected host; enterprise endpoints must belong to that tenant and cannot redirect. Sessions and catalogs are separated by host, including in-flight discovery and same-key 401 refresh. Host changes invalidate the Copilot catalog; README guidance covers re-curation and client reload.

The shared Responses adapter also keeps the announced function item ID when an upstream stream changes its transport item ID at a known function output index. Logical call IDs remain stable, conflicting references still fail, and completion-only streams retain their existing behavior. Synthetic regressions cover complete parallel calls and invalid identity/index references.

The patch adds no dependencies, UI, installer implementation, service or credential-schema changes. The installer test fixture disables automatic Git maintenance to prevent a background repack from racing its immediate local clone.

## Verification

- `npm run check`: passed (syntax, 7 application manifests, 92 changelog fragments).
- Adapter and namespace suites: 234 passed. The new complete-stream regression fails against the exact pre-fix adapter and passes with the fix.
- Isolated live enterprise Copilot test: discovery plus non-streaming and streaming tool-call/result exchanges passed. Fresh state and a random loopback port were used; current client configuration/authentication hashes were unchanged and temporary credentials/state/processes were removed. No existing conversation was loaded or resumed. Private test artifacts are excluded from this PR.
- Focused state/session/discovery/quota/CLI tests: 120 passed; Copilot routing tests: 7 passed.
- `npm test`: 5,272 passed, 39 skipped, 5 failed entries (four leaf failures plus the app-server parent), on macOS / Node 26.9.0.
- Both preserved-provider app-server failures reproduce on unchanged base `00eed6eb`: Codex completes one HTTP turn but makes two WebSocket upgrades where the test expects one.
- The two additional full-suite failures passed their isolated reruns: credential-directory disconnect encountered `EADDRINUSE` on a shared test port; the router execution-deadline case failed a timing assertion under suite load. Neither test file changed. The full-suite result above includes both failures.
- Installer clone race resolved: changed source object hashes triggered automatic background repacking in Apple Git 2.54.0. Matched immediate-clone controls failed 5/5 with maintenance enabled and passed 5/5 with it disabled. The three-line fixture fix preserves the local clone and rollback assertions; five fresh rollback runs and all seven installer test-file cases pass.
- `npm audit --omit=dev --audit-level=high`: zero vulnerabilities.
- Negative control: removing the session host-identity cache guard in a scratch copy makes the host-switch regression fail; the original passes.

This PR is a draft pending repository CI and platform validation. Deterministic automated tests use synthetic credentials and mocked/local endpoints; the separate live check is described above.

## Changelog

Added `changelog.d/enterprise-copilot-hosts.md` and `changelog.d/responses-function-item-identity.md`.

title: [Bug]: Responses WebSocket rejects Codex `response.interrupt` frames
body:
### What happened?

**Summary**

When the Codex app uses codex-router's Responses WebSocket endpoint, an in-flight turn interruption can be rejected with:

```text
400 invalid_request_error
Responses WebSocket messages must have type response.create.
```

The Codex client sends a `response.interrupt` WebSocket frame for an interruption after a response has started. The Router's current request guard accepts only `response.create` and returns this 400 for every other frame. This makes normal Codex steering/interruption incompatible with the Router's WebSocket adapter.

**Environment**

- App routed through: Codex
- Platform: macOS
- codex-router: 0.6.0, source commit `00eed6eb` (2026-10-10)
- Codex app/bundled CLI version: not recorded
- Managed endpoint/capability URL and credentials intentionally omitted

**Reproduction**

1. Run Codex through codex-router with Responses WebSocket transport active.
2. Start a response and interrupt/steer it while it is in progress.
3. When the Router receives Codex's `response.interrupt` frame, it responds with the 400 above.

The exact guard is in [`src/responses-websocket.mjs`](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/blob/main/src/responses-websocket.mjs#L829-L834). The official Codex client implementation emits `response.interrupt` for an active response at [`responses_websocket.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/main/codex-rs/codex-api/src/endpoint/responses_websocket.rs#L3413-L3456).

The user-facing 400 was observed repeatedly in Codex. A raw frame capture from the affected turn is not available, so the per-turn correlation to `response.interrupt` is not claimed as directly captured; however, the Router's rejection of that frame is deterministic from the current source.

**Expected behavior**

Handle Codex's `response.interrupt` according to its interruption semantics (including a safe response to a late interrupt), without returning this invalid-request error or breaking the WebSocket connection. A subsequent `response.create` should continue to work on the connection. Please add regression coverage for both an interrupt during an active response and a late interrupt. This should validate supported frame types rather than blindly accepting arbitrary message types.

**Actual behavior**

Every frame whose `type` is not `response.create` is rejected with HTTP 400 and `Responses WebSocket messages must have type response.create.`

**Related issues**

- [#512](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/issues/512) covered the earlier lack of Responses WebSocket support in standard signed-in mode; this report concerns handling an interrupt frame after WebSocket support is active.
- [#546](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/issues/546) and [#554](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/issues/554) cover separate WebSocket adapter failures.

### Which app do you route through?

Codex

### Platform

macOS

### Doctor output or support bundle

Not attached. No credentials, private prompts, managed endpoint URL, or unredacted logs are included.

title: Windows: start.mjs hangs after router.mjs exits 0xC0000409, so Scheduled Task never restarts the service
body:
## Summary

On Windows, after `router.mjs` exits with `0xC0000409`, `start.mjs` can stay alive with no live child processes and no listening ports. Because `start.mjs` never exits, the Scheduled Task's `RestartOnFailure` never fires and the router stays down until someone kills it by hand. It happened once on 2026-10-11; the same crash two days earlier recovered on its own.

This is a different problem from #465 (the crash itself) and #908 (gateway supervisor stall); the crash is only the trigger here. The bug is that the supervisor does not terminate afterwards.

## Environment

- codex-router `0a70b48c` (v0.6.0), Windows 11, Node via nvm4w
- Launched by the "Codex Router" Scheduled Task (LogonTrigger, `RestartOnFailure` Count=999 Interval=PT1M) through `start-codex-router-hidden.vbs` -> `start-codex-router.cmd` -> `node src/start.mjs`
- `CODEX_ROUTER_GATEWAY_HEALTH_FAILURES=8`, `NODE_OPTIONS=--report-on-fatalerror --report-uncaught-exception --report-directory=...` (`node-crash-reports` stayed empty, as the native fast-fail skips it)

## What happened

Last lines of `router.log` before the hang:

```
[codex-router] timing at=2026-10-11T15:26:27.255Z model=gpt-6-luna provider=openai status=200 ...
INFO:     127.0.0.1:50493 - "GET /health/liveliness HTTP/1.1" 200 OK
[codex-router] Codex router exited (code=3221226505, signal=null (0xC0000409 STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN)).
[codex-router] Native abort with no JS frame (0xC0000409 STATUS_STACK_BUFFER_OVERRUN): capture the Event Viewer Application entry ...
```

Nothing was written to the log after that. Checked about 9 minutes later:

- `start.mjs` (started 18:26, same process that logged the line above) was still running
- `Win32_Process` showed no child of that PID, and no python/litellm/forwarder process anywhere
- ports 4200-4203 were not listening, `/health` did not answer
- Scheduled Task state was `Running`, with `LastTaskResult=0x800710E0` on its retry attempts
- `router.log` mtime did not move

Killing the `start.mjs` PID and running `node src/service.mjs restart` brought everything back (`/health` ok).

For comparison, the 2026-10-09 17:12Z crash with the same exit code was followed immediately by `[kimi-oauth] listening`, `[api-forwarder] listening`, a new LiteLLM start and so on, so the supervisor exited and the task relaunched it as designed.

## Where I think it hangs (not verified)

In `src/start.mjs`, after `main()` returns the `finally` block does:

```js
stopChildren();
await Promise.all(children.map((child) => waitForExit(child, "child")));
```

There is no timeout on that await, so if any entry in `children` never emits `exit`, the process is stuck there and never reaches `process.exitCode = exitCode`. That is the same shape as #908, but at final teardown instead of the gateway restart path.

I could not confirm which child it was waiting on: there was no live child under the PID when I looked, so it may be a handle whose `exit` event was lost rather than a surviving process. I killed the process before capturing anything more, so I do not have a dump of the pending handles.

## Suggested fix

Bound the final wait, for example race it against a few seconds and then `process.exit(exitCode || 1)` regardless, so a nonzero exit always reaches Task Scheduler. A non-zero exit after a fatal child status should be guaranteed even when teardown is incomplete.

## Impact

Router stays down until a manual restart. Every Codex request fails with a connection error, and the Scheduled Task looks healthy (`Running`), which makes it easy to miss.

title: feat: add opt-in ChatGPT account balancing and quota failover
body:
## Summary

Saved ChatGPT profiles currently require changing the main Codex login. This adds opt-in per-conversation routing for independent native Responses requests: round-robin or fill-first allocation, with another eligible account attempted only after a structured HTTP quota refusal before output. Routing defaults off and does not replace the main Codex `auth.json`.

- Expose the policy in Control Center and the CLI, including the Windows dispatcher.
- Keep independent conversation ownership stable across caller-key rotation; preserve account-owned encrypted reasoning, compaction, uploaded files, stored response/item references, and Code Interpreter `container_id` references in full output histories or nested tool configuration.
- Enforce disabled credential discovery inside the batch reader before path inspection or opens and again after asynchronous ACL verification, closing descriptors without reading contents. Mid-request disabling fails closed and cannot overwrite ownership/cooldowns with empty policy defaults.
- Read only registered, protected, identity-matched, usable profiles. Exclude login-in-progress, paused, expired and unhealthy profiles. Persist opaque affinity and cooldown metadata without credentials or conversation content.
- Serialize full turns per conversation across Router processes. Lease and policy-lock waits follow request cancellation/deadlines, rather than a separate 30-second retry cap. Late acquisition after cancellation releases the lease before preserving the original cancellation reason.
- Use fresh asynchronous Windows batch ACL validation and asynchronous protected state writes on the request path. Hold bounded descriptors across ACL awaits and recheck identity/content metadata before and after reading; do not cache ACL verdicts or reread the pool via an unverified path.

## Collaboration is withheld

Live marker-return proofs through every installed routed agent have not been completed. The unverified account-pool collaboration path is therefore disabled in code, with no opt-in override: requests advertising collaboration tools, parent/subagent metadata, typed agent messages or collaboration envelopes are refused. Flattened namespaces and split text envelopes are covered. Native encrypted agent-message relay is refused before profile credentials or relay/cache access whenever routing is enabled or the conversation has pooled ownership. Existing pooled tree records remain refused after routing is turned off.

Ordinary encrypted reasoning and compaction in independent conversations remain supported. For native collaboration, turn routing Off and start new conversations. UI hints, the account guide, its website mirror and the changelog disclose this restriction. Synthetic tests are not presented as live collaboration proofs.

## Compatibility and limits

Only recognized structured HTTP 429/402 quota refusals allow portable history to try another account. Ordinary rate limits, auth errors, network failures, cancellation, account-bound history and accepted streams never trigger account switching. Native transient edge and connection failures retain bounded same-account retries before output; transport retry allowance and elapsed budget are shared across quota hops, and telemetry reports transport retries plus account switches. A quota error inside HTTP 200 SSE records cooldown without replay. Pooled upstream requests use HTTP; client WebSocket turns still use the shared adapter. The policy does not refresh tokens, probe live quotas, or guarantee model entitlement across plans. Image/search routing and default-off external-provider behavior are preserved.

An explicit reset refuses active turns and unknown account-owned history; pre-release capability-scoped affinity files require reset rather than guessing ownership. Windows protected writes retain their existing bounded hardening operation: cancellation during that write may wait up to its 30-second timeout before locks release. Independent conversations also serialize short shared-state ACL operations while the event loop stays responsive.

## Verification

- Full root suite in an isolated `CODEX_HOME`: **5390 tests, 5351 passed, 39 skipped, 0 failed**.
- Root syntax/repository checks and changed POSIX dispatcher syntax: passed. Control Center type/syntax checks, production renderer build, and its full integration suite: **124 tests, 123 passed, 1 Windows-only skipped, 0 failed**. UI validation was rerun at `114932af`; the final container-history fix does not change UI source. Production dependency audit: **0 vulnerabilities**.
- New regressions cover disabled discovery before path iteration and after ACL await, descriptor cleanup and unchanged routing ownership, no mid-request credential forwarding, conversation lease recovery, same-account 503/socket-reset retries, account-bound history, cancellation and retry guards, zero retries, shared cross-account allowance/budget, immutable compressed request bytes, HTTP/client WebSocket execution and usage retry telemetry. These are included in the full suite above.

- Regression coverage includes refusal with zero native/provider upstream requests over HTTP and client WebSocket, collaboration envelopes and tool namespace variants, default-off/reset/old-tree fail-closed behavior, a real 32-second overlapping lease wait, cancellation and late-acquisition cleanup, malformed Windows helper output, timeout/abort cleanup, no forwarded secrets, and file replacement/mutation/symlink refusal after ACL awaits.
- The earlier alpha smoke-test failure is corrected: additional authenticated prewarm WebSocket handshakes are allowed, while exactly one model request is still required. Previous real-binary validation passed the fallback/custom-provider cases on Codex CLI 0.162.1 and desktop 0.162.0-alpha.17.2.
- Actual Windows ACL execution and real-provider multi-account/collaboration probes were not run on this macOS host. A Windows-only ACL regression is included for its runner.
- All local tests use isolated state and synthetic upstreams. The running installed Router was not restarted or deployed.

## Changelog

Updated `changelog.d/chatgpt-account-balancing.md`; `CHANGELOG.md` is unchanged.

## Independent review and remaining merge evidence

Two independent read-only local reviews covered the complete PR against `6cf33f7d66202158d82b254029cf1483273008ed`, including routing/credential ownership, runtime integration, file security, locks, CLI/platform parity and documentation. They found one additional resource-affinity issue: `container_id` in Code Interpreter output history was portable. This is fixed, reproduced with a failing HTTP regression before the change, and independently re-reviewed afterward; no remaining reproducible P1/P2 was found in those reviewed paths. This is local review evidence, not a successful hosted CR run or formal GitHub approval.

The last hosted Codex review attempt on `114932af` failed with `Failed to sample tokens`. Seven historical review threads remain unresolved; their fixes and tests are documented above for reviewer verification. No further bot requests or maintainer messages were sent in this continuation.

Latest head: `af59378449a76f93d4859352e44f61d78aaf5675`. GitHub reports **MERGEABLE / UNSTABLE**, with no merge conflict and no valid latest-head hosted review. GitGuardian Security Checks passed for this head. All three fork workflows report **action_required**, each with **0 jobs executed**: [Provider model discovery](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/38361502765), [CI](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/38361502761), [Grok apply_patch protocol](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/38361502827). Fork workflows require approval by an upstream maintainer with write access. The current account has read-only upstream permissions and cannot approve them. Do not equate a completed `action_required` workflow with executed/passing jobs. Windows ACL execution, cross-platform packaged lifecycle checks and the locked Python/Grok protocol matrix remain unverified until the hosted workflows execute. No workflow, repository-permission or branch-protection setting was modified.

title: Stop automatic replay of rejected tool streams
body:
## Summary

After a custom tool stream is rejected locally, Codex currently receives `server_error` and automatically replays the turn. This can repeatedly consume quota without resolving the inconsistent tool input. Preserve the specific local integrity error and emit the Responses `invalid_prompt` classification for the two deterministic tool-validation failures; ordinary transport failures keep their existing retry behavior.

The integrity guard remains unchanged: mismatched or malformed tool input is never completed or executed. This change prevents retry amplification; it does not claim to fix the upstream source of an intermittent stream mismatch.

- `npm run check`: passed.
- Focused namespace, routing, response-failure and invalid-function-call suite: 426 passed.
- Installed Codex client against an offline fixture: `server_error` caused two requests; the same fixture with `invalid_prompt` caused one.
- Live GLM 5.3 and GLM 5.3 Flash: each completed a custom-tool call and consumed its result using the patched installed source on a separate local listener.
- Full `npm test`: 5,031 passed, 11 failed, 1 cancelled, 132 skipped. Failures include missing POSIX-shell checks on Windows, a profile-switch timeout, signed-out app-server fixtures, and a catalog-publication-lock timing failure; the catalog-lock file passed all four tests when rerun separately.
