Roadmap item P07 asks for more trusted search-sidecar adapters without weakening the per-model opt-in or the transport boundary. I'd like to propose Keenable Search as a second, opt-in adapter. Perplexity stays the default.

The policy change, in plain terms: `TRUSTED_SEARCH_ORIGIN` in `src/search-sidecar-policy.mjs` becomes a two-row table, one exact origin and fixed path per adapter. The Perplexity row is today's rule, unchanged. The Keenable row is `https://api.keenable.ai`, with path `/v1/search/public` when no credential is bound and `/v1/search` when one is. Allowing no credential is the only relaxation, and only for that row, because Keenable's API works without a key (a key only raises rate limits).

Everything else stays as it is: enabled `openai-chat` descriptor, `allowPrivate: false`, no extra path or query, the DNS-pinned redirect-refusing transport, and the shared result URL, DNS and credential checks. `search-sidecar set` records the adapter from the descriptor's exact origin in the binding's existing `adapter` field, and the catalog, doctor, control and request path all check against that recorded adapter, so neither adapter can be reached through the other's descriptor.

Keenable takes one query per request, so a multi-query turn sends one request per query, in order, under the same deadline. Each request carries a fixed `X-Keenable-Title: codex-router` header, which the keyless path requires; it names the app, not the user or machine.

I have this on a branch with unit, control, capability and router-path tests next to the Perplexity ones, docs (en, zh-CN, ja) and a changelog fragment. A live keyless run through `router.mjs` returned 8 results per query. If you would rather keep a credential required for every adapter, I can make Keenable key-only instead.

Disclosure: I work at Keenable, which runs this search API.

title: [Bug]: Native Responses Lite requests skip tool-result archival (additional_tools)
fix: recover native Responses Lite tool-result archives
body:
## Summary

Native Responses Lite requests carry tool declarations in developer-role `additional_tools` input items and omit top-level `tools`. Recovery previously inspected only the top-level inventory, so eligible historical results never reached archival on that path.

Recognize the native incremental declarations as candidate readback capabilities, preserving unchanged members and applying later definitions by namespace/name. Explicit tool inventories and restrictive tool choices still take precedence. Forwarded tool definitions, routed lookup, durable archive writes and signed, unexpired conversation/permission-scoped readback checks are unchanged. A declaration alone never permits omission; changed developer notices invalidate earlier proof scopes.

The runtime diff is confined to `toolResultReadbackTools()` and its native call site. The remaining changes are focused regression tests and the required one-line changelog fragment.

The regression fixture exercises real `.result` creation, exact text/hash preservation, CLI signed readback inside Desktop wrappers, later compaction, and positive saved-byte telemetry. It also verifies failed writes/readback, forged/expired/foreign proofs, permission notices and explicit restrictions retaining the original text.

Related: #1052 and #1062.

## Verification

- `npm run check` and whitespace checks passed.
- Codex Security diff review completed with no introduced security findings. Added-text and publication-metadata privacy screening found no personal details or secrets; private review/test artifacts are excluded.
- Archive, policy, settings, retention and usage suites: **133 passed**.
- Native recovery, request diagnostics, routing and Responses parser suites: **202 passed**, no skips.
- Windows follow-up (`8589305`): preserve `PSModulePath` in the isolated native fixture. The exact updated fixture passed hosted Windows checks: **102 passed, 1 skipped, 0 failed**, including real ACL hardening, archive creation, signed readback and compaction. Production code and test timeouts are unchanged.
- Negative control: the new native archive lifecycle regression fails against the unmodified base at the missing archive-pending assertion; it passes with the fix.
- Full `npm test -- --test-concurrency=2` under an isolated offline/credential-denying guard: **6,020 passed, 10 failed, 67 skipped**. Eight process/terminal failures reproduce on the untouched baseline. A DNS-pinning failure caused by the guard passes after the guard was corrected to permit verified loopback lookup results. The clone lacked Playwright; installing the locked dependencies only in a disposable baseline copy resolves that import, where 14 desktop cases pass and browser launch fails with host `SIGABRT`/`EPERM` before assertions. This is guarded local evidence, not a clean ordinary-CI result.

No live provider requests or paid inference were used. The installed router was not modified or restarted. Actual Desktop/NAS behavior still requires qualification; the full PR CI rerun for the Windows fixture follow-up is pending.

## Changelog

`changelog.d/native-lite-tool-result-archives.md`

title: fix: recognize Responses Lite additional_tools for tool-result recovery
body:
Codex's Responses Lite request builder leaves top-level `tools` unset and declares tools in developer-role `additional_tools` input items. `toolResultReadbackTools(payload)` only read `payload.tools`. On these requests it returned `undefined`, so `ageToolResultsWithRecovery` always took its no-local-tool fallback. Native sessions on Responses Lite models were evaluated but never reached retention.

`toolResultReadbackTools` now falls back to the tools from developer-role `additional_tools` input items when top-level `tools` is absent, merging all such items into one list. The existing rules are unchanged:
- An explicit top-level list, including an empty one, still takes precedence.
- `tool_choice: "none"` and forced tool choices still return `[]`.
- Requests with neither source still return `undefined`.

The router call sites are untouched. `toolResultRecoveryScope` already hashes developer-role input items, so the declarations are part of the readback scope.

Testing: added a test in `test/tool-result-recovery.test.mjs`, built on the issue's fixture. It covers:
- Recognition through `additional_tools`, including merging several items.
- Explicit empty top-level tools, a top-level list taking precedence, `tool_choice` "none" and forced choices.
- No declaration at all, and a non-developer declaration being ignored.
- Mock retention returning `undefined` or throwing, which keeps the full text.
- A real archive write with no proof, a forged proof and a proof from another scope, all of which keep the full text.
- A valid proof, which ages the result.

The new test fails without the change. `node --test test/tool-result-recovery.test.mjs` (24/24) and `test/tool-result-aging.test.mjs` (55/55) pass. I did not run full router integration tests.

title: Add free/auto: one model that walks anonymous free backends
body:
## Summary

Adds **`free/auto`**, one model ID that is backed by a pool of anonymous, no-key free models. Before this change, each free route had to be picked by hand, and a 429 or a drained quota ended the turn.

- **One picker entry.** Only `free/auto` is listed. The members are generated as unlisted models, so they never reach the Codex picker, `/v1/models`, `/cursor/v1/models` or any catalog publication.
- **Members, in try order.**
  1. Kilo's `kilo-auto/free`.
  2. The Kilo gateway's `:free` models.
  3. The OpenCode Zen free lane, minus every ID in `OPENCODE_FREE_CLIENT_GATED` or `OPENCODE_FREE_WITHDRAWN`.
  
  Only the documented anonymous endpoints already used by `kilo-free` and `opencode-free` are involved: no credential, no signed header, no client impersonation. The reference's EAC channel and its account channels (TRAE, Qoder, LobsterAI, Cline) were deliberately **not** ported.
- **Fallback.** A member that fails with 429, quota, 5xx, unavailable or a timeout *before the first relayed byte* passes the turn to the next member. Once text has streamed, the turn never switches. A plain 400 is returned as is.
- **Drains.** A failed member is drained for a cooldown: Retry-After, 10m for rate limits, 1h for quota, 2m for 5xx, 6h for 402/404/410, capped at 12h. Drains are kept in `free-pool-drains.json`, separate from provider cooldowns.
- **Pool exhausted.** When every member is drained, the router returns HTTP 429 `free_pool_exhausted` with `retry_at`.
- **Member list.** `./bin/control free-pool refresh` re-reads the member list from upstream. The router also refreshes it once a day at start while `free` is enabled. A built-in static list is the fallback.
- **Control commands.** `./bin/control free-pool status|reset`.
- **Control Center.** A new **Free Auto pool** panel on the Usage page shows requests, served, fallbacks, failed attempts, exhausted turns and tokens in/out. It also lists each backend in try order with served count and drain/cooldown, plus the recent attempts showing which backend served each one. The data is read locally through `control free-pool status`.
- **Fix found in live testing.** `recentUsageEvents` dropped `failoverFrom`, so the fallback count showed 0 after a real fallback. It now keeps the field, and a test covers it.
- **Docs.** `docs/PROVIDERS.md` (Free Auto section, with Responses and Chat Completions curl examples), the three READMEs, and AGENTS.md. Changelog fragment: `changelog.d/free-auto-pool.md`.

## Verification

- `npm run check`: pass.
- `npm test`: 6118 tests, 6045 pass, 4 fail, 69 skipped. All 4 failures also fail on `origin/main` `0076db6d` on this Linux box (`git archive` checkout), so they are environment failures, not this change:
  - `tray-rebuild` "linked package ancestors" (EISDIR);
  - the 3 `private-writer-cleanup-ownership` "parent path replacement" tests.
- New tests, all passing:
  - `test/free-pool.test.mjs`: classification, cooldowns, catalog parsing and order.
  - `test/free-pool-router.test.mjs`: the real router against a mock upstream. Covers walking past 429, quota and 503 with drains recorded; skipping drained members; no switch after text streamed; exhausted 429; Chat Completions; and the model list hiding members.
  - The `request-diagnostics` `failoverFrom` read-back.
  - A renderer test for the panel.
- `apps/control-center`: `npm run check && npm test`, 126 tests, 125 pass, 1 skipped (Windows-only).
- **Live run** of the real stack (LiteLLM, the API forwarder and the router), with an isolated state dir and ports, against the real Kilo free endpoints:
  - `free-pool refresh` read 13 live Kilo `:free` models. OpenCode Zen listed no free IDs it serves to any caller.
  - `POST /v1/responses` non-streaming: 200, `"free auto works"`.
  - `POST /v1/responses` streaming: 200 SSE with 4 `output_text.delta` events, `"1, 2, 3, 4, 5"`.
  - `POST /cursor/v1/chat/completions` non-streaming: 200 `chat.completion`, content `"5"`.
  - `POST /cursor/v1/chat/completions` streaming: 200 `chat.completion.chunk`, `"Bonjour"`.
  - `GET /cursor/v1/models`: only `free_auto` low/medium/high, with no members listed.
  - **Forced fallback** with `MODEL_ROUTER_FREE_POOL_PREFER=recursive/flint-v1.0:free`. Flint returned a real 503, was drained 2m, and the turn moved to `kilo-auto/free`: 200 `"Red"` (log `failover model=free/recursive/flint-v1.0:free status=503 -> free/auto outcome=free-pool/200`). A later turn skipped the drained member and went straight to the next one.
  - **Exhausted path.** Every member was drained by hand, and the response was 429 `free_pool_exhausted` with `retry_at`. `free-pool reset` cleared the drains.
  - Control Center (Electron) launched against that state showed the real data: 14 members, 1 drained (`UPSTREAM_ERROR, 503`), 2 fallbacks, and the backend that served each attempt.

## Changelog

`changelog.d/free-auto-pool.md`

## Caveats

- **OpenCode Zen lane is empty today.** Every free ID Zen lists right now is client-gated or withdrawn. Getting past that gate would mean impersonating the OpenCode client, so those IDs are excluded. A refresh picks up any free ID Zen serves to any caller.
- **Kilo's free models may log prompts or use them for training** (see the provider notes). Limits are per IP.
- **A refreshed member list takes effect after a router restart.**
- **Chat Completions goes through the router's `/cursor/v1/chat/completions` endpoint.** That endpoint calls Responses non-streaming internally.

Updates `dnspython` from 2.8.0 to 2.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from dnspython's releases.

dnspython 2.9.0

This release fixes a potential excessive CPU consumption issue. Thanks to Evgenios Gkritsis, Constantinos Patsakis, and George Stergiopoulos, for discovering and reporting this issue.

See What's New for details.

The minimum supported version of Python is 3.11.

My thanks to the many people who have contributed to this release. Also thanks to my co-maintainers: Nicki Křížek, Petr Špaček, and Brian Wellington.

This release was published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.

Changelog

Sourced from dnspython's changelog.

2.9.0

  • Decompression chain length is limited to 16. Prior to this change, a maliciously crafted DNS message could cause dns.name.from_wire_parser() to use excessive CPU for DNS name decompression. Applications which processed untrusted DNS wire form messages with dnspython could be degraded or DoS'd by the extra CPU use required.

    Thanks to Evgenios Gkritsis, Constantinos Patsakis, and George Stergiopoulos for finding and reporting this issue.

    See https://github.com/rthalley/dnspython/security/advisories/GHSA-45c3-73f7-pv4m

  • Httpx2 has replaced httpx for HTTPS TCP connections.

  • The minimum supported Python version is now 3.11.

  • DNSSEC now supports ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum signature algorithm.

  • The NSEC3 Next Hashed Owner Name in presentation format is now decoded as base32hex (RFC 5155 Section 1.3, RFC 4648 Extended Hex Alphabet). The letters W, X, Y, and Z are not in that alphabet; they used to be accepted and silently decoded to a different owner name, so to_text of the result did not match the input. They are now rejected.

  • The NID and L64 node/locator ids in presentation format are now rejected when a group contains anything other than hex digits. A sign or underscore, which int() silently accepts, produced a record whose text form did not parse back the same way (RFC 6742).

  • Rdata of a known type in the generic \# syntax, such as an NS record in a zone file, no longer fails to parse when it contains a name under the origin. Its names are relativized as in the type's own text form.

  • The SVCB and HTTPS ech parameter value must now be an ECHConfigList with a correct length prefix and at least 4 octets of content (RFC 9848, RFC 9849). The individual ECHConfig structures are not checked.

  • SVCB and HTTPS SvcParamKeys in presentation format, including those listed in mandatory, must now be spelled as RFC 9460 requires: 1-63 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens. Uppercase keys such as ALPN and keys with underscores such as no_default_alpn are rejected.

  • SVCB and HTTPS presentation format parsing now follows the escaping rules of RFC 9460. SvcParamKeys may not contain escapes (e.g. \097lpn=h2), and in comma-separated values (alpn, docpath) only \, and \\ are valid escapes after character-string decoding (e.g. alpn="h2\\x" is rejected).

Updates `filelock` from 3.32.2 to 4.2.1
Release notes

Sourced from filelock's releases.

4.2.1

Bug fixes

  • On a singleton wrapper, AsyncReadWriteLock.close() and AsyncSoftReadWriteLock.close() end only the holds that tasks acquired through that wrapper. A reader that arrives during close() gets the closed error instead of joining the ending hold. After synchronous code closes or force-releases the shared lock, the wrappers refuse to admit readers into the ended hold, and close() on such a wrapper returns. Closing one wrapper no longer ends a task's nested hold taken through another wrapper on the same path. #832 by @​gaborbernat.
  • ReadWriteLock locks again after a release() that an exception from a signal handler interrupted. The async read-write wrappers stop admitting readers into such a level. The async read-write locks forget a hold whose backend release failed after the backend let go, and they free the memory of each acquire that times out or is canceled. AsyncFileLock returns from release() after a few hundred acquires gave up behind a waiting one. An exception from a signal handler delivered while an AsyncFileLock call joins its queue no longer blocks every later call on that lock. #833 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix ReadWriteLock acting on -journal, -wal or -shm files another process puts beside its database: a write could land in another file, a reader could get in beside a writer, and an acquire could fail. SQLite now opens the database by name only in a directory no other account can write, and through a private hard link elsewhere. On Windows the directory's access control list decides. Where hard links are unavailable, keep the database in a directory other accounts cannot write, such as one under %LOCALAPPDATA%. The lock removes link directories through a checked descriptor rather than by name, reads a link directory's name only when the locking account owns it, and leaves alone a directory with other content renamed onto a link directory's name. A database whose schema takes more than a few kilobytes to load raises ValueError instead of running past the acquire timeout. #834 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix five bugs in opening the lock file. UnixFileLock no longer truncates a file it did not create, such as one renamed to the lock path, and no longer applies mode to it. An on_acquired hook that writes holder metadata now truncates the file itself. A lease (Linux) or an oplock (Windows) on the lock file or a soft lock's marker no longer holds acquire() past its timeout or blocking=False, and an oplock no longer holds release(); ReadWriteLock on Windows waits for its timeout and raises Timeout. On Windows, a mode without group and other bits, such as 0o600, now creates the lock file with an owner-only permission list; the ReadWriteLock database gets the same. The soft locks' writability check no longer follows a symlink swapped in at the lock path. On a filesystem without flock, a contender from another account now waits on a marker it cannot write instead of raising PermissionError. #835 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing a live holder's marker in three cases: the holder and the contender run in Linux time namespaces with different boottime offsets; only one of them can read the boot id; a process other than the owner rewrote the marker. Soft markers no longer carry group or other write bits. A process name containing a carriage return or another line separator no longer makes the stale check raise ValueError. When /proc/self/ns/time exists but cannot be read, the stale check no longer compares start times and keeps the marker. #836 by @​gaborbernat.
  • The async read-write locks record their hold under a task owner, so synchronous code on the executor thread that took the hold can no longer re-enter or release it. AsyncSoftReadWriteLock gives back one level on release, so synchronous readers of a shared singleton keep theirs. SoftReadWriteLock tracks read levels per thread: release() from a thread that holds none raises RuntimeError. After its heartbeat recorded a lost hold, it refuses new acquires until that hold is released. #838 by @​gaborbernat.
  • StrictSoftFileLock creates <path>.filelock and its claims directory with the lock's mode and sets the sticky bit (a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it) on both. On the next acquisition it narrows a directory it owns that an earlier release created wider; it leaves a directory of another account as it is, so remove such leftovers by hand. It reaches claims through a descriptor opened without following symlinks; on Windows it holds both directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). Under a sticky parent such as /tmp it refuses a coordination directory of another account, as SoftReadWriteLock does for <path>.rw. One read grace now covers a whole claim scan, a failed claim cleanup no longer leaves the sentinel descriptor open, and a non-regular node at a sentinel private-record name raises SoftFileLockProtocolError. On Windows, contenders read claims without blocking their owner's unlink. #839 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix a lock reporting a hold the OS had dropped after a signal handler raised during acquire or release. A release that a signal handler cuts short after it has started now completes before the error propagates. A handler that acquires the lock its own thread is releasing now gets RuntimeError instead of a hold that stays held. The singleton cache no longer hands out an is_singleton=True lock or a ReadWriteLock whose finalizer is running, which released the new holder's lock. A signal during os.fork() no longer leaves the other threads blocked in their next lock call, and a fork from another thread no longer waits for a ReadWriteLock acquire on a busy database. #840 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix a lock on a relative path locking a file in the directory the process changed to while the lock waited, and leaving its marker behind on release after such a change. The path resolved when an acquisition starts stays in use until the hold ends. An is_singleton=True lookup no longer returns a cached lock whose relative path now resolves to another file; a held lock still matches the file it holds. A rename of the lock's directory during a hold no longer leaves the marker behind or reports a false lease compromise, and a waiter no longer creates a second lock file in a directory that was renamed away. #841 by @​gaborbernat.
  • SoftReadWriteLock reaches its records through descriptors of <path>.rw and gen or holders opened without following symlinks. On Windows it holds those directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). A tree swapped in after an earlier acquire therefore cannot redirect them. Its heartbeat rewrites a holder record only when the name still leads to the file it created, and does not block on a FIFO (a named pipe). A heartbeat that finds <path>.rw replaced by a symlink or junction reports the hold lost instead of ending the heartbeat thread. A live lock object repeats the ownership check whenever the tree it opens is not the one it prepared. #842 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing or displacing a live holder's marker in five cases. ext4 gave a freed inode number to the next marker. A stalled FileLock removed its ENOSYS placeholder after a peer replaced it. A failed acquire cleaned up after a successor took the path. A stale break left the lock path empty while it checked the marker it had moved. A lifetime break judged a marker by a reused inode number. On Linux and macOS a stale marker now changes hands in one atomic exchange. On other platforms without one, except Windows, including NFS and SMB, the marker stays in place and waits for timeout or break_lock(). Restoring a marker no longer follows a symlink found under the break name. A holder that releases while a peer's exchange has its marker aside leaves a record no lock parses, so the put-back lands a marker that ages out. A lease heartbeat that finds another file at the lock path once, while a peer's break has its marker aside, waits for the next refresh before it reports a compromise. A contender that finds a dead breaker's marker puts back the marker that breaker left under its break name. A marker is the breaker's own only when it names the breaker's process on this host; the same process number on another host is a holder. A contender takes a stranded marker under a name of its own before it puts the marker back, so two contenders no longer reverse each other's exchange and remove the live holder's marker. A claim left behind by a failed put-back is retried on the next poll. #843 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Canceling an AsyncReadWriteLock or AsyncSoftReadWriteLock acquire that waits for another process now stops the wait and raises the cancellation. It used to wait until that process released, or raise Timeout. A thread_local=True AsyncFileLock that threads with their own event loops share no longer deadlocks when one thread waits for the lock while another holds it. #844 by @​gaborbernat.
  • SoftReadWriteLock refuses a commit that lands a whole retention window behind the log, so two committers stalled at adjacent generations can no longer admit a second writer. Its stale check samples the clock before it reads a holder record, so a pause between the two no longer counts as time the record stayed unchanged. #845 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix a SoftFileLock contender evicting an empty marker after two seconds while its owner held the lock. The owner is a SoftFileLock before 3.22, which writes nothing into its marker, or a current one still writing its record. An empty marker now reads as held, and timeout, lifetime or break_lock() clears it. A contender that finds an empty marker a dead breaker left aside puts it back instead of removing it. #846 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix ReadWriteLock on Windows acting on -journal and -wal files another account places beside its database: an acquire could fail with OperationalError, or SQLite could replay the journal and delete the file it names. The lock now reads the database directory's access control list. Where an account other than the locking account, SYSTEM and Administrators can add or remove names, SQLite opens a hard link inside a directory only those accounts can write. A filesystem without hard links raises OSError. #854 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix SoftReadWriteLock subclasses sharing singleton instances with the base class or sibling subclasses. Each concrete class now keeps its own cache and construction guard, including after fork, while preserving cooperative class-definition keywords. #855 by @​AryanRG.

Performance

Updates `litellm` from 1.96.2 to 1.100.4
Release notes

Sourced from litellm's releases.

v1.100.4

Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.4

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.100.4/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.4

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

What's Changed

  • ci: enable trusted publishing releases (v3.x) by @​mcollina in fastify/fast-uri#229

Updates `undici` from 6.29.0 to 6.29.1
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v6.29.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

CVE-2026-109932 · GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

Updates `fast-uri` from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9
Release notes

Sourced from fast-uri's releases.

v3.1.9

Security

This security release fixes four URI parsing and normalization vulnerabilities in fast-uri 3.x. Applications that process untrusted URI input should upgrade to v3.1.9.

  • Medium — URI scheme spoofing through percent-encoded schemes (GHSA-w74x-v6f9-j3xg, CVE-2026-110306): percent-encoded scheme input is now rejected instead of being decoded into a live scheme.
  • Medium — Host confusion during domain-host canonicalization (GHSA-wjr9-j795-jxcr, CVE-2026-110180): malformed domain hosts containing ambiguous delimiters or stripped control characters are now rejected instead of being silently rewritten.
  • Low — Incorrect relative-reference normalization (GHSA-xhq7-xmqj-769h, CVE-2026-110095): dot-segment removal now preserves the resolution semantics of relative references.
  • Low — Scheme injection in suffix references (GHSA-333x-w4r6-6crp, CVE-2026-110725): first-segment colons in path-only suffix references are now escaped so the output is not reparsed as a scheme.

Upgrade with:

npm install fast-uri@3.1.9

Thanks to @​zekth for reporting the scheme, host, and relative-reference issues, and to @​UlisesGascon for finding the suffix-reference issue and reviewing the remediations.

Updates `undici` from 8.11.2 to 8.12.3
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v6.29.1

Security fixes

High severity

Denial of service via TLS 1.2 certificate-changing renegotiation

CVE-2026-87018 · GHSA-qrxm-fqhp-jwvm

A malicious or compromised HTTPS server could crash the Node.js process by initiating TLS 1.2 renegotiation and presenting a different, CA-trusted certificate whose hostname did not match the requested host. The resulting socket error reached an assertion in undici's HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 connection handling. This release handles post-connect certificate errors without terminating the process.

TLS certificate validation bypass through dropped Agent options

CVE-2026-109383 · GHSA-2m5v-pch6-74hx

Agent used a JSON-based clone for constructor options, which silently removed function-valued TLS options such as checkServerIdentity. Applications relying on custom certificate or public-key verification could therefore accept a certificate that the callback was intended to reject. This release preserves TLS options when creating per-origin dispatchers.

Denial of service through excessive Content-Encoding values

CVE-2026-109869 · GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c

A malicious HTTP server could crash the Node.js process by returning more than five content codings and closing the connection before sending the body. Although fetch() rejected the response, an error from an orphaned internal stream could remain unhandled. This release validates the content-encoding chain before creating the body stream and aborts oversized chains safely.

Medium severity

Denial of service through unbounded EventSource parser state

CVE-2026-109924 · GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685

A malicious Server-Sent Events endpoint could exhaust process memory by sending many tiny data: fields without completing an event, or by splitting an unfinished line across many chunks. This release bounds retained EventSource parser state, including field counts, buffered chunks, unfinished-line length, and retained field data.

Denial of service through unbounded automatic WebSocket PONG buffering

CVE-2026-109932 · GHSA-9fm3-97px-rjf6

A malicious WebSocket server could exhaust process memory by flooding the client with PING frames while not reading the automatic PONG responses. undici previously ignored socket backpressure and allowed the outbound queue to grow without bound. This release pauses frame parsing when PONG writes encounter backpressure and resumes after the socket drains.

title: chore(deps): bump the pip group across 1 directory with 3 updates
body:
Bumps the pip group with 3 updates in the /requirements directory: [dnspython](https://github.com/rthalley/dnspython), [filelock](https://github.com/tox-dev/py-filelock) and [litellm](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm). Updates `dnspython` from 2.8.0 to 2.9.0
Release notes

Sourced from dnspython's releases.

dnspython 2.9.0

This release fixes a potential excessive CPU consumption issue. Thanks to Evgenios Gkritsis, Constantinos Patsakis, and George Stergiopoulos, for discovering and reporting this issue.

See What's New for details.

The minimum supported version of Python is 3.11.

My thanks to the many people who have contributed to this release. Also thanks to my co-maintainers: Nicki Křížek, Petr Špaček, and Brian Wellington.

This release was published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing.

Changelog

Sourced from dnspython's changelog.

2.9.0

  • Decompression chain length is limited to 16. Prior to this change, a maliciously crafted DNS message could cause dns.name.from_wire_parser() to use excessive CPU for DNS name decompression. Applications which processed untrusted DNS wire form messages with dnspython could be degraded or DoS'd by the extra CPU use required.

    Thanks to Evgenios Gkritsis, Constantinos Patsakis, and George Stergiopoulos for finding and reporting this issue.

    See https://github.com/rthalley/dnspython/security/advisories/GHSA-45c3-73f7-pv4m

  • Httpx2 has replaced httpx for HTTPS TCP connections.

  • The minimum supported Python version is now 3.11.

  • DNSSEC now supports ML-DSA-44, a post-quantum signature algorithm.

  • The NSEC3 Next Hashed Owner Name in presentation format is now decoded as base32hex (RFC 5155 Section 1.3, RFC 4648 Extended Hex Alphabet). The letters W, X, Y, and Z are not in that alphabet; they used to be accepted and silently decoded to a different owner name, so to_text of the result did not match the input. They are now rejected.

  • The NID and L64 node/locator ids in presentation format are now rejected when a group contains anything other than hex digits. A sign or underscore, which int() silently accepts, produced a record whose text form did not parse back the same way (RFC 6742).

  • Rdata of a known type in the generic \# syntax, such as an NS record in a zone file, no longer fails to parse when it contains a name under the origin. Its names are relativized as in the type's own text form.

  • The SVCB and HTTPS ech parameter value must now be an ECHConfigList with a correct length prefix and at least 4 octets of content (RFC 9848, RFC 9849). The individual ECHConfig structures are not checked.

  • SVCB and HTTPS SvcParamKeys in presentation format, including those listed in mandatory, must now be spelled as RFC 9460 requires: 1-63 lowercase letters, digits, or hyphens. Uppercase keys such as ALPN and keys with underscores such as no_default_alpn are rejected.

  • SVCB and HTTPS presentation format parsing now follows the escaping rules of RFC 9460. SvcParamKeys may not contain escapes (e.g. \097lpn=h2), and in comma-separated values (alpn, docpath) only \, and \\ are valid escapes after character-string decoding (e.g. alpn="h2\\x" is rejected).

Updates `filelock` from 3.32.2 to 4.2.1
Release notes

Sourced from filelock's releases.

4.2.1

Bug fixes

  • On a singleton wrapper, AsyncReadWriteLock.close() and AsyncSoftReadWriteLock.close() end only the holds that tasks acquired through that wrapper. A reader that arrives during close() gets the closed error instead of joining the ending hold. After synchronous code closes or force-releases the shared lock, the wrappers refuse to admit readers into the ended hold, and close() on such a wrapper returns. Closing one wrapper no longer ends a task's nested hold taken through another wrapper on the same path. #832 by @​gaborbernat.
  • ReadWriteLock locks again after a release() that an exception from a signal handler interrupted. The async read-write wrappers stop admitting readers into such a level. The async read-write locks forget a hold whose backend release failed after the backend let go, and they free the memory of each acquire that times out or is canceled. AsyncFileLock returns from release() after a few hundred acquires gave up behind a waiting one. An exception from a signal handler delivered while an AsyncFileLock call joins its queue no longer blocks every later call on that lock. #833 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix ReadWriteLock acting on -journal, -wal or -shm files another process puts beside its database: a write could land in another file, a reader could get in beside a writer, and an acquire could fail. SQLite now opens the database by name only in a directory no other account can write, and through a private hard link elsewhere. On Windows the directory's access control list decides. Where hard links are unavailable, keep the database in a directory other accounts cannot write, such as one under %LOCALAPPDATA%. The lock removes link directories through a checked descriptor rather than by name, reads a link directory's name only when the locking account owns it, and leaves alone a directory with other content renamed onto a link directory's name. A database whose schema takes more than a few kilobytes to load raises ValueError instead of running past the acquire timeout. #834 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix five bugs in opening the lock file. UnixFileLock no longer truncates a file it did not create, such as one renamed to the lock path, and no longer applies mode to it. An on_acquired hook that writes holder metadata now truncates the file itself. A lease (Linux) or an oplock (Windows) on the lock file or a soft lock's marker no longer holds acquire() past its timeout or blocking=False, and an oplock no longer holds release(); ReadWriteLock on Windows waits for its timeout and raises Timeout. On Windows, a mode without group and other bits, such as 0o600, now creates the lock file with an owner-only permission list; the ReadWriteLock database gets the same. The soft locks' writability check no longer follows a symlink swapped in at the lock path. On a filesystem without flock, a contender from another account now waits on a marker it cannot write instead of raising PermissionError. #835 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing a live holder's marker in three cases: the holder and the contender run in Linux time namespaces with different boottime offsets; only one of them can read the boot id; a process other than the owner rewrote the marker. Soft markers no longer carry group or other write bits. A process name containing a carriage return or another line separator no longer makes the stale check raise ValueError. When /proc/self/ns/time exists but cannot be read, the stale check no longer compares start times and keeps the marker. #836 by @​gaborbernat.
  • The async read-write locks record their hold under a task owner, so synchronous code on the executor thread that took the hold can no longer re-enter or release it. AsyncSoftReadWriteLock gives back one level on release, so synchronous readers of a shared singleton keep theirs. SoftReadWriteLock tracks read levels per thread: release() from a thread that holds none raises RuntimeError. After its heartbeat recorded a lost hold, it refuses new acquires until that hold is released. #838 by @​gaborbernat.
  • StrictSoftFileLock creates <path>.filelock and its claims directory with the lock's mode and sets the sticky bit (a directory flag that lets only a file's owner remove it) on both. On the next acquisition it narrows a directory it owns that an earlier release created wider; it leaves a directory of another account as it is, so remove such leftovers by hand. It reaches claims through a descriptor opened without following symlinks; on Windows it holds both directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). Under a sticky parent such as /tmp it refuses a coordination directory of another account, as SoftReadWriteLock does for <path>.rw. One read grace now covers a whole claim scan, a failed claim cleanup no longer leaves the sentinel descriptor open, and a non-regular node at a sentinel private-record name raises SoftFileLockProtocolError. On Windows, contenders read claims without blocking their owner's unlink. #839 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix a lock reporting a hold the OS had dropped after a signal handler raised during acquire or release. A release that a signal handler cuts short after it has started now completes before the error propagates. A handler that acquires the lock its own thread is releasing now gets RuntimeError instead of a hold that stays held. The singleton cache no longer hands out an is_singleton=True lock or a ReadWriteLock whose finalizer is running, which released the new holder's lock. A signal during os.fork() no longer leaves the other threads blocked in their next lock call, and a fork from another thread no longer waits for a ReadWriteLock acquire on a busy database. #840 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix a lock on a relative path locking a file in the directory the process changed to while the lock waited, and leaving its marker behind on release after such a change. The path resolved when an acquisition starts stays in use until the hold ends. An is_singleton=True lookup no longer returns a cached lock whose relative path now resolves to another file; a held lock still matches the file it holds. A rename of the lock's directory during a hold no longer leaves the marker behind or reports a false lease compromise, and a waiter no longer creates a second lock file in a directory that was renamed away. #841 by @​gaborbernat.
  • SoftReadWriteLock reaches its records through descriptors of <path>.rw and gen or holders opened without following symlinks. On Windows it holds those directories open and refuses a junction (a directory that points at another directory). A tree swapped in after an earlier acquire therefore cannot redirect them. Its heartbeat rewrites a holder record only when the name still leads to the file it created, and does not block on a FIFO (a named pipe). A heartbeat that finds <path>.rw replaced by a symlink or junction reports the hold lost instead of ending the heartbeat thread. A live lock object repeats the ownership check whenever the tree it opens is not the one it prepared. #842 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix SoftFileLock, MarkerSoftFileLock and SoftFileLease removing or displacing a live holder's marker in five cases. ext4 gave a freed inode number to the next marker. A stalled FileLock removed its ENOSYS placeholder after a peer replaced it. A failed acquire cleaned up after a successor took the path. A stale break left the lock path empty while it checked the marker it had moved. A lifetime break judged a marker by a reused inode number. On Linux and macOS a stale marker now changes hands in one atomic exchange. On other platforms without one, except Windows, including NFS and SMB, the marker stays in place and waits for timeout or break_lock(). Restoring a marker no longer follows a symlink found under the break name. A holder that releases while a peer's exchange has its marker aside leaves a record no lock parses, so the put-back lands a marker that ages out. A lease heartbeat that finds another file at the lock path once, while a peer's break has its marker aside, waits for the next refresh before it reports a compromise. A contender that finds a dead breaker's marker puts back the marker that breaker left under its break name. A marker is the breaker's own only when it names the breaker's process on this host; the same process number on another host is a holder. A contender takes a stranded marker under a name of its own before it puts the marker back, so two contenders no longer reverse each other's exchange and remove the live holder's marker. A claim left behind by a failed put-back is retried on the next poll. #843 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Canceling an AsyncReadWriteLock or AsyncSoftReadWriteLock acquire that waits for another process now stops the wait and raises the cancellation. It used to wait until that process released, or raise Timeout. A thread_local=True AsyncFileLock that threads with their own event loops share no longer deadlocks when one thread waits for the lock while another holds it. #844 by @​gaborbernat.
  • SoftReadWriteLock refuses a commit that lands a whole retention window behind the log, so two committers stalled at adjacent generations can no longer admit a second writer. Its stale check samples the clock before it reads a holder record, so a pause between the two no longer counts as time the record stayed unchanged. #845 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix a SoftFileLock contender evicting an empty marker after two seconds while its owner held the lock. The owner is a SoftFileLock before 3.22, which writes nothing into its marker, or a current one still writing its record. An empty marker now reads as held, and timeout, lifetime or break_lock() clears it. A contender that finds an empty marker a dead breaker left aside puts it back instead of removing it. #846 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix ReadWriteLock on Windows acting on -journal and -wal files another account places beside its database: an acquire could fail with OperationalError, or SQLite could replay the journal and delete the file it names. The lock now reads the database directory's access control list. Where an account other than the locking account, SYSTEM and Administrators can add or remove names, SQLite opens a hard link inside a directory only those accounts can write. A filesystem without hard links raises OSError. #854 by @​gaborbernat.
  • Fix SoftReadWriteLock subclasses sharing singleton instances with the base class or sibling subclasses. Each concrete class now keeps its own cache and construction guard, including after fork, while preserving cooperative class-definition keywords. #855 by @​AryanRG.

New Contributors

  • @​AryanRG made their first contribution in #855

🐍 PyPI release

📜 Full Changelog

4.2.0

Bug fixes

  • Fix StrictSoftFileLock raising SoftFileLockProtocolError on Windows when a contender read a claim whose owner was still finishing its unlink. #829 by @​gaborbernat.

Performance

  • import filelock is about twice as fast: lock types other than FileLock load on first use. #831 by @​gaborbernat.

Release notes

v1.100.4

Verify Docker Image Signature

All LiteLLM Docker images are signed with cosign. Every release is signed with the same key introduced in commit 0112e53.

Verify using the pinned commit hash (recommended):

A commit hash is cryptographically immutable, so this is the strongest way to ensure you are using the original signing key:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/0112e53046018d726492c814b3644b7d376029d0/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.4

Verify using the release tag (convenience):

Tags are protected in this repository and resolve to the same key. This option is easier to read but relies on tag protection rules:

cosign verify \
  --key https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BerriAI/litellm/v1.100.4/cosign.pub \
  ghcr.io/berriai/litellm:v1.100.4

Expected output:

The following checks were performed on each of these signatures:
  - The cosign claims were validated
  - The signatures were verified against the specified public key

title: test: isolate homes and host Keychain before runtime imports
body:
## Summary

Ordinary tests can import runtime paths before choosing fixture state, inherit higher-priority credential/state overrides, and reach the host Keychain even after changing HOME. Preload temporary homes and synthetic Keychain handling before imports in root, Windows CI, and Control Center test entrypoints. Child commands retain explicitly selected fixture paths.

Use the locked Playwright headless shell outside the isolated home in Electron CI and native macOS UI builds. Renderer tests use the installed default browser unless explicitly overridden, release local servers on launch failure, and await actual login-child settlement. Startup cleanup fixtures isolate every forwarder port.

## Latest main compatibility

Upstream #1110 added a free/auto Usage test that still asserted an explicit Chromium path was present. With this PR's default-browser policy that override is correctly undefined, despite a working installed browser. This caused identical pre-launch failures in Linux and Windows Electron jobs of run 41053392400.

Head `08506cc48513d0f73ea3d27a3d3e5fda32e59e30` integrates main `7118c99d2acd0b6c732995ce4bf438beaa3ce34f` and deletes that single obsolete assertion. Actual browser launch and every free/auto UI assertion are unchanged. The complete PR remains the same 18-file isolation change: +363/-53 against that main revision.

## Verification

- With a built renderer and installed default headless browser, the original free/auto test fails at the obsolete assertion when no override is set. The same real test passes after that one-line deletion.
- Full local desktop suite: **121 passed, 6 Windows platform skips**. App TypeScript/JavaScript checks, production UI build, root `npm run check`, and whitespace checks pass.
- Fresh full CI is required for current head `08506cc4`. Prior-head successes and the failed run above are historical evidence, not current-head results.

This replaces [#1104](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/pull/1104); its discussion and earlier validation remain there. Source review: [fork PR #54](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/54).

## Changelog

`isolate-test-credentials.md`, `renderer-server-launch-cleanup.md`, and `generation-renderer-launch-cleanup.md`.

title: refactor: reuse locale fallback and preserve selected UI languages
body:
Four partial native language tables repeat 624 English source strings as identical English values. The existing lookup already returns the source text when a translation is absent. Separately, quota accessibility labels reduce the selected language to a Chinese Boolean, so Traditional Chinese countdowns become English; five partial browser-panel catalogs also contain a copied Chinese savings message.

Remove the duplicate native entries and use the existing fallback. Pass the selected language directly to the quota formatter and remove its obsolete Boolean parameter. Delete the five incorrect panel overrides so they use the existing English message with the same interpolated counters. Real translations and both complete Chinese catalogs are preserved. The change removes 666 lines and adds 45 across source, tests and changelog fragments.

Validation:

- Compared all 2,360 original native-table lookups before and after: identical output. Deleting a real translation is detected by the same comparison in each of the four tables.
- Compared 3,621 panel translations using the actual `t()` implementation: only the five intended savings messages change; interpolation and both Chinese catalogs remain intact. All 18 focused panel/localization tests pass.
- Exact source head `97a65262` passed the fork's full CI, including 142 executed native Swift tests, desktop packaging and all three runtime platforms. Native test logs confirm the new Traditional Chinese accessibility and language-fallback cases ran.
- Reviewed against current main `7118c99d`: all affected source/test files are unchanged since the original review base, and the merge preview is clean. This change has no dependency on #1115. The new upstream CI will validate the merge with current main.

Fork review and backup: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/38

title: fix: preserve reasoning and vendor metadata in assistant tool history
body:
When a Responses-to-Chat bridge splits an assistant tool turn into a call item and a commentary item, the API forwarder's duplicate coalescer keeps content and tool calls but discards reasoning and vendor metadata on the later item. For example, two reasoning fragments become only the first fragment before reaching the provider.

Reuse the existing shared assistant-history repair and delete the duplicate implementation. If conflicting opaque metadata prevents merging, preserve the original history and real tool result; the subsequent missing-result repair must not replace that result with a synthetic stub. Ordinary mergeable histories and missing-result repair retain their existing behavior.

Validation:

- The same mock-forwarder regression fails with the original implementation: `first thought` instead of `first thought\nsecond thought`. It passes with this change, including vendor metadata and conflicting-history assertions.
- Three real loopback API-forwarder cases and 30 shared-fold/reasoning-replay tests pass using synthetic data and an isolated test environment.
- Exact source head `0ea94d7e` passed full fork CI on Windows, Linux and macOS, plus desktop packaging. Current main `7118c99d` has no changes to the affected forwarder, routing tests, shared fold or reasoning replay; the merge preview is clean.
- JavaScript syntax, application-manifest, changelog and whitespace checks pass. This change has no dependency on #1115 or #1116; its new upstream CI will validate integration with current main.

Fork review and backup: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/39

title: fix: release native error peek before relaying the original response
body:
An oversized native auto-review error can hang before Codex receives it. The classifier reads a cloned response; canceling that peek waits for the original tee branch, while the router cannot start relaying the original until the peek returns.

Let this peek start cancellation without awaiting the separately owned branch. Ordinary body readers still await their cleanup, and overflow cancellation runs once. Keep the original response's status, headers and body intact.

Validation:

- The same loopback Router regression times out with the original implementation and succeeds with the fix, preserving the original 400 status, header and complete error body with one upstream request.
- Tested the change combined with current main `7118c99d` (merge tree `078facb0`): all 22 body-reader, reviewer-state and Router integration tests pass. These cover oversized and aborted clones, ordinary owned-stream cleanup, reviewer exhaustion and successful native decisions.
- Changed JavaScript syntax, application manifests, changelog fragments and whitespace checks pass. Full fork CI for exact source head `78344b00` already passed on Windows, Linux and macOS, including desktop packaging; the new upstream CI will check current-main integration again.

Fork review and backup: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/40

title: refactor: use durable Antigravity project context
body:
Successful Antigravity project discovery is persisted before returning. Later calls already read that durable record and return a resolved project before reaching the separate in-memory success cache, so the cache and its generation counters add a second representation that normal resolved requests never use.

Delete the success cache and the bookkeeping used only to populate it. Keep concurrent-discovery deduplication, session-generation checks, durable project-revision checks, cross-process invalidation and the existing 30-minute absence retry window. The OAuth session change only updates a comment about what disconnect clears.

Validation:

- All 13 project tests pass with both the original and simplified implementations, including concurrent discovery, delayed cross-process invalidation, disconnect, account replacement and observing updated durable metadata without another discovery request.
- A deliberate stale-caller-read control makes the durable-metadata regression fail, confirming that it detects the wrong authority.
- Additional controls verify no discovery inside the absence window, one discovery at its exact 30-minute boundary, and explicit refresh inside that window. All use synthetic credentials and mocked upstream responses.
- Changed JavaScript syntax, application manifests, changelog fragments and whitespace checks pass. Full fork CI for exact source head `92e9bdf9` passed on Windows, Linux and macOS, including desktop packaging. Current main `7118c99d` has no changes to the Antigravity implementation or tests, and the merge preview is clean.

Fork review and backup: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/41

CI follow-up: the original upstream Windows Electron run timed out waiting for the first Traditional Chinese Settings heading. Its precise mechanism remains unconfirmed. Commit `c9683223` adds failure-only selection events, language/heading state and browser-error evidence while preserving the original assertion, timeout and exception. Both complete Chinese UI flows pass locally, and a deliberately absent heading still fails with the new evidence. Current-head fork CI `41180457330` and upstream CI `41180458518` passed; these green runs are not claimed as proof of the earlier timeout's root cause.

title: test: remove wasteful fixtures and false-positive assertions
body:
Log-rotation tests write roughly 128 MiB across four oversized fixtures even though the existing API accepts a test byte limit. Installer and release tests can also accept a missing prerequisite because `indexOf()` returns `-1`, which compares before a later operation.

Use the existing byte-limit argument to reduce those four fixture payloads to 159 bytes, retain the explicit production 32 MiB default check, compare exact file contents and exercise a real failed rename. Share an order assertion that requires both operations to exist before comparing positions. Remove one panel test that duplicates its own expressions without exercising the renderer; tests invoking the actual speed helper remain. Product code is unchanged.

Validation:

- All four affected suites pass locally: 74 passed, 11 existing platform/shell skips. Exact source head `1c10590e` also passed full fork CI on Windows, Linux and macOS, including desktop packaging.
- Complete callbacks for five affected order checks accept the shipped scripts. Removing the prerequisite still passes the original callbacks and fails the corrected ones; missing-before, missing-after and reversed-order controls also pass.
- Mutating the real rotation implementation to ignore the injected limit or skip the rename is detected by the small-file tests. The product file is restored after each control.
- Reviewed against latest main `c3119715`: affected tests, installer scripts, release workflow and rotation implementation have no intervening changes; the merge preview is clean.

Fork review and backup: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/42

title: refactor: remove unused internal helper entry points
body:
Several internal helpers have no production consumers, while the supported commands already implement the same work elsewhere. Remove those extra entry points: the duplicate setup onboarding flow, the Antigravity token-writer alias, the old local-model removal helper, and the parsed-object number coercer. Keep the shared terminal prompts and the actual setup, session writer, uninstall transaction, and raw JSON argument normalization paths.

The desktop picker also has an array-shaped bulk mutation that no preload, type declaration, or renderer caller exposes. Keep its Boolean show/hide-all API, which publishes once. Replace the Vertex helper-only assertion with an invocation of the real setup command.

Validation:

- Reviewed every hunk and searched callers on current upstream main `7c5e75b80640ea838495ac22c7c1a236e9316be5`; no new consumers of the removed entry points. Clean merge preview; the shared terminal prompt bodies are identical.
- Actual picker callbacks preserve Boolean show/hide behavior and each publish once. A positive control reaches the old repeated-publication array path; the revised callback rejects that shape before publication.
- The retained uninstall transaction passes injected success, cancellation, publication-failure and removal-failure controls, including state restoration. No installed model, live service, or provider is used.
- Local related suites: 235 passed, 10 platform skips, one existing Antigravity worker-readiness timeout. The failed assertion waits five seconds for a fixture worker; no session execution code changed. Both current-main and revised session modules pass the isolated case. Timing traces show two Windows ACL subprocess operations before readiness; delaying those operations reproduces the same timeout with either module. The original failure had no per-step timing, so its exact OS-level delay remains unconfirmed. No timeout, retry, or assertion was weakened for this PR.
- The exact published source head passed full fork CI on Windows, macOS and Linux, both Electron jobs, Homebrew formula validation and the unified native macOS application: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40993165131 . Changed JavaScript parses and `git diff --check` passes.

Reviewed source: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/43 . This PR carries only that existing audit item.

title: refactor: remove standalone subagent readiness report
body:
Remove the standalone subagent readiness report and its mandatory skill step. The script maintains its own state-path lookup and infers client availability from a catalog-wide listing, file mtimes and a guessed eight-model display boundary. It has no runtime caller; its only callers are the skill and one certification document.

Point route troubleshooting at the existing `control subagents explain <slug>` command, which reports selection, capability and agent-definition blockers through the shared runtime. The old catalog-wide listing, mtime warning and guessed display boundary are deliberately removed. Model publication, capability policy, verification and spawning implementations are unchanged.

Validation:

- Reviewed all four changed files against current main `65b2f5b8dec192cb798976b565965fea70a3bf66`; clean merge preview, with no new consumers of the deleted report.
- Temporarily integrated main `7c5e75b80640ea838495ac22c7c1a236e9316be5` into the reviewed head and ran multi-agent state, route explanation, real CLI explanation and override-documentation tests: **32 passed, zero skipped**. The CLI cases cover ready and blocked routes and verify that explanation leaves fixture state unchanged. Main subsequently merged #1121; its unrelated helper deletions changed none of this item's files, the explanation/state implementations, or these tests, so those results are reused.
- A positive-control search finds the two report references on main; the revised tree has none. The report file is absent. `git diff --check` passes; the temporary integration was removed and the reviewed worktree is clean.
- Reused complete fork CI for this exact source head `79f5c82c8d374fee0662de7f1b78207eba4be5fe`: Windows, macOS and Linux runtime suites, both Electron jobs, Homebrew formula checks and unified native macOS packaging passed. https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40851899852

Reviewed source: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/44 . No new command or paid provider probe is introduced.

title: refactor: remove heuristic tool-result shaping
body:
Remove the separate RTK-style tool-result shaper, its compaction flag and newly emitted shaping counters. Its keyword/indentation rules cannot establish which evidence is dispensable: an injected pure-policy control turns an 18,828-byte Chinese configuration into 378 bytes and loses an explicit business requirement. After deletion, both string and structured newest results stay exact.

That control is **not evidence of data loss in the current Router integration**. The whole-history summarizer already clears its tools, so the local-readback gate keeps its results intact. Delete the separate shaping path rather than maintain another policy around it. Ordinary aging still considers only eligible consumed old results, retains exact originals and requires authenticated local readback. Previously issued receipts and historical shaping usage records remain readable.

Update the English, Simplified Chinese and Japanese client docs and the documentation site. This makes no claim about provider-billed token savings; the current tool-less compaction path already receives full results. Also make the existing forged-proof test change the proof deterministically instead of occasionally leaving its suffix unchanged.

Validation against main `65b2f5b8dec192cb798976b565965fea70a3bf66`:

- Reviewed every changed hunk and all remaining shaping references. No live shaper imports or flags remain; remaining counters read historical usage, and retained receipt prefixes identify older records.
- **126 tests passed, zero skipped** on a temporary integration of that main: aging, recovery, retention, settings and usage events. Includes exact Unicode/CRLF readback, expiry, access/storage failures, forged and cross-context proofs, and instruction preservation.
- **Three actual loopback Router tests passed, zero skipped**: native aging opt-in and consumed-only behavior, exact newest output on ordinary/tool-less compaction requests, and compaction image limits. No provider generation or deployed Router was used.
- Before/after pure-policy controls cover both text representations. Ordinary consumed-result receipts match main exactly; previously issued receipt formats remain unchanged. The temporary integration was removed and the published worktree is clean. Changed JavaScript parses and `git diff --check` passes.
- Full three-platform runtime and desktop CI passed for runtime/test revision `4eec95945a9bd51e714d1619dec02e3a2d12bd59`: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40851943564 . Published head `80cf4e77635438c6e3a93e1e6ce6581c46421b06` adds only the documentation-site correction; runtime and test bytes are identical. Its fresh fork CI is also running.

Reviewed source: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/45 . This is one existing audit item, with its missing companion documentation corrected.

title: Strip internal message metadata from native input
body:
Native replay can include `internal_chat_message_metadata_passthrough` on input items. Forwarding that bookkeeping object causes the native endpoint to reject affected histories with HTTP 400 (`content_token_count` is unknown).

This removes only that top-level field in the shared native input normalizer, before message, call, reasoning and compaction handling. Conversation content, call IDs, encrypted state and nested fields are preserved.

Validation:
- Focused regression failed before the fix and passes afterward (1/1).
- Source/test syntax checks, changelog validation and whitespace checks pass.
- The test executes the source helper with identity stubs for surrounding normalizers; full routing integration and live provider checks were not run.

title: refactor: remove unconnected credential migration API
body:
Remove the credential-store migration and rollback exports, their snapshot/manifest helpers, legacy-only parser branches, and migration-directory override. Latest main has no installer, control command, or runtime consumer of these exports; only their dedicated tests invoke them. Keep the metadata schema, secret-reference operations, provider binding, redaction, private atomic writes and existing secret readers used by the running router.

Routing fixtures now register a reference through the same add operation as production. Four touched fixtures also bind the highest-priority state alias to their own temporary directories. Unsupported metadata schemas remain rejected; this does not migrate, delete or rewrite an installed user's credential files.

Validation against main `39894f9ea8fb6d1482b64affd1858e285baedb2b`:

- Reviewed every changed hunk and all six live import sites of the credential-store module. Removed exports have no live callers; current schema parsing and reference operations remain. Clean merge preview; affected source and test files have not drifted from the original review base on main.
- Exact source head `7b5667cc315e07248485c8b15a3d702c9f854d38` passed complete Windows, macOS and Linux runtime CI, both Electron jobs, Homebrew formula checks and unified native macOS packaging: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40837206531 . No source adaptation is included.
- Temporary current-main integration ran the five credential suites: **29 passed, one locally cancelled at its existing 30-second test deadline**. Two real-symlink cases were excluded after this host returned `EPERM` when creating a fixture symlink; those tests remain unchanged and are covered by the published CI.
- The cancelled case was instrumented: status returned while the publication lock was held; a diagnostic-only larger outer wait completed every original assertion in 35.7 seconds (status approximately 7.3 seconds, mutation 20.9 seconds, plus setup). The original test deadline was restored. No runtime timeout, retry or assertion was weakened.
- Four real fixture-initialization probes with a hostile inherited state alias preserved their sentinel directories. Removing one fixture's alias binding makes the negative control detect a mismatched cached production `STATE_DIR`; the fixture was restored byte-for-byte.
- Additional end-to-end hostile-environment probes were not uniformly green: one forwarding run returned 503 without a captured error body; another reached the successful response but its remaining-cooldown assertion observed 125.5 seconds after local work elapsed. The pool's five-second retry budget and that timing oracle are unchanged by this PR. The first 503's exact mechanism remains unconfirmed; these extra probes are not reported as passing or attributed to this deletion.
- Changed JavaScript parses and `git diff --check` passes. Temporary integration and diagnostic edits were removed; the reviewed worktree is clean. All operations used temporary fixtures and loopback servers.

Reviewed source: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/46 . This carries only that existing audit item.

title: fix: keep damaged provider policy from enabling routes
body:
An unreadable or incompatible provider-selection file currently falls back to every built-in provider. A selection containing only unknown IDs does the same, and pruning deletes that file, turning it into the legacy no-file default. A configured model the operator did not select can consequently become a failover or vision candidate.

Keep a present damaged policy empty and diagnostic, and retain an explicit empty selection when pruning unknown-only IDs. Validate member types before resolving IDs. An ENOENT read uses the legacy default only when the directory entry itself is absent, so a dangling symlink cannot enable unrelated routes. Existing absent-file compatibility, explicit show-all overrides, aliases, variant families, generic-provider handling and strict writes are preserved.

Validation:

- The unchanged reviewed head `77ab49a63ee4215f2e280474f82b4b7a5be18ac3` passed the [fork's full CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40993419501), including Linux/macOS/Windows runtime and desktop checks.
- Temporarily integrated with current upstream main `39894f9ea8fb6d1482b64affd1858e285baedb2b`: provider selection, model failover, vision bridge and vision state suites passed 157 tests; the real file-symlink fixture was skipped because this Windows host lacks symlink privilege. Deterministic directory-entry fault cases passed.
- Three negative controls failed against main's original implementation and passed with the fix: non-string members, ENOENT with a present/inaccessible entry, and a configured remote model excluded from failover and vision under damaged policy. The latter also proves that explicit selection makes the model eligible and explicit recovery selects only the requested family.
- Repository syntax/changelog/application checks and `git diff --check` passed on that integration. The temporary merge was then aborted; the published source remains the exact reviewed head.

Source review: [TruthNian/codex-router#47](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/47), audit finding `providers:P6`. No unmerged prerequisite is included.

title: fix: preserve discovery opt-out at credential reader boundaries
body:
A damaged discovery policy can currently re-enable reads of retained router keys or another CLI's session. Keep discovery disabled for corrupt, unreadable or unrecognized markers and report the setup recovery action. Missing-marker compatibility, valid enabled/disabled modes and explicit environment overrides retain their behavior.

Enforce the opt-out at direct Kimi, Grok and Devin session readers/refreshers and before service environment rendering inspects pooled secrets. The latest main integration preserves Kimi's captured request context and checks the opt-out before even inspecting an explicitly supplied context.

Necessary CI adaptations are limited to fixture reliability and failure evidence:
- The Windows main-test step uses the existing bounded synchronous PowerShell startup allowance of 45 seconds after an observed 15-second ACL helper timeout. Production sync/async defaults, ACL verification, assertions, concurrency and job limits remain unchanged.
- The namespace relay fixture reuses the existing disjoint non-ephemeral port pool instead of releasing an ephemeral reservation before the child binds.
- Failure-only renderer diagnostics report bounded heading/ancestor visibility state. Redirect fixture diagnostics report bounded request method/path/byte count/body hash, never request content. Original timeouts, single-send assertions and product at-most-once behavior remain unchanged.

Local verification includes Ubuntu 98 related discovery/session tests and Windows 97 with one actual symlink-privilege skip; 18 Windows renderer tests; 25 Windows ACL/bridge/startup tests with one POSIX-only skip; and 78 namespace/native-retry/port-pool tests on each platform. Controlled tests verify the startup budget still fails closed, disjoint non-ephemeral allocation, and that injected extra requests still fail the original redirect assertion. Full syntax, seven application definitions, 224 changelog fragments and all 41 final diff hunks are verified.

The earlier renderer visibility timeout and extra three redirect-fixture requests have not been reproduced as product defects; their precise triggers remain unproven. The observed EADDRINUSE and PowerShell deadline failures have concrete fixture adaptations. No live provider calls, production actions or product retry/security-helper source changes.
