title: fix: reject Connect EOF without a readable stream terminal
body:
The Devin Connect runtime currently treats HTTP EOF, an unfinished frame or unreadable end-of-stream JSON as successful completion. A partial generation can consequently leave the forwarder with a normal success marker.

Require a readable logical terminator and reject missing/truncated endings. Reuse the existing terminal classifier, tightening it to reject non-object terminals and invalid error fields. Keep empty/JSON success terminals, `error:null` compatibility, existing error-code mappings and separate runtime/probe framing scanners.

Validation:

- The exact reviewed head `b876e516fc3b52d7413f16b1d2b9cda671c421a1` passed the [fork's full CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40843210598), including all three runtime platforms, desktop checks and repository validation. No source adaptation was needed.
- Temporarily integrated with upstream main `39894f9ea8fb6d1482b64affd1858e285baedb2b`: 108 tests passed across terminal auditing, Connect runtime, loopback forwarder, injected probe, protobuf codec/schema and turn translation, with no skips.
- Seven original-runtime negative cases fail against main: empty/message-only EOF, incomplete header/payload, malformed JSON, array terminal and invalid error field. The terminal-shape regression also fails against the original classifier. All pass with this patch.
- Loopback forwarding checks require buffered failures to return 502 and partial streaming failures to emit an error without `[DONE]` or a successful stop. Every request dispatches once and synthetic private values remain absent from diagnostics. Additional controls verify empty/JSON/`error:null` success, consumer cancellation and response-body cleanup.
- Changed-file syntax, changelog fragments and whitespace checks passed locally. The temporary merge was aborted and the exact reviewed head remains clean; its full repository CI is reused.

These are fixture-based transport checks; Devin's live-provider verification status is unchanged. No live account or paid generation was used.

Source review: [TruthNian/codex-router#49](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/49), audit finding `wire:W1`. No unmerged prerequisite is included.

title: fix: require completed compaction evidence without replaying partial generations
body:
Routed compaction currently accepts text deltas followed by HTTP EOF as a completed summary, and ignores an explicitly unsuccessful status in buffered JSON. Partial output can therefore replace history. Diagnostic event names can also feed failure classification and dispatch another generation.

Require successful logical completion for SSE and reject explicitly unsuccessful JSON statuses using the existing Responses outcome classifier. Keep supported complete JSON without a status. An incomplete generation stops before retry/failover classification; explicit HTTP refusals retain their status-based fallback. Preserve reported failed-generation usage while withholding partial output from checkpoints.

Validation:

- The unchanged reviewed head `f40fc9bff73e52dba5a9f5bfb9574f918892d904` passed [full fork CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40845014424) and the [three-platform Grok protocol workflow](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40845014414). Exact-head repository/platform/desktop checks are reused.
- Temporarily integrated with upstream main `39894f9ea8fb6d1482b64affd1858e285baedb2b`: 47 compaction/checkpoint/outcome/native-stream tests and 33 selected Router compaction/replay tests passed, with no skips. The resulting delta remains only these three files and preserves main's dense-shaping removal.
- A real Router negative control using main's original source accepted delta-only EOF with HTTP 200 where the regression requires 502. The patched V1/V2 matrix passes across SSE and JSON: no checkpoint from incomplete output, no second dispatch from partial-generation diagnostics, and reported 37-input/3-output usage stays on the failed-generation rows.
- Explicit HTTP 429 controls in both SSE and JSON reach a genuinely configured synthetic fallback, with exactly two dispatches. Successful terminals, status-less complete JSON, native replay, reasoning handling and existing image/search compaction paths remain covered.
- Changed-file syntax, changelog fragments and whitespace checks passed locally. The temporary merge was aborted; the original reviewed head remains clean. No live provider or paid generation was used.

title: opencode-go: four documented Go models are unroutable (gpt-6-luna, claude-haiku-5-5, minimax-m3.1-flash, kimi-k3.1-pro)
body:
`CURATION_ROUTES["opencode-go"]` (`src/opencode-curation.mjs`) omits four ids that `GET https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/models` currently advertises. `curate-models opencode-go --models <id>` refuses each of them with:

> This Codex Router version has not verified whether the model uses Chat, Messages, Responses, or Gemini, so it cannot be added safely.

Each model's `api` object in that same catalog response names exactly one wire, so no guessing is required:

| id | wire | $/M input | $/M output | context |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `gpt-6-luna` | `responses` | 0.10 | 0.50 | 1,050,000 |
| `claude-haiku-5-5` | `messages` | 0.10 | 0.50 | 1,000,000 |
| `minimax-m3.1-flash` | `chat-completions` | 0.15 | 0.60 | 1,000,000 |
| `kimi-k3.1-pro` | `chat-completions` | 2.00 | 10.00 | 1,048,576 |

Suggested placement:

- `responsesModels` += `gpt-6-luna`
- `messagesModels` += `claude-haiku-5-5`
- `primaryModels` += `minimax-m3.1-flash`, `kimi-k3.1-pro`

## Note on prefix rules

`minimax-m3` is served on Messages while `minimax-m3.1-flash` is served on Chat Completions, so a `minimax-` prefix rule would misroute the 3.1 Flash. Explicit per-id entries are needed rather than family-prefix inference.

## Verification

`gpt-6-luna` was probed live against the Go endpoint with a Go credential:

```
POST https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/responses
{"model":"gpt-6-luna","input":"Reply with exactly: OK","max_output_tokens":32}
-> HTTP 200, output_text "OK", usage 11 in / 5 out
```

The request requires the `x-opencode-session` header (without it the gateway answers `400 MissingSessionID` before considering the model). `applyOpenCodeSessionHeaders()` in `src/opencode-session.mjs` already covers every provider with `ownedBy: "opencode"`, including `opencode-go-responses`, so the transport needs no change — only the routing table entry.

## Why this matters

OpenCode desktop 2.2.5 ships `gpt-6-luna` on Go as its default model, and the Go plan bills it against the subscription allowance. Codex through codex-router cannot select it at all, so the same paid subscription exposes different model sets depending on the client.

title: refactor: read each image once with the selected engine
body:
Image reading currently retries failures and can walk additional engines after the selected one fails. That can spend additional calls or send image content to another provider. Partial native responses can also become cached evidence, while local cache identity omits the actual model and destination.

Use one selected engine and one request per read. Remove retry/fallback traversal, require successful Responses completion, and keep successful evidence caching plus explicit per-image failure output. Local cache identity includes the selected model and endpoint. Lazy candidate construction, caller-session gating, native account isolation, quota metadata and redirect refusal remain in place. Update the English, Chinese and Japanese guidance accordingly.

Validation:

- The unchanged reviewed head `1995ce45b1c3bb16d239d1c4f7429cf39ff9ffd8` passed [full fork CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40993742446) and the [three-platform protocol workflow](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40993742452). Exact-head repository/platform/desktop checks are reused.
- Temporarily integrated with upstream main `39894f9ea8fb6d1482b64affd1858e285baedb2b`. Four negative controls fail against main's original source: retry count, missing completion, multiline SSE framing and stale local model/endpoint cache identity. The patched controls pass.
- Real loopback Router checks cover failed/truncated/native and buffered JSON image reads with genuine configured alternatives still available: only the selected engine is called, incomplete content is excluded, a refusal does not purchase an alternate read, and completed evidence is reused. Unit checks cover native caller/account boundaries, successful evidence and question caching, quota metadata and redirect refusal. The actual local-cache function distinguishes three model/endpoint identities while reusing an unchanged identity.
- Initial parallel local execution reported 101 passes, three timeouts and one optional LiteLLM integration skip. Two failures occurred before image assertions in the fixture's unchanged 10-second Router-readiness wait; the third was an unchanged Windows private-file ACL PowerShell subprocess timeout. The failed-startup fixture left owned test processes/sockets, which were cleaned up. All three original cases then passed with test-file concurrency reduced to one, unchanged code, assertions and timeouts; force-exit bounded the fixture's known failed-startup handle leak. The underlying host-latency mechanism is not established by these results.
- Changed-file syntax, changelog fragments and whitespace checks passed. The temporary merge was aborted and the exact reviewed head is clean. No production restart or live/paid provider request was used.

Source review: [TruthNian/codex-router#51](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/51), findings `context:C7` and `context:C8`. No unmerged prerequisite is included.

Maintainer feedback and author decision:

The reported availability regression is real: a transient 429/502 followed by success can recover on main, while this PR returns the first failed image read. After examining the execution boundary, the author chooses to retain the single-submission design and disclose that cost. A 5xx response does not prove that generation was never executed. A synthetic loopback counterexample executes the first request and then returns 502; one retry produces two requests and two executions. A separate 429 fixture rejects before execution and then succeeds, producing one execution over two requests. These demonstrate possible delivery states, not actual provider billing or the frequency of either case. Status alone cannot distinguish them across every supported destination.

A bounded retry limits the number of attempts but does not establish idempotency. This PR favors avoiding bridge-initiated duplicate execution and cross-provider image disclosure over automatic recovery from transient refusals. This also preserves the intent of the existing [native generation delivery policy](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/blob/main/docs/native-generation-retries.md): no caller output alone is insufficient permission to replay a POST. This is the bridge's own automatic-submission boundary; it cannot prevent a caller or another intermediary from retrying independently. An explicit endpoint idempotency or delivery-policy contract could support a different choice later, but no new retry mode is introduced here.

An experimental broad429/5xxretry commit was prepared locally during review, then rejected before publication after this reassessment. It is not part of this PR. Current published head remains `1995ce45b1c3bb16d239d1c4f7429cf39ff9ffd8`, with its own applicable upstream CI passing and mergeability checked independently. Malformed, partial or empty successful responses still fail closed; no alternate engine is contacted.

title: fix: preserve explicit Command Code relay failures
body:
Command Code relay errors can currently be swallowed into a successful answer or deferred into another credential attempt. Preserve explicit stream errors, read failures, invalid UTF-8/JSON events, and nonempty malformed tool arguments through the existing error response, without replaying a submitted generation. SSE keepalive comments remain harmless.

Compatibility policy: clean EOF and received `finish`/`finish-step` events retain main's reason fallback, including `unknown`, `other`, future reason strings, and an omitted reason. Missing final tool input, null final input, and delta-free tool calls retain main's `{}` convention. An explicit final empty object still completes an incremental tool call once. Nonempty malformed argument fragments are rejected on both caller protocols.

Clean EOF without any finish event retains main's stop/end_turn convention too. No published contract or live trace establishes that the internal gateway always sends finish events. This deliberately does not claim that clean EOF or an SDK-generated finish proves origin completion. SDK flush may remain indistinguishable from a successful gateway finish under the legacy convention. No real Command Code success traces were obtained; unsupported assumptions about their absence are not used to narrow compatibility.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#52](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/52), original reviewed fork head `54ef0f8caefa4ffec289c3841d4f79f949bdaaf6`. Current adapted head: `8ed2c3dd47c7a788071fc06475d65833a685fbe9`.

Validation:

- 64 focused tests across all five Command Code suites pass on the adapted head and its clean integration with main `7f7b6287d2b12003f45a42c753db3290643b23dd` (tree `02627fa641a4a899178f8661bc61aa396343c94c`).
- Eighteen legacy cases across OpenAI and Anthropic compare exactly to main for both buffered bodies and complete SSE output. Relay tests additionally cover streamed/buffered legacy shapes with one submission and no replay.
- Explicit error finishes, malformed nonempty arguments, bad event JSON/UTF-8, reset/cancellation and response commitment regressions remain covered.
- Repository syntax, v2 application validation, changelog validation, and whitespace checks pass. The latest pushed head requires its own new upstream CI; previous green heads are historical evidence only.

The existing refusal-clock fixture corrections remain test-only. No production deployment/restart/configuration change or further paid generation was performed. These controlled traces do not identify the historical UI timeout's root cause.

title: fix: preserve tool operation domains and reference constraints
body:
A tool whose object schema contains several operations could advertise only the first operation after root projection. For example, an automation tool with view/create/update/delete branches could reach a strict provider with `mode: { const: "view" }`, hiding the other valid operations. Spreading a referenced schema together with assertion siblings could also change the meaning of a closed object's constraints.

Preserve every branch property's alternatives in the provider-facing object projection. Complete string-literal domains become a typed enum; complex alternatives retain their schemas through `anyOf`. Preserve root constraints and close the projected union when every operation is closed. The client's complete original execution schema remains intact, including branch associations that the provider projection cannot express.

Only inline foreign references with annotation siblings. Retain object/array/unknown reference conjunctions when moving assertions would change their scope, while keeping the existing scalar UUID repair. Unsupported reference conjunctions can therefore still be rejected by a strict provider instead of being silently weakened.

Source review: [TruthNian/codex-router#53](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/53), exact reviewed head `85f163350b757fb1e8a97fa511b0f6c54c73c81f`. This is the original five-file change, without source or test edits. Its temporary integration with latest upstream main `39894f9ea8fb6d1482b64affd1858e285baedb2b` merged cleanly and was removed after verification; the original branch is clean.

Validation:
- 337 schema, chat-tool surface, namespace/custom relay, Grok/Gemini/Antigravity and Azure compatibility tests passed on the latest-main integration.
- Five real Router controls passed: deferred Moonshot definition repair, namespace forwarding/restoration, non-streaming dispatch restoration, tool-search discovery restoration, and the OpenCode Go Responses function-tool contract in both response modes.
- Four negative controls failed against original main and passed with this patch: complete operation domains across eager/discovered/deferred tools, namespace reference conjunctions, closed-object reference constraints, and conflicting branch property alternatives.
- Full repository check passed: syntax, seven v2-agent applications and 191 changelog fragments. All 18 final hunks and shared callers reviewed; whitespace passed.
- The [exact reviewed head's cross-platform and desktop CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40846357386) passed. The new upstream PR must receive and pass its own CI runs. No live provider or production probes were used.

title: refactor: remove inferred subagent interrupt injection
body:
The router could turn a stored `FINAL_ANSWER` handoff into an `interrupt_agent` invocation that the model never requested. This could add an interrupt beside a model-authored follow-up or to an otherwise empty completed response, including native turns whose lifecycle definitions were deferred.

Remove history-based finished-child inference and interrupt injection from JSON/SSE responses. Relay explicit model-authored lifecycle calls, preserving native namespace identity, call IDs and raw argument strings. Keep routed namespace/custom-tool restoration, subagent model/effort inheritance, and the native-tool availability constraint used by failover.

Source review: [TruthNian/codex-router#55](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/55), original reviewed head `f7370ae39626efc2ac10c7c0c8ce4c3554fc1dd6`. This adaptation starts from current upstream main `39894f9ea8fb6d1482b64affd1858e285baedb2b`. The seven reviewed patch files match the clean original-review/main merge, retaining main's Router and native-replay changes. Two additional content-only hunks correct troubleshooting advice that promised automatic interruption/recommended a restart, and identify the old closer as historical in an HTTP compatibility comment. The original fork branch and review head remain intact.

Validation on the adapted main-based change:
- 279 shared subagent, namespace/custom relay, Grok structured-patch, failover, model inheritance, effort, routing and turn-accounting tests passed.
- 15 real Router tests passed, including seven nested native replay identity cases, completed history without fabricated calls, explicit native calls, reasoning/plaintext handoff replay, routed call restoration, and subagent model pinning across both route types.
- Three negative controls failed against original main and passed with the patch: a follow-up acquiring an extra interrupt, terminal-only output acquiring a lifecycle call, and native completed history fabricating a call.
- Full repository check passed: syntax, seven v2-agent applications and 191 changelog fragments. Whitespace passed and all 72 original adaptation hunks reviewed. Removed internal helpers have no remaining runtime callers.

The original reviewed head passed [full cross-platform/desktop CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40988201319) and [Grok apply_patch protocol CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40988201320). These are provenance for the reviewed change; the adapted commit must pass its own new upstream CI. Validation used isolated synthetic state and loopback fixtures, with no live provider or production probes. Existing evidence limits on historical UI timeout causes remain unchanged.

Feedback clarification (docs-only head `4124fc0a704c3a1b238d2c76d5a382f49849cacb`): align HOW-IT-WORKS with the explicit-only implementation. The automatic Codex 0.147 badge compensation is intentionally removed; finished children still need a model-authored interrupt or a manual status refresh on affected clients. No supported-client fix range has been established. The author has explicitly chosen this design with its badge cost disclosed; maintainer acceptance remains pending. This does not claim that the client bug is fixed. Executable sources are unchanged from `710ffac8f2d0db9cd01ef17d3b0c1917c49b1dc5`; the new documentation hunk and whitespace were reviewed. New-head CI is required independently.

Independent assessment of the proposed version gate: the client badge defect is a real compatibility concern, but detecting an affected client version does not establish authority to interrupt a child now. An offline counterexample gives the old planner a historical FINAL_ANSWER followed by an explicit new follow-up and a working result; it still reports that child as a pending interrupt target. The old relay appends interrupts for those targets without a task-revision check. This demonstrates an information gap in the inference, not a claimed live incident. Keep lifecycle operations explicit rather than using historical completion to authorize a new side effect; the parent/model still has to issue the required interrupt when a child actually finishes. A future client fix or a richer task-status contract could change the compatibility decision, but no such fixed-version evidence is asserted here.

title: refactor: remove inferred local subagent certification
body:
A machine-local record could promote a route to the native child role or make an explanation call it verified, even though the old certification runner inferred delegation from text containing an agent name and marker. Historical verified records could also enter automatic probe selection again.

Remove the speculative local certification runner, its CLI/Electron API and proof-based capability overlay. Resolve publication from registry capabilities and explicit operator selection. Keep hidden models and explicit off choices authoritative. Retain historical diagnostics, treat verified history as settled for automatic probe selection, and preserve the separate explicitly forced diagnostic verification path.

This adaptation starts from latest upstream main `39894f9ea8fb6d1482b64affd1858e285baedb2b`. The reviewed runtime/test change integrates cleanly with main. Additional adjustments align AGENTS with the removed helper/local-promotion behavior and remove an orphan certification-timeout comment from IPC. The original fork branch and review head remain intact; registry certifications and accepted application artifacts are unchanged.

Validation on the adapted main-based change:
- 176 capability, state, catalog/publication, diagnostics, explanation, model inheritance, selection policy and UI tests passed.
- Both desktop preload IPC exposure/argument tests passed. Desktop TypeScript passed with no output/cache emission, using existing dependencies that match all six checked pinned versions. Changed Electron IPC/preload syntax passed.
- Three negative controls failed against original main and passed with the patch: a complete local record granting v2, a local flag claiming certification, and historical verified diagnostics being automatically re-probed.
- Full repository check passed: syntax, seven v2-agent applications and 191 changelog fragments. Whitespace and all 61 final hunks reviewed; removed runtime APIs have no remaining callers.

The [original reviewed head's full cross-platform and desktop CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40872914686) passed. title: test: remove unrelated thread creation from skill verification
body:
The skill-injection verifier rejected otherwise valid same-turn injection evidence unless that turn also contained a create_thread call with prompt/target arguments. Thread creation is unrelated to proving that the app supplied the managed skill pack and a model tool call referenced it.

Remove that extra assertion and its thread-call collector/result field. title: fix: preserve client default choices across catalog publication
body:
Routine catalog refresh currently re-enables Gemini's default after `--no-default-model`, while repeated DSH default takeover replaces the user's original recovery snapshot with the router's own selection.

title: fix: launch guided OAuth through the Windows command adapter

title: fix: preserve client terminal and cancellation evidence
body:
Claude and Cursor adapters could label an output-token cutoff or an incomplete response as normal completion. Gemini could turn EOF after partial text into STOP, and Cursor Agent continuation could keep working after its RunSSE connection closed.

Preserve output-token limits as Claude max_tokens / Cursor length, report unsupported incomplete or missing terminals as errors, and close Gemini EOF with OTHER rather than fabricating STOP. Parse canonical CRLF SSE, multiline data and split UTF-8 correctly. Tie Cursor continuation and pending local execution to the client connection so cancellation aborts canonical work and prevents later writes or tool requests.

Source review: [TruthNian/codex-router#60](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/60), original reviewed head `be280030ca6276750343c93036f92f9f45e7a701`. Current head `1ebf3f2408b1f6dbea5618325999f1609fbfc020` adds only the CI test synchronization described below; every runtime source byte is unchanged from the reviewed head. The reviewed client delta is 11 files / 49 hunks (+292/-34), with one additional test file / five hunks (+13). Original review SHA and fork PR remain available; the same existing branch was advanced for the necessary CI fix.

Client verification:
- Ten regression groups fail with current main's runtime files and pass with the client change: Claude terminal/usage handling, Cursor terminal and real disconnect behavior, Gemini EOF/read failure, cancellation and CRLF/Unicode framing.
- Integrated temporarily with main `a115a938d1e146dc2298a1323c84c10c1cc6a462`, clean merge tree `0465d05f51f1a2c933d9c8a87417a6edb629690c`. All 89 tests in eight suites pass, including adjacent Claude cancellation, Cursor public-edge and Gemini schema/trailing-turn coverage.
- Full repository check passed on that original integration: syntax, seven v2 applications and 203 changelog fragments. All 49 client hunks and whitespace reviewed; temporary merge aborted. The test-only follow-up was separately syntax-checked and tested; the changed head requires its own new upstream CI.

Ubuntu CI diagnosis and bounded fix:
- Initial [CI41386007376](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/41386007376) reports 6,059 passing cases, one failure and 69 skips. Its sole failure is `test/node-fixture.test.mjs`: HTTP readiness already succeeded, but the test immediately asserts an IPC request notice has arrived. HTTP and child IPC are separate channels with no such ordering guarantee. The related fixture files are identical to main; this is not evidence of a client startup timeout.
- Delaying only the fixture's IPC notice by 100ms, with the HTTP response unchanged, reproduces the exact failing assertion. A bounded event wait before the existing notice assertions makes all five fixture tests pass under that same injected ordering and normally. The 1,000ms HTTP budget, other readiness limits and all original assertions are retained. The fixture source used for injection is restored byte-for-byte; only the test synchronization is committed.
- The PR's own [CI41390727243](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/41390727243), belonging to exact head `1ebf3f24`, has now completed successfully on Ubuntu, macOS and Windows, with packaging/application checks also passing; [its discovery run](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/actions/runs/41390727234) passed. Independently rechecked on 8 November 2026: the PR is mergeable with no new review feedback. No blind rerun was used as the repair. The healthy real-provider proof and its failure-path limits are recorded below.

Real-provider verification, explicitly authorized by the operator on 2 November 2026:

| Isolated PR adapter | HTTP | Observed terminal | Duration | Router-reported input/output tokens |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Claude streaming | 200 | end_turn + message_stop | 1,075ms | 25 / 2 |
| Cursor Chat streaming | 200 | stop + DONE | 1,061ms | 25 / 2 |
| Gemini streaming | 200 | STOP | 687ms | 25 / 2 |

Exactly three probe generation requests were made through the existing configured `custom/z-ai/glm-5.3` route, one per protocol, with a synthetic request to reply only OK, low reasoning effort and a requested output cap of 128 tokens. The current PR adapters ran on a temporary private loopback listener; the existing router was used only as their canonical backend. No deployment, restart, proxy/configuration change, tool execution or user conversation input was involved. Matched per-request router metering reports provider custom, completed outcomes, one upstream attempt and no scheduled retry for each request, totaling 75 input and six output tokens. Concurrent unrelated usage was excluded by request interval and matching token/effort/tool-count metadata. Provider-origin execution and monetary billing were not independently reconciled.

A post-response probe-wrapper mistake treated the void-returning Gemini handler as an unhandled route and attempted a second header write after the valid HTTP200/STOP response. It was reproduced offline as ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT and corrected in the wrapper; it is not a client adapter failure. A persisted-evidence guard was verified without issuing any further paid requests.

These are real-provider HTTP protocol-adapter checks, not retail client application/UI runs. Truncation, cancellation and transport-fault paths remain separately covered by controlled fixtures; the three healthy calls do not prove every provider's failure behavior. The unchanged reviewed head's [fork CI](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40875491153) is historical source provenance, not the new head's CI. None of this establishes the exact cause of historical UI timeouts.

title: fix: keep the shared router available for every installed client
body:
Follow-Codex presence currently checks only DSH publication and terminal Codex. Closing the desktop apps can therefore stop the shared router while another published client still needs it. Cursor Agent-only setup also creates an owned launcher without a Cursor App publication snapshot, so removing Codex can incorrectly leave no installed clients and retire the service.

Share the existing read-only installation detector between presence and service retirement, and recognize the same ownership marker that the Cursor launcher writer uses. Any published non-Codex client keeps the effective presence mode at `always`; removing its last marker restores the stored preference. Managed Codex blocks, retained-catalog handling, foreign launcher protection, and the existing installed-target export remain intact.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#61](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/61), reviewed runtime head `9d9fe7254b65d9d1b0d20cc87c4e794ec545f3c5`. Submitted head `bb9868687fed3d787c96f756366510089008e24b` adds one test-only line to isolate `CODEX_HOME`: integration validation on a machine with Codex installed exposed the fixture reading that real installation marker. Runtime source is unchanged from the reviewed head. This item has no unmerged batch prerequisite.

Validation against freshly fetched main `a115a938d1e146dc2298a1323c84c10c1cc6a462`:

- Clean integration tree `f921c4be1f2fb0f038715d62c848df28e52cd016`; all 8 files and 22 default-context hunks reviewed. Its final main diff exactly matches the reviewed delta plus the isolated test fix.
- Presence, installed-target, and Cursor integration: 30 pass, 1 existing platform skip. Both new regression groups fail when replayed with main's presence and target-detector runtime, then pass with this change.
- Broader control, DSH install, native-catalog drift, and Claude configuration checks: 43 pass, 2 existing skips, reused after the one-line fixture repair because those tests and runtime bytes did not change. The initial broader run's sole failure was the Cursor fixture isolation issue described above; its 5 tests also pass separately after repair.
- Full repository syntax, 7 v2 applications, 201 changelog fragments, and whitespace checks pass. The original exact reviewed head also passed fork CI on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows; this upstream PR still needs its own CI for the submitted head.

Validation used isolated fixture directories. It did not stop, restart, or deploy the user's running router. No live-provider generation is needed to establish this installation-state contract, and these checks do not establish the cause of historical UI timeouts.

title: fix: report only established YAML configuration evidence
body:
YAML harness status currently compares the managed endpoint and then reports the entire provider configuration and model catalog as valid. Changing OMP or Hermes to a different protocol can therefore leave doctor green even though the diagnostic never checked that protocol.

Report that evidence at its actual scope: a current managed YAML endpoint returns `configValid: null`, and a matching publication marker returns `catalogFresh: null`. Doctor explains the unverified protocol/model contents as a warning; known-invalid state still fails. JSON providers retain their full comparison. Caller-key rotation uses the valid managed state and current owned endpoint it actually needs for YAML, retaining all installation/ownership prerequisites and the strict JSON preflight. The rotation transaction, locks, and credential writers are unchanged.

A YAML integration can consequently remain a warning after republishing. This change does not add a YAML semantic parser or claim that a warning proves the live configuration is broken.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#62](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/62). Reuses the exact reviewed head `640058e9207d3c2a78bd6ca351c9a09853dad515`, with no unmerged batch prerequisite.

- Clean integration tree `f522098edca6fca68280e0820dbc84ad2c46655d`; all 6 files and 11 default-context hunks reviewed. The integrated main diff exactly matches the original reviewed delta.
- 69 tests pass across caller-key CLI/auth, rotation, maintenance, client refresh, routed harnesses, idle/routing diagnostics, and generic-provider diagnostics. Fixtures use temporary client documents and synthetic caller capabilities.
- Three regression groups fail with main's runtime: changed YAML protocol evidence, unknown-versus-invalid doctor results, and YAML rotation with precise ownership evidence. All pass with this change; malformed JSON and each missing YAML rotation prerequisite remain rejected.
- Full repository syntax, 7 v2 applications, 201 changelog fragments, and whitespace checks pass. The same reviewed head passed fork CI on Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows; this upstream PR still requires its own new CI runs.

title: fix: preserve received HTTP responses without automatic replay
body:
The shared retry helper currently cancels a received HTTP error body before replaying the request. A subsequent delivery-gate change can leave the caller with that canceled response, and awaiting cancellation can also delay relaying the provider's diagnostic body.

Return every received `Response` intact from `fetchWithRetry`, without status-based replay, backoff, or cancellation. Only thrown transport failures enter its existing bounded retry loop. The default pre-send requirement, explicit availability-mode transport policy, caller-output and abort gates, budget checks, request-byte ownership, and attempt metadata remain in place.

This deliberately changes availability mode and safe methods too: a received 502/503/504 or other HTTP result is returned once rather than automatically retried by this helper. Protocol-specific caller decisions and the exported status classifier used by the provider key pool are unchanged. The retry guide and repository instructions describe the narrower transport-only policy. In router.mjs, routed models, image calls, and the separate empty-completion attempt explicitly pass retries: 0 already; those paths do not gain or lose HTTP status retries. Accepting the changed policy for callers that did enable retries remains an upstream maintainer decision.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#63](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/63). Reuses exact reviewed head `68a8dd2ff75f3e70dcb9166bca659e545f648021`; no unmerged batch prerequisite.

Validation against fresh main `50d853524a6704994bae3d2357946425eab7e2c6`:

- Clean integration tree `89f2a2f04632de648d2045eafb8364e0ab09b636`. All 6 files and 15 default-context hunks reviewed; integrated delta has the same stable patch ID as the original review (`c62481934591fd6fe27cf8b742178ff0487d274b`). Only AGENTS line offsets moved with main.
- 66 tests pass across native HTTP relay, delivery boundaries, pre-TLS recovery, HTTP body/decompression handling, provider routing, and request diagnostics. Real loopback fixtures check the original 503 body/header, one submitted POST, readable response identity, no cancellation/backoff for received responses, and permitted transport recovery.
- Three regression groups fail with main's retry runtime, then pass with this change. Revoked permission, exhausted budget, caller cancellation, and relayed output still prevent another transport submission; the positive recovery case retains identical request bytes.
- Repository syntax, 7 v2 applications, 202 changelog fragments, and whitespace checks pass. The upstream PR's own exact-head CI has now passed Ubuntu, macOS, Windows, discovery, packaging and application checks; this was independently rechecked on 8 November 2026. The maintainer's remaining hold is the explicit availability-policy decision described above, not pending platform tests.

All HTTP origins were isolated local fixtures. No paid provider generation, production deployment/restart, proxy/configuration change, or claim about the historical UI timeout's exact cause is involved.

title: fix: keep heartbeat observation bounded after response identity
body:
The heartbeat observer currently applies its partial-event limit only before a response identity is known. After `response.created`, an unfinished event can keep growing the observer's retained parse buffer for the remainder of the response.

Apply the existing 4,194,304-character partial-event threshold regardless of identity. Crossing it releases the parse buffer and calls the existing stop path, clearing the timer and disabling later observation/rearming. Original chunks are still forwarded unchanged. This intentionally stops synthetic heartbeats for the rest of an oversized partial stream while preserving its original bytes.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#64](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/64). Reuses exact reviewed head `06ed58601dd8c09da8b82c52cd275e9ac8efc3a6`; no unmerged batch prerequisite.

- 125 tests pass across heartbeat behavior, response-failure metadata, usage observation, and response piping. The new regression covers both pre-identity and post-identity oversized partial frames, later framing/identity events, disabled heartbeats, and byte-exact relay.
- A real isolated Router test also passes: normal silent Grok streams receive heartbeats, and other providers do not. The oversized-partial regression fails with main's runtime and passes with this change.
- Full repository syntax, 7 v2 applications, 205 changelog fragments, and whitespace checks pass. The exact reviewed fork head passed all-platform CI and its protocol workflow; this upstream PR still requires its own new CI runs.

Validation used local fixtures and made no paid provider generation or production service/configuration changes. These checks establish the observer's bound and relay behavior; they do not identify the historical UI timeout's exact cause.

title: fix: confine every local authentication header to the Kimi boundary
body:
The Kimi forwarder accepts the internal service key through Authorization, X-Api-Key, or X-Goog-Api-Key. Its upstream filter previously removed only Authorization, so the other two accepted local credentials could be forwarded alongside the provider OAuth token.

Filter all three local authentication headers at the Kimi boundary. The provider OAuth Authorization header is still injected afterward. Body normalization, token refresh, response relay, and other providers are unchanged.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#65](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/65), exact reviewed head `7bb21409b2f166e23caca18784da204afd76057d`. No unmerged prerequisite.

Validation:

- Reviewed all 3 files/hunks; +26/-15. Clean integration on latest main `b462793aab9d2c4ec5cdb7df7253713dae7f9133`, tree `479a751c661eb40374d0710d7221cfb648c10099`.
- 17 tests pass across the real loopback Kimi forwarder, OAuth refresh/session, caller authentication, protected caller-key command, and provider API-key forwarding. The forwarder accepts all three local authentication forms, sends only the synthetic Kimi OAuth token upstream, and preserves content type and existing normalization assertions.
- The regression fails against main's forwarder by capturing the leaked local API key. Full syntax, 7 v2 applications, 205 changelog fragments and whitespace checks passed on main 2dfc3444 integration. Main subsequently advanced only by the independent heartbeat change #1145; Kimi/auth/helper sources remain identical, so that evidence is reused.
- Original exact-head all-platform fork CI passed. This upstream PR requires its own new CI runs.

Only isolated loopback fixtures and synthetic credentials were used. No paid generation, production service/configuration changes, or real credential disclosure.

title: fix: cache only whole successfully completed reasoning chains
body:
The streaming reasoning replay observer can currently cache a truncated chain: after its turn limit is exceeded it drops one delta but can append later deltas. It also commits at EOF or [DONE] without a supported successful finish.

Discard the whole observed turn after overflow, malformed JSON/UTF-8, explicit errors, unsupported finish reasons, or an unfinished terminal. Cache only a whole chain ending in stop or tool_calls, matching the existing JSON tap. Disable further observation after either storing or discarding; keep the response bytes unchanged. The partial-line buffer and observed tool-ID count also stop at their existing limits.

This intentionally removes replay fallback for streams lacking supported completion evidence. A later compacted tool history may then lack required reasoning; retaining no chain is preferable to sending a fabricated partial chain. This does not turn those responses into transport failures or establish what every provider emits.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#67](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/67), exact reviewed head `ef551edc3d7f9a3a4ba4a39206e1fce15defc966`; no unmerged prerequisite.

Validation against fresh main `0b10ec7813b9aabcc7991b09a7814695ebb3637b`:

- Clean integration tree `16a56502713a4fd743f33a6d6e9df4ddbb981de6`; all 3 files/20 analyzer hunks reviewed. Integrated main diff exactly matches the original reviewed delta.
- 69 tests pass across replay, reasoning contracts, real local JSON-forwarder integration, chat tool surfaces, and tool arguments. One local LiteLLM-dependent test is conditionally skipped. Tests use isolated router state so operator catalog settings do not hide fixture models.
- Three regression groups fail against main's replay runtime: DONE without a successful finish, whole-chain overflow/terminal handling, and tool-ID overflow.
- Six additional boundary fixtures verify explicit error, unknown finish, clean EOF, oversized partial line, oversized message reasoning, and successful message-form caching; each asserts byte-exact relay.
- Full syntax, 7 v2 applications, 207 changelog fragments and whitespace checks pass. Exact-head all-platform fork CI passed; this upstream PR requires its own new CI.

No paid provider generation or production service/configuration changes. No historical UI timeout root-cause claim.

title: fix: bound lifecycle reordering with exact-once overflow passthrough
body:
Lifecycle reordering currently retains interleaved item frames and partial SSE frames without a byte bound. Use the shared buffered-response allowance to bound their combined retained bytes.

When the next chunk would exceed the allowance, flush retained original frames and the partial buffer, forward that chunk, then remain in passthrough mode. Queued frames are copied so a short subarray does not keep an entire incoming chunk alive. Normal promotion and terminal flushing release the held-byte accounting.

This deliberately gives up lifecycle repair for the remainder of an oversized stream. Clients may then receive overlapping lifecycles; the fallback preserves every event rather than dropping, duplicating, or inventing a terminal. Ordering already applied before fallback is not undone. An individual incoming chunk larger than the allowance also selects passthrough. The budget counts retained response bytes, not every object allocation or downstream queue.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#68](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/68), exact reviewed head `fc0d0615c99396307b1fd61a318ffe39affac64c`; no unmerged prerequisite.

- 93 normalizer, early-tool completion, response-pipe and stream-failure tests pass, plus 21 downstream message-phase tests. No skips. Coverage includes queued and partial overflow before EOF, permanent raw passthrough, invalid UTF-8 byte preservation, normal interleaved repair, fragmented input, CRLF, terminal flushing, and event multiset identity.
- The new overflow regression fails against main's runtime because retained data is not released before EOF.
- Full syntax, 7 v2 applications, 207 changelog fragments and whitespace checks pass. Exact-head all-platform fork CI passed; this upstream PR requires its own new CI.

title: fix: settle WebSocket turns at the logical terminal event
body:
A Responses WebSocket turn currently waits for the internal HTTP SSE body to end even after relaying a logical terminal. A provider that leaves the body open can hold the next request behind that drain. Closing that completed HTTP leg can also make routed usage appear canceled.

Use the shared response-outcome classifier to settle at the first logical terminal. Initiate reader cancellation without waiting for its cleanup promise, release the reader lock, and stop consuming trailers. Successful completed/done responses can establish continuation state; failed, incomplete, canceled and indeterminate terminals cannot. Preserve the serving attempt's completed usage when the HTTP leg closes, including the existing empty-completion repair's provider/model, aggregate tokens and metadata. A disconnect before completion still meters as cancellation.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#69](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/69), exact reviewed head `3cc9da46c1cb82a2e1877bceed299bfcd250fe43` (four original commits from `2e3fd008`). No unmerged batch prerequisite.

Validation against fresh main `0b10ec7813b9aabcc7991b09a7814695ebb3637b`:

- Clean integration tree `8ddeeda55c54ee61f6b68fd338cc9b33b0e79378`; all 6 files/22 analyzer hunks reviewed. Integrated stable patch ID matches the reviewed delta: `69ea13c9adf74623a8597800adad8574b36f2c6f`.
- 154 tests pass with no skips across WebSocket server/client, real loopback Router retry/usage, response usage and outcome handling. Tests cover retained HTTP bodies, a cancel hook that never settles, terminal aliases/statuses, successful continuation input, rejected unsuccessful continuation, interruption/backpressure, first-attempt and empty-repair completion usage, and preterminal disconnects.
- Main's WebSocket runtime fails the new queue-release test with a frame timeout. Main's Router runtime fails both routed accounting cases with status 0 instead of 200. These negative controls are separate from production behavior.
- Full syntax, 7 v2 applications, 207 changelog fragments, UI diagnostic-test syntax and whitespace checks pass. The original exact head passed all-platform fork CI and its protocol workflow; this upstream PR needs its own new runs.

The existing UI-test diagnostic hunk preserves language-transition failure evidence (page/console/request state) without weakening its assertions or timeout. It does not establish the historical UI timeout's cause. There are no UI product changes.

Only synthetic local fixtures were used; no paid generation, production deployment/restart, or configuration changes. Transport cancellation is initiated at terminal; this does not guarantee that every provider immediately stops all background work.

title: fix: require real assistant completion when certifying stream compatibility
body:
The streaming compatibility probe currently searches the raw response body for the marker and completion words. An unfinished assistant delta containing `response.completed [DONE]`, or echoed input/reasoning, can therefore certify a stream that never completed successfully.

Parse fully framed SSE blocks with the existing multiline parser and shared outcome observer. Require the marker in typed assistant output and an actual completed/done response object whose observed outcome is successful. Quoted terminal words, [DONE] alone, incomplete/failed responses, unframed data, input echoes and reasoning text cannot certify streaming. Preserve supported delta, output-text-done, terminal output_text, assistant output parts, CRLF and multiline shapes.

This tightens the certification oracle; it does not change the generation relay. A stream lacking complete framing or a supported successful terminal now fails certification. Requests, timeouts, exact-route headers, quick mode and the caller's probe budget are unchanged. It does not prove all provider/client compatibility properties.
