title: fix: use one SSE event identity for empty completion guards
body:
Data-only Responses events and generic `event: message` frames currently get different effective identities in the empty-completion content guard and its downstream terminal guard. An empty completion can bypass the same verdict or terminal hold that an explicitly named frame receives.

Resolve the effective event name in the shared SSE field parser, using the JSON type for data-only/empty/generic message events while preserving explicit named-event precedence. Use that identity for content, liveness, supported explicit failures and terminal suppression. Malformed payloads remain indeterminate; content and explicit failures retain their original bytes. Retry policy and the boundary against retrying already relayed output are unchanged.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#71](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/71), exact reviewed head `88090bb19bd4e609f8d923aca930afed09eda8f8`; no unmerged prerequisite.

Validation against fresh main `0b10ec7813b9aabcc7991b09a7814695ebb3637b`:

- Clean integration tree `6b53591dbd8257f7a36f7487fb6ca617664f51c7`; all 3 files/7 hunks reviewed. Integrated main diff exactly matches the original reviewed delta.
- New regressions cover typed/data-only/generic frames, fragmented bytes, LF/CRLF/EOF, initial reasoning or created events, empty terminal withholding, real output, supported failure terminals and malformed uncertainty. Main fails the data-only and generic-message cases.
- Expanded local validation ran 129 guard/DeepSeek/Router/native-retry tests: 127 passed using temporary startup observation; two unrelated GLM cancellation fixtures also fail on main because their finite 10ms mock stream naturally ends before cancellation. Keeping only those verification mock streams open makes both original cancellation assertions pass. No assertion was removed; all temporary fixture changes were restored.
- Startup evidence is retained separately: the original suite had eight pre-listener readiness timeouts. A main control using the repository's existing fixture observer passed nine selected cases and measured a listener at 7.84s, beyond the original total 5s deadline. The observer preserves a 5s HTTP readiness budget after bounded warm-up. This is not an unmodified 129-test green claim.
- Full syntax, 7 v2 applications, 207 changelog fragments and whitespace checks pass. The exact reviewed fork head passed all-platform CI and its protocol workflow. This upstream PR must pass its own new applicable CI.

Only isolated local fixtures and synthetic credentials were used. No paid generation, production service/configuration changes, or historical UI timeout root-cause claim.

title: fix: keep native alias slots bound to their selected destinations
body:
Login-free native alias slots are currently reallocated by the current model ordering. Hiding/removing a model or refreshing priorities can therefore send an old native-looking model selection to a different paid model, or let a withdrawn alias fall through as native traffic.

Persist each slot's canonical destination separately from its active visibility. Reserve withdrawn bindings, restore their original slots when available again, and use one strict alias snapshot per request/publication. In login-free mode, withdrawn or unloaded destinations return 409 before either routed or native dispatch. Unreadable/invalid alias state returns 503 for native-looking requests; canonical registered routes remain independent. Catalog publication preserves bindings in native mode and rolls back its private files on publication failure. Legacy v1 active aliases seed the binding history.

Tradeoffs and adoption boundary:

- Withdrawn slots stay reserved, so finite native-slot capacity can be exhausted instead of reassigning an old identity. Previously lost legacy reservations cannot be reconstructed.
- Adopt a Router that rejects withdrawn aliases before publishing binding changes. The version-1 document keeps active aliases readable by older code, but older Routers do not understand reservations.
- Switching native/login-free mode emits a Codex reload requirement; a mode change does not prove the client has reloaded. Explicit native mode retains native passthrough. No running service is changed by this PR.

Source: [TruthNian/codex-router#72](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/72), exact reviewed head `4cb168bdcdfa34d373c471b0e18c7fad92e834d4`; no unmerged prerequisite.

Validation against fresh main `0b10ec7813b9aabcc7991b09a7814695ebb3637b`:

- Clean integration tree `54a75b30ed2d38c55366c48f463b062207217b5a`; all 10 files/33 analyzer hunks reviewed. Stable patch ID matches the reviewed delta: `68a42937f0b111a90e1b2318f5b32f0fa8baaec0`.
- Eight suites cover alias assignment/snapshot, repeated real catalog publication, private writer/rollback, auth-mode control, real Router failover/compaction routing, state ownership, refresh and config readers. The seven non-config-manager suites passed 195 cases. Config-manager passed 62 cases with one conditional skip after removing a verification-environment override that shadowed its per-test state directory. This is 257 unique passing cases and one skip across separate runs; the initial setup failures are retained in the evidence log.
- Main's assignment implementation rebinds destinations when ordering changes. Main's Router returns 200 for a withdrawn slot where the new regression requires 409. Both negative controls fail at the intended contract assertion.
- Nine additional strict-state cases cover absence, legacy migration, malformed/schema/conflicting maps, a directory masquerading as a state file, and withdrawn resolution without a lookup.
- Full syntax, 7 v2 applications, 207 changelog fragments and whitespace checks pass. Exact reviewed fork CI and its protocol workflow passed on all platforms. This upstream PR requires its own new CI runs.

The removed picker-import text scanner mistakes an environment key in the new child-process fixture for a parent-process assignment after import. Existing ownership/isolation tests remain, and the real publication fixture uses a scratch CODEX_HOME/state with synthetic credentials.

No paid generation, production deployment/restart, proxy/configuration change, or historical UI timeout root-cause claim.

title: refactor: reuse one kernel lease for local model operation starts
body:
Local model controllers use stale claim-file reclamation for their short check-and-seed section. This change reuses the kernel-owned lease already used by Antigravity: Windows named pipes and deterministic exclusive loopback listeners on Linux/macOS. A busy or colliding endpoint grants no ownership; process death releases the handle.

Ollama install/removal and MLX starts await the same gate before checking peer state and seeding their existing durable operation record. The redundant nested MLX file claim is removed. Antigravity retains its canonical credential identity, namespaces/port ranges, Windows pending-pipe workaround and bounded close behavior. Its five extracted helper function bodies were compared with main and are unchanged.

Review source: [TruthNian/codex-router#73](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/73), original reviewed head `9b940403bf1d77735f1fcfee06976d8ae4efc231`. The original fork review branch is preserved. The upstream adaptation also corrects an ordering assertion that accidentally accepted a missing match (`indexOf(...) === -1`); it now requires awaited gate acquisition.

The initial upstream Ubuntu CI failed two existing routing integration tests: the Z.ai headers-only case observed four requests instead of two, and a nested Groq tool-choice case hit Undici's 300-second body timeout. Both passed on Windows/macOS CI. The original Ubuntu triggers have not been reproduced locally, including on Ubuntu 24.04 with the same Node 24.22.1 and the exact CI-era integration source; this is not evidence that their cause is known or fixed.

Further investigation did reproduce a fixture cleanup defect: `server.close()` alone waits on an abandoned headers-only response. The two affected fixture files now stop admission and close remaining connections during teardown. A bounded, passive request observer adds failure-only method/path, response completion, read-phase and Router diagnostics without consuming request bodies or recording query strings/payloads. No production transport, retry policy, assertion or existing timeout was changed.

Validation of the updated integration against main `f6e633cf0ba29c804e7f0dcd3d9d496c96962a4d`:

- Ubuntu 24.04 / Node 24.22.1: 144 tests passed across both full routing files, local model/MLX operation suites and fixture regressions, with no skips and no preload instrumentation. Windows: all four targeted fixture/routing tests passed.
- Old-cleanup negative control fails with an active response; fixed cleanup passes. Injecting two abandoned GETs still fails the original `4 !== 2` assertion and records their methods, while teardown completes promptly. An injected body-read failure retains the original error and the response phase/gateway completion evidence. These are controlled faults, not a claim that the original CI received those injected GETs.
- Full repository syntax, seven agent applications, 210 changelog fragments and whitespace checks passed. All 72 final hunks were reviewed. Original unchanged-runtime all-platform fork CI [40993002107](https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/actions/runs/40993002107) remains historical source evidence; the latest head requires its own upstream CI.
- An instrumented full-root Linux diagnostic run did not reproduce the original two failures, but produced other archive/environment and observer-sensitive failures; it is not claimed as a clean full-suite run.

Upgrade boundary: old file-claim controllers and new kernel-claim controllers do not coordinate. Avoid overlapping controller versions during an upgrade. POSIX endpoint collisions can deny a start; they cannot admit a second owner. Existing durable operation state and long-running worker reconciliation remain unchanged. No model installation, paid-provider call, production deployment or Router restart was performed.

title: fix: omit raw upstream quota error messages
body:
MiniMax and Z.ai quota API error bodies can echo the submitted credential. These errors are copied into account usage snapshots consumed by the CLI and control center. Return the provider and numeric status instead of upstream status_msg/msg text; for MiniMax malformed JSON, replace parser errors that quote response text with a constant diagnostic.

Successful quota metrics, endpoints, authentication, unavailable-state handling and other transport errors are preserved. Vendor-specific error detail is intentionally reduced; a Z.ai business error delivered with HTTP 200 remains unavailable and reports HTTP 200. This does not claim redaction of every provider or transport error.

Adapted from TruthNian/codex-router#74 (reviewed source 7db4e228086c8146631f32b4df59da72534509f0). The additional malformed-JSON regression reproduced an echoed synthetic key in the parser exception. Final comparison against main 84bd2fd1d98183602964a347463e8b7c27a2a83c is 3 files, +54/-13.

Validation: account usage and consumer suites passed 73/73 on Windows and Ubuntu 24.04 / Node 24.22.1; nine additional synthetic privacy/status/transport boundary controls passed. All three regression cases fail against the original main implementation. Repository syntax, seven application manifests and 211 changelog fragments pass; all seven final hunks reviewed. No live provider calls or production changes.

title: fix: consume GGUF 16-bit metadata at its encoded width
body:
The GGUF metadata reader consumes UINT16 and INT16 values using a four-byte read, which advances into the next field and can make a valid model context length appear unknown. Read exactly two little-endian bytes, preserving signedness, so scalar values and array elements leave following metadata aligned.

This is the independent adoption of TruthNian/codex-router#75 (reviewed source bc6c77fdc6d4e677644b1134f995983e3cbac8a7), adapted onto main fcc1ca1a25d09af0e6759cda9c39092fb627b353. Only the decoder, synthetic regression fixture and changelog change: 3 files, +20/-1. Registry requests, download behavior, other value types, model selection and schemas are unchanged.

Validation: local-model and local-LLM consumer suites pass 55/55 on Windows and Ubuntu. The added regression fails against the original main decoder. Eighteen additional raw-byte assertions pass on both platforms, covering signed/unsigned extrema, two-byte arrays, truncation at a value, and the mocked ranged-registry consumer. The exact relevant source/test/lock blobs are unchanged by the subsequent main merge; final-head focused Ubuntu tests and repository syntax/manifest/changelog checks also pass. All five final hunks reviewed. No live downloads, model execution or provider calls.

title: fix: clean up headless Ollama until durable adoption succeeds
body:
When headless Ollama fails readiness or its process identity check throws, startup reports failure without stopping the child it just spawned. Keep readiness, identity verification and ownership-state publication inside one cleanup boundary, sending SIGTERM to that child on failure until durable adoption succeeds.

Reachable external daemons are not adopted or stopped. Successful durable adoption retains the child and the managed shutdown contract is unchanged. SIGTERM remains best effort; this does not cover errors before the readiness block or after adoption.

Independently adapted from TruthNian/codex-router#76 (reviewed source fdd3aa595bec194fbd3274541be0c65a0f2cc16c) onto main 2f6aaa6ae3dfdbc29be9b648101be167f677cb15. The append conflict preserves both main's kernel-gate test and the cleanup regression. Final difference: 3 files, +31/-14.

Validation: related local-model and local-LLM suites pass 55/55 on Windows and Ubuntu before the unrelated GGUF main merge; runtime, lifecycle test and lock blobs remain identical afterward. Final Ubuntu verification passes 16 focused tests including merged GGUF, kernel-gate and Ollama cases. Six mock-child boundary controls pass on both platforms: readiness, throwing/missing identity, state-write failure, success and external reuse. The new regression fails against the original main implementation. Five final hunks reviewed; repository syntax, application manifest and changelog checks pass. No production daemon or configuration changes.

title: fix: share the smallest advertised serving context limit
body:
Generic model curation takes the first advertised context field, so a model advertising 1,000,000 tokens with a 65,536-token serving endpoint can publish the larger window. Share the minimum-positive-integer parser with built-in discovery, considering all supported advertised scopes.

Generic metadata continues to accept decimal numeric strings; built-in context discovery continues to ignore strings. Invalid context values are ignored, and a record with no usable context value omits that claim rather than throwing for that field. Other metadata validation and the canonical context maximum remain enforced. Existing cached catalogs are not migrated or automatically republished, and provider advertisements are not proof of live serving capacity.

Adapted independently from TruthNian/codex-router#77 (reviewed source 7fd66ee5035d5714777f0bc10192f6f93b020945) onto main 3b212b8a5f63f9378fe7b27a45a8c49e227153ee. The helper's comment now documents the string distinction and the orphaned duplicate comment is removed. Final difference: 4 files, +31/-30.

Validation: capability, discovery, discovery-audit, untrusted-discovery and curation suites pass 100/100 on Windows and Ubuntu. Twenty extra boundary scenarios pass on each, covering all eight field locations, invalid values, string policy and existing validation limits. The new regression fails against original main with 1,000,000 instead of 65,536. Relevant source/test/lock blobs are identical after the unrelated Ollama main merge; final-head capability tests, 20 scenarios, changed-source syntax, seven application manifests and 214 changelog fragments pass. Initial full syntax check and all six final hunk reviews pass. No live provider calls or production changes.

title: fix: recheck the pool retry budget before extra dispatches
body:
The API-key pool can spend its remaining retry budget in backoff or locked credential selection, then dispatch an extra request. Recheck the budget at the loop entrance and after locked selection, only for retries (index > 0). The caller's first request remains eligible after a long initial selection wait, including when the retry budget is zero.

This preserves main's first-dispatch behavior, as requested in review. It does not add retryable statuses, increase the attempt cap, replay committed responses, cancel in-flight work or impose a hard deadline on selection/backoff/asynchronous send work. A first selection can still wait under the existing 120s pool-lock timeout; the 5s retry budget suppresses extra dispatches, not the original request.

Adapted independently from TruthNian/codex-router#78 (reviewed fork head f47dd8bfaf7dc5a716db8fd38c8364fd0b1667a1, both original commits), with the first-dispatch review correction at 09dc507e0b558f5816378a8fe3f11a3415ed9473, onto main 5bf59341961cbf842029c9c2fad0a0301da747fc. Final difference: 3 files, +59/-0.

Current fix validation: Ubuntu pool, forwarder, Command Code relay and redirect suites: 51 passed, zero failed, one conditional LiteLLM skip. Windows: three focused policy/deadline/first-dispatch tests passed. Six additional boundary scenarios pass on both platforms. Published head 8f459a0d fails the new first-dispatch control (zero sends instead of one), while unmodified main fails the retry control (two sends instead of one); the corrected head passes both. Changed runtime syntax, seven application manifests, 215 changelog fragments and all seven hunk reviews pass.

Local Windows full-suite limitation remains: before the correction, 49 passed, one failed creating a symlink with EPERM, one was conditionally skipped. The same symlink failure reproduces on unmodified main; no assertion or OS permissions were changed. Earlier upstream CI passed on 8f459a0d, and is historical evidence only. New-head upstream CI must pass independently. No live provider calls or production changes.

title: refactor: preserve empty TOML tables without post-processing
body:
The config manager cosmetically removes empty TOML tables using raw line matching after managed-block removal. A multiline instruction can contain the legacy agents marker and table-looking lines; cleanup can then delete actual user prose. Remove these cosmetic passes and keep the existing scanner-aware managed-block and owned-value removal.

Successful disable may leave legal empty [features]/[agents] tables and blank separators. This is intentional: managed settings are removed without promising cosmetic whole-file byte identity. Existing failure rollback remains byte-exact, and tests continue to require the original provider section and private-file protection. No public configuration schema or production configuration is changed.

Independently adopted from TruthNian/codex-router#79, reviewed head 4751b997ccd2ad99e55e1ac767246eb92937e440 (both original commits), onto main 30135a17f0815ba0b2b6cc4b598e60a40902a3e6. Final difference: 3 files, +48/-79.

Validation: full config-manager suite passes 64/64 on Ubuntu; Windows passes 63 with one platform-conditional refresh-catalog skip, covered on Ubuntu. The new prose-preservation regression fails against unmodified main. Six additional cases on each platform perform 18 real CLI enable/enable/disable operations, independently parse every result using Python tomllib, and assert exact literal/basic multiline bytes plus user feature/role values. Syntax, seven application manifests, 216 changelog fragments and all twelve final hunks pass review. An initial Ubuntu harness failure was traced to a shell subprocess not finding portable Node; adding its bin directory only to the validation process PATH yields the passing run. All configs/state are synthetic temporary fixtures; no production config or runtime-data backup operation.

title: fix: honor the explicit image modality answer during curation
body:
Interactive curation can retain provider-advertised image input even after the operator explicitly answers no, because only documented modalities are cleared. Always store the interactive image answer as text/image or text-only. When the operator changes the catalog default, do not label that modality choice as provider-advertised.

Also clear an already-generated generic catalog description when no advertised fields remain. Without this, a catalog that declares image support but no context size can leave stale modality provenance after an opt-out. Scripted curation still uses the catalog, and existing curated entries remain untouched. An operator answer is not proof of live provider image support.

Independently adapted from TruthNian/codex-router#80, reviewed source ba0adc601fb255d51160b34f87fe5d5229b65869, onto main 1adc720d2fbc56693c7881f4fada9434fc6be739, with the missing no-context provenance cleanup. Final difference: 3 files, +44/-8.

Validation: curation, capability, discovery and catalog suites pass 160/160 on Windows and Ubuntu. Twelve additional real CLI cases on each platform cover eight interactive catalog/context/answer combinations and four scripted catalog controls. The expanded regression fails on main because it retains image input, and on the original fork because it retains the stale description; the adapted head passes both. Syntax, seven application manifests, 217 changelog fragments and all six final hunk reviews pass. Synthetic catalog fixtures and --no-apply only; no production model changes or live provider calls.

title: fix: avoid capability caches without content or publisher provenance
body:
A local model tag can be replaced without changing its name, so a tag-keyed capability cache can retain old tools or image support. Cache local capabilities only when the caller supplies a content ID; keep cache hits for unchanged IDs and inspect models without IDs again.

Vertex discovery also loses authority when publisher resources are flattened to IDs and later requalified using only the static support catalog. Stop reading/writing that discovery cache and classify each explicit Model Garden response with its publisher provenance intact. Static catalog inspection remains separate, the existing configured-identity check remains, and inference adapters are untouched.

Tradeoffs: missing-ID local inspections can run more Ollama show subprocesses; each explicit Vertex discovery refetches its pages and can fail offline instead of using an ID-only cache. Existing cache files are left alone. Supplied IDs retain their existing content-ID contract; this does not add digest-format validation.

Independently adopted from TruthNian/codex-router#81, reviewed source 0394a7d116791ff7d16046634ae2b67393cdd1aa, onto main 7fe2abc244d037773b513c38b3d32cf67bc746bd. The append conflict preserves both main's GGUF regression and the new cache regression. Final difference: 6 files, +65/-65.

Validation: local model/local-LLM, Vertex provider, provider catalog cache, discovery and catalog suites pass 189/189 on Windows and Ubuntu. Nine extra boundary scenarios pass on each, covering mutable tags, unchanged/new IDs, failure and empty-capability handling, repeated Vertex discovery, offline refusal, static inspection, publisher mismatch and configured-project identity changes. Both new regressions fail on original main. Syntax, seven application manifests, 219 changelog fragments and all thirteen final hunk reviews pass. Synthetic callbacks/fixtures only; no live provider generation or production actions.

title: refactor: share credential pool authority with read-only consumers
body:
Model discovery and account usage can read a different legacy account even when an API-key pool is configured. Use the shared pool authority for discovery identity, audit readiness/redaction and account usage. Discovery and audit opt into stable priority/id ordering among eligible resolved credentials; usage retains the ordinary non-committing dispatch preview. A paused, invalid or otherwise unusable pool refuses the read instead of falling back to an unrelated key; an absent pool keeps the legacy behavior.

The payload uses its authorized identity without a second legacy lookup. Read-only consumers do not advance pool selection or rewrite credential references. Request dispatch, retry policy, OAuth-specific account flows and special Vertex/generic discovery paths remain unchanged.

Validation: Ubuntu 169 passed and Windows 144 passed across the relevant discovery, audit, usage, credential, catalog-cache and API-key routing/control suites (the updated suites also include the API-key forwarder; Ubuntu additionally includes the full pool suite). Each platform has one genuine macOS-only keychain skip. Full syntax, seven application definitions and 220 changelog fragments pass. The new regression fails on main's runtime at the pooled-versus-legacy identity assertion; it also checks paused/invalid refusal without fetch, unchanged pool/store bytes and pool-secret audit error redaction. No live provider or production actions.

Source review: TruthNian/codex-router#82 at f9aa4cd6af9563b344016f3fa6217958be024003; adapted independently to main 56c71a1531b1f87f29e3a37f091969770ddc98f7 with stronger regression assertions. No unmerged prerequisite code is included.

Catalog regression follow-up (105463d6): a real locked round-robin dispatch during catalog fetch previously triggered a false credential-change error. Stable catalog selection ignores cursor and quota ranking, while retaining the actual selected-key/endpoint fingerprint and all eligibility checks. Regression coverage verifies successful fetch/cache reuse across normal rotation, quota-ranking independence, unchanged committing dispatch, true credential replacement rejection, paused-account cache invalidation and all-paused refusal. An eligibility or priority change may still invalidate the selected account; catalogs are never combined across accounts.

title: fix: bind Kimi refresh and retries to one credential context
body:
A Kimi CLI login or region switch during refresh can make the router save a refreshed token into another credential slot. The forwarder can also retry its original API URL with credentials and device headers resolved from the newly selected login.

Capture one Kimi environment per operation and pass it through token reads, refresh host, device headers, locked rereads, recovery/tombstone writes and the 401 retry. In-flight refreshes are shared only for the same credential slot and OAuth host; a waiting different account retains its own context and force setting. Account usage uses the same captured context for its refresh and quota request. No-argument session helpers remain supported; later operations observe the new CLI selection.

Validation: Windows and Ubuntu each pass 157 tests across Kimi session/forwarder/region/private-writer/onboarding/doctor, OAuth health, account usage, provider usage and file locks. Two additional quota controls pass on each platform. Main-runtime negative controls fail for the intended session-slot, 401 credential and quota-region mismatches. Full syntax, seven application definitions and 220 changelog fragments pass. Synthetic credentials and loopback/mocked endpoints only; no live Kimi or production actions.

The private-writer fixture forbids reads outside its root, including dependencies reached through external symlinks. Initial validation reproduced that same failure on the unchanged main session module; using physically local, lock-matching dependencies made all tests pass without changing the guard or product code.

Source review: TruthNian/codex-router#83 at cc2515c4057b3795e89cb90f6be4d113ab8114db; independently applied to main 56c71a1531b1f87f29e3a37f091969770ddc98f7. No unmerged prerequisite code included. Context pins the selected path/host/home; existing official CLI token rotation under the lock remains supported.

title: fix: verify local operation process identity before cancellation
body:
Cancelling a local download, uninstall, or MLX operation currently trusts a recorded live PID. After PID reuse, that can stop another process. This change stores the process start identity in controller/worker records and requires it to match before sending a stop request. The MLX process-group ESRCH fallback rechecks the identity before signalling the individual PID. The uninstall worker retains its identity when replacing the controller handoff record.

The adaptation preserves main's asynchronous kernel-owner lease and existing cleanup tests. It changes only the original fork #84 behavior; no unmerged prerequisite code is included.

Validation on ef9d2b8ec1366478ddef049875e234a513c9f514, based on main 9de1d251da6fc942c6a197ccb93e0dee33b9b8f2:
- Windows and Ubuntu: 119 tests each, 117 passed and 2 platform-conditional skips, across local LLM/MLX/model operations, uninstall identity, process identity and overlay publication.
- Both new cancellation regression tests fail with the unchanged main cancellation modules restored. The final source was restored byte-for-byte afterward.
- 21 additional isolated controls cover controller records, default lookup failure/mismatch, Windows tree arguments, permission refusal and successful same-identity PID fallback. All process signals/state in these controls are synthetic.
- Full syntax/application/changelog checks and all 49 changed-hunk review checks pass.

Missing identity metadata or an unavailable identity query fails closed, so an older active operation may no longer be cancellable through this API. This does not provide an atomic OS process handle: identity lookup and signal delivery still have a race window. The existing bounded identity helper and its timeouts are unchanged. No production deployment/restart or live provider generation was used.

Original reviewed source: https://github.com/TruthNian/codex-router/pull/84 (61a0e51c7ddf80b4f0e75b3fec8c7b7a302d734e; original fork CI 40994995664).

title: refactor: keep model families as read-only route summaries
body:
A multi-route model family currently exposes an aggregate switch that chooses one preferred route when enabled and withdraws multiple routes one by one when disabled. It cannot withdraw client-managed routes and can repeat catalog publication for each route.

This keeps the family on/off availability summary, makes it readable by assistive technology, and uses the existing per-route controls for changes. A single-route family retains its shortcut switch, addressed directly to its sole route. Multi-route users expand the family to choose exact routes. The summary still means that any usable route is visible, rather than that every route is enabled. Native-managed and unavailable-route guards remain in place.

Validation on afd4d58fc6edfdfdcbc4b017aaa5771ad4125981, based on main 9de1d251da6fc942c6a197ccb93e0dee33b9b8f2:
- Windows: 125 relevant tests, 119 passed and 6 POSIX-conditional skips, including all 18 production-renderer browser tests.
- Ubuntu: 107 Electron control/harness/usage tests, 106 passed and 1 platform-conditional skip. Type checking, production builds and full static/application/changelog checks passed on both systems.
- Rebuilding with the main ModelsPage makes the new real-browser assertion fail because the aggregate checkbox remains present. The final source was restored byte-for-byte and rebuilt.
- Additional isolated browser controls verify that the single-route shortcut submits only its exact slug, and an expanded multi-route choice submits only the chosen route slug while updating the family summary. These use fixture IPC and no real provider requests.
- All 12 changed hunks reviewed, with a clean immutable comparison boundary.

No backend control API, configuration schema, provider routing, or protocol changes are included. title: refactor: reuse the core Codex executable resolver in desktop integration
body:
Desktop executable lookup independently searches for Codex, so it can disagree with the core resolver about CODEX_BIN, bundled Windows binaries and router shims. Its generic executable lookup also returns the realpath target, losing the command name that version-manager dispatchers need.

This delegates desktop Codex detection/login lookup to the existing core findCodexBinary authority. For other commands, it keeps the existing search/access/regular-file checks and returns the validated candidate path with its executable name. The packaged app imports the version-matched helper from the already bundled router-src tree.

The Windows CI test step sets the existing synchronous private-ACL helper override to 45 seconds after a shared-runner private session-index publication exceeded the 15-second default. This is scoped to that CI step: production defaults, ACL checks, assertions, concurrency and other deadlines are unchanged. The exact slow PowerShell phase was not logged.

The local-operation contention test now acquires an available fixture namespace before checking exclusion and release. A kernel lease can legitimately be denied when an unrelated listener occupies its hashed endpoint. Fixture setup is bounded to 32 candidates; every exclusion/release assertion still uses one acquired namespace without retry. The original CI log did not identify its denied endpoint or occupant, so that historical trigger is not claimed proven.

title: [Bug]: macOS service generation drops the archive directory override
body:
### What happened?

The macOS service generator omits the documented `MODEL_ROUTER_TOOL_RESULT_RETENTION_DIR` setting. When an update, reinstall, or repair regenerates the LaunchAgent, a manually configured override is lost and new archives return to `<state dir>/retained-tool-results`.

Observed on an installed service: the override was absent from both the saved plist and loaded environment; new `.result` files appeared locally while the custom directory still existed.

### Reproduce without changing the service

From a checkout on macOS:

```sh
MODEL_ROUTER_TOOL_RESULT_RETENTION_DIR=/Volumes/Archive/router-results \
  node src/service-macos.mjs render |
  plutil -extract EnvironmentVariables.MODEL_ROUTER_TOOL_RESULT_RETENTION_DIR raw -o - -
```

**Expected:** prints `/Volumes/Archive/router-results` (a generic example).

**Actual:** `plutil` exits 1 because the key is missing. Reproduced with an isolated temporary home/state directory.

### Cause

[`environmentEntries()`](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/blob/9de1d251da6fc942c6a197ccb93e0dee33b9b8f2/src/service-macos.mjs#L72-L115) excludes the override even when supplied to the generator. [`writePlist()`](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/blob/9de1d251da6fc942c6a197ccb93e0dee33b9b8f2/src/service-macos.mjs#L227-L236) replaces the existing definition, and [archive directory selection](https://github.com/duolahypercho/codex-router/blob/9de1d251da6fc942c6a197ccb93e0dee33b9b8f2/src/tool-result-retention.mjs#L9-L11) falls back to the local default. Ordinary restarts do not regenerate the plist.

### Expected fix

Preserve the selected archive directory across service regeneration, including maintenance without the original shell environment. Add regression coverage for preservation, explicit changes, and returning to the default. Keep existing storage and readback safeguards intact.

Codex

### Platform

macOS

### Doctor output or support bundle

Codex Router 0.6.0, revision 9de1d251da6fc942c6a197ccb93e0dee33b9b8f2.
macOS / Codex Desktop.

Confirmed with read-only service rendering. Windows/Linux not tested.

title: fix: keep the router port open while LiteLLM starts
body:
## Summary

A service restart could make Codex fail with `stream disconnected before completion: Connection refused (os error 61)`.

**Before:** `start.mjs` spawned the router only after the gateway was healthy, so port 4202 stayed closed for the whole LiteLLM cold start. Codex's retries hit a closed port. In the incident behind this fix, 4 retries were refused within about 3 seconds. Successful responses resumed about 18 seconds later.

**Now:**
- The router spawns right after the forwarders, before any dependency wait.
- Native turns are served as soon as the port opens.
- Routed, embeddings and decision requests wait through a new startup gate (`src/startup-dependency-gate.mjs`) for only the local dependencies they use, up to 60 seconds by default (`CODEX_ROUTER_STARTUP_HOLD_MS`, capped at 120 seconds, 0 turns it off).
- Each dependency latches open on its first healthy probe or at the bound and never closes again, so a later gateway crash behaves as before.
- A router that cannot bind now fails startup immediately instead of waiting out the gateway's allowance.
- `ready` still means the whole stack is healthy.

`AGENTS.md` gains a section with the rules for keeping this behavior.

## Verification

Real LiteLLM on isolated ports, with a dummy provider key and no model requests:

| | Port open, before | Port open, after | Stack ready, before | Stack ready, after |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Cold boot | 5076 ms | 578 ms | 5180 ms | 3560 ms |
| Relaunch | 5121 ms | 625 ms | 5197 ms | 3477 ms |

- `test/startup-restart-gap.test.mjs` drives the real `start.mjs` with a stand-in gateway: a native request is served during the cold start, a routed request is held until the gateway is up, and a router bind failure fails fast. These tests failed before the fix.
- `npm run check` and `git diff --check`: clean.
- `npm test`: 6182 tests, 6110 pass, 6 fail, 66 skipped. The failures are `test/desktop-panel.test.mjs` and `reviewed PR backlog: end-to-end acceptance` with its subtests (`timeout-ready`, `timeout-unready`, `startup proceeds past two real venv probe timeouts and keeps conclusive failures fatal`, `Claude subprocess controls reject before spawn and preserve resumed sessions`). The same names fail on unpatched `main` at 09edd659.
- This branch is 3 commits behind `main`. A trial merge is clean, but the suite was not rerun on the merged result.

**Not covered:**
- Not tested on a live restart of the installed service. The port stays closed for about 2 seconds while the old process stops and launchd starts the new one, so this shortens the gap and does not remove it.
- No end-to-end test for a client disconnecting during a hold, for the embeddings and decisions holds, or for per-route dependency selection through the real router. The gate's per-dependency logic has unit tests only.
- What triggered the original restart was not identified.
- The final per-dependency revision has not had a follow-up code review; the review covered the earlier version, and its findings are fixed here.
- Only lines 1–897 of `AGENTS.md` were read in full, plus section headings, keyword matches and the upstream retry section.

## Changelog

title: fix(router): keep Responses subagent effort nested
body:
## Summary

Fix configured subagent reasoning-effort overrides on Responses-native routes. A child can select the intended operator-configured Responses model correctly but fail on its first request with HTTP 400, while ordinary parent turns on the same model succeed.

## Symptom and root cause

The local API forwarder logs `Error (invalid_responses_request)` and the caller receives:

```text
HTTP 400: The API-provider forwarder could not complete the request.
```

The failure occurs locally, before the provider receives the request:

1. Codex sends a child request marked by `x-openai-subagent`, normally with `reasoning: { effort, summary }`.
2. A per-model subagent effort override is configured.
3. `buildRoutedRequest()` applies that override to both `reasoning.effort` and the legacy flat `reasoning_effort` field for every route except direct DeepSeek Responses.
4. Responses-native routes pass through `normalizeOpenAIRequest()`, which correctly rejects simultaneous aliases: `Use either reasoning or reasoning_effort, not both.`

Thus successful model selection or a working ordinary-turn smoke test does not establish that configured child turns work. This is not an upstream quota failure, a provider login failure, or evidence that the child selected the wrong model.

## Fix

- Responses-native routes carry the override only in `reasoning.effort`, removing any inherited flat alias.
- Chat Completions routes keep their existing flat-plus-nested compatibility behavior.
- Preserve the other reasoning fields, such as `summary`.
- Do not change provider/model selection, subagent inheritance, authentication, retry/failover policy, or adapter validation.
- Parent turns and unconfigured children remain unchanged; conflicting aliases on an ordinary request still fail closed.

The patch changes only the protocol gate and removes the stale alias. It does not relax the public adapter's validation to accept ambiguous requests.

## Regression evidence

The new real-Router -> real-API-forwarder -> loopback mock-upstream regression fails on unmodified main with the same HTTP 400 and `invalid_responses_request` signature. With the fix, it checks:

- A streamed child request with canonical nested reasoning reaches the mock provider with the configured override.
- A legacy flat-only child request is canonicalized.
- A child with inherited/conflicting aliases receives one canonical overridden effort.
- Other reasoning fields and readable collaboration task content survive.
- Parent turns and unconfigured children retain their own effort.
- Invalid parent requests still return 400 without reaching upstream.
- Built-in Meta and OpenCode Go Responses routes also omit inherited flat aliases.

Existing Chat Completions effort tests remain green.

## Validation

Based on upstream `main` at `9de1d251da6fc942c6a197ccb93e0dee33b9b8f2`.

```text
node --test test/routing.test.mjs test/namespace-relay-routing.test.mjs test/generic-ws-routing.test.mjs
223 passed, 0 failed

node --test test/openai-adapters.test.mjs test/generic-routing.test.mjs test/deepseek-responses-routing.test.mjs test/subagent-effort.test.mjs test/subagent-routing.test.mjs test/subagent-model-inherit.test.mjs test/multi-agent-state.test.mjs
83 passed, 0 failed

npm run check
passed

git diff --check
passed
```

All provider execution in these tests is local and synthetic; no paid provider or live model probe was used. The full repository suite and platform-specific packaging checks were not run for this bounded request-shaping change.

## Privacy and scope

Only router source, synthetic regression tests, and a changelog fragment are included. No credentials, private endpoints, operator configuration files, real task prompts, or production logs are included. Unrelated local model-menu changes are excluded.

title: fix(catalog): defer to the account catalog instead of appending bundled-only models
body:
Fixes #1098.

## What was wrong

`captureNative` merged the account-aware catalog with `codex debug models --bundled` using the default `includeBundledOnly: true`. The bundled catalog ships every model the build can address — published ones included. On a Free ChatGPT account, the bundled-only entries are therefore exactly the models the plan cannot call, so `gpt-6.1-sol` (and 7 more here) appeared in the picker and every turn answered *"This model isn't available"*.

Neither the installed revision nor `origin/main` (88 commits ahead) changes this; `mergeNativeCatalogs` and its call site are identical upstream.

## The change

A valid account catalog is the only list that reflects the plan, so capture now passes `includeBundledOnly: false` when it has one:

```js
const parsed = mergeNativeCatalogs(account, fallback, {
  includeBundledOnly: !validNativeCatalog(account),
});
```

This is the option already on the function — it just was not used during capture. The concerns from the issue thread are preserved:

- **Schema backfill still happens.** Bundled data continues to supply fields the remote cache may omit (`base_instructions` and friends) for every slug both lists share. Only the bundled-*only* entries are dropped.
- **The stale-cache safety is unchanged where it matters.** If no account catalog is read, `validNativeCatalog(account)` is false, `includeBundledOnly` stays `true`, and the bundled list is still the whole capture.

## Verification

Tests added in `test/catalog.test.mjs`:

- a source-level assertion that capture passes the account-authoritative flag;
- a behavioural case shaped like the report (one entitled model, a full bundled catalog beside it) asserting only the entitled entry survives **and** still receives its bundled `base_instructions`;
- the no-account-catalog path still capturing everything.

`node --test test/catalog.test.mjs` — 81/81 pass. `node scripts-check.mjs` — syntax and changelog fragments valid.

Measured on the affected Free account before/after: native capture drops from 13 models to the 5 the account lists (`gpt-6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, plus two hidden utility ids), and each of the three selectable ones still passes a live `responses` probe.

## Answering the maintainer's question

> Could you run `codex debug models` (not `--bundled`) with the router disabled and confirm GPT-6-Sol is absent there?

Yes — confirmed on a Free account. `GET /backend-api/codex/models` returns exactly 5 models and GPT-6.1 Sol / Terra / Astra / 5.6-Sol / 5.5 are all absent, while they are all present in `--bundled`. Codex's own account list is the right source of truth for the plan. The stale-cache caveat is real for a paid account whose cache lags a new release, but that is a refresh problem: the account catalog can be refreshed, whereas a plan entitlement cannot be inferred from the binary, so treating the bundled list as available was the wrong default.

title: [Bug]: [Bug] install.ps1 deletes itself after installing Codex CLI, damaging other router processes
body:
### What happened?

**Expected behavior:**  
`install.ps1` should persist on disk after being downloaded, and should not interfere with other router processes.

**Observed behavior:**  
After installing the Codex CLI, `install.ps1` started disappearing on its own between runs (without any local guard scripts). Additionally, other router processes started failing or behaving incorrectly.

**Timeline:**
- Before installing the Codex CLI, the desktop app was already installed and working.
- After installing the Codex CLI, `install.ps1` began disappearing inexplicably.
- Other router processes also started being affected (failures or incorrect behavior).

**Local mitigation attempt (now removed from report scope):**  
We initially created local helper files (`ensure-install.ps1` and a guard script) to re-download `install.ps1` when missing. However, the underlying issue is that the file deletes itself without any local intervention.

**Antivirus ruled out:**  
Windows Defender was checked and did **not** report any detection, quarantine, or removal related to `install.ps1`.

**Evidence:**
On a new run of `.\codex-router.ps1 doctor --fix --migrate-known`, the launcher reports:

[codex-router] install.ps1 no encontrado, descargando desde GitHub (commit 1a71b56e526a0718ebafc9be2ef5e29ff004c6b4)...
[codex-router] install.ps1 descargado y verificado.

This means `install.ps1` was missing at the start of the run, even though it had been downloaded in a previous run.

**Suspected causes (unconfirmed):**
- Something introduced by the Codex CLI installation is deleting or interfering with `install.ps1`.
- Installer rollback or another background process removing the file.
- A conflict between the CLI and the desktop app affecting router processes.

**Suggested improvement:**  
Investigate whether the Codex CLI installation introduces a process or policy that deletes/interferes with `install.ps1` and other router processes. Log clearly when and why `install.ps1` is removed.

title: fix: recover desktop page results that have no call id
body:
## Summary

Recover ambient app state that Codex Desktop injects without a paired tool call, so a routed request is no longer rejected locally before the provider sees it.

The first version of this patch allowlisted two page names. That was not the whole class. With the in-app browser open, Desktop also injects `agent.browser_tabs` with no `call_id`, and the same 400 returned on the first send of a turn. The retry omitted that item and succeeded. The recovery now covers every unpaired result in the `codex_app` and `agent` namespaces, which is the set Desktop has used for this state.

## Symptom and root cause

A routed model fails immediately with:

```text
HTTP 400: The API-provider forwarder could not complete the request.
```

The API forwarder log records only:

```text
[api-forwarder] request failed: Error (invalid_responses_request)
```

The public message is intentional. `formatErrorChain(..., { messages: false })` keeps upstream bodies out of the service log, so the caller cannot see which adapter check failed. The status is still the adapter's own 400. The provider process never receives the request.

Desktop persists ambient app state as a `function_call_output` that has a name, a namespace, an item id, and an output, but no `call_id` and no preceding `function_call`. Observed names:

- `codex_app.send_message_to_thread` and `codex_app.create_thread` on older builds
- `agent.codex_apps_open_page`
- `agent.codex_apps_selected_page`, including `_part_<n>_of_<m>`
- `agent.browser_tabs` while the in-app browser is open

`normalizeOpenAIRequest()` rejects any `function_call_output` that cannot be paired: `A function_call_output input item requires call_id and output.` The existing recovery rewrote only `namespace === "codex_app"`. A name allowlist for the two page tools still left `browser_tabs` on the failing path. A small probe without these items, and the client's retry after it drops the ambient item, both succeed on the same route. A synthetic `call_id` would not repair the item: there is still no matching call.

## Fix

`isOrphanCodexAppOutput()` recovers a named `function_call_output` with output and no `call_id` when its namespace is `codex_app` or `agent`. The result becomes readable history:

```text
[Codex app tool result: agent.browser_tabs]
<original output>
```

Left unchanged on purpose:

- A result that already has a `call_id` stays a tool result, including one in the `agent` namespace.
- A malformed result with no namespace, or with any other namespace, still fails closed at the adapter.
- The adapter itself still requires `call_id` on a real `function_call_output`. This does not loosen that check.

## Verification

Based on upstream `main` at `e449fd4`.

```text
node --test --test-name-pattern="router preserves orphan Codex app outputs as readable history" test/routing.test.mjs
1 passed, 0 failed

node scripts-check.mjs
syntax checks passed
changelog fragments valid

git diff --check
passed
```

The regression covers the old `codex_app` recovery, the page names and a paged part, `browser_tabs`, an unseen future `agent` name, a paired `agent` result, and unpaired results outside these two namespaces. The full `npm test` suite was not run for this request-shaping change.

After restarting a local build, one exact-route request carrying the page items and `browser_tabs` returned HTTP 200. That live call is not part of the repository suite.

## Changelog

`changelog.d/agent-page-tool-outputs.md`

## Privacy and scope

Only router source, the synthetic regression, and the changelog fragment are included. No credentials, private endpoints, operator configuration, real page text, or production logs are included.

title: feat(providers): add Standard Compute as a catalog-only provider
body:
Adds Standard Compute as a catalog-only provider, following the same shape as the Atlas Cloud provider (#1055).

Standard Compute is an OpenAI-compatible gateway at `https://api.stdcmpt.com/v1`. Its default model `StandardCompute` sends each request to the cheapest enabled model that can handle it, with automatic fallback; pinned model ids are listed by the public `GET https://api.stdcmpt.com/v1/models`. Website: https://standardcompute.com

## Changes

- `config/standardcompute/standardcompute.json`: provider `standardcompute`, kind `openai-compatible`, key `STANDARDCOMPUTE_API_KEY`, endpoint override `STANDARDCOMPUTE_API_BASE_URL`, keychain service `codex-router-standardcompute`. No preselected models.

- `test/standardcompute-provider.test.mjs` plus provider counts in `test/provider-catalogs.test.mjs` (47 to 48 canonical, 56 to 57 total).

## Protocol note

The gateway serves Chat Completions, not the Responses API. As far as I can tell from `src/api-forwarder.mjs`, `openai-compatible` providers without an `openai-responses` protocol are forwarded on `/chat/completions`, the same as the other catalog-only providers, so no Responses support is required from the upstream.

## Testing

Tests were not run locally; I am relying on CI. The test and count changes mirror #1055.

Disclosure: I work on Standard Compute.

title: chore(deps-dev): bump playwright from 1.64.1 to 1.65.0
body:
Bumps [playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) from 1.64.1 to 1.65.0.
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.65.0

🥟 Run tests with Bun

The test runner now runs under Bun. Bun transpiles your TypeScript test files itself, so Playwright does not use Babel or its compilation cache. Pass the --bun flag, because without it bunx playwright test runs on Node.js:

bunx --bun playwright test

Our CI runs the test runner tests under Bun 1.4.3 on Linux. Some features work differently under Bun:

  • There is no watch mode. UI mode does not run tests again when files change, and --only-changed does not follow imports.
  • Bun loads modules itself, so --tsconfig and the JSX options in tsconfig.json have no effect, and custom ESM loaders are not supported.
  • Stack traces do not include async frames, and API names do not include the class name: click instead of locator.click. This changes some step locations, step titles and error messages.
  • Console output of a test does not get into the trace and UI mode.

🚨 Reports with only failures

New failures reporter prints failures and successful retries as they occur, followed by a summary, without progress output.

New onlyFailures option of the HTML, JSON and JUnit reporters keeps only tests with unexpected outcomes, flaky tests and interrupted tests:

// playwright.config.ts
import { defineConfig } from '@playwright/test';

export default defineConfig({
reporter: [
['failures'],
['html', { onlyFailures: true }],
],
});

🎯 Test runner

  • New built-in -exclusive- test lock runs a test only when no other tests are running. All other tests continue to run in parallel with each other:

    test('restart the server', { lock: '-exclusive-' }, async () => {
  // No other test runs while this one is running.
});

  • test.skip(), test.fixme(), test.fail() and test.slow() now accept only a description. It is recorded in the test annotation:

    test('upload a file', async ({ page }) => {
  test.skip('Not implemented yet');
});

title: chore(deps): bump undici from 8.12.3 to 8.12.4
body:
Bumps [undici](https://github.com/nodejs/undici) from 8.12.3 to 8.12.4.
Release notes

Sourced from undici's releases.

v8.12.4

⚠️ Security Fixes

This release fixes six vulnerabilities.

CVE-2026-116592 / GHSA-mqg3-3v4r-cm32 (high)

Undici 8.12.2 and 8.12.3 could cache the final response from a redirect chain under the original request key without applying the origin, cache policy, freshness, or Vary requirements of every intermediate hop. This could poison a cache or expose one user's response to another user. The fix validates every redirect hop, combines their Vary fields, limits freshness and stale serving to the most restrictive hop, and invalidates persistent SQLite entries written by vulnerable releases.

CVE-2026-120474 / GHSA-7xg3-fphp-28hg (medium)

A shared cache used with compose(redirect(), cache()) could store a credential-dependent response from a same-origin redirect under the original URL. A later authenticated or unauthenticated request could then receive another user's response. Redirected requests carrying Authorization, Cookie, or Proxy-Authorization are no longer stored under the original alias key.

CVE-2026-116630 / GHSA-5rm8-gv32-r954 (medium)

A cross-origin redirect during cache revalidation could let a 304 Not Modified response from the redirect target validate a cached response from the original origin. Undici now checks that the revalidation target matches the cached URL and that any returned validator matches the stored representation before replaying the cached body.

CVE-2026-120415 / GHSA-9v6h-8rgp-m69f (medium)

The redirect interceptor did not strip credentials correctly when request headers were supplied as an array of [name, value] pairs. With a header-normalizing interceptor outside redirect(), credentials could be sent to a cross-origin redirect target. Undici now handles both tuple arrays and flat header arrays when removing sensitive headers.

CVE-2026-120222 / GHSA-3g9m-rv3r-w5w2 (medium)

A downstream handler exception during cache replay could escape as an uncaught exception or unhandled promise rejection and terminate the process. This included dump size-limit failures, excessive Content-Encoding values in decompress, asynchronous cache-store failures, and cached-body replay after a 304. These failures are now reported as request errors.

CVE-2026-120423 / GHSA-r4pc-4jcp-7pqc (medium)

fetch() could skip Subresource Integrity verification when valid integrity metadata was separated or surrounded by ASCII whitespace other than a space, including a horizontal tab. Integrity metadata is now split on all ASCII whitespace before SHA-256, SHA-384, or SHA-512 verification.

title: 修复 Responses WebSocket 丢失上游拒绝原因
body:
## 飞书文档与关联 MR

- 飞书文档：无。
- 关联 MR：无。

## 背景

Codex 经本地 Responses WebSocket 桥接收到 HTTP 400 时，如果错误正文使用 JSON `detail`、字符串、纯文本或 SSE 格式，现有转换会丢失具体原因，显示 `The local router rejected the Responses request.`，让上游拒绝看起来像 Router 自身故障。

本次调查中的两次原始 HTTP 400 正文未被保存，因此本 PR 修复可复现的错误信息丢失，不推断当时的具体拒绝原因。测试中的图片数量错误是合成用例。

## 改动内容

- 保留现有结构化错误以及 JSON `detail`、字符串错误和有界纯文本中的说明，并保留字符串类型的 `param`。
- 复用已有 SSE 解析器提取 `error` 和 `response.failed` 的错误信息。
- 无法读取的正文报告原 HTTP 状态，不再归因于本地 Router；HTML 和无关诊断字段不透传。
- 补充错误格式、文本字节边界、损坏 SSE、字段过滤和同连接后续请求的回归覆盖。

## 影响范围

仅影响 Responses WebSocket 对非成功 HTTP 响应的错误转换。保留原 HTTP 状态、已有限额元数据和不自动重试失败生成的行为；不修改上游请求、图片预算、模型选择、账号配置或服务生命周期。

title: [Bug]: Command Code DeepSeek V4.1 Flash repeatedly auto-compacts when eager tool schemas exceed the 850K threshold
body:
### What happened?

`commandcode/deepseek-v4.1-flash` at Max repeatedly auto-compacts within a single Codex turn on a tool-heavy installation. Compaction succeeds and reduces the local context count, but the next ordinary model response immediately recreates the above-threshold count. The task makes little progress.

Expected: compaction should leave enough usable context for ordinary work to continue, or deferred discovery should prevent the static tool catalog from exceeding the compaction threshold on each request.

### Which app do you route through?

Codex.

### Platform

macOS. Observed November 9–10, 2026.

### Environment and sanitized diagnostics

- Installed router source: `0.6.0`, commit `1a71b56e526a0718ebafc9be2ef5e29ff004c6b4`.
- Desktop app: `26.1103.60933`; bundled `codex-cli 0.167.0-alpha.3.2`.
- Exact route: `commandcode/deepseek-v4.1-flash`; upstream model `deepseek/deepseek-v4.1-flash`; effort Max.
- Published catalog: `supports_search_tool: false`, `context_window: 1000000`, `auto_compact_token_limit: 850000`.
- Rollout reports an effective `model_context_window: 950000`.
- No global `model_context_window` or `model_auto_compact_token_limit` override in the current Codex configuration.
- Both ordinary requests below returned HTTP 200. Provider input usage was zero; the router recorded fallback estimates separately. The estimates exactly match Codex's subsequent input-token events.

Second affected conversation, November 10 (UTC):

| Event | Input/context count | Router tool diagnostics |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Ordinary response around 07:53:06 | estimated input `948404` | `inputTokens: 0`, `estimatedInputTokens: 948404`, `providerToolCount: 1600`, `providerToolSchemaBytes: 2959056` |
| Successful compact around 07:53:07 | local `total_tokens: 41472` | — |
| Next ordinary response around 07:53:28 | estimated input `949880` | `inputTokens: 0`, `estimatedInputTokens: 949880`, same 1600 tools / 2959056 schema bytes |
| Successful compact immediately afterward | local `total_tokens: 42341` | — |

A separate November 9 conversation showed 13 compaction events in the captured in-progress turn. Representative ordinary requests carried 1607 tools / 2972638 schema bytes and fallback input estimates around 950K–959K; compacted local context repeatedly dropped to about 38K–41K before jumping back on the next response.

These are estimates, **not evidence of actual provider token consumption or billing**. No full support bundle or fresh doctor output is attached; this report uses narrowly selected rollout/usage-ledger fields to avoid exposing private prompts, connector data, credentials, or caller URLs.

### Reproduction conditions

1. Use Codex with a large connected-tool inventory and select this exact Command Code route at Max.
2. Start an ordinary task requiring tools; allow a model response and tool continuation.
3. Compare rollout token events with the router's `estimatedInputTokens`, `providerToolCount`, and `providerToolSchemaBytes`.
4. Observe successful compaction followed immediately by another ordinary response above the 850K threshold, without significant conversation growth.

### Analysis and possible direction

The installed `estimateInputTokens()` counts serialized model-visible request bytes at 3.3 bytes/token, including tool schemas. The 2972638 schema bytes alone correspond to approximately 901K estimated tokens, already above this route's 850K auto-compaction threshold. Summarizing history cannot remove the static tool-definition payload from the next ordinary request. This supports a self-recreating tool-surface/accounting trigger; it does not establish that the estimator is inaccurate.

The checked-in route lacks `searchTool`. Rechecked current main `bf13c0e261304c029361d7618daed3c4ab5f425f` on November 10: its descriptor still omits that declaration and retains `autoCompact: 850000`. Related precedents: #297 and #846. This is evidence for this provider/model route, not a request to change other DeepSeek routes or globally increase context limits.

### Exact-route compatibility evidence and limits

A small non-streaming synthetic probe through the installed router, using its exact-route-probe header to prevent substitution, succeeded at Max:

1. The provider requested discovery; the router restored native `tool_search_call` with client execution.
2. A manually supplied `tool_search_output` exposed one harmless namespaced fixture; the next response restored the correct namespace/name and `{}` arguments.
3. After a synthetic function result, the final response exactly matched the supplied verification value.

All three requests returned HTTP 200. No real connector operation was executed. This supports testing a model-specific `searchTool.mode: "standalone"` declaration using the existing relay, but does **not** certify actual Codex client-side search execution, streaming, catalog publication, or elimination of the loop at production tool scale. Those remain acceptance checks before declaring a fix.

An earlier probe retained a duplicate deferred definition at top level and failed. Codex's public `tool_search_returns_deferred_tools_without_follow_up_tool_injection` test shows a different normal follow-up shape; correcting the probe to that shape produced the successful result above. That separate synthetic relay edge case is **not** being claimed as this incident's cause.

No local live catalog, credentials, model settings, router source, or services were changed while collecting this evidence.

title: Deduplicate tool screenshots in Responses WebSocket turns
body:
## Summary
- Remove exact duplicate screenshots from tool results before forwarding a Responses WebSocket turn.
- Bound native screenshot history, replacing older images with receipts while retaining the newest capture.
- Retry a native HTTP 400 with fewer older images when the backend returns an opaque `{"detail":"Bad Request"}` and no response has reached Codex.
- Preserve readable upstream error details if the bounded retries still fail.

## Evidence
The original failed tool result contained two identical screenshots. A later computer-use thread continued receiving HTTP 400 after the static image-byte bound had trimmed older captures. Controlled probes showed that six full-resolution screenshots could fail while ten small images succeeded, so a byte bound alone cannot predict the backend's acceptance. After this change, a synthetic request carrying eight of the same full-resolution screenshot was initially rejected, retried with four images, retried with two, and completed with HTTP 200. The router log records both retries and the successful final response.

## Verification
- `node --test test/responses-websocket.test.mjs` (66 passed)
- `node --test test/native-retry.test.mjs` (25 passed)
- `npm run check` (passed)
- Live image-rejection replay through the installed router: HTTP 200 and `response.completed`.

title: [Bug]: Collaboration v2 threads fail with 400 invalid_responses_request — adapter rejects function_call_output items without call_id
body:
## Summary

When a Codex thread uses native multi-agent collaboration (v2), child-agent tool results are written into the thread context as `function_call_output` items that carry `id` and `namespace: "agent"` but **no `call_id`**. `normalizeResponsesRequest` in `src/openai-adapters.mjs` rejects such items with `invalid_responses_request`, so every subsequent turn of the thread fails with HTTP 400 (`provider_api_proxy_error`) before the request ever reaches the upstream. The native ChatGPT backend accepts these items — the same thread works when the router is bypassed.

## Evidence

- Forwarder log: `[api-forwarder] request failed: Error (invalid_responses_request)`; the gateway surfaces `400 Bad Request` with `{"error":{"type":"provider_api_proxy_error","message":"The API-provider forwarder could not complete the request."}}` (observed through the jev-codex-router fork, but the rejecting code lives in this repo's adapter).
- The Codex session rollout for the failing thread contains items shaped like:

```json
{"type": "function_call_output", "id": "fco_01a1cf82-0661-7d63-814b-386e9857182c", "namespace": "agent", "name": "browser_tabs", "output": "..."}
```

i.e. no `call_id` at all. The failure bursts correlate with the appearance of these items to the second (item written 11:26:07.457Z → first 400 at 11:26:07.552Z).
- Retries fail deterministically: Codex retried the identical request 3 times, 3 × 400. Threads without child-agent tool results pass — locally ~3000 successful routed requests vs 46 failures, all 46 in multi-agent threads (first occurrence 2026-10-06).
- Affected tool result names seen so far: `browser_tabs`, `codex_apps_open_page`, `codex_apps_selected_page_part_1_of_1` — all with `namespace: "agent"`.

## Root cause

`src/openai-adapters.mjs`, `normalizeResponsesRequest`:

```js
if (
  item.type === "function_call_output" &&
  (typeof item.call_id !== "string" || !item.call_id || item.output === undefined)
) {
  throw adapterError("A function_call_output input item requires call_id and output.");
}
```

The strictness was added deliberately ("harden OpenAI Responses adapter" / "fail closed on malformed Responses payloads", Aug 24–26), and the test suite even pins it (`invalid tool lifecycle fails closed`). But Codex's collaboration-v2 wire shape legitimately omits `call_id` on these relayed child-agent results, so the router ends up stricter than the upstream it proxies for — and the whole thread becomes unusable.

## Suggested fix

Stay transparent for `call_id`-less outputs (let the upstream judge them, as it already accepts them), keep failing closed on genuinely broken items:

```js
if (
  item.type === "function_call_output" &&
  (item.output === undefined ||
    (item.call_id !== undefined && (typeof item.call_id !== "string" || !item.call_id)))
) {
  throw adapterError("A function_call_output input item requires output and, when present, a valid call_id.");
}
```

I have this running locally with a regression test (pass-through for a `call_id`-less `function_call_output` with `id`/`namespace`; still throws on missing `output` or empty-string `call_id`). Happy to open a PR if you agree with the direction.

## Environment

- Codex desktop app 26.1106.x on macOS, ChatGPT sign-in, native models via `/v1/responses` through LiteLLM → api-forwarder.
- Multi-agent v2 enabled (`multi_agent_v2` feature); parent thread spawns child agents that use browser/codex_apps tools.
- Codex CLI/app retries surface this to the user as a hard 400 from the router.

title: fix(native): bound zstd window to prevent image-history HTTP 400s
body:
## Summary

Native ChatGPT requests containing repeated inline images can fail with a bare HTTP 400 even though the decoded JSON is valid. The router recompresses these requests with Node's default Zstandard settings, which can select a 2 MiB history window.

Set `ZSTD_c_windowLog` to `19` in `compressedNativeBody`, limiting the window to 512 KiB. The JSON, model, images and tool history are preserved. Existing small-body and compression-failure fallbacks are retained. Repeated large images can require more upload bandwidth with the smaller window.

A controlled comparison against the native ChatGPT Responses endpoint used the same authentication, `gpt-6-astra`, and byte-identical 4,199,362-byte JSON containing four synthetic 512×512 images, with tools disabled:

| Encoding | Wire bytes | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Zstandard level 3, default 2 MiB window | 788,383 | HTTP 400, `Bad Request` |
| Zstandard level 3, 512 KiB window | 3,151,424 | HTTP 200, `response.completed` |

Only the compression-window setting changed. This demonstrates a compression-dependent incompatibility on the tested endpoint; it does not establish a universal documented backend decoder limit.

The outgoing recompression path originated in #103. Related native Codex symptom and compression comparison: https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/58569.

## Related PRs

- #1192 improves upstream error visibility and adds a context-pressure diagnosis after an opaque HTTP 400 when the estimated input reaches the catalog compaction threshold. It does not change Zstandard encoding. That threshold alone cannot distinguish context pressure from the compression-dependent failure reproduced here.
- #1184 preserves upstream rejection details across the Responses WebSocket bridge. It improves the reported error but leaves the outgoing compression window unchanged.
- #1187 deduplicates tool screenshots, bounds native image history, and retries some rejected turns with fewer older images. It also leaves the compression window unchanged. This PR addresses the reproduced failure while preserving the complete decoded request, including all images, rather than reducing the history.

These changes can complement this fix. This PR adds the explicit compression-window bound and a regression that rejects the previous encoder's frame; it does not include the related diagnostic, image-retention or retry changes.

## Verification

- `npm run check` — passed.
- Full suite, `npm test -- --test-concurrency=1` — **6,158 passed, 68 skipped, 0 failed** on macOS with Node 24.18.0. The forwarded concurrency flag did not serialize files in this Node invocation; this remained a parallel full-suite run.
- The initial `npm test` run encountered a port-4212 conflict in the unchanged startup-cleanup fixture. That fixture passed in isolation and in the full rerun. No startup test or production startup changes are included.
- Strengthened the existing native-compression routing test with a decoder constrained to 512 KiB. Its negative control rejects the previous encoder's frame, while the patched router sends the same request successfully.
- The live comparison above used synthetic image data only; no private conversations, credentials or project media are included in this PR.

## Changelog

Added `changelog.d/native-zstd-window.md` and documented the encoding behavior and bandwidth tradeoff in `docs/native-generation-retries.md`.

title: [Bug]: Tray update fails with "npm is required but was not found on PATH" when node is a symlink in a PATH prefix
body:
`bin/install` bootstraps `node` and `npm` independently: each tool is accepted if `command -v` finds it, and only a missing tool falls back to a fixed list (`/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin`, `$HOME/.local/bin`, `$HOME/.npm-global/bin`, `$HOME/.volta/bin`, `$HOME/.asdf/shims`).

A Node installation outside those directories but reachable through a symlink inside one of them splits that pair:

```
~/.npm-global/bin/node -> ~/.local/node/bin/node   # node found
~/.local/node/bin/npm                              # real npm, directory not in the list
~/.npm-global/bin/npm                              # does not exist
```

So node resolves, npm does not, and the installer exits before it does anything:

```
npm is required but was not found on PATH.
```

## Why it matters

This is what the macOS tray hits on every click. `ModelRouterTray` prepends `~/.npm-global/bin`, `~/.local/bin`, `/opt/homebrew/bin`, `/usr/local/bin` to the GUI session PATH, so `Update & Verify` fails deterministically for this layout, while the identical `./bin/install` from a login shell succeeds because that shell also carries `~/.local/node/bin`.

The failure cascades, because `src/update.mjs` rolls back on install failure and the rollback re-runs the same installer:

```
npm is required but was not found on PATH.
Update failed and automatic rollback also failed. The previous commit is 9de1d251...
```

That leaves the checkout detached at the old revision with a manifest that never advances, so every later update attempt repeats it. The tray only surfaces the stderr tail, so the user sees the Node code frame for `codex-maintenance.mjs:64` instead of the single line that explains the failure.

## Suggest

When `node` is found, look for `npm` beside it (resolving the symlink) as well, or add `$HOME/.local/node/bin` to the candidate list. npm always ships beside node, so the two lookups have no reason to be independent.

Repro: macOS 27.2.0, Node v24.18.1, codex-router 0.6.0. Workaround: `ln -s ~/.local/node/bin/{npm,npx} ~/.npm-global/bin/`.
